title: High-Rate Scalable Entanglement Swapping Between Remote Entanglement Sources On Deployed New York City Fibers
authors: Alexander N. Craddock, Tyler Cowan, Niccolò Bigagli, Suresh Yekasiri, Dylan Robinson, Gabriel Bello Portmann, Aditya Verma, Ziyu Guo, Michael Kilzer, Jiapeng Zhao, Mael Flament, Javad Shabani, Reza Nejabati, And Mehdi Namazi
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander N. Craddock, Tyler Cowan, Niccolò Bigagli, Suresh Yekasiri, Dylan Robinson, Gabriel Bello Portmann, Aditya Verma, Ziyu Guo, Michael Kilzer, Jiapeng Zhao, Mael Flament, Javad Shabani, Reza Nejabati, and Mehdi Namazi

Performing high-rate entanglement swapping between independent sources over 17.6 km of deployed commercial fiber establishes a scalable architecture for metropolitan quantum networks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043028] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates high-rate entanglement swapping between independent entanglement sources over 17.6 km of deployed commercial fiber in New York City, establishing a scalable architecture for metropolitan quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require entanglement distribution between independent remote sources over real-world fiber infrastructure at high rates.
method: The authors perform entanglement swapping between remote entanglement sources using deployed commercial fiber links spanning 17.6 km in New York City.
result: They achieve high-rate entanglement swapping over metropolitan fiber, demonstrating a practical architecture for scalable quantum networking.
conclusion: This work advances experimental quantum network demonstrations and provides a path toward scalable metropolitan-scale entanglement distribution.

title: Second Law Of Thermodynamics In Closed Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Yuuya Chiba, Yasushi Yoneta, Ryusuke Hamazaki, And Akira Shimizu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuuya Chiba, Yasushi Yoneta, Ryusuke Hamazaki, and Akira Shimizu

A new theoretical framework reconciles the second law of thermodynamics with quantum mechanics, resolving a long-standing paradox by demonstrating how macroscopic thermodynamic principles emerge even from pure quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043023] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework shows how the second law of thermodynamics emerges in closed quantum many-body systems from purely unitary quantum dynamics.
motivation: There is a long-standing tension between the reversible dynamics of closed quantum systems and the irreversible second law of thermodynamics; this paper aims to resolve it by deriving macroscopic thermodynamic behavior from pure quantum states.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for closed quantum many-body systems, analyzing how thermodynamic irreversibility and macroscopic laws emerge from quantum mechanical evolution without invoking external randomness or collapse.
result: They demonstrate that macroscopic thermodynamic principles, including the second law, can emerge naturally even when the underlying quantum state remains pure and evolves unitarily.
conclusion: The work reconciles quantum mechanics with thermodynamics in isolated many-body systems and clarifies the emergence of macroscopic irreversibility from quantum dynamics.

title: On-Demand Millisecond Storage Of Spectrotemporal Modes At Telecom Wavelength
authors: Anuj Sethia, Nasser Gohari Kamel, And Daniel Oblak
abstract:
Author(s): Anuj Sethia, Nasser Gohari Kamel, and Daniel Oblak

The realization of scalable quantum networks for distribution of entanglement over long distances hinges on quantum repeaters. To outperform the exponential transmission loss in optical fibers, quantum repeaters must employ multiplexing schemes in the temporal, spectral, or spatial domain. The perfo…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 190801] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates on-demand millisecond storage of spectrotemporal modes at telecom wavelength for multiplexed quantum repeater applications.
motivation: Scalable long-distance quantum networks require quantum repeaters with multiplexing to overcome fiber loss, and practical repeaters need efficient quantum memories at telecom wavelengths.
method: The authors implement and characterize a quantum memory capable of storing spectrotemporal modes on demand for millisecond durations at telecom wavelengths, targeting compatibility with multiplexed repeater architectures.
result: The memory achieves millisecond-scale storage of spectrotemporal modes at telecom wavelength, supporting temporal/spectral multiplexing relevant to quantum repeater performance.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum network hardware by providing a telecom-compatible, multiplexable quantum memory building block for future quantum repeaters.

title: Exact Quantum Speed Limits For Quantum Gates From Space Curve Geometry
authors: Hunter Nelson And Edwin Barnes
abstract:
Author(s): Hunter Nelson and Edwin Barnes

The speed of quantum evolution is limited under finite energy resources. While most quantum speed limits (QSLs) are formulated in terms of quantum states, they can be extended to the evolution operator itself and thus impose fundamental limits on how quickly logical gate operations can be implemente…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052426] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives exact quantum speed limits for logical gate implementations by mapping the evolution operator to space curves and using geometric quantities to bound gate time.
motivation: Quantum speed limits traditionally constrain state evolution, but extending them to the full evolution operator is necessary to understand fundamental limits on how fast quantum gates can be performed under finite energy resources.
method: The authors formulate gate speed limits using space-curve geometry, relating the geometry of the evolution operator's trajectory to exact bounds on gate duration.
result: They obtain exact quantum speed limits for quantum gates in terms of geometric properties of space curves, providing tighter and more direct constraints than state-based QSLs.
conclusion: These geometric gate speed limits offer a fundamental framework for assessing and optimizing the speed of quantum operations, with implications for quantum computing and control.

title: Information Thermodynamics Of Agents: The Work Capacity Of Channels With Memory
authors: Lukas J. Fiderer, Paul C. Barth, Isaac D. Smith, And Hans J. Briegel
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas J. Fiderer, Paul C. Barth, Isaac D. Smith, and Hans J. Briegel

An information-theoretic model of agents, i.e., complex self-organizing systems, shows that agents must forget parts of their past actions in order to operate at thermodynamic efficiency.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041004] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an information-theoretic model of agents as self-organizing systems and shows that thermodynamic efficiency requires forgetting parts of past actions.
motivation: Understanding how complex adaptive agents process information under physical constraints is central to information thermodynamics, particularly the relation between memory, work, and efficiency.
method: The authors formulate work capacity for information channels with memory and analyze agents' thermodynamics within an information-theoretic framework.
result: They find that agents operating at thermodynamic efficiency must discard some information about their past actions, linking memory limitations to work extraction.
conclusion: The work connects channel memory, information processing, and thermodynamic efficiency, providing constraints on the design of physical agents.

title: Quantum Speed Limit For Measurement Probabilities
authors: Agung Budiyono And Sebastian Deffner
abstract:
Author(s): Agung Budiyono and Sebastian Deffner

Any protocol to process quantum information has to conclude with a measurement, aimed at producing a specific set of probabilities of measurement outcomes. In this work we investigate the time, energy, and importantly the genuine quantum resources necessary for transforming a set of measurement prob…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052210] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives quantum speed limits for transforming sets of measurement probabilities, quantifying the time, energy, and genuinely quantum resources required.
motivation: Every quantum information protocol ends in a measurement, so understanding fundamental limits on how quickly desired measurement statistics can be produced is important for quantum information processing.
method: The authors formulate the problem of transforming measurement probabilities and derive speed limits using time-energy and quantum-resource bounds.
result: They obtain bounds relating the minimal time and energy needed to realize a given transformation of measurement probabilities to the required quantum resources.
conclusion: The results clarify fundamental constraints on measurement-based quantum information tasks and connect quantum speed limits with resource requirements for processing quantum information.

title: Thermodynamic Speed Limits In Isolated Quantum Systems
authors: Rikuya Kobashi
abstract:
Author(s): Rikuya Kobashi

We derive thermodynamic speed limits for isolated quantum systems undergoing finite-time unitary driving. The key ingredient is a set of generalized second-law inequalities: For the Gibbs entropy and for several thermodynamically motivated observational entropies, the entropy production is bounded f…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043140] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives thermodynamic speed limits for isolated quantum systems under finite-time unitary driving using generalized second-law inequalities for entropy production.
motivation: Finite-time quantum processes are constrained by both thermodynamic and dynamical limits, but unified bounds connecting entropy production to driving speed in isolated systems remain important for quantum thermodynamics.
method: The author introduces generalized second-law inequalities for Gibbs entropy and several observational entropies, then uses them to bound entropy production in terms of finite-time driving parameters.
result: The inequalities yield thermodynamic speed limits showing how entropy production is constrained by the duration and nature of unitary driving for isolated quantum systems.
conclusion: These results provide a thermodynamic-speed-limit framework for finite-time unitary quantum dynamics and clarify fundamental tradeoffs between speed, entropy production, and thermodynamic observables.

title: Hardy-type Self-testing And Exposedness Of Tripartite Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger Correlations
authors: Smritikana Patra, Soumyajit Pal, And Ranendu Adhikary
abstract:
Author(s): Smritikana Patra, Soumyajit Pal, and Ranendu Adhikary

Nonlocality can be witnessed either through Bell-inequality violations or through logical contradictions such as Hardy's paradox. In the bipartite two-input two-outcome scenario, these two routes have distinct geometric behavior: Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt maximal correlations are exposed points of …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052423] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Hardy-type self-testing for tripartite GHZ correlations and analyzes their geometric exposedness in Bell correlation space.
motivation: Nonlocality can be witnessed through Bell inequalities or logical contradictions such as Hardy's paradox, but the geometric and self-testing properties of tripartite GHZ correlations are less understood than bipartite CHSH correlations.
method: The authors construct Hardy-type arguments for tripartite GHZ correlations and examine whether these correlations are exposed points in the relevant convex set of nonsignaling correlations.
result: They establish a Hardy-type self-testing result for tripartite GHZ correlations and characterize their exposedness, revealing geometric distinctions between Bell-inequality and Hardy-paradox routes in the multipartite setting.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of multipartite nonlocality by connecting Hardy-type logical contradictions with self-testing and convex-geometric properties of GHZ correlations.

title: Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation For Generalized Time-reversal Observables
authors: Tetta Indo And Yoshihiko Hasegawa
abstract:
Author(s): Tetta Indo and Yoshihiko Hasegawa

Time-reversal symmetry plays an essential role in the thermodynamic uncertainty relations, which bound the fluctuations of observables in terms of the associated dissipation. In fact, thermodynamic uncertainty relations are typically derived under the assumption that the observable of interest is an…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054119] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper generalizes thermodynamic uncertainty relations to observables with generalized time-reversal properties, extending fluctuation bounds beyond standard time-reversal-odd observables.
motivation: Thermodynamic uncertainty relations typically assume the observable is odd under time reversal, which limits their applicability to more general non-equilibrium observables.
method: The authors derive thermodynamic uncertainty relations by relaxing the standard time-reversal symmetry assumption and considering generalized time-reversal observables within stochastic thermodynamics.
result: They obtain generalized bounds relating fluctuations of broader classes of observables to entropy production or dissipation.
conclusion: The work broadens the scope of thermodynamic uncertainty relations and provides tighter or more applicable fluctuation-dissipation constraints in non-equilibrium systems.

title: Level 2.5 Large Deviations And Uncertainty Relations For Non-Markov Self-Interacting Dynamics
authors: Francesco Coghi, Amarjit Budhiraja, And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Coghi, Amarjit Budhiraja, and Juan P. Garrahan

We address the general problem of formulating the dynamical large deviations of non-Markovian systems in a closed form. Specifically, we consider a broad class of “self-interacting” jump processes whose dynamics depends on the past through a functional of a state-dependent empirical observable. Expl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 197101] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper formulates level-2.5 large deviations and uncertainty relations for non-Markovian self-interacting jump processes.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics with memory and self-interaction lack a closed-form large-deviation framework, limiting uncertainty relations beyond Markovian stochastic thermodynamics.
method: The authors consider self-interacting jump processes whose dynamics depend on the past through a functional of a state-dependent empirical observable and derive level-2.5 large deviations.
result: They obtain closed-form dynamical large deviations and corresponding uncertainty relations for this broad class of non-Markovian self-interacting processes.
conclusion: The work extends large-deviation and uncertainty-relation techniques from Markovian to non-Markovian self-interacting dynamics, with implications for stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Spectral Small-Incremental Entangling: Breaking Quasipolynomial Complexity Barriers In Long-Range Interacting Systems
authors: Donghoon Kim, Yusuke Kimura, Hugo Mackay, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Hideaki Nishikawa, Carla Rubiliani, Cheng Shang, Ayumi Ukai, And Tomotaka Kuwahara
abstract:
Author(s): Donghoon Kim, Yusuke Kimura, Hugo Mackay, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Hideaki Nishikawa, Carla Rubiliani, Cheng Shang, Ayumi Ukai, and Tomotaka Kuwahara

Researchers establish universal limits on quantum entanglement-spectrum evolution, enabling efficient classical simulations of long-range interacting systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041035] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes universal constraints on entanglement-spectrum evolution in long-range interacting systems, enabling efficient classical simulation beyond previous quasipolynomial complexity barriers.
motivation: Classical simulation of long-range interacting quantum systems is challenging because entanglement can grow rapidly, and existing complexity barriers limit efficient simulation methods.
method: The authors derive spectral small-incremental entanglement bounds that control how entanglement spectra evolve under long-range interactions, and use these bounds to construct efficient classical simulation algorithms.
result: They obtain universal limits on entanglement-spectrum evolution and show that these limits break quasipolynomial complexity barriers for simulating long-range interacting systems.
conclusion: The work provides new entanglement-theoretic tools for classical simulation and clarifies when long-range quantum systems remain efficiently simulable.

title: Intrinsic Hamiltonian Of Mean Force And Strong-Coupling Quantum Thermodynamics
authors: Ignacio González, Sagnik Chakraborty, And Ángel Rivas
abstract:
Author(s): Ignacio González, Sagnik Chakraborty, and Ángel Rivas

A unified theoretical framework allows one to measure thermodynamic quantities in strongly coupled quantum systems using only local information, offering a practical foundation for designing next-generation quantum thermal devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043014] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a unified theoretical framework for defining thermodynamic quantities in strongly coupled quantum systems using only local information.
motivation: Standard quantum thermodynamics assumes weak system-bath coupling, which breaks down for many experimental platforms; a consistent local formulation of strong-coupling thermodynamics is needed for quantum thermal devices.
method: They introduce an intrinsic Hamiltonian of mean force and build a framework for computing work, heat, and entropy using local (reduced) state information rather than global system-plus-bath quantities.
result: The framework yields well-defined thermodynamic quantities for strongly coupled quantum systems that agree with consistency conditions and are operational using local measurements.
conclusion: This provides a practical and unified basis for strong-coupling quantum thermodynamics, supporting the design of next-generation quantum thermal devices.

title: Tripartite Haar Random State Has No Bipartite Entanglement
authors: Zhi Li, Takato Mori, And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi Li, Takato Mori, and Beni Yoshida

Researchers demonstrate that bipartite Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen entanglement cannot be distilled from tripartite Haar random states by local operations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041013] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The authors prove that bipartite EPR entanglement cannot be distilled from tripartite Haar-random states under local operations, revealing a sharp structural obstruction in random-state entanglement.
motivation: Haar-random states are standard benchmarks for quantum information tasks and are often assumed to contain rich, generic entanglement; whether tripartite random states can yield bipartite entanglement via local operations was unclear.
method: Analytical arguments in entanglement theory combined with probabilistic/averaging techniques over the Haar measure are used to bound the extractable bipartite entanglement from tripartite random states under local operations and classical communication.
result: Bipartite EPR entanglement is shown to be non-distillable from tripartite Haar-random states by local operations, establishing a strong separability-like constraint on the bipartite entanglement content of generic tripartite states.
conclusion: Generic tripartite random states are far less useful for bipartite entanglement distribution than their global entanglement would suggest, with implications for entanglement measures, monogamy, and random-state-based protocols.

title: High-Performance Spin-State Memory For Telecom Quantum Information Applications
authors: James Stuart, Kieran Smith, Morgan Hedges, Rose Ahlefeldt, And Matthew Sellars
abstract:
Author(s): James Stuart, Kieran Smith, Morgan Hedges, Rose Ahlefeldt, and Matthew Sellars

A new work on erbium quantum memory reports a record classical efficiency and spin-state storage with multiple temporal modes, showing potential for practical quantum networks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043031] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: An erbium-doped quantum memory for telecom wavelengths demonstrates record classical efficiency and spin-state storage of multiple temporal modes, advancing practical quantum network hardware.
motivation: Telecom-compatible quantum memories with long-lived spin storage and multimode capacity are a key missing component for entanglement distribution and quantum repeaters over deployed fiber.
method: The authors use an erbium-doped crystal (rare-earth ion) platform at telecom wavelengths, implementing spin-state storage and measuring efficiency and multimode capacity via classical pulsed recall experiments.
result: The work reports a record classical efficiency for an erbium memory together with spin-state storage of several temporal modes, showing that the memory meets key performance metrics needed for network operation.
conclusion: The results indicate that erbium-based spin memories are viable candidates for practical quantum repeaters and networked quantum information processing at telecom wavelengths.

title: Extracting Information From A Superradiant Burst Using Simple Measurements
authors: Federico Belliardo, Anjun Chu, Martin Koppenhöfer, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Anjun Chu, Martin Koppenhöfer, and Aashish A. Clerk

A new quantum metrology protocol exploring many-body spin superradiance is presented.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043029] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a quantum metrology protocol that extracts information from many-body spin superradiance using simple measurements.
motivation: Superradiant bursts in spin ensembles are a rich many-body phenomenon, but practical protocols for extracting useful information from them are needed.
method: The authors propose and analyze a quantum metrology protocol based on many-body spin superradiance and simple measurement strategies.
result: The protocol enables information extraction from the superradiant burst, likely improving estimation performance in spin-ensemble settings.
conclusion: This work connects spin superradiance to quantum metrology and provides a practical measurement approach for hybrid quantum systems.

title: High-Dimensional Quantum Key Distribution Via Full Core-Mode Encoding Over Deployed Multicore Fibers
authors: G. H. Dos Santos, K. B. Sawada, N. Villalba, C. Jara, N. Guerrero, C. Melo, M. H. Magiotto, D. Martinez, G. B. Xavier, J. Cariñe, G. Saavedra, E. S. Gómez, S. P. Walborn, And G. Lima
abstract:
Author(s): G. H. dos Santos, K. B. Sawada, N. Villalba, C. Jara, N. Guerrero, C. Melo, M. H. Magiotto, D. Martinez, G. B. Xavier, J. Cariñe, G. Saavedra, E. S. Gómez, S. P. Walborn, and G. Lima

A four-dimensional quantum key distribution protocol utilizing full core-mode encoding over deployed multicore fibers is demonstrated, establishing a viable architecture for high-rate quantum-secure communications.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043012] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a four-dimensional quantum key distribution protocol using full core-mode encoding over deployed multicore fibers.
motivation: High-dimensional quantum key distribution can offer higher information rates and improved noise resilience, while multicore fibers provide a practical path for spatial-mode encoding in deployed quantum communication links.
method: The authors implement a four-dimensional QKD protocol that encodes information in the full core-mode space of a deployed multicore fiber and evaluate its performance as a quantum-secure communication architecture.
result: The demonstration establishes a viable architecture for high-rate quantum-secure communications using high-dimensional encoding over deployed multicore fiber infrastructure.
conclusion: The work supports the practical deployment of high-dimensional QKD in realistic fiber networks and highlights multicore fibers as a promising platform for quantum communication.

title: Adaptive Negativity Estimation Via Collective Measurements
authors: Martin Zeman, Vojtěch Trávníček, Antonín Černoch, Jan Soubusta, And Karel Lemr
abstract:
Author(s): Martin Zeman, Vojtěch Trávníček, Antonín Černoch, Jan Soubusta, and Karel Lemr

This paper explores an efficient method for entanglement quantification in two-qubit and qubit-qutrit quantum systems based upon the framework of collective measurements in conjunction with machine learning. We introduce an adaptive measurement procedure in which measurement settings are dynamically…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043152] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an adaptive collective-measurement and machine-learning approach for efficient negativity-based entanglement quantification in two-qubit and qubit-qutrit systems.
motivation: Entanglement quantification is resource-intensive, especially when full state tomography is required, so more efficient measurement strategies are needed for practical quantum information tasks.
method: The authors combine collective measurements with machine learning and dynamically adaptive measurement settings to estimate negativity in two-qubit and qubit-qutrit systems.
result: The adaptive procedure is presented as an efficient method for entanglement quantification, likely reducing measurement overhead compared with standard approaches.
conclusion: Adaptive collective measurements offer a promising route to practical entanglement estimation, though the contribution is more methodological and applied than foundational.

title: Certifying Localizable Quantum Properties With Constant Sample Complexity
authors: Zhenyu Du, Jinchang Liu, Elias X. Huber, Zi-Wen Liu, And Xiongfeng Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenyu Du, Jinchang Liu, Elias X. Huber, Zi-Wen Liu, and Xiongfeng Ma

Researchers develop a versatile quantum certification framework that verifies global state properties and fidelity using local Pauli measurements.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041027] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a quantum certification framework that verifies global state properties and fidelity using only local Pauli measurements with constant sample complexity.
motivation: Certifying global properties of quantum states typically requires many measurements, so efficient methods with rigorous sample-complexity guarantees are needed for scalable quantum information processing.
method: The authors develop a versatile certification framework based on local Pauli measurements and analyze its sample complexity for verifying global state properties and fidelity.
result: The framework certifies localizable quantum properties and state fidelity with constant sample complexity, making global certification feasible with local measurements.
conclusion: This work provides an efficient and broadly applicable tool for quantum state certification, with implications for verifying quantum devices and resources.

title: Non-Abelian Quantum Signal Processing: A Composite Pulse For Fast Analytic Control Of Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Processors
authors: Shraddha Singh, Baptiste Royer, And Steven M. Girvin
abstract:
Author(s): Shraddha Singh, Baptiste Royer, and Steven M. Girvin

Researchers extend quantum signal processing to noncommuting control variables, enabling analytical control of hybrid oscillator-qubit quantum processors.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041018] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends quantum signal processing to noncommuting control variables and introduces a composite-pulse framework for fast analytic control of hybrid oscillator-qubit processors.
motivation: Hybrid oscillator-qubit architectures require fast, high-fidelity control, but standard quantum signal processing techniques typically assume commuting control variables and are not directly suited to noncommuting controls.
method: The authors develop a non-Abelian formulation of quantum signal processing and use it to construct composite pulse sequences for analytic control of hybrid oscillator-qubit processors.
result: The proposed framework enables analytical control of hybrid oscillator-qubit systems using noncommuting control variables, yielding a composite-pulse protocol for fast control.
conclusion: Non-Abelian quantum signal processing provides a practical analytic route to fast control in hybrid oscillator-qubit processors and broadens the scope of quantum signal processing beyond commuting-variable settings.

title: Phonon-Bottlenecked Spin Relaxation Of ${\mathrm{Er}}^{3+}:{\mathrm{CaWO}}_{4}$ At MilliKelvin Temperatures
authors: S. Rajendran, B. Mistri, P. K. Sharma, S. E. Kubatkin, A. V. Danilov, S. Dhomkar, S. E. de Graaf, And V. Ranjan
abstract:
Author(s): S. Rajendran, B. Mistri, P. K. Sharma, S. E. Kubatkin, A. V. Danilov, S. Dhomkar, S. E. de Graaf, and V. Ranjan

We study spin-lattice relaxation times of electron spins in [MATH] coupled to a low mode-volume superconducting resonator at millikelvin temperatures in a regime where resonant phonons are cooled to near their quantum ground state. At large magnetic field supporting…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 206704] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally studies spin-lattice relaxation of Er3+ spins in CaWO4 coupled to a superconducting resonator at millikelvin temperatures, identifying a phonon-bottleneck regime relevant to hybrid quantum platforms.
motivation: Rare-earth spins coupled to superconducting circuits are promising for quantum memories and microwave-to-optical transducers, but their spin relaxation dynamics at millikelvin temperatures and in low-mode-volume resonators are not fully understood.
method: The authors measure spin-lattice relaxation times of Er3+:CaWO4 electron spins coupled to a low mode-volume superconducting resonator at millikelvin temperatures, in a regime where resonant phonons are near their quantum ground state.
result: They observe phonon-bottlenecked spin relaxation at large magnetic fields, showing that the relaxation dynamics are modified by the reduced phonon density of states and resonator coupling.
conclusion: The findings clarify relaxation mechanisms in Er3+-doped CaWO4 and have implications for designing rare-earth-based hybrid quantum devices such as microwave quantum memories and transducers.

title: Nature Is Stingy: Universality Of Scrooge Ensembles In Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Wai-Keong Mok, Tobias Haug, Wen Wei Ho, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Wai-Keong Mok, Tobias Haug, Wen Wei Ho, and John Preskill

Researchers introduce Scrooge
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041003] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces Scrooge ensembles to quantify how constrained quantum many-body systems can still achieve universal randomness and deep thermalization.
motivation: It aims to understand how universal random ensembles and deep thermalization emerge in quantum many-body systems under constraints, a question at the interface of quantum information and statistical mechanics.
method: The authors define and analyze Scrooge ensembles as a theoretical framework for characterizing constrained random ensembles in quantum many-body dynamics.
result: They establish universality of Scrooge ensembles across quantum many-body systems, showing that constrained systems can nonetheless produce universal randomness and deep thermalization.
conclusion: The work provides a general lens on randomness and thermalization in constrained quantum systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and many-body information dynamics.

title: Predicting Magic From Very Few Measurements
authors: J. M. Varela, L. L. Keller, A. de Oliveira Junior, D. A. Moreira, R. Chaves, And R. A. Macêdo
abstract:
Author(s): J. M. Varela, L. L. Keller, A. de Oliveira Junior, D. A. Moreira, R. Chaves, and R. A. Macêdo

A near-optimal method quantifies nonstabilizerness—the resource that enables universal quantum computation—from a small number of Pauli measurements, extending its estimation to system sizes beyond the reach of standard techniques.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043009] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a near-optimal method to quantify nonstabilizerness, or magic, from very few Pauli measurements, enabling estimation for system sizes beyond standard techniques.
motivation: Magic is the key resource for universal quantum computation, but its estimation typically requires many measurements and becomes impractical for large systems.
method: The authors develop a measurement-efficient protocol based on a small number of Pauli measurements to estimate nonstabilizerness, with theoretical guarantees of near-optimality.
result: The method accurately quantifies magic using significantly fewer measurements than existing approaches and extends estimation to larger system sizes.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and scalable tool for resource-theoretic characterization of nonstabilizerness, advancing operational quantum resource theories.

title: Ising On The Donut: Regimes Of Topological Quantum Error Correction From Statistical Mechanics
authors: Lucas H. English, Sam Roberts, Stephen D. Bartlett, Andrew C. Doherty, And Dominic J. Williamson
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas H. English, Sam Roberts, Stephen D. Bartlett, Andrew C. Doherty, and Dominic J. Williamson

An exact mapping to the 2D Ising model produces closed-form logical failure rates for the toric code, offering an analytic tool kit for benchmarking topological codes beyond current computational limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043004] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper maps the toric code to the 2D Ising model to derive closed-form logical failure rates and analytic benchmarking tools for topological quantum error correction.
motivation: Topological codes such as the toric code are central to fault-tolerant quantum computing, but benchmarking their performance at large code sizes is computationally demanding.
method: The authors construct an exact statistical-mechanics mapping between toric-code logical failure and the 2D Ising model, using it to obtain analytic expressions for failure rates across error-correction regimes.
result: They provide closed-form logical failure rates and identify distinct regimes of topological error correction, extending analysis beyond current numerical limits.
conclusion: The Ising mapping yields a practical analytic toolkit for benchmarking topological codes and understanding their error-correction thresholds and performance.

title: Stabilizer Entropy Of Subspaces
authors: Simone Cepollaro, Gianluca Cuffaro, Matthew B. Weiss, Stefano Cusumano, Alioscia Hamma, And Seth Lloyd
abstract:
Author(s): Simone Cepollaro, Gianluca Cuffaro, Matthew B. Weiss, Stefano Cusumano, Alioscia Hamma, and Seth Lloyd

We consider the costs and benefits of embedding the states of one quantum system within those of another. Such embeddings are ubiquitous, e.g., in error-correcting codes and in symmetry-constrained systems. In particular, we investigate the impact of embeddings in terms of the resource theory of non…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052428] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies stabilizer entropy for quantum subspaces to quantify how embedding states into larger systems affects non-stabilizerness as a resource.
motivation: Embeddings of one quantum system into another appear in error-correcting codes and symmetry-constrained systems, and the authors aim to understand the associated costs and benefits in the resource theory of magic.
method: The authors analyze stabilizer entropy in the subspace setting, characterizing how non-stabilizerness behaves under embeddings and constraints relevant to codes and symmetric systems.
result: They show how subspace stabilizer entropy captures the magic content of embedded state families and identify tradeoffs in non-stabilizerness arising from the embedding.
conclusion: Stabilizer entropy of subspaces provides a useful resource-theoretic tool for quantifying non-stabilizerness in structured quantum systems such as codes and symmetry-constrained spaces.

title: Negative Quasiprobability Trajectories For Bell-diagonal States Under Local Decoherence
authors: Qing Yu, Kun Zhang, Yang-Yang Chen, And Xiao-Hui Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Qing Yu, Kun Zhang, Yang-Yang Chen, and Xiao-Hui Wang

The fluctuation theorem (FT) relates microscopic trajectory distributions to macroscopic averages. Using quasiprobability trajectories, this framework has recently been extended to quantum information dynamics. Despite sharing the form of conventional thermodynamic FTs, information FTs involve quasi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054108] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates negative quasiprobability trajectories in information fluctuation theorems for Bell-diagonal states undergoing local decoherence.
motivation: Fluctuation theorems connect microscopic trajectory distributions to macroscopic averages, and recent work extends this framework to quantum information dynamics via quasiprobability trajectories.
method: The authors analyze quasiprobability trajectories for Bell-diagonal states under local decoherence and derive information-fluctuation-theorem-type relations.
result: The study identifies negative quasiprobability contributions and characterizes how local decoherence affects trajectory distributions in this class of states.
conclusion: Negative quasiprobability trajectories provide insight into the thermodynamic-information structure of decohered Bell-diagonal states and the quantum corrections to information fluctuation theorems.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Quantum Processors: Simulating Fermions, Bosons, And Gauge Fields
authors: Eleanor Crane, Kevin C. Smith, Teague Tomesh, Alec Eickbusch, John M. Martyn, Stefan Kühn, Lena Funcke, Michael Austin Demarco, Isaac L. Chuang, Nathan Wiebe, Alexander Schuckert, And Steven M. Girvin
abstract:
Author(s): Eleanor Crane, Kevin C. Smith, Teague Tomesh, Alec Eickbusch, John M. Martyn, Stefan Kühn, Lena Funcke, Michael Austin DeMarco, Isaac L. Chuang, Nathan Wiebe, Alexander Schuckert, and Steven M. Girvin

Researchers develop a hybrid qubit-boson quantum processor framework to simulate interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041008] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: Researchers develop a hybrid qubit-boson quantum processor framework to simulate interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields.
motivation: Simulating quantum many-body systems and gauge fields is challenging for classical computers, and hybrid oscillator-qubit processors offer a promising platform for quantum simulation.
method: They propose a framework that combines qubits and bosonic modes (e.g., in circuit QED) to encode and simulate fermionic, bosonic, and gauge field models.
result: The framework enables efficient simulation of these models, potentially with resource advantages over purely qubit-based approaches.
conclusion: Hybrid oscillator-qubit processors are a versatile and powerful platform for quantum simulation of complex many-body physics.

title: Enabling Deterministic Passive Quantum State Transfer With Giant Atoms
authors: Oliver Diekmann, Enrico Di Benedetto, Nicolas Jungwirth, Daniele de Bernardis, Zeyu Kuang, Francesco Ciccarello, Stefan Rotter, Peter Rabl, Alejandro González-Tudela, And Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver Diekmann, Enrico Di Benedetto, Nicolas Jungwirth, Daniele De Bernardis, Zeyu Kuang, Francesco Ciccarello, Stefan Rotter, Peter Rabl, Alejandro González-Tudela, and Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero

Tailored coupling between giant atoms and a waveguide enables deterministic quantum state transfer at above 99% fidelity, without any time-dependent control.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043013] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: Tailored coupling between giant atoms and a waveguide enables deterministic passive quantum state transfer with above 99% fidelity without time-dependent control.
motivation: High-fidelity quantum state transfer between distant nodes is a key primitive for quantum networks, but conventional schemes often require active time-dependent control.
method: The authors propose a waveguide QED scheme using giant atoms with engineered frequency-dependent coupling to realize deterministic state transfer in a passive manner.
result: The protocol achieves deterministic quantum state transfer with fidelity exceeding 99% without any time-dependent control.
conclusion: Giant-atom waveguide systems offer a promising platform for robust passive quantum interconnects in future quantum network architectures.

title: Fermionic Non-Gaussianity Via Bell Sampling: Monotones And Efficient Quantum Algorithms
authors: Poetri Sonya Tarabunga
abstract:
Author(s): Poetri Sonya Tarabunga

An experimentally accessible measure of fermionic non-Gaussianity not only bounds state-preparation complexity but also proves the irreversibility of exact Gaussian conversions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033065] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces experimentally accessible monotones for fermionic non-Gaussianity via Bell sampling and uses them to derive efficient quantum algorithms and prove irreversibility of exact Gaussian conversions.
motivation: Fermionic non-Gaussianity is a key resource for quantum computation, but experimentally accessible measures and operational consequences were lacking.
method: The author develops Bell-sampling-based protocols to estimate fermionic non-Gaussianity monotones and connects them to state-preparation complexity and Gaussian conversion irreversibility.
result: The proposed monotones bound state-preparation complexity and certify the irreversibility of exact Gaussian conversions, with efficient quantum algorithms for their estimation.
conclusion: Bell sampling provides a practical route to quantify and exploit fermionic non-Gaussianity as a quantum resource.

title: Fully Integrated Entangled Photon-pair Source On A Photonic Chip For A Wavelength-multiplexed Multiparty Quantum Key Distribution Network
authors: Maximilian Mengler, Jakob Kaltwasser, Erik Fitzke, Thomas Hoffmann, And Thomas Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Maximilian Mengler, Jakob Kaltwasser, Erik Fitzke, Thomas Hoffmann, and Thomas Walther

The development of QKD networks as a possible answer to the threat to encrypted communication posed by quantum computers has given rise to a variety of concepts and implementations in recent years. In terms of the scalability of such systems, photonic integrated circuits (photonic chips) are a promi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052607] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated photonic-chip entangled photon-pair source is demonstrated for a wavelength-multiplexed multiparty quantum key distribution network.
motivation: Scalable QKD networks require compact, integrated, and multiplexable entangled-photon sources to support multiple users and practical network architectures.
method: The authors develop an on-chip entangled photon-pair source and integrate it with wavelength-multiplexing functionality for multiparty QKD network operation.
result: The integrated source enables wavelength-multiplexed entangled photon-pair distribution suitable for multiparty QKD network implementations.
conclusion: Photonic-chip integration combined with wavelength multiplexing offers a promising path toward scalable multiparty quantum communication networks.

title: Floquet-engineered Dissipative Stabilizer Pumping In Neutral-atom Arrays
authors: F. Q. Guo, Shi-Lei Su, Weibin Li, And X. Q. Shao
abstract:
Author(s): F. Q. Guo, Shi-Lei Su, Weibin Li, and X. Q. Shao

Autonomous stabilization of many-body quantum states requires a mechanism that continuously removes stabilizer violations without relying on measurement and feedback. Here we develop a Floquet-Lindblad framework for scalable stabilizer pumping in neutral-Rydberg-atom arrays. Periodically modulated R…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052424] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a Floquet-Lindblad framework for autonomous dissipative stabilizer pumping in neutral Rydberg-atom arrays.
motivation: Autonomous stabilization of many-body quantum states requires continuously removing stabilizer violations without relying on measurement and feedback.
method: It uses periodically modulated Rydberg interactions and dissipation within a Floquet-Lindblad master-equation approach to engineer stabilizer pumping.
result: The framework provides a scalable route to dissipative stabilizer pumping in neutral-atom arrays, relevant to autonomous stabilization of many-body quantum states.
conclusion: Floquet-engineered dissipation offers a platform-relevant control strategy for stabilizer pumping and state stabilization in Rydberg-atom quantum systems.

title: Realization Of A Cavity-Coupled Rydberg Array
authors: Jacopo de Santis, Balázs Dura-Kovács, Mehmet Öncü, Adrien Bouscal, Dimitrios Vasileiadis, And Johannes Zeiher
abstract:
Author(s): Jacopo De Santis, Balázs Dura-Kovács, Mehmet Öncü, Adrien Bouscal, Dimitrios Vasileiadis, and Johannes Zeiher

Individual atoms trapped in a tweezer array are coupled to a high-cooperativity cavity and coherently excited to Rydberg states, uniting efficient light-matter interfacing with quantum logic operations on a single platform.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041039] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally realizes a hybrid platform in which individual atoms in an optical tweezer array are coupled to a high-cooperativity cavity and coherently excited to Rydberg states.
motivation: Combining strong light-matter interfaces with Rydberg-mediated quantum logic could enable new capabilities for neutral-atom quantum computing and networking.
method: Single atoms are trapped in a tweezer array, coupled to a high-finesse cavity, and optically excited to Rydberg states to demonstrate coherent cavity-Rydberg coupling.
result: The work demonstrates a cavity-coupled Rydberg array that unites efficient light-matter interfacing with Rydberg-based quantum logic on a single neutral-atom platform.
conclusion: This platform is a promising building block for hybrid quantum systems that combine cavity QED, Rydberg interactions, and scalable atom arrays.

title: A Guide To Higher-Order Quantum Operations
authors: Philip Taranto, Simon Milz, Mio Murao, Marco Túlio Quintino, And Kavan Modi
abstract:
Author(s): Philip Taranto, Simon Milz, Mio Murao, Marco Túlio Quintino, and Kavan Modi

The framework of higher-order quantum operations is laid out and its numerous applications across quantum information are presented in a unified and accessible manner.


[PRX Quantum 7, 042001] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: A unified and accessible guide to higher-order quantum operations and their applications across quantum information.
motivation: Higher-order quantum operations generalize standard quantum channels and are relevant to causal structure, supermaps, and quantum comb frameworks, but their diverse applications are often scattered across specialized literature.
method: The authors present the framework of higher-order quantum operations in a tutorial/review style, unifying concepts and surveying applications across quantum information.
result: The paper provides a coherent overview of higher-order quantum operations, including their formal structure and a broad range of uses in quantum information tasks.
conclusion: This guide serves as a useful reference for understanding supermaps, quantum combs, and higher-order transformations, though it is primarily expository rather than introducing a new core result.

title: Frequency- And Amplitude-Modulated Gates For Universal Quantum Control
authors: Qi Ding, Shoumik D. Chowdhury, Agustin Di Paolo, Réouven Assouly, Alan V. Oppenheim, Jeffrey A. Grover, And William D. Oliver
abstract:
Author(s): Qi Ding, Shoumik D. Chowdhury, Agustin Di Paolo, Réouven Assouly, Alan V. Oppenheim, Jeffrey A. Grover, and William D. Oliver

A new theoretical framework based on Floquet analysis enables quantum gate optimization using frequency and amplitude modulations, finding high fidelity and fast gates in superconducting circuits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033066] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a Floquet-analysis framework for optimizing frequency- and amplitude-modulated quantum gates, enabling fast high-fidelity universal control in superconducting circuits.
motivation: High-fidelity quantum gates are essential for quantum computing, and superconducting qubits require control methods that balance speed, fidelity, and leakage suppression.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on Floquet analysis to optimize gate protocols using simultaneous frequency and amplitude modulation of control fields.
result: The approach identifies high-fidelity and fast gate solutions for superconducting circuits, demonstrating improved gate performance through modulation-based control.
conclusion: Frequency- and amplitude-modulated gates within a Floquet framework offer a promising route to universal quantum control with high fidelity in superconducting qubit platforms.

title: Fundamental Limitations On The Reliabilities Of Power And Work In Quantum Batteries
authors: Brij Mohan, Tanmoy Pandit, Maciej Lewenstein, And Manabendra Nath Bera
abstract:
Author(s): Brij Mohan, Tanmoy Pandit, Maciej Lewenstein, and Manabendra Nath Bera

A fundamental quantum uncertainty relation reveals an unavoidable trade-off between the reliabilities of the charging power and the work deposited during the charging and discharging of quantum batteries, establishing essential design limits for future quantum energy storage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033057] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a fundamental quantum uncertainty relation showing an unavoidable trade-off between the reliability of charging power and the reliability of the work deposited in quantum batteries during charging and discharging.
motivation: Quantum batteries are promising candidates for future energy storage, but it was unclear whether power and work can be simultaneously made reliable; fundamental design limits were lacking.
method: The authors formulate and prove a quantum uncertainty relation between fluctuations (reliabilities) of power and work for charging and discharging processes of quantum battery models, presumably via uncertainty-relation techniques for observables and their dynamics.
result: An unavoidable trade-off is established: improving the reliability of charging power necessarily degrades the reliability of the deposited work, and vice versa, yielding intrinsic bounds on battery performance.
conclusion: The derived bounds provide essential design constraints for quantum energy storage devices and highlight the information-theoretic/thermodynamic limits on reliable energy manipulation at the quantum scale.

title: Logical Accreditation: A Framework For Efficient Certification Of Fault-Tolerant Computations
authors: James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, And Elham Kashefi
abstract:
Author(s): James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, and Elham Kashefi

Verification of encoded quantum systems is made possible with a scalable tool that assesses computational accuracy under general device noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033053] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces logical accreditation, a scalable framework for certifying the correctness of fault-tolerant quantum computations under general device noise.
motivation: Verifying encoded quantum computations is challenging because realistic devices are noisy and fault-tolerant protocols are complex, so efficient certification tools are needed to assess computational accuracy.
method: The authors develop a framework that accredits logical computations by testing encoded quantum systems and assessing their output against general noise models, enabling scalable certification of fault-tolerant implementations.
result: The framework provides a practical and efficient way to certify fault-tolerant computations, offering confidence in computational accuracy even when the underlying hardware is imperfect.
conclusion: Logical accreditation bridges fault-tolerant quantum computing and verification, providing a scalable certification method relevant to reliable quantum computation.

title: Breakdown Of The Kerr-Cat Qubit Tunneling Time Induced By Auxiliary Circuit Modes
authors: Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Cristóbal Lledó, And Alexandre Blais
abstract:
Author(s): Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Cristóbal Lledó, and Alexandre Blais

Researchers show that auxiliary circuit modes trigger multiphoton resonances that break down Kerr-cat qubit coherence under strong driving.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041012] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: Auxiliary circuit modes in Kerr-cat qubit architectures generate multiphoton resonances that degrade the qubit's noise-biased coherence under strong drives.
motivation: Kerr-cat qubits promise hardware-efficient biased-noise protection for superconducting quantum processors, but their coherence under strong two-photon driving is limited by spurious resonances whose microscopic origin was unclear.
method: The authors analyze the full circuit model of a Kerr-cat qubit coupled to auxiliary modes, identifying multiphoton resonance conditions and computing their effect on the tunneling time (bit-flip rate) via effective Hamiltonian and master-equation treatments.
result: Auxiliary circuit modes are shown to activate multiphoton transitions that dramatically shorten the Kerr-cat tunneling time, breaking down the exponential bit-flip suppression expected under strong driving.
conclusion: Design rules must account for auxiliary-mode-induced resonances to preserve Kerr-cat coherence at large drive amplitudes, an important constraint for biased-noise superconducting qubit hardware.

title: Free Mutual Information And Higher-Point Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlators
authors: Shreya Vardhan And Jinzhao Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shreya Vardhan and Jinzhao Wang

Researchers introduce a new entropic measure of quantum chaos, providing a physical interpretation to higher-point out-of-time-ordered correlation functions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043017] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce 'free mutual information,' a new entropic measure that gives a physical, information-theoretic interpretation to higher-point out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs).
motivation: Higher-point OTOCs diagnose quantum chaos and scram dynamics but lack a transparent physical meaning, unlike the four-point OTOC which is tied to commutators and information scrambling. The work aims to close this gap by linking them to an entropic quantity.
method: They define free mutual information using entropy measures (likely Rényi/free-energy-based) and derive relations showing that higher-point OTOCs are captured by the time evolution of this entropic quantity, presumably in chaotic many-body or holographic settings.
result: The free mutual information provides a quantitative entropic characterization of chaos that reproduces and generalizes the information-scrambling interpretation of higher-point OTOCs.
conclusion: The results establish an entropic, information-theoretic lens on multipoint chaos diagnostics, bridging quantum chaos indicators with entropic measures of information spreading.

title: Qubit Noise Sensing Via Induced Photon Loss In A Superconducting Cavity
authors: Nitzan Kahn, Dror Garti, Uri Goldblatt, Lalit M. Joshi, Fabien Lafont, And Serge Rosenblum
abstract:
Author(s): Nitzan Kahn, Dror Garti, Uri Goldblatt, Lalit M. Joshi, Fabien Lafont, and Serge Rosenblum

Characterizing noise in superconducting qubits is essential for improving coherence and gate performance. Conventional noise-sensing methods typically use the qubit itself as the sensor, which limits both accessible bandwidth and applicability during driven operation. Here, we measure qubit frequenc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 200801] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a method to sense noise in superconducting qubits by measuring induced photon loss in a coupled cavity rather than using the qubit itself as the sensor.
motivation: Characterizing noise in superconducting qubits is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but conventional qubit-based noise sensing is limited in bandwidth and incompatible with driven operation.
method: The authors use a superconducting cavity coupled to a qubit and infer qubit frequency noise from the photon loss induced in the cavity, enabling noise characterization without directly probing the qubit.
result: This cavity-based sensing scheme provides access to noise spectra over a broader bandwidth and can be applied during driven qubit operation, overcoming limitations of conventional qubit-based noise sensing.
conclusion: Induced photon loss in a superconducting cavity offers a practical and versatile approach for characterizing noise in superconducting qubit systems, with potential benefits for coherence and gate performance optimization.

title: Universal Criticality Of Entropy Production In Chemical Reaction Networks
authors: Kyota Tamano And Keiji Saito
abstract:
Author(s): Kyota Tamano and Keiji Saito

In homogeneous reversible chemical reactions, a prototypical nonequilibrium phenomenon, entropy-production fluctuations represent a sharper probe of nonequilibrium criticality than entropy-production response to variations in the chemical species concentrations.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 207101] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that entropy-production fluctuations provide a universal and sharper probe of nonequilibrium criticality in homogeneous reversible chemical reaction networks.
motivation: Nonequilibrium criticality in chemical reaction networks is typically probed via responses to concentration changes, but entropy-production fluctuations may offer a more sensitive thermodynamic signature.
method: The authors analyze homogeneous reversible chemical reaction networks within stochastic thermodynamics, comparing entropy-production fluctuations with entropy-production response to variations in chemical species concentrations.
result: Entropy-production fluctuations are found to exhibit universal critical behavior and serve as a sharper indicator of nonequilibrium criticality than the entropy-production response.
conclusion: The work establishes entropy-production fluctuations as a powerful universal probe of criticality in chemical reaction networks, with implications for nonequilibrium thermodynamics beyond quantum systems.

title: Symbolic Quantum-Trajectory Method For Multichannel Dicke Superradiance
authors: Raphael Holzinger, Nico S. Bassler, Julian Lyne, Susanne F. Yelin, And Claudiu Genes
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Holzinger, Nico S. Bassler, Julian Lyne, Susanne F. Yelin, and Claudiu Genes

We solve Dicke superradiance with two or more competing collective decay channels of tunable rates using a symbolic quantum-trajectory construction. The method yields closed time-domain populations and observables as finite combinations of exponential terms for arbitrary numbers of emitters and arbi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 193602] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a symbolic quantum-trajectory framework to solve multichannel Dicke superradiance for arbitrary numbers of emitters and competing collective decay channels.
motivation: Multichannel collective decay in Dicke superradiance is analytically challenging, and closed-form time-domain solutions are needed to understand competing emission pathways.
method: A symbolic quantum-trajectory construction is used to derive populations and observables as finite combinations of exponential terms for arbitrary emitter numbers and tunable decay-channel rates.
result: The method yields closed time-domain expressions for multichannel Dicke superradiance, providing analytic access to observables across competing collective decay channels.
conclusion: This approach enables systematic analytic study of multichannel superradiance and is applicable to collective emission phenomena in hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Impact Of Quenched Disorder And Multiphoton Interaction On The Dynamics Of A Quantum Battery
authors: Azam Mirzaei, Hamid Reza Baghshahi, And Mohammad Javad Faghihi
abstract:
Author(s): Azam Mirzaei, Hamid Reza Baghshahi, and Mohammad Javad Faghihi

Quantum batteries (QBs) represent a promising and emerging class of energy storage devices that exploit the principles of quantum mechanics to achieve superior performance compared to conventional, classical batteries. In this work, we investigate the charging dynamics of a QB in a bipartite system …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054107] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how quenched disorder and multiphoton interactions affect the charging dynamics of a bipartite quantum battery.
motivation: Quantum batteries are promising quantum-enhanced energy storage devices, but their performance under realistic disorder and nonlinear interaction effects remains to be understood.
method: The authors analyze the charging dynamics of a bipartite quantum battery model incorporating quenched disorder and multiphoton interactions.
result: The study characterizes how disorder and multiphoton coupling modify the battery's charging behavior and energy-storage performance.
conclusion: The findings clarify the interplay between disorder and nonlinear interactions in quantum battery dynamics, with implications for robust quantum energy-storage protocols.

title: High-fidelity State Transfer In Silicon-vacancy-phononic Networks With Closed Mechanical Subsystems
authors: Weihu Xu, Juntao Li, Zeyang Liao, And Xiaoqi Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Weihu Xu, Juntao Li, Zeyang Liao, and Xiaoqi Zhou

Building on the alternating-waveguide closed-mechanical-subsystem architecture introduced by Kuzyk and Wang [
tldr: The paper proposes a diamond phononic network using silicon-vacancy centers and closed mechanical subsystems for high-fidelity quantum state transfer.
motivation: It aims to overcome the coupling-hierarchy bottleneck in the alternating-waveguide closed-mechanical-subsystem architecture and improve on nitrogen-vacancy-based implementations.
method: The authors design a silicon-vacancy-phononic network with closed mechanical subsystems and analyze state-transfer fidelity through the mechanical modes.
result: The architecture enables high-fidelity state transfer in a phononic network while addressing the coupling-hierarchy limitations of prior designs.
conclusion: Silicon-vacancy phononic networks with closed mechanical subsystems are promising for reliable quantum state transfer and scalable quantum network architectures.

title: Stability, Degeneracy, And Scalability Of A 600-Site Cavity Array Microscope
authors: Anna Soper, Danial Shadmany, Adam L. Shaw, Lukas Palm, David I. Schuster, And Jonathan Simon
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Soper, Danial Shadmany, Adam L. Shaw, Lukas Palm, David I. Schuster, and Jonathan Simon

A scalable cavity array microscope architecture is presented, featuring over 600 independent optical cavities for parallelized light-matter interactions, providing opportunities for quantum networking and sensing applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041009] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a scalable cavity array microscope with over 600 independent optical cavities for parallelized light-matter interactions.
motivation: Scalable platforms for many independent optical cavities are needed to enable parallel quantum networking, sensing, and light-matter experiments.
method: The authors design and demonstrate a cavity array microscope architecture featuring more than 600 independent optical cavities.
result: The platform achieves stable, degenerate operation across the cavity array and supports parallelized light-matter interactions at scale.
conclusion: This architecture offers a practical route toward large-scale cavity-based quantum networking and sensing applications.

title: Topological Mixed States: Phases Of Matter From Axiomatic Approaches
authors: Tai-Hsuan Yang, Bowen Shi, And Jong Yeon Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Tai-Hsuan Yang, Bowen Shi, and Jong Yeon Lee

A quantum information framework classifies mixed-state topological phases for open quantum systems, introducing phase invariants based on an information convex set, memory capacity, and secret sharing.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041002] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an axiomatic quantum-information framework to classify mixed-state topological phases in open quantum systems using information convex sets, memory capacity, and secret sharing.
motivation: Topological phases are well understood for pure states, but classifying topological order in mixed states and open quantum systems requires new invariants that capture quantum information properties.
method: The authors introduce phase invariants based on an information convex set, memory capacity, and secret sharing, and use these axiomatic quantum-information quantities to define and distinguish mixed-state topological phases.
result: The framework yields invariants that classify mixed-state topological phases and connects mixed-state topological order to operational notions such as quantum memory and secret sharing.
conclusion: This work provides a quantum-information foundation for topological phases of open quantum systems and suggests new information-theoretic characterizations of mixed-state topological order.

title: Surface Adsorbates Suppress Low-Frequency Noise For Shallow Nitrogen-Vacancy Centers
authors: Zhiyang Yuan, David A. Fehr, Kalliope Zervas, Sorawis Sangtawesin, Lila V. H. Rodgers, Patryk Gumann, Michael E. Flatté, And Nathalie P. de Leon
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyang Yuan, David A. Fehr, Kalliope Zervas, Sorawis Sangtawesin, Lila V. H. Rodgers, Patryk Gumann, Michael E. Flatté, and Nathalie P. de Leon

Surface adsorbates, long blamed for decoherence in diamond quantum sensors, can actually suppress low-frequency noise and extend spin coherence.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043026] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: Surface adsorbates on diamond can suppress low-frequency noise and extend spin coherence for shallow nitrogen-vacancy centers, contrary to their usual role as a decoherence source.
motivation: Shallow NV centers are promising for nanoscale quantum sensing and networking, but low-frequency surface noise limits their coherence; the role of surface adsorbates was poorly understood.
method: The authors experimentally characterize shallow NV centers under controlled surface adsorbate conditions, measuring spin coherence and low-frequency noise to identify how adsorbates affect decoherence.
result: They find that surface adsorbates can reduce low-frequency noise and improve coherence times for shallow NV centers, reversing the conventional expectation that adsorbates degrade performance.
conclusion: Surface chemistry is a key control knob for shallow NV center coherence, with implications for improving NV-based quantum platforms through adsorbate engineering.

title: Quantum Gibbs Sampling Through The Detectability Lemma
authors: Di Fang, Jianfeng Lu, Yu Tong, And Chu Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Di Fang, Jianfeng Lu, Yu Tong, and Chu Zhao

A new approach for quantum algorithm design and analysis that bypasses Lindbladian simulation overhead yields improved scaling with system size and a quadratic improvement in spectral-gap dependence for quantum Gibbs sampling algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043025] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a detectability-lemma-based approach to quantum Gibbs sampling that avoids Lindbladian simulation overhead and improves spectral-gap scaling.
motivation: Quantum Gibbs sampling via Lindbladian simulation can be costly, especially due to simulation overhead and slow convergence controlled by the spectral gap.
method: The authors design and analyze a quantum algorithm for preparing Gibbs states using the detectability lemma, bypassing explicit Lindbladian simulation.
result: The approach yields improved scaling with system size and a quadratic improvement in the spectral-gap dependence for quantum Gibbs sampling.
conclusion: This provides a more efficient algorithmic route to quantum Gibbs sampling, with relevance to thermal-state preparation and open-system-inspired quantum algorithms.

title: Algorithmic Construction Of Gapped Boundaries For Topological Stabilizer Codes: A Route To Low-Overhead Planar qLDPC Codes
authors: Zijian Liang (梁子健), Bowen Yang (杨博闻), Joseph T. Iosue, And Yu-An Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zijian Liang (梁子健), Bowen Yang (杨博闻), Joseph T. Iosue, and Yu-An Chen (陳昱安)

An algorithmic framework for constructing gapped boundaries in two-dimensional topological Pauli stabilizer codes enables low-overhead planar qLDPC architectures and fault-tolerant logical operations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043016] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an algorithmic framework for constructing gapped boundaries in two-dimensional topological Pauli stabilizer codes, enabling low-overhead planar qLDPC architectures with fault-tolerant logical operations.
motivation: Planar architectures for quantum codes require well-characterized gapped boundaries to host logical operations and connect code patches, but constructing such boundaries systematically for general topological stabilizer codes is difficult.
method: The authors develop an algorithmic procedure that, given a two-dimensional topological Pauli stabilizer code, constructs its gapped boundaries and uses them to build planar qLDPC layouts supporting logical operations.
result: The framework yields planar qLDPC code architectures with reduced overhead and provides fault-tolerant logical operations derived from the constructed boundaries.
conclusion: Algorithmic boundary construction offers a general route to practical, low-overhead planar qLDPC codes, bridging abstract topological stabilizer codes and physical architectures.

title: Refinements Of The Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis Under Local Rotational Invariance Via Free Probability
authors: Elisa Vallini, Laura Foini, And Silvia Pappalardi
abstract:
Author(s): Elisa Vallini, Laura Foini, and Silvia Pappalardi

Using the mathematical language of free probability theory, researchers reveal how local rotational invariance structures matrix-element correlations, including their first subleading corrections.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043007] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper refines the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis by using free probability to characterize matrix-element correlations and their subleading corrections under local rotational invariance.
motivation: ETH is central to understanding thermalization in isolated quantum many-body systems, but its detailed correlation structure and symmetry-constrained corrections remain incompletely understood.
method: The authors apply free probability theory to analyze how local rotational invariance organizes matrix-element correlations, including first subleading corrections beyond standard ETH assumptions.
result: They obtain a structured characterization of ETH matrix elements and their fluctuations under local rotational invariance, revealing corrections to conventional random-matrix-like behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a mathematically sharper formulation of ETH in rotationally invariant settings, with implications for quantum thermalization and chaotic many-body dynamics.

title: Information-Theoretic Principle Of Emergent 1-Form Symmetries
authors: Yu-Jie Liu, Wen-Tao Xu, Frank Pollmann, And Michael Knap
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Jie Liu, Wen-Tao Xu, Frank Pollmann, and Michael Knap

Viewing emergent 1-form symmetries through the lens of quantum error correction(QEC) makes them detectable with QEC decoders, providing efficient protocols for revealing emergent symmetry structure and probing phase transitions in quantum many-body systems.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043006] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper recasts emergent 1-form symmetries in quantum many-body systems as quantum error-correcting codes, so that standard QEC decoders can detect the symmetry structure and locate phase transitions.
motivation: Emergent higher-form symmetries characterize topological order and deconfined phases, but diagnosing them is typically indirect and computationally costly; the authors seek an operational, decoder-based probe.
method: They establish an information-theoretic mapping between emergent 1-form symmetries and quantum error-correcting codes, then apply QEC decoders to extract the symmetry structure and use decoder success/failure as an order parameter for phase transitions.
result: QEC decoding provides an efficient protocol that reveals emergent 1-form symmetry structure and signals transitions in quantum many-body systems, including topologically ordered regimes.
conclusion: The QEC lens makes higher-form symmetries operationally accessible and yields practical numerical probes of topological phases, bridging quantum error correction and many-body physics.

title: Free Cumulants In Full Eigenstate Thermalization From Boundary Scrambling
authors: Felix Fritzsch, Gabriel O. Alves, Michael A. Rampp, And Pieter W. Claeys
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Fritzsch, Gabriel O. Alves, Michael A. Rampp, and Pieter W. Claeys

The introduction of boundary scrambling as a solvable many-body quantum model yields an analytically tractable study of higher-order out-of-time-order correlation function dynamics and new insights into free probability and the emergence of random-matrix behavior.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043003] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces boundary scrambling as a solvable many-body quantum model to analytically study higher-order out-of-time-order correlators and the emergence of random-matrix behavior via free cumulants.
motivation: Understanding full eigenstate thermalization and higher-order OTOC dynamics in many-body quantum systems is central to quantum chaos and thermalization, but analytically tractable models remain limited.
method: The authors define and analyze a boundary-scrambling model using free probability and free cumulants to compute higher-order OTOC dynamics and connect them to random-matrix universality.
result: They obtain analytically tractable expressions for higher-order OTOCs and show how free cumulants capture the emergence of random-matrix behavior in the eigenstate thermalization framework.
conclusion: Boundary scrambling provides a useful solvable setting for studying full ETH and higher-order scrambling, linking free probability to many-body quantum chaos.

title: In Situ Benchmarking Of Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits: Clifford Circuits
authors: Xiao Xiao, Dominik Hangleiter, Dolev Bluvstein, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Michael J. Gullans
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao Xiao, Dominik Hangleiter, Dolev Bluvstein, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Michael J. Gullans

Using only existing error syndrome data and no additional calibration circuits, it is possible to efficiently benchmark quantum hardware and verify encoded computations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033055] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an in situ method to benchmark fault-tolerant quantum circuits and verify encoded computations using existing error syndrome data, without extra calibration circuits.
motivation: Benchmarking fault-tolerant quantum hardware and encoded computations typically requires dedicated calibration or validation circuits, which can be costly and disruptive.
method: The authors use error syndrome data generated during Clifford-circuit execution to efficiently characterize hardware performance and verify encoded computations in situ.
result: The approach enables efficient benchmarking and verification of fault-tolerant encoded computations using only existing syndrome data.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route for in situ validation of fault-tolerant quantum circuits, supporting hardware benchmarking and encoded-computation verification.

title: Rapid Cavity-Based Midcircuit Measurement And Feedforward In A Neutral Atom Array
authors: Tsai-Chen Lee, Jacquelyn Ho, Yue-Hui Lu, Tai Xiang, Nathaniel B. Vilas, Zhenjie Yan, And Dan M. Stamper-Kurn
abstract:
Author(s): Tsai-Chen Lee, Jacquelyn Ho, Yue-Hui Lu, Tai Xiang, Nathaniel B. Vilas, Zhenjie Yan, and Dan M. Stamper-Kurn

Measuring part of a quantum system in the midst of its evolution and acting on the result in real time is essential for numerous quantum information protocols. Neutral-atom arrays are a leading platform for quantum information processing, but their midcircuit measurement-and-feedforward cycle times …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 203601] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates rapid cavity-based midcircuit measurement and real-time feedforward in a neutral-atom array, improving a key operational capability for neutral-atom quantum information processing.
motivation: Midcircuit measurement with feedforward is essential for many quantum information protocols, but neutral-atom arrays have faced relatively slow measurement-and-feedforward cycle times.
method: The authors use a cavity-based measurement scheme to perform midcircuit readout within an evolving neutral-atom array and apply real-time feedforward conditioned on the measurement outcome.
result: They achieve rapid measurement-and-feedforward operation in a neutral-atom platform, reducing the cycle time and demonstrating a practical building block for conditional quantum protocols.
conclusion: This work advances neutral-atom arrays as a platform for quantum information processing by making midcircuit measurement and feedforward faster and more viable for protocol integration.

title: Excitation Flow, Positivity, And Fisher Information For Open Subsystems Of An $N$-qubit Network
authors: Tommy Chin And Sarah Shandera
abstract:
Author(s): Tommy Chin and Sarah Shandera

An observer of an autonomous quantum system has no privileged initial time, reference state, or subsystem boundary, so the natural framework for the open dynamics is an ensemble of propagators over many subsystems and time windows. We derive such an ensemble analytically for a closed [MATH]-qubit netwo…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052427] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives an analytic ensemble of propagators for open subsystem dynamics in a closed N-qubit network, analyzing excitation flow, positivity, and Fisher information without privileged time, reference state, or subsystem boundary.
motivation: An observer of an autonomous quantum system lacks a preferred initial time, reference state, and subsystem boundary, motivating a framework based on ensembles of propagators over many subsystems and time windows.
method: The authors analytically derive such a propagator ensemble for a closed N-qubit network and use it to study open-subsystem excitation flow, positivity, and Fisher information.
result: They obtain an explicit ensemble description and characterize how excitation flow, positivity, and Fisher information behave across open subsystems and time windows in the network.
conclusion: The work provides an observer-agnostic framework for open quantum subsystem dynamics in N-qubit networks, relevant to information-theoretic analyses of positivity and parameter estimation.

title: Modeling Logical Gates And Readout Of Superconducting Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Qubits
authors: Mackenzie H. Shaw, Andrew C. Doherty, And Arne L. Grimsmo
abstract:
