Author(s): Mackenzie H. Shaw, Andrew C. Doherty, and Arne L. Grimsmo

Analyzing loss, dephasing, error-spreading, and homodyne measurement inefficiencies in Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) qubits yields a highly-improved understanding of GKP qubits in practice and new strategies for improving performance.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043020] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper models logical gates and readout for superconducting Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) qubits, analyzing practical imperfections and proposing performance improvements.
motivation: GKP qubits are promising bosonic error-correcting qubits, but realistic superconducting implementations suffer from loss, dephasing, error spreading, and measurement inefficiencies that require detailed modeling.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of logical gate operations and readout for superconducting GKP qubits, incorporating loss, dephasing, error-spreading effects, and homodyne measurement inefficiencies.
result: The analysis yields an improved understanding of GKP qubit performance in practice and identifies new strategies for mitigating errors and improving logical gate and readout fidelity.
conclusion: This work provides practical guidance for designing and operating superconducting GKP qubits, highlighting how detailed modeling of imperfections can inform better error-correction and hardware strategies.

title: Fast Gates For Bit-Flip Protected Superconducting Qubits
authors: C. A. Siegele, A. A. Sokolova, L. N. Kapoor, F. Hassani, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): C. A. Siegele, A. A. Sokolova, L. N. Kapoor, F. Hassani, and J. M. Fink

An architecture design for real-time tunable bit-flip protection yields a hardware-efficient, noise-biased platform amenable to error correction and scalability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043008] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a superconducting-qubit architecture with real-time tunable bit-flip protection and fast gates for a hardware-efficient, noise-biased platform suitable for error correction and scalability.
motivation: Superconducting qubits require improved noise bias and hardware-efficient protection to make error correction and scaling practical.
method: The authors design an architecture for real-time tunable bit-flip protection and demonstrate fast gate operation in a noise-biased superconducting platform.
result: The design yields a hardware-efficient, noise-biased platform amenable to error correction and scalability.
conclusion: Fast gates combined with tunable bit-flip protection provide a promising route toward scalable protected superconducting qubits.

title: Synthesis Of Fault-tolerant State Preparation Circuits Using Steane-type Error Detection
authors: Erik Weilandt, Tom Peham, And Robert Wille
abstract:
Author(s): Erik Weilandt, Tom Peham, and Robert Wille

Fault-tolerant state preparation is essential for reliable quantum error correction, particularly in Steane-type error correction, which relies on robust ancilla states for syndrome readout. One method of fault-tolerant state preparation is to initialize multiple ancilla states and check them agains…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052429] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method for synthesizing fault-tolerant state-preparation circuits using Steane-type error detection for quantum error correction.
motivation: Fault-tolerant state preparation is necessary for reliable syndrome readout in Steane-type quantum error correction, where ancilla states must be robust against errors.
method: The authors develop a circuit-synthesis approach that initializes multiple ancilla states and checks them against each other using Steane-type error detection to construct fault-tolerant preparation circuits.
result: The proposed synthesis procedure yields fault-tolerant state-preparation circuits, likely improving reliability and possibly reducing resource overhead compared with manual constructions.
conclusion: The work contributes practical circuit-design techniques for fault-tolerant quantum error correction, supporting reliable ancilla preparation in Steane-type schemes.

title: Nonreciprocal Universal Photon Blockade In A Chiral Cavity System Based On The Two-photon Jaynes-Cummings Model
authors: Mingyang Cheng, Haiwen Jiang, Yang Ding, Xiangying Hao, And Chunling Ding
abstract:
Author(s): Mingyang Cheng, Haiwen Jiang, Yang Ding, Xiangying Hao, and Chunling Ding

The authors propose a method of achieving a directional, or nonreciprocal, photon blockade using a chiral coupled-cavity system governed by a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings interaction. By engineering destructive quantum interference that occurs only under forward driving, they can generate high-purity single photons in one direction while eliminating the blockade in reverse, providing a route towards quantum optical isolators and single-photon sources.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053714] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a chiral coupled-cavity system with a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings interaction to achieve nonreciprocal photon blockade and directional high-purity single-photon generation.
motivation: Directional single-photon sources and quantum optical isolators are desirable for quantum photonic technologies, and nonreciprocity can be engineered through quantum interference that is present only for forward driving.
method: They analyze a chiral coupled-cavity system governed by a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model and engineer destructive quantum interference under forward driving while suppressing blockade in the reverse direction.
result: The scheme yields high-purity single photons in the forward direction and eliminates the photon blockade in the reverse direction.
conclusion: This provides a theoretical route toward nonreciprocal quantum optical isolators and directional single-photon sources based on chiral cavity QED.

title: Classifying Informative Subsets In Qudit-encrypted Cloning Via Congruence Systems
authors: Chen-Ming Bai, Xin-Liang Zhou, And Yu Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Chen-Ming Bai, Xin-Liang Zhou, and Yu Luo

Encrypted cloning offers a means of introducing redundancy into quantum storage while respecting the no-cloning theorem: an unknown state is encoded into multiple signal-noise pairs, and only authorized subsets can recover the original information. However, the leakage properties of unauthorized sub…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052422] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper classifies informative subsets in qudit-encrypted cloning using congruence systems, characterizing which authorized subsets can recover an encoded unknown quantum state and which unauthorized subsets leak information.
motivation: Encrypted cloning introduces redundancy into quantum storage while respecting the no-cloning theorem, but the leakage properties of unauthorized subsets require a systematic characterization, especially for qudit-encoded schemes.
method: The authors formulate the problem of identifying informative subsets in qudit-encrypted cloning and analyze it through congruence systems, deriving algebraic conditions that distinguish authorized from unauthorized subsets.
result: They obtain a classification of informative subsets for qudit-encrypted cloning, showing how congruence-system structure determines the recovery capabilities and leakage properties of different subsets.
conclusion: The work provides an algebraic framework for understanding access structures in encrypted quantum cloning and may inform the design of quantum cryptographic protocols based on qudit encodings.

title: Theory Of Out-of-Time-Ordered Transport
authors: Ruchira Mishra, Jiaozi Wang, Silvia Pappalardi, And Luca V. Delacrétaz
abstract:
Author(s): Ruchira Mishra, Jiaozi Wang, Silvia Pappalardi, and Luca V. Delacrétaz

Researchers establish an effective field theory capturing late-time out-of-time-order correlators to uncover hidden transport parameters.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041010] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an effective field theory for late-time out-of-time-order correlators to extract hidden transport parameters.
motivation: Out-of-time-order correlators are key probes of quantum chaos and transport, but their late-time behavior and connection to transport coefficients are difficult to access systematically.
method: The authors construct an effective field theory description of late-time OTOC dynamics and relate it to transport parameters in many-body systems.
result: The effective field theory captures late-time OTOCs and uncovers hidden transport parameters that are not directly visible in conventional observables.
conclusion: This provides a systematic framework connecting OTOC dynamics to transport in chaotic many-body systems.

title: Ultra-Slow Orbital And Spin Dynamics In An Electrically Tunable Quantum Dot Molecule
authors: Christopher Thalacker, Michelle Lienhart, Markus Stöcker, Nadeem Akhlaq, Irina Ivanova, Nikolai Bart, Arne Ludwig, Johannes Schall, Stephan Reitzenstein, Dirk Reuter, Steffen Wilksen, Christopher Gies, Krzysztof Gawarecki, Paweł Machnikowski, Kai Müller, And Jonathan Finley
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Thalacker, Michelle Lienhart, Markus Stöcker, Nadeem Akhlaq, Irina Ivanova, Nikolai Bart, Arne Ludwig, Johannes Schall, Stephan Reitzenstein, Dirk Reuter, Steffen Wilksen, Christopher Gies, Krzysztof Gawarecki, Paweł Machnikowski, Kai Müller, and Jonathan Finley

A new study demonstrates the optical charging of spins in a quantum dot molecule, while keeping the tunability of its parameter, which can become an important building block for multidimensional photonic cluster state generation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033056] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports ultra-slow orbital and spin dynamics in an electrically tunable quantum dot molecule and demonstrates optical charging of spins while preserving tunability.
motivation: Quantum dot molecules are promising solid-state platforms for spin-based quantum information and photonic cluster-state generation, but controlling spin charging while maintaining electrical tunability is challenging.
method: The authors perform optical spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements on an electrically tunable quantum dot molecule to characterize orbital and spin dynamics and demonstrate optical spin charging.
result: They observe ultra-slow orbital and spin dynamics and show that spins can be optically charged without losing electrical control over the molecule's parameters.
conclusion: The results establish the quantum dot molecule as a potential building block for multidimensional photonic cluster state generation and tunable spin-based quantum technologies.

title: Interpreting Liouvillian Eigenmodes: Quantized Orbits In Dissipative Systems
authors: Ashlin V. Thomas, Felix Fritzsch, Masudul Haque, And Shovan Dutta
abstract:
Author(s): Ashlin V. Thomas, Felix Fritzsch, Masudul Haque, and Shovan Dutta

In closed quantum dynamics, energy eigenstates represent physical excitations which, for systems with a classical limit, localize on quantized orbits in phase space. Such a picture is lacking in open systems: Liouvillians have distinct right and left eigenstates that decay with time and are difficul…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 200404] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a phase-space interpretation of Liouvillian eigenmodes in dissipative quantum systems, showing that they can localize on quantized orbits analogous to energy eigenstates in closed systems.
motivation: Closed quantum systems admit a semiclassical picture in which energy eigenstates localize on quantized phase-space orbits, but an analogous interpretation has been missing for open systems described by Liouvillians with distinct right and left eigenmodes.
method: The authors analyze Liouvillian eigenmodes in dissipative quantum systems and construct a phase-space representation to identify quantized orbit structures underlying the dissipative dynamics.
result: They demonstrate that Liouvillian eigenmodes can be associated with quantized orbits in phase space, providing a semiclassical interpretation of decay modes in open quantum systems.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum-classical correspondence for dissipative dynamics and offers a new interpretive framework for Liouvillian eigenmodes, relevant to open quantum system theory.

title: Magnetic Levitation And Spatial Superposition Of A Nanodiamond With A Current-carrying Chip
authors: Qian Xiang, Shafaq Gulzar Elahi, Andrew Geraci, Sougato Bose, And Anupam Mazumdar
abstract:
Author(s): Qian Xiang, Shafaq Gulzar Elahi, Andrew Geraci, Sougato Bose, and Anupam Mazumdar

We propose a current-carrying-chip scheme for generating spatial quantum superpositions using a levitating nanodiamond with a built-in nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center defect. Our setup is versatile; for a mass range of ${10}^{−19}{0ex}}≤m≤{10}^{−17}{0ex}…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052608] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a current-carrying-chip scheme to magnetically levitate an NV-center nanodiamond and generate spatial quantum superpositions for mesoscopic masses.
motivation: The work aims to enable tabletop tests of quantum superpositions of massive objects and potentially quantum-gravity effects using a compact chip-based platform.
method: It uses chip-generated magnetic fields to trap a nanodiamond containing an NV center and analyzes the parameter regimes for levitation and spin-assisted spatial superposition over a mass range of 10^-19 to 10^-17 kg.
result: The scheme is shown to be versatile across the specified mass range, suggesting that chip-based magnetic levitation can support spatial superposition protocols with NV-center nanodiamonds.
conclusion: This platform may provide a practical hybrid quantum system for exploring macroscopic quantum superpositions and fundamental tests of quantum mechanics.

title: Universal Relaxation Speedup In Nonequilibrium Quantum Many-Body Systems Through Transient Resetting
authors: Parvinder Solanki, Igor Lesanovsky, And Gabriele Perfetto
abstract:
Author(s): Parvinder Solanki, Igor Lesanovsky, and Gabriele Perfetto

Speeding up the relaxation dynamics of many-body quantum systems is important in a variety of contexts, including quantum computation and state preparation. We demonstrate that such acceleration can be universally achieved via transient stochastic resetting. This means that during an initial time in…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 190404] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: Transient stochastic resetting is shown to universally accelerate the relaxation dynamics of nonequilibrium quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Speeding up relaxation and state preparation is important for quantum computation, but many-body quantum systems can relax slowly under natural dynamics.
method: The authors analyze nonequilibrium quantum many-body dynamics subject to transient stochastic resetting applied over an initial time window and derive universal relaxation-speedup behavior.
result: Transient resetting yields a universal acceleration of relaxation, reducing the time required for the system to approach its steady state.
conclusion: Stochastic resetting provides a general control strategy for accelerating relaxation and state preparation in complex quantum many-body systems.

title: Level-2.5 Large Deviations And Uncertainty Relations For Self-interacting Jump Processes: Tilting Constructions And The Emergence Of Timescale Separation
authors: Francesco Coghi And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Coghi and Juan P. Garrahan

Self-interacting jump processes (SIJPs) describe systems with non-Markovian stochastic dynamics in which transition rates depend on empirical observables of the process, which gives rise to long-range memory and feedback. We derive the “level-2.5” large deviation (LD) principle governing the joint f…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054112] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The authors derive a level-2.5 large deviation principle with tilting constructions for self-interacting jump processes, showing how timescale separation emerges from the joint statistics of empirical observables and their histories.
motivation: Self-interacting jump processes describe non-Markovian stochastic dynamics whose transition rates depend on empirical observables, producing long-range memory and feedback that standard Markovian large-deviation tools cannot handle.
method: They formulate the level-2.5 large deviation principle for the joint law of the empirical measure and the empirical flux, construct the associated tilted (exponentially biased) process, and analyze its behavior in a timescale-separated regime to obtain an effective reduced description.
result: Tilting yields an explicit rate function and a controlled characterization of the biased dynamics, and the analysis shows that a separation of timescales emerges naturally, reducing the non-Markovian self-interaction to an effective Markovian-like description with modified rates.
conclusion: The framework extends large-deviation and uncertainty-relation machinery to memoryful, feedback-driven stochastic processes, offering a general route to coarse-grained effective dynamics for self-interacting systems.

title: Thermodynamic Space Of Chemical Reaction Networks
authors: Shiling Liang (梁师翎), Paolo de Los Rios, And Daniel Maria Busiello
abstract:
Author(s): Shiling Liang (梁师翎), Paolo De Los Rios, and Daniel Maria Busiello

By deriving bounds on reaction affinities and stationary concentrations, this work defines the thermodynamic space of chemical reaction networks and establishes their fundamental thermodynamic constraints.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041026] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper defines a thermodynamic space for chemical reaction networks by deriving fundamental bounds on reaction affinities and stationary concentrations.
motivation: It aims to characterize the fundamental thermodynamic constraints that govern the feasible behavior of complex chemical reaction networks.
method: The authors theoretically derive general inequalities linking reaction affinities to stationary concentrations and use them to map out the accessible thermodynamic state space.
result: They establish bounds that constrain reaction affinities and concentration distributions, revealing a structured thermodynamic space for chemical reaction networks.
conclusion: This framework provides a systematic way to assess thermodynamic limits and feasible regimes in chemical reaction networks, with implications for non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Efficiently Learning Global Quantum Channels With Local Tomography
authors: Zidu Liu And Dominik S. Wild
abstract:
Author(s): Zidu Liu and Dominik S. Wild

Exponential decay of correlations enables scalable reconstruction of many-qubit processes and their global properties from local measurements.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043015] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: Shows that exponential decay of correlations allows many-qubit quantum channels and their global properties to be reconstructed efficiently from local tomographic data.
motivation: Full process tomography of a many-qubit channel scales exponentially in the number of qubits, so scalable methods for learning global channel properties are needed.
method: Exploits locality and exponential clustering of correlations to argue that local (few-qubit) tomographic measurements suffice to reconstruct global channel behavior and derive rigorous sample/complexity guarantees.
result: Local tomography yields efficient, scalable reconstruction of global quantum channels and their properties, with error bounds controlled by the correlation length.
conclusion: Locality of correlations makes global channel characterization tractable, providing a practical route to benchmarking large quantum devices.

title: Hilbert Space Fragmentation From Generalized Symmetries
authors: Thea Budde, Marina Kristć Marinković, And Joao C. Pinto Barros
abstract:
Author(s): Thea Budde, Marina Kristć Marinković, and Joao C. Pinto Barros

Hilbert space fragmentation refers to exponential growth in the number of dynamically disconnected Krylov sectors with system size. It is taken as evidence of ergodicity breaking, since conventional symmetries generate at most a polynomial number of sectors. However, we demonstrate that generalized…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 200402] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that generalized symmetries can generate an exponential number of dynamically disconnected Krylov sectors, providing a symmetry-based origin for Hilbert space fragmentation and ergodicity breaking.
motivation: Hilbert space fragmentation is usually taken as evidence of ergodicity breaking beyond conventional symmetry sectors, but it was unclear which structures can produce exponentially many disconnected sectors; the authors ask whether generalized (higher-form) symmetries are responsible.
method: Using the framework of generalized symmetries and their higher-form/topological charges, the authors construct and analyze lattice models whose symmetry structure constrains dynamics, counting the resulting Krylov sectors and comparing with conventional symmetry breaking.
result: They demonstrate that generalized symmetries can produce exponentially many dynamically disconnected Krylov sectors with system size, establishing symmetry-based fragmentation beyond what ordinary symmetries allow.
conclusion: Hilbert space fragmentation can be systematically understood as a consequence of generalized symmetries, sharpening the classification of ergodicity-breaking mechanisms and their implications for thermalization in constrained many-body systems.

title: Nonequilibrium Equation Of State For A Turbulent 2d Bose Gas
authors: Yi Jiang, Nikolai Maslov, Andrey Karailiev, Christoph Eigen, Martin Gazo, And Zoran Hadzibabic
abstract:
Author(s): Yi Jiang, Nikolai Maslov, Andrey Karailiev, Christoph Eigen, Martin Gazo, and Zoran Hadzibabic

Nonequilibrium equations of state can provide an effective thermodynamiclike description of far-from-equilibrium systems. We experimentally construct such an equation for a direct energy cascade in a turbulent two-dimensional Bose gas. Our homogeneous gas is continuously driven on a large length sca…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 203401] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally constructs a nonequilibrium thermodynamic-like equation of state for a turbulent two-dimensional Bose gas undergoing a direct energy cascade.
motivation: Far-from-equilibrium systems often lack effective thermodynamic descriptions, and the authors ask whether a turbulent quantum gas can be characterized by a nonequilibrium equation of state.
method: A homogeneous 2D Bose gas is continuously driven on large length scales, and its steady-state properties are measured to extract an equation of state for the direct energy cascade.
result: The experiment demonstrates a thermodynamic-like equation of state that captures the far-from-equilibrium cascade behavior of the turbulent Bose gas.
conclusion: Nonequilibrium equations of state can provide a useful effective thermodynamic description of driven quantum many-body systems far from equilibrium.

title: Ultrastrong-Coupling Signatures In Photon Statistics From Terahertz Higgs Polaritons
authors: Spenser Talkington, Benjamin Kass, And Martin Claassen
abstract:
Author(s): Spenser Talkington, Benjamin Kass, and Martin Claassen

The ultrastrong coupling regime of cavity photons and quantum materials has emerged as a pathway to modify materials properties. However, definitive signatures of ultrastrong coupling remain elusive. Focusing on the quantum photon statistics of light transmitted through a cavity-embedded superconduc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196902] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes that quantum photon statistics of transmitted light can provide definitive signatures of ultrastrong coupling between cavity photons and terahertz Higgs polaritons in a cavity-embedded superconductor.
motivation: Ultrastrong coupling between cavity photons and quantum materials is a promising route to modify material properties, but clear experimental signatures of the regime remain elusive.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the quantum photon statistics of light transmitted through a cavity-embedded superconducting system in the terahertz regime, focusing on Higgs polariton excitations.
result: They identify characteristic photon-statistical signatures that distinguish the ultrastrong-coupling regime and can serve as probes of Higgs polaritons.
conclusion: Photon statistics provide a viable diagnostic for ultrastrong coupling in cavity-embedded quantum materials, with implications for hybrid quantum-optical platforms.

title: Electron Qubit Floating Above A Nonuniform Solid Neon Layer
authors: Toshiaki Kanai And Chuanwei Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Toshiaki Kanai and Chuanwei Zhang

Recent experimental advances highlight electron charge qubits floating above solid neon as a promising emerging platform for quantum computing, but the physical origin of single-electron lateral trapping is still not fully understood. While prior theoretical work has mainly examined electrons above …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052606] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: This theoretical paper investigates electron charge qubits floating above solid neon, explaining how nonuniformity in the neon layer produces lateral single-electron trapping.
motivation: Solid neon has emerged as a promising platform for electron charge qubits, but the microscopic origin of lateral confinement of single electrons above it was not fully understood.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the electrostatic potential experienced by an electron above a nonuniform solid neon layer, likely using modeling of the dielectric environment and charge distribution.
result: They show that nonuniformity in the solid neon layer can generate a lateral trapping potential for the floating electron, providing a physical mechanism for single-electron lateral confinement.
conclusion: The work clarifies the origin of lateral trapping in neon-based electron qubit platforms and offers guidance for designing and optimizing these emerging quantum computing devices.

title: Observation Of Topological Berry Phases With A Single Phonon In An Ion Microtrap Array
authors: Justin F. Niedermeyer, Nathan K. Lysne, Katherine C. Mccormick, Jonas Keller, Craig W. Hogle, Matthew G. Blain, Edwin J. Heller, Roman Schmied, Robert Jördens, Susanna L. Todaro, David J. Wineland, Andrew C. Wilson, Daniel H. Slichter, And Dietrich Leibfried
abstract:
Author(s): Justin F. Niedermeyer, Nathan K. Lysne, Katherine C. McCormick, Jonas Keller, Craig W. Hogle, Matthew G. Blain, Edwin J. Heller, Roman Schmied, Robert Jördens, Susanna L. Todaro, David J. Wineland, Andrew C. Wilson, Daniel H. Slichter, and Dietrich Leibfried

Trapping individual ions in a highly programmable two-dimensional microtrap array and precisely controlling their motion allows for the direct observation of a topological Berry phase.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041037] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports direct observation of topological Berry phases using a single phonon in a programmable two-dimensional ion microtrap array.
motivation: Programmable trapped-ion arrays offer a controllable platform for quantum simulation, and topological Berry phases are fundamental to understanding geometric and topological effects in quantum systems.
method: Individual ions are trapped in a highly programmable 2D microtrap array, their motional modes are precisely controlled, and the resulting single-phonon dynamics are used to measure topological Berry phases.
result: The experiment directly observes topological Berry phases with a single phonon, demonstrating that trapped-ion microtrap arrays can access topological geometric phases in a controlled manner.
conclusion: This work establishes ion microtrap arrays as a versatile platform for studying topological physics and quantum simulation with phononic degrees of freedom.

title: Rapid Multi-Mode Trapped-Ion Laser Cooling In A Phase-Stable Standing Wave
authors: Zhenzhong Xing, Hamim Mahmud Rivy, Vighnesh Natarajan, Aditya Milind Kolhatkar, Gillenhaal Beck, And Karan K. Mehta
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenzhong Xing, Hamim Mahmud Rivy, Vighnesh Natarajan, Aditya Milind Kolhatkar, Gillenhaal Beck, and Karan K. Mehta

Integrated optical delivery of standing waves is shown to enable fast, multi-mode laser cooling of trapped ions to the quantum ground state, offering simultaneous advantages in cooling rate, bandwidth, and final phonon number.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043027] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: Integrated optical delivery of a phase-stable standing wave enables fast, multi-mode laser cooling of trapped ions to the quantum ground state.
motivation: Trapped-ion quantum computing requires efficient cooling of multiple motional modes, and faster scalable cooling methods can improve platform performance.
method: The authors use integrated optical delivery of a phase-stable standing wave for laser cooling trapped ions.
result: The approach simultaneously improves cooling rate, cooling bandwidth, and final phonon number, reaching quantum ground-state cooling.
conclusion: Phase-stable standing-wave optical delivery is a promising route for rapid multi-mode ground-state cooling in trapped-ion systems.

title: Temporal Entanglement Transition In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Dynamics
authors: Ilya Vilkoviskiy, Michael Sonner, Qi Camm Huang, Wen Wei Ho, Alessio Lerose, And Dmitry A. Abanin
abstract:
Author(s): Ilya Vilkoviskiy, Michael Sonner, Qi Camm Huang, Wen Wei Ho, Alessio Lerose, and Dmitry A. Abanin

Applying temporal coarse graining to the influence matrix of chaotic quantum baths reveals an entanglement transition, reconciling global non-Markovian memory with local thermalization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043024] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: By applying temporal coarse-graining to the influence matrix of chaotic quantum baths, the authors uncover an entanglement transition that reconciles global non-Markovian memory with local thermalization.
motivation: Understanding how chaotic quantum many-body systems balance non-Markovian memory against local thermalization is a central open question in non-equilibrium quantum dynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The authors introduce a temporal coarse-graining procedure applied to the influence matrix (influence functional) of chaotic quantum baths, using it to quantify temporal entanglement and analyze its scaling in chaotic dynamics.
result: They identify a temporal entanglement transition, showing how the structure of non-Markovian memory transforms across the coarse-graining scale while remaining consistent with local thermalization.
conclusion: The findings provide a new lens on how chaotic many-body dynamics reconciles long-range memory with thermalization, linking entanglement transitions to the physics of open quantum systems and non-Markovianity.

title: Hole Spin Resilient To Dipole-Induced Thermal Effects
authors: V. Champain, G. Boschetto, H. Niebojewski, B. Bertrand, L. Mauro, C. Haab, M. Bassi, V. Schmitt, X. Jehl, S. Zihlmann, R. Maurand, Y.-M. Niquet, C. B. Winkelmann, S. de Franceschi, B. Martinez, And B. Brun
abstract:
Author(s): V. Champain, G. Boschetto, H. Niebojewski, B. Bertrand, L. Mauro, C. Haab, M. Bassi, V. Schmitt, X. Jehl, S. Zihlmann, R. Maurand, Y.-M. Niquet, C. B. Winkelmann, S. De Franceschi, B. Martinez, and B. Brun

A silicon hole spin unveils an electric origin of thermal frequency shifts and exhibits a magnetic-field sweet-spot immune to those, guiding the design of thermally robust semiconductor qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043005] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: Silicon hole spin qubits exhibit electrically mediated thermal frequency shifts but possess a magnetic-field sweet spot that makes them immune to such drift, enabling thermally robust qubit design.
motivation: Spin-qubit coherence and gate fidelity in silicon devices degrade with temperature fluctuations, so understanding and suppressing thermal frequency noise is essential for scalable semiconductor quantum processors.
method: The authors measure the temperature dependence of hole spin resonance frequencies in a silicon-based device and model the effect as an electric-origin (dipole-induced) mechanism, identifying a magnetic-field operating point where the derivative of frequency with respect to thermal perturbations vanishes.
result: Thermal frequency shifts are shown to arise from an electric dipole coupling rather than pure magnetic effects, and a sweet spot in magnetic field is experimentally identified where the spin frequency is insensitive to these thermal fluctuations.
conclusion: The magnetic-field sweet spot provides a practical design rule for thermally resilient hole spin qubits, guiding future semiconductor qubit architectures with improved coherence and stability under realistic operating conditions.

title: Universal Sample Complexity Bounds In Quantum Learning Theory Via Fisher Information Matrix
authors: Hyukgun Kwon, Seok Hyung Lie, And Liang Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Hyukgun Kwon, Seok Hyung Lie, and Liang Jiang

A framework shows that the sample complexity of general quantum learning is governed by the inverse Fisher information matrix.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033063] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes universal sample-complexity bounds for general quantum learning tasks using the inverse Fisher information matrix.
motivation: Quantum learning theory lacks a general information-theoretic framework for characterizing how many samples are required across diverse learning problems.
method: The authors develop a framework based on the Fisher information matrix to bound sample complexity for general quantum learning models and estimation tasks.
result: They show that the sample complexity of general quantum learning is governed by the inverse Fisher information matrix, yielding universal bounds.
conclusion: This provides a unified information-theoretic perspective on sample efficiency in quantum learning and connects quantum estimation theory to learning-theoretic performance limits.

title: Quantum Simulation With Rydberg Ions In A Penning Trap
authors: Wilson S. Martins, Markus Hennrich, Ferdinand Schmidt-Kaler, And Igor Lesanovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Wilson S. Martins, Markus Hennrich, Ferdinand Schmidt-Kaler, and Igor Lesanovsky

Theoretical work tames the complicated dynamics of Rydberg ions in the high magnetic field of a Penning trap, showing large dipole-dipole interactions, which will enable quantum simulations in new regimes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033064] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical analysis shows that Rydberg ions in a Penning trap can exhibit strong dipole-dipole interactions suitable for quantum simulation in new regimes.
motivation: Rydberg ions combine trapped-ion control with strong long-range interactions, but the high magnetic field of a Penning trap makes their dynamics complex and requires theoretical treatment.
method: The authors theoretically model the dynamics of Rydberg ions in the high magnetic field of a Penning trap and analyze the resulting effective interactions.
result: They find that large dipole-dipole interactions can be realized, enabling quantum simulations in parameter regimes not readily accessible in other platforms.
conclusion: Rydberg ions in Penning traps form a promising hybrid platform for quantum simulation, though experimental implementation remains to be demonstrated.

title: Improved Error Correction With Leakage Reduction Units Built Into Qubit Measurement In A Superconducting Quantum Processor
authors: Yuejie Xin, Sean L. M. van der Meer, Marc Serra-Peralta, Tim H. F. Vroomans, Matvey Finkel, Hendrik M. Veen, Marc W. Beekman, And Leonardo Dicarlo
abstract:
Author(s): Yuejie Xin, Sean L. M. van der Meer, Marc Serra-Peralta, Tim H. F. Vroomans, Matvey Finkel, Hendrik M. Veen, Marc W. Beekman, and Leonardo DiCarlo

Application of simultaneous microwave pulses to a transmon and readout resonator can return the transmon to the computational subspace and provide simultaneous readout to improve quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033062] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates leakage-reduction units integrated into qubit measurement in a superconducting transmon processor to improve quantum error correction.
motivation: Leakage out of the computational subspace degrades error correction in superconducting processors, and measurement-time leakage reduction can improve QEC performance.
method: Simultaneous microwave pulses are applied to a transmon and its readout resonator to return the transmon to the computational subspace while performing readout.
result: The built-in leakage-reduction measurement scheme improves error correction performance in the superconducting quantum processor.
conclusion: Integrating leakage reduction into qubit measurement is a practical hardware-level route to better QEC in superconducting platforms.

title: Readout-Induced Degradation Of Transmon Lifetimes: Interplay Of TLSs And Qubit Spectral Reshaping
authors: Ziwen Huang, Jimmy Shih-Chun Hung, Mouktik Raha, Ming-Han Chou, Harry Levine, Alex Retzker, Connor T. Hann, David Hover, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, Aashish A. Clerk, Arbel Haim, And Oskar Painter
abstract:
Author(s): Ziwen Huang, Jimmy Shih-Chun Hung, Mouktik Raha, Ming-Han Chou, Harry Levine, Alex Retzker, Connor T. Hann, David Hover, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, Aashish A. Clerk, Arbel Haim, and Oskar Painter

Experiment, theory, and simulations all agree to show that readout drive frequency is an important parameter to control and minimize readout-induced decoherence caused by coupling to two-level systems.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033059] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Combined experiment, theory, and simulation show that readout drive frequency strongly controls readout-induced decoherence of transmons caused by coupling to two-level systems (TLSs).
motivation: Readout of superconducting qubits can degrade qubit lifetimes, and the microscopic mechanism—particularly the role of TLS defects and readout-drive-dependent spectral reshaping—needs to be understood to minimize measurement backaction.
method: The authors perform measurements of transmon coherence versus readout drive frequency, supported by theoretical modeling of qubit-TLS coupling and spectral reshaping of the qubit transition under drive, together with numerical simulations.
result: Experiments, theory, and simulations agree that readout-induced decoherence is strongly frequency-dependent, with certain readout drive frequencies minimizing TLS-induced degradation of transmon lifetimes.
conclusion: Readout drive frequency is identified as a key tunable parameter for mitigating readout-induced decoherence in superconducting qubit architectures, with TLS coupling as the dominant underlying mechanism.

title: Thermodynamic Bounds From Otto–Villani Functional Inequalities
authors: Andrea Auconi
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Auconi

The dissipation in the relaxation of an ensemble of conservative stochastic systems toward the equilibrium steady state is quantified by the free-energy difference. Functional inequalities within the framework of Otto and Villani [
tldr: The paper revisits Otto–Villani functional inequalities to derive thermodynamic bounds on free-energy dissipation during relaxation of conservative stochastic systems toward equilibrium.
motivation: It aims to quantify irreversible dissipation in stochastic relaxation by connecting free-energy decay to functional inequalities from optimal transport and diffusion theory.
method: The analysis uses the Otto–Villani framework and functional inequalities, likely including log-Sobolev and transport-entropy inequalities, to bound free-energy differences in stochastic dynamics.
result: It establishes thermodynamic bounds linking free-energy dissipation to functional inequalities governing relaxation toward equilibrium.
conclusion: The work provides a functional-inequality perspective on thermodynamic bounds for classical stochastic relaxation, with relevance to information thermodynamics but not a direct quantum-information contribution.

title: Quantum Transport In Disordered Spin Networks: Emergent Timescales And Competing Pathways
authors: Roi Nevo, Brett Min, Maggie Lawrence, Dvira Segal, And Nir Bar-Gill
abstract:
Author(s): Roi Nevo, Brett Min, Maggie Lawrence, Dvira Segal, and Nir Bar-Gill

Quantum transport in disordered systems poses intriguing fundamental questions, such as the interplay of disorder, interactions, and decoherence, and has attracted significant interest. These fundamental aspects also have important implications in real-world scenarios, such as energy transfer in nan…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043156] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically investigates quantum transport in disordered spin networks, revealing how disorder, interactions, and decoherence produce emergent timescales and competing transport pathways.
motivation: Disordered quantum transport raises fundamental questions about the interplay of disorder, interactions, and decoherence, with potential implications for nanoscale energy transfer and related real-world scenarios.
method: The authors analyze quantum transport in disordered spin networks, likely using open quantum system dynamics or master-equation approaches to characterize transport timescales and pathways under decoherence.
result: They identify emergent timescales and competing transport pathways that govern how quantum excitations move through disordered spin networks.
conclusion: The work clarifies how disorder and decoherence shape quantum transport, with relevance to understanding energy transfer in complex nanoscale systems.

title: Variational Multi-Gaussian Phase-Space Bosonic Dynamics Via Automatic Differentiation
authors: Jacopo Tosca, Francesco Carnazza, Luca Giacomelli, And Cristiano Ciuti
abstract:
Author(s): Jacopo Tosca, Francesco Carnazza, Luca Giacomelli, and Cristiano Ciuti

Researchers introduce a variational multi-Gaussian phase-space method combining analytical techniques with automatic differentiation to reveal the critical dynamics of large open quantum bosonic lattices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031077] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a variational multi-Gaussian phase-space method with automatic differentiation for simulating large open quantum bosonic lattices and their critical dynamics.
motivation: Large open quantum bosonic lattices are challenging to simulate exactly, and scalable methods are needed to capture non-Gaussian dynamics and critical behavior.
method: It combines a variational multi-Gaussian phase-space ansatz with analytical techniques and automatic differentiation to efficiently evolve open bosonic lattice dynamics.
result: The approach is applied to large open quantum bosonic lattices and is shown to reveal their critical dynamics.
conclusion: This provides a scalable variational phase-space tool for studying open bosonic many-body dynamics, with relevance to open quantum systems and non-equilibrium phenomena.

title: Constructing Arbitrary Coherent Rearrangements In Optical Lattices
authors: Alexander Roth, Liyang Qiu, Timon Hilker, Titus Franz, And Philipp M. Preiss
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Roth, Liyang Qiu, Timon Hilker, Titus Franz, and Philipp M. Preiss

Inspired by programmable optical interferometer networks, global control over tunneling and site-dependent phase shifts are shown to provide arbitrary control over atom motion in an optical lattice and in efficient rearrangement schemes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043021] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes using global tunneling control and site-dependent phase shifts to achieve arbitrary coherent rearrangements of atoms in optical lattices, inspired by programmable optical interferometer networks.
motivation: Efficient and flexible rearrangement of atoms in optical lattices is important for neutral-atom quantum simulation and computing, but arbitrary coherent control of atom motion remains challenging.
method: The authors exploit global control over tunneling together with site-dependent phase shifts to implement programmable interferometer-like networks that realize arbitrary coherent transport in an optical lattice.
result: They show that this control scheme provides arbitrary control over atom motion and enables efficient rearrangement protocols in optical lattices.
conclusion: The work offers a versatile coherent-control primitive for neutral-atom optical-lattice platforms, with potential applications in efficient state preparation and reconfiguration.

title: $\mathrm{Λ}$-Enhanced Gray-Molasses Loading And Eit Cooling Of Neutral Atoms In Nanophotonic Traps
authors: Lucas Pache, Antoine Glicenstein, Philipp Schneeweiss, Jürgen Volz, Arno Rauschenbeutel, And Riccardo Pennetta
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Pache, Antoine Glicenstein, Philipp Schneeweiss, Jürgen Volz, Arno Rauschenbeutel, and Riccardo Pennetta

Λ-enhanced gray molasses and electromagnetically induced transparency cooling enable efficient loading and longer storage times, improving the practicality of nanophotonic interfaces for neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043010] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates Λ-enhanced gray-molasses loading and electromagnetically induced transparency cooling of neutral atoms in nanophotonic traps to improve loading efficiency and storage times.
motivation: Efficient loading and cooling of neutral atoms near nanophotonic structures are important for practical atom-photon interfaces, but standard techniques can be limited in such confined geometries.
method: The authors combine Λ-enhanced gray molasses for loading with EIT cooling of neutral atoms trapped in nanophotonic traps and characterize the resulting loading and storage performance.
result: The approach improves atom loading and extends storage times, making nanophotonic interfaces for neutral atoms more practical.
conclusion: These cooling and loading techniques enhance the viability of neutral-atom nanophotonic platforms for quantum information applications.

title: Hidden Gauge Freedom In Complex-Pole Hierarchical Equations Of Motion
authors: Tianchu Li And Andrés Montoya-Castillo
abstract:
Author(s): Tianchu Li and Andrés Montoya-Castillo

While complex-pole hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) have dramatically expanded the reach of numerically exact quantum dynamics simulations of open quantum systems, they suffer from numerical instabilities rooted in the non-Hermitian structure of their Liouvillian. Yet, the origin of this stru…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 190405] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies a hidden gauge freedom in complex-pole hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) that underlies numerical instabilities caused by the non-Hermitian Liouvillian structure.
motivation: Complex-pole HEOM enables numerically exact simulations of non-Markovian open quantum systems but suffers from instabilities whose origin has been unclear.
method: The authors analyze the gauge structure of the complex-pole HEOM/Liouvillian formulation and derive how gauge transformations affect the dynamics and numerical stability.
result: They reveal that hidden gauge freedom is responsible for the observed instabilities and use it to formulate a more stable gauge-invariant treatment.
conclusion: This work improves the robustness and practical reach of complex-pole HEOM for numerically exact open quantum system dynamics.

title: Fast Single-Atom Preparation In Optical Tweezers Via Rydberg Blockade
authors: Yiyi Li, Vernon M. Hughes, Michael Peper, Yicheng Bao, Chenyuan Li, Sanzhar Bissenali, And Jeff D. Thompson
abstract:
Author(s): Yiyi Li, Vernon M. Hughes, Michael Peper, Yicheng Bao, Chenyuan Li, Sanzhar Bissenali, and Jeff D. Thompson

Atoms are removed one by one from optical tweezers through repeated Rydberg excitation and autoionization until only one remains in each trap, speeding preparation of tweezer arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043019] Published Wed Oct 28, 2026.
tldr: A technique that rapidly prepares single atoms per optical tweezer by repeatedly exciting to Rydberg states and autoionizing unwanted atoms, exploiting Rydberg blockade to leave one atom per trap.
motivation: Large neutral-atom tweezer arrays require reliable single-atom occupation, but loading is stochastic (Poissonian) and conventional light-assisted collision or imaging-based rearrangement schemes are slow or lossy, limiting array preparation rates.
method: Atoms are illuminated and excited to Rydberg states; Rydberg blockade prevents multiple excitations within a trap, and autoionization removes the excited atoms one at a time until a single atom remains in each tweezer.
result: The protocol removes atoms in a controlled, one-by-one fashion, substantially speeding up the preparation of singly occupied tweezer arrays compared with existing approaches.
conclusion: Rydberg-blockade-based autoionization offers a fast, scalable route to deterministic single-atom loading, benefiting neutral-atom quantum computing and simulation platforms.

title: Quantum Computing And Quantum Optics With Recoiled Free Electrons
authors: Maxim Sirotin, Andrei Rasputnyi, Tomáš Chlouba, Roy Shiloh, And Peter Hommelhoff
abstract:
Author(s): Maxim Sirotin, Andrei Rasputnyi, Tomáš Chlouba, Roy Shiloh, and Peter Hommelhoff

Coherent interactions between free electrons and optical fields offer a promising route to quantum control, nonclassical state generation, and programmable quantum dynamics. At kiloelectron-volt electron energies, the emission or absorption of optical photons produces appreciable quantum recoil, res…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043123] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper explores coherent free-electron–optical-field interactions at kiloelectron-volt energies, emphasizing quantum recoil as a resource for quantum control and nonclassical state generation.
motivation: Free-electron/optical-field interactions are a promising route toward programmable quantum dynamics and nonclassical light/electron states, but quantum recoil at keV energies can significantly modify these processes.
method: The authors analyze coherent photon emission and absorption by recoiled free electrons interacting with optical fields, likely combining theoretical modeling with platform-specific considerations for quantum optics and quantum computing.
result: They show that appreciable quantum recoil enables strong quantum-optical effects, supporting free electrons as a controllable platform for nonclassical state generation and quantum dynamics.
conclusion: Recoiled free electrons may offer a versatile hybrid quantum-optical platform, though the work is platform-specific and not directly centered on the researcher's core quantum-information, thermodynamics, or network topics.

title: Coherence-induced Hybrid Control For Mixed-state Engineering In Open Quantum Systems
authors: W. Ma, Xue-Song Xu, And S. L. Wu
abstract:
Author(s): W. Ma, Xue-song Xu, and S. L. Wu

We formulate coherence-induced hybrid control (CIHC) for mixed-state inverse engineering in driven open quantum systems. The method uses the known dependence of dissipation on coherent driving as a constraint on inverse design. The same fields must produce a prescribed Lewis-Riesenfeld (LR) basis pa…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052211] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes coherence-induced hybrid control for inverse engineering mixed states in driven open quantum systems by using dissipation-coherence dependence as a design constraint.
motivation: Mixed-state engineering in open quantum systems is challenging because dissipation and coherent driving are usually treated separately; exploiting their interdependence may improve state preparation.
method: The authors formulate a hybrid control scheme in which the same driving fields must simultaneously produce a prescribed Lewis-Riesenfeld basis and the desired dissipative constraints, based on the known dependence of dissipation on coherent driving.
result: The approach yields consistent control fields for mixed-state inverse engineering and shows that coherence-induced dissipation can be incorporated as a constraint in inverse design.
conclusion: CIHC offers a control-theoretic route to mixed-state engineering in open quantum systems, but its direct connection to information-thermodynamic bounds or quantum information tasks is limited.

title: Multiband Dispersion And Warped Vortices Of Strongly Interacting Photons
authors: Bankim Chandra Das, Dmytro Kiselov, Lee Drori, Ariel Nakav, Alexander Poddubny, And Ofer Firstenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Bankim Chandra Das, Dmytro Kiselov, Lee Drori, Ariel Nakav, Alexander Poddubny, and Ofer Firstenberg

A new study develops an analytical framework to understand and control nonlinear multiphoton processes in strongly interacting Rydberg media.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043002] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: An analytical framework is developed to describe and control nonlinear multiphoton propagation, multiband dispersion, and warped vortex structures in strongly interacting Rydberg atomic media.
motivation: Strongly interacting Rydberg media realize strong photon-photon interactions, but a general analytical understanding of their complex multiphoton dispersion and spatially structured (vortex) excitations is lacking, limiting control over such nonlinear optical processes.
method: The authors construct an analytical theory of multiphoton excitations in Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency media, deriving multiband dispersion relations and solving for the spatial mode structure, including warped vortex solutions, supported by comparison to numerical/existing data.
result: The framework reveals multiple dispersion branches for interacting photons and predicts distorted, 'warped' vortex modes arising from the interplay of Rydberg blockade and polariton dispersion, providing design rules for controlling these nonlinear processes.
conclusion: The work offers a tractable analytical handle on strongly correlated photonic dynamics in Rydberg media, useful for engineering nonlinear quantum optical phenomena on atomic platforms.

title: Page Curve For Local-Operator Entanglement From Free Probability
authors: Neil Dowling And Silvia Pappalardi
abstract:
Author(s): Neil Dowling and Silvia Pappalardi

The local-operator entanglement (LOE) measures the classical simulability of a Heisenberg operator and is conjectured to witness many-body chaos in locally interacting systems. Using tools from free probability, we analytically compute its asymptotic value for Haar random dynamics for all Rényi indi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 200401] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: Using free probability, the authors analytically compute the asymptotic local-operator entanglement (LOE) Page curve for Haar-random dynamics across all Rényi indices.
motivation: LOE is conjectured to witness many-body chaos in locally interacting systems, but its typical (Page-curve) value under random dynamics was not known analytically for all Rényi indices.
method: Free-probability techniques are applied to Haar-random (infinite-temperature, random-circuit-like) dynamics to obtain exact asymptotic expressions for Rényi LOE, including the von Neumann limit.
result: The asymptotic LOE follows a Page-curve form whose value is obtained in closed form for every Rényi index, providing a benchmark for simulability and chaos diagnostics.
conclusion: Free probability yields a universal reference value for operator entanglement in chaotic dynamics, useful for quantifying deviations in locally interacting many-body systems.

title: Tunable Discrete-time Quasicrystal From A Single Drive
authors: Xu Feng, Shuo Liu, Shu Chen, And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xu Feng, Shuo Liu, Shu Chen, and Shi-Xin Zhang

The authors show that a single periodic drive can generate discrete-time quasicrystalline oscillations in a dissipative collective-spin system. Varying the drive strength continuously tunes the oscillation frequency, with distinct regions where the dominant response locks to rational fractions of the driving frequency.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L050201] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: A single periodic drive can generate tunable discrete-time quasicrystalline oscillations in a dissipative collective-spin system.
motivation: Discrete time crystals and quasicrystals typically require complex driving or multiple incommensurate frequencies; this work asks whether a single periodic drive can induce quasicrystalline temporal order in an open quantum system.
method: The authors study a dissipative collective-spin system under a single periodic drive and analyze the emergent oscillation frequencies and locking behavior as the drive strength is varied.
result: The oscillation frequency is continuously tunable with drive strength, and distinct regimes appear where the dominant response locks to rational fractions of the driving frequency.
conclusion: The results demonstrate a route to discrete-time quasicrystalline behavior from a single drive, offering a tunable platform for driven dissipative quantum dynamics.

title: Lindblad Master Equation For Twisted Photons In A Turbulent Atmosphere
authors: Tim Ehret, Vyacheslav Shatokhin, And Andreas Buchleitner
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Ehret, Vyacheslav Shatokhin, and Andreas Buchleitner

We revisit a Lindblad master equation for the propagation of photons carrying orbital angular momentum through a turbulent atmosphere. This equation is here independently derived from the stochastic Hamiltonian formulation of paraxial optics, accounts for the Kolmogorov power spectrum of turbulence,…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053713] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a Lindblad master equation for orbital-angular-momentum photons propagating through a turbulent atmosphere, modeling decoherence from Kolmogorov turbulence.
motivation: Atmospheric turbulence degrades spatial modes of photons, which is important for free-space quantum communication and entanglement distribution using orbital angular momentum.
method: The authors independently derive a Lindblad master equation from the stochastic Hamiltonian formulation of paraxial optics, incorporating the Kolmogorov turbulence power spectrum.
result: The resulting master equation describes the open-system dynamics and decoherence of twisted photons in a turbulent atmospheric channel.
conclusion: This provides a theoretical framework for modeling turbulence-induced effects on OAM-encoded photons, relevant to free-space quantum communication but not directly advancing core quantum network architectures.

title: Tensor-Network Framework For Lindbladian Spectra And Steady States
authors: Philipp Westhoff, Mattia Moroder, Ulrich Schollwöck, And Sebastian Paeckel
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp Westhoff, Mattia Moroder, Ulrich Schollwöck, and Sebastian Paeckel

Researchers develop a tensor-network framework using complex-time evolution to accurately compute low-lying excitation spectra of open quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041020] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a tensor-network framework that uses complex-time evolution to compute low-lying Lindbladian excitation spectra and steady states of open quantum systems.
motivation: Accurately extracting spectra and steady states of open quantum many-body systems is challenging due to the high dimensionality of Lindblad dynamics.
method: The authors develop a tensor-network representation and employ complex-time evolution to target low-lying Lindbladian eigenmodes and steady states.
result: The framework enables efficient computation of low-lying excitation spectra and steady states for open quantum systems.
conclusion: This tensor-network approach provides a practical numerical tool for studying spectral properties and long-time behavior of Lindbladian dynamics.

title: Meson Spectroscopy Of Exotic Symmetries Of Ising Criticality In Rydberg Atom Arrays
authors: Joseph Vovrosh, Julius de Hond, Sergi Julià-Farré, Johannes Knolle, And Alexandre Dauphin
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph Vovrosh, Julius de Hond, Sergi Julià-Farré, Johannes Knolle, and Alexandre Dauphin

A programmable array of atoms reveals how symmetry of the quantum Ising chain transforms when chains are coupled together, providing experimental signatures of a new excitation spectrum.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043018] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: A programmable Rydberg atom array is used to reveal how the symmetries of quantum Ising chains transform when chains are coupled, producing experimental signatures of a meson-like excitation spectrum.
motivation: The work aims to probe exotic symmetry structures and emergent excitation spectra of coupled quantum Ising chains using a controllable quantum-simulation platform.
method: Programmable Rydberg atom arrays realize coupled Ising chains, and spectroscopy of the resulting excitation spectrum is used to identify signatures of the transformed symmetries.
result: The experiment observes meson-like excitations and experimental signatures of a new excitation spectrum associated with coupled Ising criticality.
conclusion: Rydberg atom arrays provide a viable platform for spectroscopic studies of exotic symmetries and mesonic excitations in quantum Ising systems.

title: Vacuum-induced Interference In Light Scattering By Multilevel Atomic Chains
authors: Aleksei Konovalov, Giovanna Morigi, And Nicola Piovella
abstract:
Author(s): Aleksei Konovalov, Giovanna Morigi, and Nicola Piovella

We investigate cooperative light scattering by an ordered chain of multilevel emitters, which possess two quasiresonant transitions with parallel dipole moments. Interference between dipole transitions induced by coupling with the vacuum gives rise to so called cross damping and cross shifts, that m…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053710] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies cooperative light scattering by an ordered chain of multilevel atoms with two quasiresonant parallel-dipole transitions, showing that vacuum-induced interference produces cross damping and cross shifts.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how vacuum-mediated interference between nearly degenerate dipole transitions modifies collective light scattering in multilevel atomic chains.
method: They analyze an ordered chain of multilevel emitters coupled via vacuum-induced dipole transitions, deriving cooperative scattering effects including cross damping and cross shifts.
result: Interference between the two quasiresonant transitions leads to additional collective decay and frequency-shift terms that alter the scattering response of the atomic chain.
conclusion: Vacuum-induced interference is an important ingredient in cooperative scattering by multilevel atomic chains and can qualitatively modify their optical properties.

title: Open Wilson Chain Numerical Renormalization Group Approach To Steady-state Nonequilibrium Quantum Transport
authors: Anand Manaparambil And Frithjof B. Anders
abstract:
Author(s): Anand Manaparambil and Frithjof B. Anders

The numerical renormalization group (NRG) approach was developed to identify and quantify different equilibrium regimes of quantum impurity systems with unprecedented accuracy by a tailored finite-size representation. Out of equilibrium, the steady-state density operator is not of the Boltzmannian f…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 305112] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an open Wilson chain numerical renormalization group method to compute steady-state nonequilibrium quantum transport in quantum impurity systems.
motivation: Equilibrium NRG is highly accurate for quantum impurity problems, but nonequilibrium steady states are not Boltzmannian and require a finite-size open-system representation.
method: The authors formulate an open Wilson chain NRG approach that represents the steady-state density operator of a quantum impurity coupled to reservoirs and use it to calculate nonequilibrium transport properties.
result: The approach provides a tailored finite-size description of steady-state nonequilibrium quantum transport, extending NRG beyond equilibrium Boltzmannian density operators.
conclusion: Open Wilson chain NRG offers a controlled numerical framework for steady-state nonequilibrium quantum impurity transport, relevant to open quantum systems but not directly to core information-thermodynamic questions.

title: Mixed-State Phases From Local Reversibility
authors: Shengqi Sang, Leonardo A. Lessa, Roger S. K. Mong, Tarun Grover, Chong Wang, And Timothy H. Hsieh
abstract:
Author(s): Shengqi Sang, Leonardo A. Lessa, Roger S. K. Mong, Tarun Grover, Chong Wang, and Timothy H. Hsieh

Researchers establish a framework using local reversibility to correctly classify phases of matter in open and noisy quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041014] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a local-reversibility framework for classifying phases of matter in open and noisy quantum systems.
motivation: Standard phase classification is well developed for closed, pure-state quantum systems but becomes ambiguous in open and noisy settings where mixed states and decoherence dominate.
method: The authors define an equivalence notion based on local reversible operations for mixed quantum states and use it to organize and classify mixed-state phases.
result: They establish a framework that correctly classifies phases of matter in open and noisy quantum systems using local reversibility.
conclusion: Local reversibility provides a principled way to characterize and distinguish mixed-state phases beyond the closed-system paradigm.

title: Heisenberg-Limited Hamiltonian Learning Without Short-Time Control
authors: Myeongjin Shin, Junseo Lee, And Changhun Oh
abstract:
Author(s): Myeongjin Shin, Junseo Lee, and Changhun Oh

A new approach for learning Hamiltonians achieves the Heisenberg limit even when experiments cannot access short evolution times, easing a demanding control requirement.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043011] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a Hamiltonian-learning approach that attains Heisenberg-limited precision without requiring access to short evolution times.
motivation: Hamiltonian learning typically relies on short-time evolution to achieve optimal scaling, but such control is experimentally demanding. The work seeks to relax this requirement while preserving Heisenberg-limited performance.
method: It develops a learning strategy that extracts Hamiltonian parameters from longer-time dynamics, circumventing the need for short-time control while aiming for Heisenberg scaling.
result: The proposed approach achieves the Heisenberg limit even when experiments cannot access short evolution times, thereby easing a demanding control requirement.
conclusion: This makes Heisenberg-limited Hamiltonian learning more experimentally feasible, but it is peripheral to the researcher's listed core interests in entanglement, nonlocality, entropy, cryptography, and thermodynamics.

title: Squeezed-light-enhanced Multiparameter Quantum Estimation In Cavity Magnonics
authors: Hamza Harraf, Mohamed Amazioug, And Rachid Ahl Laamara
abstract:
Author(s): Hamza Harraf, Mohamed Amazioug, and Rachid Ahl Laamara

Improving multiparameter quantum estimation in magnonic systems via quantum noise suppression is a well-established and critical research objective. In this work, we propose an experimentally realistic scheme to improve the precision of simultaneously estimating different parameters in a cavity-magn…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053510] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a squeezed-light-driven cavity magnonic scheme to enhance the precision of simultaneously estimating multiple parameters, using quantum noise suppression.
motivation: Multiparameter quantum estimation in magnonic platforms is limited by quantum noise, and improving precision is a key goal for sensing applications of cavity magnonics.
method: An experimentally realistic cavity-magnonics setup (magnon mode coupled to a microwave cavity, driven by squeezed light) is analyzed with the quantum Fisher information / covariance-based multiparameter estimation framework to assess simultaneous estimation precision.
result: Squeezing the input field is shown to suppress noise and improve the achievable precision for joint estimation of the relevant magnonic and cavity parameters, quantified via estimation bounds.
conclusion: Squeezed-light injection provides a practical route to enhanced multiparameter estimation in cavity magnonic devices, with potential use in quantum sensing with hybrid spin-photon platforms.

title: Time-local Nonequilibrium Green's Function Method For Real-time Dynamics In Quantum Systems Coupled To Superconducting Leads
authors: Taira Kawamura
abstract:
Author(s): Taira Kawamura

We develop a time-local nonequilibrium Green's function formulation for real-time dynamics in quantum systems coupled to superconducting leads. The superconducting lead self-energy is a strongly frequency-dependent matrix in Nambu space, giving rise to nonlocal memory kernels in the time domain. Thi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254512] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a time-local nonequilibrium Green's function formulation for real-time dynamics of quantum systems coupled to superconducting leads.
motivation: Superconducting leads produce strongly frequency-dependent self-energies, which become nonlocal memory kernels in time and complicate real-time simulations.
method: The authors formulate a time-local NEGF approach in Nambu space to handle the nonlocal memory effects induced by superconducting lead self-energies.
result: The method enables real-time dynamics calculations while managing the frequency-dependent superconducting lead self-energy in a time-local framework.
conclusion: This provides a practical theoretical tool for studying nonequilibrium dynamics in open quantum systems with superconducting reservoirs.

title: Metastable Phase Separation And Information Retrieval In Multicomponent Liquids
authors: Davide Marcato, Rodrigo Braz Teixeira, Izaak Neri, And Pablo Sartori
abstract:
Author(s): Davide Marcato, Rodrigo Braz Teixeira, Izaak Neri, and Pablo Sartori

A thermodynamic theory shows that multicomponent liquid mixtures can store prescribed compositions as metastable states and retrieve them from partial seeds, realizing associative memory in a demixing liquid.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041033] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: A thermodynamic theory shows that multicomponent liquid mixtures can store prescribed compositions as metastable states and retrieve them from partial seeds, realizing associative memory in a demixing liquid.
motivation: The paper explores whether phase-separating liquid mixtures can serve as physical substrates for information storage and associative memory, connecting metastability with information retrieval.
method: The authors develop a thermodynamic theory of multicomponent liquid mixtures in which prescribed compositions are encoded as metastable states and recovered from partial compositional cues.
result: They demonstrate that demixing multicomponent liquids can store multiple compositions and retrieve them from partial seeds, functioning as associative memory.
conclusion: Metastable phase separation in multicomponent liquids provides a thermodynamic mechanism for information storage and retrieval, extending associative memory concepts to classical liquid mixtures.

title: Metrological Channels Induced By Encrypted Quantum Cloning: Optimal-probe Fisher-information Broadcasting And Single-use Operational Recovery
authors: Nalan Kandirmaz
abstract:
Author(s): Nalan Kandirmaz

Encrypted quantum cloning creates multiple individually inaccessible signal systems from which an unknown input state can be recovered by combining any selected signal with a shared quantum key. Here we study parameter estimation when a local sensing transformation is applied after encrypted cloning…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052421] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes parameter estimation (metrology) with encrypted quantum cloning, deriving optimal-probe Fisher-information broadcasting bounds and single-use operational recovery of the estimated parameter using a shared quantum key.
motivation: Encrypted quantum cloning produces several inaccessible copies of an unknown state recoverable only with a shared key; the authors ask how this structure affects quantum-limited parameter estimation when a local sensing transformation acts after cloning.
method: Quantum Fisher information (and its broadcasting/distribution among the cloned signals) is computed for the encrypted-cloning channel, together with a single-use operational recovery protocol that combines one signal with the key to reconstruct the estimated parameter.
result: Bounds on how Fisher information is broadcast among the encrypted clones are established, and single-use recovery is shown to be operationally optimal under the stated conditions, characterizing the metrological channel induced by encrypted cloning.
conclusion: Encrypted cloning induces well-defined metrological channels whose estimation performance can be quantified and, using the key, partially recovered in a single-shot operational setting, linking cloning-based encryption with quantum estimation theory.

title: Steering And Local Tunneling Signatures Of Majorana Corner Modes In Altermagnetic Josephson Junctions
authors: Yu-Xuan Li And Tao Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Xuan Li and Tao Zhou

Dynamical manipulation of Majorana zero modes and their reliable distinction from topologically trivial states remain paramount challenges in topological quantum computation. Here, we propose a phase-biased altermagnetic Josephson junction as a versatile platform for generating and controlling Major…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274507] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a phase-biased altermagnetic Josephson junction as a platform for generating, steering, and detecting Majorana corner modes via local tunneling signatures.
motivation: Reliable dynamical control of Majorana zero modes and their unambiguous distinction from trivial Andreev bound states are key obstacles for topological quantum computation.
method: A theoretical model of an altermagnetic Josephson junction with phase bias is analyzed, computing the spectrum and local tunneling conductance/steering response of the Majorana corner modes.
result: The authors identify distinctive signatures—phase-tunable steering of the corner modes and characteristic local tunneling features—that separate topological Majorana corner modes from trivial states.
conclusion: Altermagnetic Josephson junctions offer a controllable setting for manipulating and identifying Majorana corner modes, with potential relevance to topological qubit architectures.

title: Fractional Quantum Hall States Under Density Decoherence
authors: Zijian Wang, Ruihua Fan, Tianle Wang, Samuel J. Garratt, And Ehud Altman
abstract:
Author(s): Zijian Wang, Ruihua Fan, Tianle Wang, Samuel J. Garratt, and Ehud Altman

Statistical mechanics mappings reveal that quantum information stored in the non-Abelian anyons of Moore-Read states resists arbitrary density dephasing, whereas that stored in the Laughlin states has an infinite robustness only above a critical filling factor.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031074] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: A statistical-mechanics mapping shows that quantum information encoded in non-Abelian Moore-Read anyons survives arbitrary density dephasing, while Laughlin-state information is infinitely robust only above a critical filling factor.
motivation: Topological orders are candidate quantum memories, so it is crucial to know how robustly the quantum information they store survives realistic local decoherence such as density/dephasing noise.
method: The authors map the decoherence dynamics of fractional quantum Hall states (Laughlin and Moore-Read) under density dephasing onto statistical-mechanics models, extracting the lifetime/robustness of the encoded anyonic information as a function of filling factor.
result: Moore-Read (non-Abelian) states retain their encoded information under arbitrary density dephasing, whereas Laughlin states exhibit infinite robustness only above a critical filling factor.
conclusion: Non-Abelian fractional quantum Hall states offer intrinsically decoherence-resilient quantum information storage, sharpening the case for topological anyonic memories while delineating regimes of failure for Abelian states.

title: No-go Theorem For Maximally $ψ$-epistemic Models Using Two Pure States Of A Qubit
authors: Sagnik Ray, Anubhav Chaturvedi, And Debashis Saha
abstract:
Author(s): Sagnik Ray, Anubhav Chaturvedi, and Debashis Saha

This work addresses the fundamental question concerning the nature of quantum states, specifically to what extent they represent an agent's knowledge about the system, that is, is epistemic in nature. We show that, despite the existence of the Kochen-Specker model, which is a maximally [MATH]-epistemic…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052213] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves a no-go theorem showing that maximally ψ-epistemic models of quantum states cannot reproduce quantum predictions when considering two pure states of a qubit, despite the existence of the Kochen-Specker model.
motivation: The work addresses the foundational question of whether quantum states represent an agent's knowledge about a system (epistemic) or are ontic, and challenges the viability of maximally ψ-epistemic interpretations.
method: The authors construct a no-go theorem using two pure qubit states, analyzing the constraints on maximally ψ-epistemic models and comparing them with the Kochen-Specker model.
result: They show that no maximally ψ-epistemic model can reproduce the quantum statistics for two pure qubit states, thereby ruling out a broad class of epistemic interpretations.
conclusion: The result strengthens no-go theorems against ψ-epistemic models and clarifies the limits of epistemic interpretations of quantum states, with implications for quantum foundations.

title: Hierarchy Of Mixed Symmetry Protected Topological States In Extended Cluster States Under Subsystem Decoherence
authors: Yoshihito Kuno And Takahiro Orito
abstract:
Author(s): Yoshihito Kuno and Takahiro Orito

We study the effect of subsystem decoherence on an extended cluster state, which is a symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phase. The model includes many subsystem [MATH] symmetries. We report that subsystem decoherence induces local charge fluctuations, leading to a mixed SPT state in the unaffe…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254108] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how subsystem decoherence produces a hierarchy of mixed symmetry-protected topological states in an extended cluster-state model.
motivation: Mixed-state topological phases and their robustness under decoherence are important for understanding quantum order beyond pure states, but the paper focuses specifically on SPT phases in a condensed-matter-inspired setting.
method: The authors analyze an extended cluster state possessing many subsystem symmetries and examine the effect of subsystem decoherence on its SPT character.
result: Subsystem decoherence induces local charge fluctuations and leads to mixed SPT states in regions unaffected by the decoherence, revealing a hierarchy of mixed SPT phases.
