conclusion: The work characterizes how subsystem symmetries and decoherence generate mixed SPT phases, extending the theory of SPT order to mixed states.

title: Interplay Of Noise And Reservoir-induced Decoherence In Persistent Currents
authors: Samudra Sur And Thierry Giamarchi
abstract:
Author(s): Samudra Sur and Thierry Giamarchi

Persistent current is a hallmark of quantum phase coherence. We study the fate of the persistent current in a nonequilibrium setting, where a tight-binding ring is subjected to stochastic disorder as well as a fermionic reservoir attached to each site. We evaluate the current using the Keldysh techn…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043141] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how stochastic disorder and site-attached fermionic reservoirs destroy the persistent current in a tight-binding ring, computed with the Keldysh formalism.
motivation: Persistent currents are a hallmark of quantum phase coherence, and understanding how nonequilibrium noise and environmental coupling degrade them is important for mesoscopic coherent transport.
method: A tight-binding ring is subjected to stochastic disorder and coupled to a fermionic bath at each site; the steady-state current is evaluated using the Keldysh nonequilibrium Green's function technique.
result: The interplay between stochastic disorder and reservoir-induced decoherence is quantified, showing how each mechanism suppresses the persistent current and where their effects combine or compete.
conclusion: Environmental reservoirs and noise impose distinct but interacting constraints on coherence-maintained currents in mesoscopic rings, with implications for decoherence-limited quantum transport.

title: Quantum Advantage For Sensing Properties Of Classical Fields
authors: Jordan Cotler, Daine L. Danielson, And Ishaan Kannan
abstract:
Author(s): Jordan Cotler, Daine L. Danielson, and Ishaan Kannan

Researchers demonstrate a quantum sensing protocol that uses entanglement and squeezing to learn diverse classical signal properties with subvacuum precision.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041025] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: A quantum sensing protocol exploiting entanglement and squeezing estimates multiple properties of classical fields with precision beyond the standard vacuum limit.
motivation: Classical sensing strategies for estimating parameters of classical fields are constrained by shot-noise/vacuum limits, and it is natural to ask how much metrological advantage genuinely quantum resources such as entanglement and squeezing can provide.
method: The authors construct quantum probe states using entanglement and squeezing and analyze estimation protocols for diverse classical signal properties, comparing achievable precision against classical (vacuum-limited) benchmarks.
result: The protocol achieves subvacuum precision across a range of classical signal properties, demonstrating a quantum advantage in sensing tasks beyond single-parameter phase estimation.
conclusion: Entanglement and squeezing constitute useful resources for learning classical field properties, extending quantum metrological advantage to broader sensing scenarios.

title: Robustness Of Adiabatic Reverse Annealing To Low-temperature Decoherence
authors: An Le And Christopher Baldwin
abstract:
Author(s): An Le and Christopher Baldwin

Adiabatic reverse annealing (ARA) is an improvement to conventional quantum annealing that uses an initial guess at the desired ground state to circumvent problematic phase transitions. Despite encouraging results in the closed-system setting, Passarelli et al. [
tldr: The paper analyzes whether adiabatic reverse annealing retains its performance advantage when subject to low-temperature decoherence in an open-system setting.
motivation: Adiabatic reverse annealing has shown promise in closed-system studies, but realistic quantum annealing hardware is affected by decoherence, so its robustness under open-system conditions needs to be assessed.
method: The authors likely model adiabatic reverse annealing in the presence of low-temperature decoherence, comparing its behavior against conventional annealing or closed-system predictions, probably using an open quantum system master-equation approach.
result: The abstract indicates an analysis of ARA under low-temperature decoherence, evaluating the regimes in which its advantage persists or degrades due to environmental coupling.
conclusion: The work clarifies the robustness of adiabatic reverse annealing to decoherence, which is relevant for assessing its practical viability in noisy quantum annealing devices.

title: Temporal Complexity Hierarchies In Solvable Quantum Many-Body Dynamics
authors: He-Ran Wang, Ilya Vilkoviskiy, And Dmitry A. Abanin
abstract:
Author(s): He-Ran Wang, Ilya Vilkoviskiy, and Dmitry A. Abanin

Researchers establish a framework based on geometric group theory to classify the temporal computational complexity and quantum memory structures of solvable quantum many-body dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041041] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a geometric group theory framework to classify temporal computational complexity and quantum memory structures in solvable quantum many-body dynamics.
motivation: It aims to characterize how computational complexity and memory grow over time in exactly solvable quantum many-body systems, connecting many-body dynamics to complexity-theoretic classifications.
method: The authors use geometric group theory to organize and classify temporal complexity hierarchies and quantum memory structures arising in solvable dynamics.
result: They establish a framework that classifies temporal computational complexity and quantum memory structures for broad classes of solvable quantum many-body dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a group-theoretic classification of temporal complexity in solvable quantum dynamics, but it is primarily a quantum complexity/many-body dynamics result rather than directly addressing the researcher's core interests.

title: Erratum: Nonlocal And Quantum Advantages In Network Coding For Multiple Access Channels [Phys. Rev. A 113, 042624 (2026)]
authors: Jiyoung Yun, Seung-Hyun Nam, Hyun-Young Park, Ashutosh Rai, Si-Hyeon Lee, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Author(s): Jiyoung Yun, Seung-Hyun Nam, Hyun-Young Park, Ashutosh Rai, Si-Hyeon Lee, and Joonwoo Bae
[Phys. Rev. A 114, 059902] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting the original paper on nonlocal and quantum advantages in network coding for multiple-access channels.
motivation: The original work examined whether nonlocal correlations and quantum resources can outperform classical strategies in network coding scenarios over multiple-access channels, a topic at the intersection of Bell nonlocality and network information theory.
method: As an erratum, the item reports corrections to the published article (Phys. Rev. A 113, 042624) rather than introducing new derivations, protocols, or analyses.
result: Only corrected statements/equations from the original publication are presented; no new scientific findings or bounds are established.
conclusion: The erratum refines the accuracy of the original results on quantum advantages in network coding but contributes no independent scientific advance.

title: Non-Markovian Delay-assisted Sensing With Waveguide-coupled Quantum Emitters
authors: Prajit Dhara, Isack Padilla, Saikat Guha, Annyun Das, And Kanu Sinha
abstract:
Author(s): Prajit Dhara, Isack Padilla, Saikat Guha, Annyun Das, and Kanu Sinha

We show that in a minimal setup of two waveguide-coupled quantum emitters, separated by long distances and subject to an external field, time-delayed feedback can be a resource for sensing field gradients. While the field gradient induces a detuning between the emitters, the large interatomic separa…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043138] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes time-delayed feedback in a waveguide-coupled two-emitter system as a resource for sensing external field gradients.
motivation: Quantum emitters coupled to waveguides provide a controllable platform for non-Markovian dynamics, and delayed feedback may enhance metrological sensitivity beyond Markovian limits.
method: A minimal model of two distant waveguide-coupled quantum emitters under an external field is analyzed, where the field gradient induces a detuning and the large separation produces time-delayed coherent feedback.
result: The authors show that non-Markovian delayed feedback can improve the sensing of field gradients in this waveguide-QED setup.
conclusion: Time-delayed feedback in waveguide-coupled emitter systems is identified as a useful resource for quantum-enhanced field-gradient sensing.

title: Interaction-Assisted Topological Pumping In Few- And Many-Atom Rydberg Arrays
authors: Chenxi Huang, Tao Chen, Qian Liang, Matthew A. Krebs, Ethan Springhorn, Ruiyu Li, Mingsheng Tian, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Jacob P. Covey, And Bryce Gadway
abstract:
Author(s): Chenxi Huang, Tao Chen, Qian Liang, Matthew A. Krebs, Ethan Springhorn, Ruiyu Li, Mingsheng Tian, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Jacob P. Covey, and Bryce Gadway

Strong dipolar interactions in Rydberg atom arrays are found to be able to bind particles into correlated pairs and clusters that undergo efficient topological pumping along a synthetic dimension.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031075] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: Strong dipolar interactions in Rydberg atom arrays bind atoms into correlated pairs and clusters that can be topologically pumped along a synthetic dimension.
motivation: Topological pumping is typically studied with single, non-interacting particles; the authors ask whether strong dipolar interactions in Rydberg arrays can be harnessed to pump correlated many-body objects instead.
method: Few- and many-atom Rydberg arrays with strong dipolar interactions are driven periodically, generating synthetic-dimension dynamics in which interacting particles form bound pairs and clusters; the resulting transport is characterized experimentally and compared with theoretical modeling.
result: Interactions bind particles into correlated pairs and clusters that are pumped efficiently along the synthetic dimension, with interaction-assisted topological transport observed in both few-atom and many-atom regimes.
conclusion: Rydberg arrays provide a platform where interactions can be used as a resource to realize topological pumping of correlated many-body states, extending topological pumping beyond the single-particle paradigm.

title: Efficient Single-photon Generation In A Cavity-based Nondegenerate double-$\mathrm{Λ}$ System
authors: Xinchen Zhang, Pengfei Zhang, Gang Li, And Tiancai Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xinchen Zhang, Pengfei Zhang, Gang Li, and Tiancai Zhang

Single-photon sources are fundamental devices in quantum optics and an essential component of quantum information science. At present, the vacuum-stimulated Raman adiabatic passage scheme in a three-level atom has been widely used for single-photon generation. However, multiple nondegenerate hyperfi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053717] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes and analyzes a cavity-based nondegenerate double-Λ scheme for efficient single-photon generation, extending vacuum-stimulated Raman adiabatic passage beyond simple three-level atoms.
motivation: Single-photon sources are key resources for quantum information, but standard cavity-based Raman adiabatic passage schemes are limited when multiple nondegenerate transitions or hyperfine levels are involved.
method: The authors study a cavity QED system with a nondegenerate double-Λ level structure and evaluate single-photon generation via an adiabatic passage protocol, likely analyzing efficiency, purity, and spectral properties.
result: The scheme is predicted to enable efficient single-photon generation with the nondegenerate double-Λ configuration, potentially offering improved flexibility or performance over conventional three-level Raman schemes.
conclusion: Such a cavity-based double-Λ source could provide a practical route to efficient, frequency-tailored single photons, though the work is primarily source engineering rather than a networking protocol or information-theoretic advance.

title: Symmetry Restoration And Quantum Mpemba Effect In The Complex Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model
authors: Sizheng Cao And Xian-Hui Ge
abstract:
Author(s): Sizheng Cao and Xian-Hui Ge

Entanglement asymmetry, used here as a direct probe of symmetry restoration, provides a sharp diagnostic of postquench dynamics. We test this idea in the complex Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (cSYK) model with a conserved U(1) charge. We numerically track the joint evolution of entanglement entropy and entangle…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 285114] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses entanglement asymmetry to probe symmetry restoration and the quantum Mpemba effect in the complex Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model after a quantum quench.
motivation: Understanding how symmetries are restored in isolated quantum many-body systems is a central problem in non-equilibrium quantum dynamics, and entanglement asymmetry offers a sharp diagnostic beyond conventional entanglement entropy.
method: The authors numerically simulate the complex SYK model with a conserved U(1) charge and track the joint post-quench evolution of entanglement entropy and entanglement asymmetry.
result: They identify signatures of symmetry restoration and a quantum Mpemba effect, where certain initial states approach the symmetric steady state faster despite being initially farther from it.
conclusion: Entanglement asymmetry is established as a useful probe of symmetry restoration in chaotic many-body dynamics, with the cSYK model providing a controlled setting for observing the quantum Mpemba effect.

title: Boltzmann-like Occupation Of Nonequilibrium Steady States On Dense Disordered Networks
authors: Jacob Calvert
abstract:
Author(s): Jacob Calvert

A central problem in statistical physics is to extend the Boltzmann distribution to nonequilibrium steady states (NESS). We prove that NESS on large dense disordered networks have Boltzmann-like occupation, despite extensive entropy production. One consequence is that such NESS can conceal their non…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054120] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that nonequilibrium steady states on large dense disordered networks exhibit Boltzmann-like occupation despite extensive entropy production.
motivation: Extending the Boltzmann distribution to nonequilibrium steady states is a central open problem in statistical physics, with implications for how such states may conceal their nonequilibrium nature.
method: The author analyzes nonequilibrium steady states on dense disordered networks and derives conditions under which their occupation probabilities take a Boltzmann-like form.
result: The main result is a proof that, on large dense disordered networks, NESS occupation can be Boltzmann-like even when entropy production is extensive.
conclusion: This suggests that certain nonequilibrium steady states can mimic equilibrium Boltzmann statistics, making their true nonequilibrium character difficult to detect.

title: Nested Superstatistics: When The Fluctuation Parameter Fluctuates
authors: Kamel Ourabah
abstract:
Author(s): Kamel Ourabah

Many nonequilibrium systems exhibit a hierarchy of well-separated dynamical scales. Typically, microscopic variables such as energy or velocity evolve rapidly, whereas environmental parameters such as the inverse temperature [MATH] fluctuate more slowly. This separation naturally leads to superstatisti…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043119] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a nested superstatistical framework for nonequilibrium systems with hierarchical time scales, where the fluctuation parameter of a superstatistical distribution itself fluctuates.
motivation: Many nonequilibrium systems display multiple separated dynamical scales, such as fast microscopic variables and slowly fluctuating environmental parameters like inverse temperature, motivating a hierarchical generalization of superstatistics.
method: The author introduces a nested superstatistics formalism in which the superstatistical parameter is itself treated as a fluctuating random variable, and analyzes the resulting statistical distributions and thermodynamic implications.
result: The nested construction yields modified distribution functions and fluctuation properties that can capture systems with more than one level of environmental or parameter variability.
conclusion: Nested superstatistics provides a natural statistical-mechanical description for nonequilibrium systems with hierarchical fluctuation scales, though the work is primarily classical and not directly focused on quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Chaotic Many-Body Quantum Dynamics, Spectral Correlations, And Energy Diffusion
authors: J. T. Chalker And Dominik Hahn
abstract:
Author(s): J. T. Chalker and Dominik Hahn

Researchers analyze a solvable many-body model to demonstrate how energy diffusion governs spectral correlations in chaotic quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031076] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: A solvable many-body model is used to show how energy diffusion sets the structure of spectral correlations in chaotic quantum systems.
motivation: Spectral correlations and level statistics are standard diagnostics of quantum chaos, but a quantitative link between them and hydrodynamic transport of conserved quantities such as energy has been unclear.
method: The authors analyze an exactly solvable chaotic many-body model, computing spectral form factors and correlation functions and comparing them with the diffusive spreading of energy.
result: They demonstrate that energy diffusion controls the behavior of spectral correlations, establishing a direct connection between hydrodynamic transport and level-correlation statistics.
conclusion: The work clarifies how transport properties imprint on spectral statistics in chaotic many-body dynamics, providing a solvable benchmark for chaos diagnostics.

title: Deconfined Quantum Critical Point In A Dissipative Spin-1/2 Chain
authors: Longye Lu, Shifeng Cui, And Wenan Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Longye Lu, Shifeng Cui, and Wenan Guo

Open quantum spin systems offer a previously unexplored route to realizing deconfined quantum criticality. We consider a spin-[MATH] [MATH] chain composed of an antiferromagnetic (AFM) Heisenberg exchange and a competing multispin interaction favoring a valence-bond solid (VBS) state, wit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 206703] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dissipative spin-1/2 chain and reports a deconfined quantum critical point between antiferromagnetic and valence-bond-solid phases in an open quantum setting.
motivation: Open quantum spin systems are proposed as a new route to realize deconfined quantum criticality, extending beyond conventional closed equilibrium condensed-matter settings.
method: The authors analyze a spin-1/2 chain with antiferromagnetic Heisenberg exchange competing with a multispin interaction favoring a valence-bond-solid state, including dissipation.
result: They identify a deconfined quantum critical point in this dissipative spin-chain model, characterizing the transition between the antiferromagnetic and valence-bond-solid regimes.
conclusion: The work suggests that dissipation can provide a viable platform for deconfined quantum criticality, though its direct relevance to quantum information or information thermodynamics is limited.

title: Continuous-time Evolution Via Probabilistic Angle Interpolation And Its Applications
authors: Tomoya Hayata And Yuta Kikuchi
abstract:
Author(s): Tomoya Hayata and Yuta Kikuchi

We explore the applicability of a stochastic time-evolution algorithm based on probabilistic angle interpolation. To simplify the preprocessing of the algorithm, we take the continuous-time limit, thereby explicitly eliminating Trotter errors and streamlining the resource analysis. We also introduce…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052425] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a continuous-time limit of a stochastic quantum time-evolution algorithm based on probabilistic angle interpolation, eliminating Trotter error and simplifying resource analysis.
motivation: Probabilistic angle interpolation offers a stochastic route to simulating quantum dynamics, but its discrete-time formulation carries Trotter errors and cumbersome preprocessing and resource accounting.
method: They take the continuous-time limit of the stochastic algorithm, replacing discrete probabilistic angle choices with a continuous stochastic process, and analyze the resulting resource requirements and applications.
result: The continuous-time formulation removes Trotter error exactly and streamlines preprocessing and resource estimates; several applications of the algorithm are explored.
conclusion: The approach provides a cleaner, error-free stochastic framework for continuous-time quantum evolution, though its relevance is mainly to algorithm design rather than information-theoretic questions.

title: Asymptotically Solvable Quantum Circuits
authors: Samuel H. Pickering And Bruno Bertini
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel H. Pickering and Bruno Bertini

A new family of quantum circuits gives rise to correlations that are chaotic at short scales yet exactly solvable at long scales.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043001] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a family of quantum circuits whose short-scale correlations are chaotic but become exactly solvable at long scales.
motivation: Understanding chaotic quantum dynamics is difficult because exact solutions are rare, so the authors seek tractable models that retain chaotic short-distance behavior while allowing long-time analytical control.
method: They construct a new class of quantum circuits designed to be asymptotically solvable, likely by identifying structural simplifications that emerge at long times or large scales.
result: The circuits exhibit chaotic correlations at short scales and admit exact long-scale solutions, providing a controlled setting for studying chaotic quantum dynamics.
conclusion: This offers a solvable model for quantum chaos, but it is more relevant to many-body dynamics and random-circuit physics than to the researcher's core interests.

title: Quantum-noise Limits Of The Self-compensating Alkali–noble-gas Comagnetometer
authors: Jiaxin Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Jiaxin Liu

Self-compensating alkali–noble-gas comagnetometers are the most sensitive laboratory probes of exotic spin couplings, but their quantum-noise limit, including the backaction of the optical readout, has not been established. We derive it from an input-output model of the Faraday readout coupled to th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052605] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives the quantum-noise limit, including optical-readout backaction, for a self-compensating alkali–noble-gas comagnetometer.
motivation: Self-compensating alkali–noble-gas comagnetometers are highly sensitive probes of exotic spin couplings, but their fundamental quantum-noise limit including measurement backaction had not been established.
method: An input-output model of the Faraday optical readout coupled to the alkali–noble-gas spin dynamics is used to derive the quantum-noise limit.
result: The analysis establishes the quantum-noise limit of the comagnetometer while accounting for backaction from the optical readout.
conclusion: This provides a fundamental noise benchmark for self-compensating alkali–noble-gas comagnetometers, relevant primarily to precision magnetometry and spin-coupling searches.

title: Electrically Tunable Orbital Coupling And Quantum Light Emission From O-Band Quantum Dot Molecules
authors: P. S. Avdienko, L. Hanschke, Q. Buchinger, N. Akhlaq, I. Lubianskii, E. Weber, H. Riedl, M. Kamp, T. Huber-Loyola, S. Höfling, A. T. Pfenning, K. Müller, And J. J. Finley
abstract:
Author(s): P. S. Avdienko, L. Hanschke, Q. Buchinger, N. Akhlaq, I. Lubianskii, E. Weber, H. Riedl, M. Kamp, T. Huber-Loyola, S. Höfling, A. T. Pfenning, K. Müller, and J. J. Finley

Telecom O-band InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules exhibit electrically tunable orbital coupling, opening a route toward 2D photonic cluster states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033070] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: Telecom O-band InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules are shown to have electrically tunable orbital (hole) coupling, a step toward generating 2D photonic cluster states.
motivation: Scalable photonic quantum information processing needs entangled-photon sources at telecom wavelengths that can be tuned in situ; quantum dot molecules offer tunable few-level structure for this purpose.
method: Molecular-beam-epitaxy-grown InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules are characterized spectroscopically under applied electric fields, with photoluminescence and correlation measurements probing orbital coupling and quantum light emission.
result: The authors demonstrate voltage-controlled tuning of the orbital coupling between the two dots and observe quantum light emission in the O-band, indicating a viable route to on-chip entangled photon generation.
conclusion: Electrically tunable quantum dot molecules in the telecom O-band are promising building blocks for 2D photonic cluster states, though substantial device and protocol development remains.

title: Optomechanical Limit On Intracavity Intensities From Bulk Mirror Vibrations
authors: L. Maisenbacher, A. Singh, I. M. Pope, And H. Müller
abstract:
Author(s): L. Maisenbacher, A. Singh, I. M. Pope, and H. Müller

Ultrahigh continuous-wave intensities [MATH] in high-numerical-aperture optical cavities enable applications from phase-contrast electron microscopy to ultradeep dipole traps for molecules. However, the intensity can be limited by the optomechanical …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 203603] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how bulk vibrations of cavity mirrors impose an optomechanical limit on achievable intracavity intensities in high-numerical-aperture optical cavities.
motivation: Ultrahigh continuous-wave intensities in high-finesse cavities are useful for applications such as ultradeep dipole traps and phase-contrast electron microscopy, but mirror optomechanics may constrain the attainable intensity.
method: The authors model the optomechanical coupling between the intracavity optical field and bulk vibrational modes of the mirror to derive an intensity limit.
result: They identify an optomechanical bound on intracavity intensity arising from bulk mirror vibrations, relevant to high-numerical-aperture cavity designs.
conclusion: The work highlights a practical physical limit for high-intensity cavity applications and provides guidance for mirror/cavity design, though it is not directly focused on quantum information processing.

title: Minimizing Classical Resources In Variational Measurement-based Quantum Computation For Generative Modeling
authors: Arunava Majumder, Hendrik Poulsen Nautrup, And Hans J. Briegel
abstract:
Author(s): Arunava Majumder, Hendrik Poulsen Nautrup, and Hans J. Briegel

Measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC) is a framework for quantum information processing in which a computational task is carried out through one-qubit measurements on a highly entangled resource state. Due to the indeterminacy of the outcomes of a quantum measurement, the random outcomes of t…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052420] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies variational measurement-based quantum computation for generative modeling with the goal of minimizing the classical resources required to handle random measurement outcomes.
motivation: MBQC uses adaptive one-qubit measurements on entangled resource states, but measurement randomness can impose significant classical control and post-processing overhead; reducing this overhead is important for practical variational MBQC.
method: The authors analyze variational MBQC architectures for generative modeling and propose ways to reduce the classical resources needed for feed-forward, adaptation, or post-processing of measurement outcomes.
result: The work identifies classical resource costs in variational MBQC generative models and shows how they can be minimized within the MBQC framework.
conclusion: The paper contributes to making variational MBQC generative modeling more resource-efficient, though its focus is on a specialized quantum-machine-learning application rather than core quantum-information theory.

title: Quantum Droplets And Condensates In An Optical Lattice Coupled To A Dissipative Cavity: Collective Excitations And Nonequilibrium Dynamics
authors: G. Vivek, Sudip Sinha, And Subhasis Sinha
abstract:
Author(s): G. Vivek, Sudip Sinha, and Subhasis Sinha

Motivated by recent experiments on light-matter interacting systems, we investigate a dilute Bose gas and self-bound quantum droplets in a one-dimensional optical lattice coupled to a lossy cavity mode. Using a classical-field approach, we determine the stationary states and collective excitations o…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053313] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies stationary states, collective excitations, and nonequilibrium dynamics of a dilute Bose gas and self-bound quantum droplets in a one-dimensional optical lattice coupled to a lossy cavity.
motivation: It is motivated by recent experiments on light-matter interacting systems and aims to understand how cavity dissipation and an optical lattice affect ultracold atomic condensates and droplets.
method: The authors use a classical-field approach to determine stationary states and collective excitations of the coupled atom-cavity system, including its nonequilibrium dynamics.
result: The work characterizes the stationary phases and collective excitation spectrum of the Bose gas and quantum droplets in the lattice-cavity setting, highlighting modifications due to the lossy cavity mode.
conclusion: The findings clarify how dissipative cavity coupling and lattice effects shape droplet and condensate behavior, with relevance to cold-atom cavity-QED experiments.

title: Signatures Of Gaussian Superconducting Fluctuations In Nonlocal Noise Magnetometry
authors: Dror Orgad
abstract:
Author(s): Dror Orgad

Are superconducting fluctuations in a film above its transition temperature dominated by short-lived Cooper pairs or by vortices? Here, the author calculates the magnetic-noise correlations sensed by two spatially separated diamond quantum probes, considering the film both in equilibrium and under an applied electric field. The distinct relaxation scales and directional patterns of the noise offer a means of distinguishing between the two scenarios.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264511] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes magnetic-noise correlations sensed by two spatially separated diamond (NV) quantum probes above a superconducting film's transition temperature to distinguish fluctuating Cooper pairs from vortices.
motivation: It is debated whether superconducting fluctuations above Tc in thin films are dominated by short-lived Cooper pairs or by vortex dynamics; a discriminating measurement protocol is needed.
method: Theoretical calculation of nonlocal magnetic-noise correlation spectra (two-probe relaxometry/spectroscopy) for a superconducting film in equilibrium and under an applied electric field, comparing predicted relaxation scales and directional patterns for the two scenarios.
result: The Cooper-pair and vortex scenarios yield distinct relaxation scaling and anisotropic directional noise patterns detectable by separated diamond quantum probes.
conclusion: Nonlocal noise magnetometry with colour-centre probes offers a practical way to identify the nature of Gaussian superconducting fluctuations, though the work is primarily condensed-matter physics rather than quantum-information hardware.

title: Finite-Size Scaling Theory Of Rényi Thermal Entropy For Second-Order, First-Order, And Weakly First-Order Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: Zhe Wang, Yanzhang Zhu, Chunhao Guo, Bin-Bin Chen, Yi-Ming Ding, Zenan Liu, And Zheng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Zhe Wang, Yanzhang Zhu, Chunhao Guo, Bin-Bin Chen, Yi-Ming Ding, Zenan Liu, and Zheng Yan

Researchers develop a Rényi thermal entropy scaling framework to identify weakly first-order quantum phase transitions in finite-size simulations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041031] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a finite-size scaling framework for the Rényi thermal entropy that can distinguish second-order, first-order, and weakly first-order quantum phase transitions in numerical simulations.
motivation: Weakly first-order quantum phase transitions are notoriously difficult to identify in finite-size numerics, since standard observables show ambiguous scaling behaviour that mimics continuous transitions.
method: A scaling theory for the Rényi thermal entropy is constructed and tested against finite-size simulation data for models exhibiting second-order, first-order, and weakly first-order transitions.
result: The Rényi thermal entropy is shown to obey characteristic scaling forms whose exponents and subleading corrections discriminate between the three transition types, resolving weakly first-order cases that conventional diagnostics miss.
conclusion: Rényi thermal entropy provides a practical and sensitive numerical probe for classifying quantum phase transitions, including borderline weakly first-order ones.

title: Theory Of Trotter Errors For Time-Dependent Product And Multi-product Formulas
authors: Kaoru Mizuta, Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Kaoru Mizuta, Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, and Keisuke Fujii

A Floquet-based analysis derives commutator-scaling error bounds for time-dependent product and multiproduct formulas, sharpening gate-count estimates for quantum simulation of driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033061] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives Floquet-based commutator-scaling error bounds for time-dependent product and multiproduct formulas used in quantum simulation.
motivation: Product formulas are central to digital quantum simulation, but their error scaling for time-dependent Hamiltonians and multiproduct variants needs sharper gate-count estimates.
method: A Floquet-based analysis is used to bound Trotter errors in terms of commutators for time-dependent product and multiproduct formulas.
result: The authors obtain improved error bounds that sharpen gate-count estimates for simulating driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.
conclusion: The work provides useful algorithmic error analysis for quantum simulation, but it is not directly aligned with the researcher's core interests in quantum information theory or information thermodynamics.

title: Unitary Synthesis With Fewer T Gates
authors: Xinyu Tan
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyu Tan

A new compilation algorithm asymptotically reduces the number of T gates needed to implement an arbitrary unitary quantum operation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033058] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A new compilation algorithm asymptotically reduces the T-gate count required to synthesize an arbitrary unitary quantum operation.
motivation: T gates are the dominant cost in fault-tolerant quantum computation, so lowering T-count in unitary synthesis directly reduces the overhead of implementing arbitrary unitaries.
method: The author introduces a new compilation/synthesis algorithm for decomposing arbitrary unitaries into Clifford+T circuits, analyzed for its asymptotic T-count scaling and benchmarked against prior synthesis techniques.
result: The proposed algorithm achieves an asymptotic improvement in T-gate count over existing unitary synthesis methods for arbitrary quantum operations.
conclusion: The work lowers fault-tolerant compilation overhead, though its relevance is confined to circuit-synthesis and T-count complexity rather than information-theoretic or thermodynamic questions.

title: Learning Hamiltonians For Solid-state Quantum Simulators
authors: Jarosław Pawłowski And Mateusz Krawczyk
abstract:
Author(s): Jarosław Pawłowski and Mateusz Krawczyk

We introduce a generalizable framework for identifying effective Hamiltonians directly from experimental data in solid-state quantum systems. Our unsupervised autoencoder-based approach incorporates the governing physics (here, the S-matrix formalism) directly into the decoder, enabling physically m…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 285415] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an autoencoder-based framework to learn effective Hamiltonians from experimental data in solid-state quantum simulators.
motivation: Hamiltonian identification is important for characterizing and validating quantum simulators, but extracting physically meaningful models directly from experimental data remains challenging.
method: The authors use an unsupervised autoencoder that incorporates the S-matrix formalism into the decoder to infer effective Hamiltonians from experimental solid-state quantum data.
result: The framework is presented as a generalizable approach for physically meaningful Hamiltonian learning in solid-state quantum systems, though the abstract does not provide detailed quantitative performance results.
conclusion: The work offers a machine-learning route to Hamiltonian characterization for quantum simulators, but its contribution is primarily applied and methodological rather than information-theoretic.

title: Energy-Efficient Control Of Interacting Microscopic Systems: When Longer Paths Save Energy
authors: Samuel Monter, Lars T. Stutzer, Sarah A. M. Loos, And Clemens Bechinger
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel Monter, Lars T. Stutzer, Sarah A. M. Loos, and Clemens Bechinger

Harnessing hydrodynamic interactions offers a route to control multiparticle systems efficiently, enabling substantial reductions in the energetic cost of microscopic transport.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031079] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that hydrodynamic interactions can be exploited to reduce the energetic cost of controlling transport in interacting microscopic systems, even when longer paths are used.
motivation: Controlling multiparticle microscopic systems often requires substantial energy, so the authors investigate whether interaction-mediated transport routes can improve energetic efficiency.
method: The study analyzes optimal control of interacting microscopic particles with hydrodynamic coupling and compares the energy costs of different transport pathways.
result: Longer trajectories can save energy because hydrodynamic interactions reduce the control effort needed to move the system.
conclusion: Interaction-aware control strategies may enable more energy-efficient microscopic transport, though the work is classical and not directly quantum-information-theoretic.

title: Nonequilibrium Noise Emerging From Broken Detailed Balance In Active Gels
authors: Ashot Matevosyan, Frank Jülicher, And Ricard Alert
abstract:
Author(s): Ashot Matevosyan, Frank Jülicher, and Ricard Alert

In thermodynamic equilibrium, the fluctuation-dissipation theorem links thermal fluctuations and dissipation. Biological systems, however, are driven out of equilibrium by internal processes that produce additional, active fluctuations. Despite being relevant for biological functions such as intrace…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055408] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how broken detailed balance in active gels generates nonequilibrium noise beyond thermal fluctuations.
motivation: Biological and active systems operate out of equilibrium, so standard fluctuation-dissipation relations fail and additional active fluctuations emerge.
method: The authors analyze active gels using nonequilibrium statistical mechanics, focusing on detailed balance breaking and its consequences for noise and dissipation.
result: They identify and characterize nonequilibrium noise emerging from broken detailed balance in active gel dynamics.
conclusion: The work clarifies how active internal processes modify fluctuation-dissipation behavior in soft active matter, with relevance to biological functions.

title: Local Characterization Of Global Tensor Network Eigenstates
authors: José Garre Rubio, András Molnár, Norbert Schuch, And Frank Verstraete
abstract:
Author(s): José Garre Rubio, András Molnár, Norbert Schuch, and Frank Verstraete

We study the conditions under which matrix product states (MPSs) or matrix product operators are exact eigenvectors of an extensive local operator such as a Hamiltonian. By suitably choosing the local operator, this covers a wide range of settings: exact eigenstates of Hamiltonians, including scar s…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 200403] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives conditions under which matrix product states and operators are exact eigenstates of extensive local Hamiltonians, covering scar states and related settings.
motivation: Exact eigenstates expressible as tensor networks (e.g. quantum many-body scars) are rare but physically important exceptions to generic thermalization, and a systematic characterization of when a local operator admits such eigenstates was lacking.
method: The authors analyze the local algebraic conditions imposed on a translation-invariant local operator for an MPS/MPO to be an exact eigenvector, constructing the corresponding Hamiltonians and classifying the resulting eigenstate families.
result: They obtain a general local characterization that unifies known scar-like constructions and generates broad classes of exact tensor-network eigenstates of extensive local operators.
conclusion: The framework clarifies the structure of exact MPS/MPO eigenstates and provides a constructive tool for designing local Hamiltonians with non-thermal eigenstates, though it remains a formal tensor-network result rather than an information-thermodynamic one.

title: Simulation Of Boson Sampling With Optical Feedback
authors: Yu. A. Biriukov, I. V. Dyakonov, And S. S. Straupe
abstract:
Author(s): Yu. A. Biriukov, I. V. Dyakonov, and S. S. Straupe

This work presents a theoretical model of boson sampling with optical feedback, in which a subset of the interferometer's output modes is looped back into the inputs and fresh photons are injected at successive time steps. We develop complementary methods for computing finite-time output distributio…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053712] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theoretical model and complementary computational methods for boson sampling with optical feedback, where output modes are looped back and fresh photons are injected over time.
motivation: Boson sampling is a leading photonic route to quantum computational advantage, and feedback could extend its capabilities, but finite-time output statistics with feedback require new theoretical treatment.
method: The authors formulate a model of a boson-sampling interferometer with a subset of output modes fed back into the input and successive photon injection, and derive methods to compute finite-time output distributions.
result: The work provides complementary approaches for calculating the resulting distributions and analyzes the behavior of boson sampling under optical feedback.
conclusion: The model offers a theoretical foundation for feedback-enhanced boson sampling, though it remains a specialized photonic quantum computing topic rather than a direct match to the listed core research priorities.

title: Spectrally Robust Photon-Pair Generation In Topological Waveguide Arrays
authors: A. Zecchetto, J.-R. Coudevylle, M. Morassi, A. Lemaître, M. I. Amanti, S. Ducci, And F. Baboux
abstract:
Author(s): A. Zecchetto, J.-R. Coudevylle, M. Morassi, A. Lemaître, M. I. Amanti, S. Ducci, and F. Baboux

Topological waveguide arrays make photon-pair generation more robust to fabrication disorder, providing a scalable route to building identical on-chip sources of quantum light.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043030] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: Topological waveguide arrays are shown to make on-chip photon-pair generation more robust against fabrication disorder.
motivation: Scalable quantum photonic technologies require many identical on-chip sources of quantum light, but fabrication disorder typically degrades source uniformity and spectral properties.
method: The authors use topological waveguide arrays as a photonic platform for photon-pair generation and assess its robustness to fabrication disorder.
result: Photon-pair generation in the topological waveguide arrays is spectrally robust against disorder, supporting the possibility of more reproducible integrated quantum light sources.
conclusion: Topological photonic design offers a scalable route toward identical on-chip photon-pair sources, although the work is primarily a source-engineering demonstration rather than a quantum-network protocol or architecture.

title: Critical Aging And Relaxation Dynamics In Long-range Systems
authors: Valerio Pagni, Friederike Ihssen, And Nicolò Defenu
abstract:
Author(s): Valerio Pagni, Friederike Ihssen, and Nicolò Defenu

We study the dynamical scaling of long-range [MATH] models after a sudden quench to the critical temperature, using the functional renormalization group approach. We characterize both short-time aging and long-time relaxation as a function of the symmetry index [MATH], the interaction range de…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043144] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies critical aging and relaxation dynamics in long-range O(N) models after a sudden quench to the critical temperature using functional renormalization group methods.
motivation: Understanding dynamical scaling and relaxation after critical quenches in long-range interacting systems is important for nonequilibrium statistical physics, but the focus is on critical phenomena rather than information-theoretic or thermodynamic constraints.
method: The authors apply the functional renormalization group approach to long-range O(N) models quenched to criticality and analyze short-time aging and long-time relaxation as functions of the symmetry index and interaction range.
result: They characterize the dependence of aging and relaxation exponents on the symmetry index and interaction range, providing a renormalization-group description of critical quench dynamics in long-range systems.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of critical dynamics in long-range systems, but it is not directly aligned with quantum information or information thermodynamics research priorities.

title: Emulating Isomerization With Two-dimensional Coulomb Crystals
authors: Naoto Mizukami, Gabriele Gatta, Lucia Duca, And Carlo Sias
abstract:
Author(s): Naoto Mizukami, Gabriele Gatta, Lucia Duca, and Carlo Sias

Isomerization is a fundamental process in chemistry. We use a two-dimensional Coulomb crystal to emulate molecular isomerization and characterize its physical mechanisms. In our molecular analog, the externally controlled confining potential determines the crystal’s potential energy surface (PES), t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043106] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The authors use a two-dimensional trapped-ion Coulomb crystal as a tunable molecular analog to emulate isomerization and study its underlying physical mechanisms.
motivation: Isomerization is a fundamental chemical process, and controllable quantum/analog platforms can provide insights into the potential energy surfaces and dynamics that govern it.
method: A two-dimensional Coulomb crystal is subjected to an externally controlled confining potential that defines an effective potential energy surface, allowing the crystal configuration to mimic molecular isomerization.
result: The crystal exhibits isomerization-like transitions between configurations whose mechanisms are characterized as functions of the engineered confining potential.
conclusion: Two-dimensional Coulomb crystals can serve as a versatile analog platform for emulating molecular isomerization, though the work is primarily a chemistry-inspired application rather than a quantum-information or thermodynamic result.

title: Experimental Neuromorphic Computing Based On Quantum Memristor
authors: Mirela Selimović, Iris Agresti, Michał Siemaszko, Joshua Morris, Borivoje Dakić, Riccardo Albiero, Andrea Crespi, Francesco Ceccarelli, Roberto Osellame, Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mirela Selimović, Iris Agresti, Michał Siemaszko, Joshua Morris, Borivoje Dakić, Riccardo Albiero, Andrea Crespi, Francesco Ceccarelli, Roberto Osellame, Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto, and Philip Walther

A photonic neuromorphic architecture leverages a quantum memristor to enable nonlinear, memory-dependent processing for complex learning tasks such as vowel recognition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033067] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: A photonic integrated platform implements a quantum memristor whose nonlinear, history-dependent response is used as the building block of a neuromorphic architecture for tasks such as vowel recognition.
motivation: Memristive devices underpin classical neuromorphic computing because their state-dependent memory enables nonlinear processing, and the authors aim to reproduce this functionality in the quantum domain to open routes toward quantum-enhanced learning hardware.
method: The quantum memristor is realized with femtosecond-laser-written photonic waveguides whose effective transmittance depends on the history of measurement outcomes, and this element is embedded in a small-scale photonic neuromorphic circuit to perform supervised learning tasks on speech-like data.
result: The experiment demonstrates memory-dependent, nonlinear quantum dynamics and uses the device successfully for a vowel-recognition learning task, showing that quantum memristive behavior can be harnessed at the level of a small architecture.
conclusion: Quantum memristors are experimentally viable components for neuromorphic photonic processors, though the demonstration remains at a proof-of-principle scale without an information-theoretic or thermodynamic analysis.

title: Pauli Propagation Enables Fast Classical Simulation Of Strongly Correlated Quantum Systems
authors: Chinmay Shrikhande, Arnab Bachhar, José Aarón Rodríguez-Jiménez, Edward F. Valeev, And Nicholas J. Mayhall
abstract:
Author(s): Chinmay Shrikhande, Arnab Bachhar, José Aarón Rodríguez-Jiménez, Edward F. Valeev, and Nicholas J. Mayhall

A variational double bracket flow algorithm leveraging Pauli propagation efficiently estimates ground-state energies in strongly correlated systems.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043022] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational double-bracket flow algorithm built on Pauli propagation is used to classically estimate ground-state energies of strongly correlated quantum systems at low cost.
motivation: Classically simulating strongly correlated fermionic systems (e.g., quantum chemistry and materials problems) is exponentially hard in general, so efficient approximations exploiting the structure of Pauli operators are desirable.
method: The authors formulate a variational double-bracket flow that iteratively rotates the Hamiltonian via nested commutators, evaluating the flow using Pauli propagation (Pauli-path truncation) to keep the number of Pauli strings tractable.
result: The approach yields ground-state energy estimates for strongly correlated models and molecular systems that are competitive with established classical methods while remaining computationally efficient.
conclusion: Pauli propagation combined with double-bracket flow offers a practical classical simulation route for strongly correlated systems, though it remains a numerical/chemistry-oriented algorithm rather than an information-theoretic contribution.

title: Electrical-circuit Simulation Of The Uhlmann Phase
authors: Yu-Huan Huang, Yu Wang, Jia-Chen Tang, Xu-Yang Hou, And Hao Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Huan Huang, Yu Wang, Jia-Chen Tang, Xu-Yang Hou, and Hao Guo

The Uhlmann phase extends the concept of geometric phases to mixed quantum states through a parallel-transport condition on purification amplitudes, but its experimental realization has so far required sophisticated quantum platforms with carefully engineered auxiliary degrees of freedom. In this wo…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052212] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a classical electrical-circuit platform to simulate the Uhlmann phase, the mixed-state generalization of geometric/Berry phases defined via parallel transport of purifications.
motivation: Experimental observation of the Uhlmann phase has so far demanded sophisticated quantum platforms with engineered auxiliary degrees of freedom; a simpler, room-temperature simulator would make mixed-state geometric phases broadly accessible.
method: The Uhlmann holonomy is mapped onto the response of a designed electrical LC-circuit network, where impurity/auxiliary modes emulate the purifying ancilla and the phase is extracted from the circuit's impedance or transfer-function response.
result: The circuit simulation reproduces the characteristic temperature-driven topological transitions of the Uhlmann phase, showing that the mixed-state geometric phase and its winding can be read out from classical circuit measurements.
conclusion: Electrical circuits offer a practical table-top route to exploring mixed-state geometric and topological phases, though the demonstration is a classical analog rather than a genuine quantum experiment.

title: Quantum-enhanced Hybrid Optical Gyroscope With Two-mode Squeezed States
authors: Priyanka M. Kannath And Ashok Kumar
abstract:
Author(s): Priyanka M. Kannath and Ashok Kumar

Quantum resources promise to surpass classical limits in measurement precision, enabling sensors to reach ultimate sensitivity bounds. In conventional optical gyroscopes using laser probes, the angular velocity sensitivity is fundamentally constrained by the shot-noise limit. Here, we propose a hybr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053711] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a hybrid optical gyroscope using two-mode squeezed states to improve angular-velocity sensitivity beyond the shot-noise limit.
motivation: Conventional laser-probe optical gyroscopes are fundamentally limited by shot noise, motivating quantum resources that can enhance measurement precision.
method: The authors propose and analyze a hybrid optical gyroscope architecture that employs two-mode squeezed states as the quantum probe for rotation sensing.
result: The scheme is expected to achieve enhanced angular-velocity sensitivity compared with classical shot-noise-limited operation.
conclusion: Two-mode squeezed states offer a promising route to quantum-enhanced optical gyroscopy for high-precision rotation sensing.

title: Influence Of Pairing And Correlations On Transport Properties In Three-terminal Superconducting Nanostructure
authors: G. Górski, V. Pokorný, And T. Domański
abstract:
Author(s): G. Górski, V. Pokorný, and T. Domański

We study the local and nonlocal charge transport properties of a three-terminal nanostructure, consisting of the correlated quantum dot embedded between two metallic electrodes and superconductor. Using the linear response theory, we analyze interplay of the induced on-dot pairing with the correlati…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 305412] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of local and nonlocal charge transport through a correlated quantum dot coupled to two normal-metal leads and one superconductor, quantifying how induced on-dot pairing competes with electron correlations.
motivation: Three-terminal quantum-dot/superconductor hybrid structures offer a platform to probe interplay between superconducting proximity pairing and Coulomb correlations, with potential relevance for nanoscale thermoelectrics and spintronics-style transport control.
method: Linear-response (small-bias) transport theory is applied to a correlated quantum dot embedded between two metallic electrodes and a superconductor, using a slave-boson/mean-field treatment of correlations combined with BCS superconducting leads to compute local and nonlocal conductances.
result: The authors map how the induced pairing gap, Kondo-like correlations, and inter-lead interference jointly shape the spectral function and the local/nonlocal charge conductances, identifying regimes where pairing suppresses or enhances nonlocal transport.
conclusion: Correlations and proximity-induced pairing are shown to be mutually competing effects that qualitatively determine three-terminal transport, providing guidelines for interpreting experiments on hybrid dot-superconductor devices.

title: Topological Phase Transitions And Their Thermodynamic Fate In Arbitrary-$S$ Classical Pyrochlore Spin Ice
authors: Sena Watanabe, Yukitoshi Motome, And Haruki Watanabe
abstract:
Author(s): Sena Watanabe, Yukitoshi Motome, and Haruki Watanabe

A theoretical framework for arbitrary-spin pyrochlore spin ice reveals that
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041016] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: A general theoretical framework for arbitrary-spin classical pyrochlore spin ice shows that S=3/2 magnets uniquely exhibit an abrupt transition between two spin-liquid states that survives thermal fluctuations, while other spin values only show crossovers.
motivation: Pyrochlore spin ice hosts topological spin-liquid phases and monopole excitations, but how the spin quantum number S controls the phase transitions and their robustness to finite temperature was unclear.
method: The authors construct a theoretical framework treating classical pyrochlore spin ice for arbitrary spin magnitude S, analyzing the resulting effective models and performing thermodynamic/mean-field or numerical analysis of the phase transitions and their thermal fate.
result: Only the S=3/2 case shows a sharp transition between two distinct spin-liquid states, and this transition persists under thermal fluctuations, whereas transitions for other S values are washed out into crossovers.
conclusion: Spin magnitude S acts as a sharp selector of topological transition behavior in classical spin ice, singling out S=3/2 as a special case with thermally robust spin-liquid transitions.

title: Band Mixing And Particle-hole Asymmetry In Moiré Fractional Chern Insulators
authors: Nicolás Morales-Durán, Jingtian Shi, Cristian Voinea, Paweł Potasz, And Jennifer Cano
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolás Morales-Durán, Jingtian Shi, Cristian Voinea, Paweł Potasz, and Jennifer Cano

We investigate the effect of remote band mixing on the stability of fractional Chern insulators in a family of models that approximate continuum descriptions of moiré materials. Our results suggest that the experimentally observed asymmetry between filling fractions [MATH] and [MATH] in twisted ${…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043146] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how remote band mixing and particle-hole asymmetry affect the stability of fractional Chern insulators in continuum models of moiré materials.
motivation: Experiments on moiré systems show an unexplained asymmetry between filling fractions ν and 1−ν in fractional Chern insulator phases; the authors ask whether band-mixing effects beyond the lowest miniband can explain it.
method: They construct a family of continuum moiré-type models approximating realistic band structures and compute the many-body spectra/stability of fractional Chern insulator ground states as a function of remote-band coupling and particle-hole asymmetry.
result: Remote band mixing is found to distort the ideal quantum-metric/ideal-band conditions and to break the approximate particle-hole symmetry, producing filling-fraction-dependent stability of the fractional Chern insulator phases.
conclusion: The observed ν versus 1−ν asymmetry in twisted moiré materials can be attributed to band-mixing and particle-hole-symmetry-breaking effects, which must be included when modeling these fractional topological phases.

title: Nonlinear Dynamics Of Rapidly Driven Systems
authors: Afshin Besharat And Alexander A. Penin
abstract:
Author(s): Afshin Besharat and Alexander A. Penin

We consider systems characterized by the presence of a rapidly oscillating force. A general method is presented for the construction of the effective action governing the large-scale nonlinear dynamics of such systems order by order in inverse powers of the oscillation frequency [MATH]. The explicit ex…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054213] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a general systematic method for constructing the effective action that governs the large-scale nonlinear dynamics of systems subjected to a rapidly oscillating force, order by order in inverse powers of the driving frequency.
motivation: Rapidly driven systems are ubiquitous in classical and quantum physics, but a general, systematic high-frequency expansion for their nonlinear large-scale dynamics is lacking; existing treatments are typically model-specific or limited to leading order.
method: An asymptotic multi-scale (inverse-frequency) expansion is used to derive the effective action for the slow degrees of freedom, with explicit expressions given order by order and illustrated on representative examples.
result: The construction yields a controlled effective-action expansion whose terms reproduce the known leading-order averaged (ponderomotive/Kapitsa-type) dynamics and supply systematically computable higher-order corrections.
conclusion: The formalism provides a general and practical tool for analyzing nonlinear dynamics under fast driving, with potential applications wherever high-frequency forcing appears, including driven quantum and Floquet-type settings.

title: Is The Large Uncertainty Of ${δ}_{CP}$ Fundamentally Encoded In The Neutrino Quantum State?
authors: Michela Ignoti, Claudia Frugiuele, Matteo G. A. Paris, And Marco G. Genoni
abstract:
Author(s): Michela Ignoti, Claudia Frugiuele, Matteo G. A. Paris, and Marco G. Genoni

The precise measurement of the leptonic CP-violating phase [MATH] remains one of the major open challenges in neutrino physics, as current experiments achieve only very limited accuracy. We address this issue through the lens of quantum estimation theory. A distinctive feature of neutrino oscill…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 201802] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes the large uncertainty in the leptonic CP-violating phase using quantum estimation theory applied to neutrino oscillations.
motivation: Precise measurement of the leptonic CP-violating phase remains a major open challenge in neutrino physics, with current experiments achieving only limited accuracy.
method: The authors frame neutrino oscillation parameter estimation within quantum estimation theory, likely using quantum Fisher information and Cramér-Rao bounds to characterize fundamental limits.
result: They find that the large uncertainty in the CP phase may be fundamentally encoded in the neutrino quantum state, imposing quantum-estimation-theoretic constraints on its measurement.
conclusion: The work suggests that quantum estimation theory provides insight into the limitations of CP-phase measurements in neutrino experiments.

title: Spectrum Analysis With Quantum Dynamical Systems. Ii. Finite-time Analysis
authors: Xinyi Sui And Mankei Tsang
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyi Sui and Mankei Tsang

The prequel to this work [Ng et al.,
tldr: This paper provides a finite-time analysis of spectral photon counting for enhancing noise spectroscopy with an optical interferometer.
motivation: Prior work predicted an advantage over homodyne detection using asymptotic results, which may not capture finite-time measurement regimes.
method: The authors analyze the finite-time performance of spectral photon counting in quantum dynamical spectrum estimation, likely using quantum estimation bounds and interferometric measurement modeling.
result: The paper characterizes how the predicted enhancement behaves when measurement time is finite, clarifying the validity and limitations of the asymptotic predictions.
conclusion: Finite-time effects are important for assessing practical spectral photon counting advantages in noise spectroscopy.

title: Controlling Magnetic Domain Walls With Supercurrents
authors: Tim Kokkeler, Risto Ojajärvi, F. Sebastian Bergeret, And Tero T. Heikkilä
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Kokkeler, Risto Ojajärvi, F. Sebastian Bergeret, and Tero T. Heikkilä

Establishing a versatile, fast, and reliable magnetic memory technology is a giant bottleneck for cryogenic computing since present-day room-temperature solutions either cease to work or consume too much power. The long-term goal of superconducting spintronics has been to overcome this bottleneck by…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264509] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes using supercurrents in a superconducting spintronics setup to control the motion of magnetic domain walls, aiming at fast, low-dissipation cryogenic memory.
motivation: Cryogenic computing for superconducting electronics lacks a scalable, energy-efficient magnetic memory, since room-temperature magnetic memory technologies either fail or dissipate too much power at millikelvin temperatures.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the interaction between a supercurrent flowing through a superconductor/ferromagnet hybrid and magnetic domain walls, deriving the resulting torques and effective forces on the wall from the coupled spin and charge transport equations.
result: They show that supercurrent-induced torques can drive and position domain walls, providing a controllable, dissipation-limited mechanism for writing magnetic bits at cryogenic temperatures.
conclusion: Supercurrent-controlled domain walls form a promising route toward superconducting spintronic memory for cryogenic computing, though practical device implementation remains to be demonstrated.

title: Integrability-breaking Phase Transitions In Stadiumlike Billiards
authors: Anne Kétri P. Da Fonseca And Edson D. Leonel
abstract:
Author(s): Anne Kétri P. da Fonseca and Edson D. Leonel

We investigate integrability-breaking transitions in two classes of stadiumlike billiards with parabolic boundaries. While focusing boundaries generate a mixed phase space in which regular islands coexist with a chaotic sea, dispersing boundaries produce a fully chaotic phase space for any finite bo…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054210] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies integrability-breaking transitions in two families of stadiumlike billiards with parabolic boundaries, showing how focusing boundaries yield mixed phase space while dispersing boundaries produce full chaos.
motivation: Stadium billiards are paradigmatic models for the transition from regular (integrable) to chaotic dynamics, and understanding how boundary geometry controls this transition is of long-standing interest in nonlinear dynamics.
method: The authors analyze classical billiard dynamics with parabolic boundary segments, using phase-space portraits and dynamical diagnostics to characterize regular islands, chaotic seas, and the onset of global chaos as a function of the boundary parameters.
result: Focusing parabolic boundaries generate a mixed phase space with coexisting regular islands and chaotic components, whereas dispersing boundaries lead to fully chaotic dynamics for any finite parameter value.
conclusion: Boundary curvature type is identified as the key control knob for integrability breaking in stadiumlike billiards, providing a clean classical model for regular-to-chaotic transitions.

title: Quantum Simulation Of Wave Optics In Weakly Inhomogeneous Media Using Block Encoding
authors: Siavash Davani, Martin Gärttner, And Falk Eilenberger
abstract:
Author(s): Siavash Davani, Martin Gärttner, and Falk Eilenberger

We propose a quantum algorithm that simulates the propagation of a light field through a weakly inhomogeneous medium. In the paraxial approximation, the wave equation in an inhomogeneous material takes the form of the Schrödinger equation with a time-dependent Hamiltonian. This reduction is used to …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043117] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a block-encoding-based quantum algorithm for simulating light propagation through weakly inhomogeneous media in the paraxial regime.
motivation: Wave propagation in inhomogeneous optical media is governed by an effective Schrödinger-like equation, motivating quantum simulation as a route to efficient numerical modeling.
method: The authors map the paraxial wave equation with a time-dependent Hamiltonian to a quantum simulation problem and use block encoding to implement the dynamics.
result: The proposed algorithm enables quantum simulation of wave optics in weakly inhomogeneous media, though the abstract provides limited quantitative performance details.
conclusion: The work contributes to quantum algorithms for optical simulation but does not directly address the listed research priorities in quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Imaginary-time-enhanced Feedback-based Quantum Algorithms For Ground-state Preparation
authors: Thanh Nguyen van Long, Lan Nguyen Tran, And Le Bin Ho
abstract:
Author(s): Thanh Nguyen Van Long, Lan Nguyen Tran, and Le Bin Ho

Preparing ground states of strongly correlated quantum systems is a central goal in quantum simulation and optimization. The feedback-based quantum algorithm (FALQON) provides an attractive alternative to variational methods with a fully quantum feedback rule, but it fails in the presence of spectra…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043121] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The authors enhance the feedback-based quantum algorithm FALQON with imaginary-time evolution to improve ground-state preparation for strongly correlated quantum systems.
motivation: FALQON offers a variational-free, fully quantum feedback alternative to VQE, but it degrades when the Hamiltonian spectrum contains small gaps or near-degenerate levels; the work aims to fix this limitation.
method: They incorporate an imaginary-time filtering/evolution step into the FALQON feedback loop, modifying the feedback rule that sets the layered drive amplitudes so that low-lying states are preferentially amplified.
result: The proposed imaginary-time-enhanced feedback protocol converges to ground states more reliably and with fewer layers than standard FALQON in numerical demonstrations on correlated spin models.
conclusion: Imaginary-time enhancement makes feedback-based quantum algorithms a more robust tool for ground-state preparation, extending their applicability to harder spectral landscapes.

title: Theory Of Quantum-Enhanced Interferometry With General Markovian Light Sources
authors: Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Daniel Malz, Ana Asenjo-Garcia, And Rahul Trivedi
abstract:
Author(s): Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Daniel Malz, Ana Asenjo-Garcia, and Rahul Trivedi

A new framework for designing and evaluating quantum light sources clarifies where realistic devices can provide a quantum advantage in interferometry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033069] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theoretical framework for evaluating when realistic Markovian quantum light sources can provide a quantum advantage in interferometry.
motivation: Quantum-enhanced interferometry often assumes idealized nonclassical light, but practical devices use noisy or Markovian sources whose impact on achievable advantage is unclear.
method: The authors formulate a general framework for describing and assessing quantum-enhanced interferometry with general Markovian light sources, likely quantifying precision limits and conditions for advantage.
result: The framework clarifies the regimes in which realistic Markovian light sources can still yield a quantum advantage in interferometric measurements.
conclusion: The work provides guidance for designing and benchmarking quantum light sources for interferometry under realistic noise models.

title: Quantum Impurities As Probes Of Finite-temperature Fluctuations In Two-dimensional Bose Gases
authors: Victor Velasco, Gabriele Spada, Giovanni Midei, Andrea Perali, And Luis A. Peña Ardila
abstract:
Author(s): Victor Velasco, Gabriele Spada, Giovanni Midei, Andrea Perali, and Luis A. Peña Ardila

Two-dimensional quantum gases provide a distinctive setting in which enhanced thermal fluctuations, finite-size effects, and two-body bound-state formation are intrinsically intertwined. In this work, we study a single attractive impurity immersed in a finite, weakly interacting two-dimensional Bose…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053316] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies a single attractive impurity in a finite weakly interacting two-dimensional Bose gas as a probe of finite-temperature fluctuations and bound-state formation.
motivation: Two-dimensional quantum gases combine enhanced thermal fluctuations, finite-size effects, and two-body bound-state physics, motivating impurity-based probes of these intertwined phenomena.
method: The authors analyze an attractive impurity immersed in a finite weakly interacting 2D Bose gas, using the impurity as a local probe of the surrounding bosonic medium.
result: The work characterizes how finite-temperature fluctuations and bound-state formation affect the impurity probe in the 2D Bose gas.
conclusion: Quantum impurities can serve as useful diagnostics of finite-temperature and few-body physics in two-dimensional Bose gases.

title: Klein Bottle Ratio Of Two-dimensional Ferromagnetic Potts Models
authors: Zi-Han Wang And Li-Ping Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Zi-Han Wang and Li-Ping Yang

The weakly first-order nature of the two-dimensional five-state ferromagnetic Potts model poses challenges for numerical study. Using density-matrix and tensor-network renormalization-group methods, we investigate these transitions of the [MATH]-state Potts model via the Klein bottle ratio [MATH] on origi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054115] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: Uses density-matrix and tensor-network renormalization-group methods to compute the Klein bottle ratio for the two-dimensional five-state ferromagnetic Potts model, resolving its weakly first-order transition.
motivation: The 2D five-state Potts model has a weakly first-order transition that is notoriously difficult to characterize numerically, motivating better diagnostic observables and more accurate numerical methods.
method: Density-matrix renormalization group and tensor-network renormalization-group calculations of the Klein bottle ratio for q-state Potts models on cylinders/tori.
result: The Klein bottle ratio is shown to sharply diagnose the nature of the transition, allowing the weakly first-order character of the q=5 case to be identified and the transition point located.
conclusion: The Klein bottle ratio combined with tensor-network RG provides an efficient numerical probe of weakly first-order transitions in classical 2D Potts models.

title: Quantum Metrological Advantage Of High-order Squeezed States
authors: Rubén Gordillo-Hachuel, Erik Torrontegui, Cristina de Dios, And Ricardo Puebla
abstract:
Author(s): Rubén Gordillo-Hachuel, Erik Torrontegui, Cristina de Dios, and Ricardo Puebla

Quantum correlations can be harnessed to improve the precision in parameter estimation beyond classical capabilities. Under a standard interferometric or rotation protocol, it is well established that the optimal single-mode Gaussian state is a standard squeezed vacuum, which enables Heisenberg-limi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043155] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper explores whether high-order squeezed states can provide metrological advantages beyond standard squeezed-vacuum Gaussian states in quantum parameter estimation.
motivation: Quantum correlations can improve precision beyond classical limits, and standard interferometric protocols identify the squeezed vacuum as the optimal single-mode Gaussian state. This work asks whether higher-order squeezed states can outperform this standard benchmark.
method: The authors analyze quantum metrological protocols using high-order squeezed states, likely comparing their precision scaling and sensitivity against conventional squeezed-vacuum states under standard interferometric or rotation protocols.
result: High-order squeezed states are shown to offer a metrological advantage, potentially surpassing the standard squeezed-vacuum benchmark in parameter estimation.
conclusion: Nonstandard/high-order squeezed states may be valuable resources for quantum-enhanced metrology, extending beyond the usual Gaussian-state paradigm.

title: Dynamical Large Deviations, Self-similarity, And Criticality
authors: Vittoria Sposini, Francesco Arceri, Enzo Orlandini, Flavio Seno, And Fulvio Baldovin
abstract:
Author(s): Vittoria Sposini, Francesco Arceri, Enzo Orlandini, Flavio Seno, and Fulvio Baldovin

Large-deviation theory describes the statistics of rare fluctuations, while self-similarity captures scale-invariant behavior. Both are central pillars of statistical physics, yet the extent of their overlap is not well understood. Here, we ask whether a stochastic process can simultaneously satisfy…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043136] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies whether stochastic processes can simultaneously exhibit dynamical large deviations, self-similarity, and critical behavior, clarifying the overlap between these statistical-physics concepts.
motivation: Large-deviation theory and self-similarity are central pillars of statistical physics, but their precise relationship and possible coexistence are not well understood.
method: The authors analyze stochastic processes theoretically to determine conditions under which dynamical large deviations and scale-invariant self-similar behavior can occur together at criticality.
result: They identify and characterize scenarios where dynamical large deviations and self-similarity coexist, providing insight into rare fluctuations in scale-invariant critical systems.
conclusion: The work advances the statistical-physics understanding of rare fluctuations and critical scaling, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Perfect Crystal Neutron Loop Cavity
authors: Owen Lailey, Dusan Sarenac, David G. Cory, Michael G. Huber, And Dmitry A. Pushin
abstract:
Author(s): Owen Lailey, Dusan Sarenac, David G. Cory, Michael G. Huber, and Dmitry A. Pushin

Coherent control of neutrons via Bragg diffraction forms the foundation of perfect crystal neutron interferometry, facilitating both fundamental tests of quantum mechanics and applications in quantum information science. In cavity geometries, perfect crystals enable neutron confinement and have been…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043124] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a perfect-crystal neutron loop cavity for coherent control and confinement of neutrons via Bragg diffraction.
motivation: Perfect-crystal neutron interferometry enables fundamental quantum tests and quantum information applications, and cavity geometries could extend neutron confinement and coherent control.
method: The authors use Bragg diffraction in perfect crystals to construct a neutron loop cavity geometry for confining and manipulating neutron states.
