result: The work establishes a neutron cavity platform based on perfect-crystal Bragg diffraction, enabling coherent neutron confinement in a loop geometry.
conclusion: Such neutron cavity technology may support fundamental tests of quantum mechanics and selected quantum information science applications.

title: Toward Complete Characterization Of Topological Insulators And Superconductors: A Systematic Construction Of Topological Invariants Based On Atiyah-Hirzebruch Spectral Sequence
authors: Seishiro Ono And Ken Shiozaki
abstract:
Author(s): Seishiro Ono and Ken Shiozaki

A framework based on the Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence in momentum space yields topological invariants that classify stable superconducting phases across 159 space groups.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041024] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a momentum-space Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence framework to systematically construct topological invariants classifying stable superconducting phases across all 159 space groups.
motivation: A complete and systematic characterization of topological insulators and superconductors in crystalline materials is needed, since existing classifications are fragmented across individual space groups and partial invariant constructions.
method: They apply the Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence in momentum space, deriving page-by-page differentials that yield explicit topological invariants for stable gapless and gapped superconducting phases organized by space group.
result: The construction produces a unified set of topological invariants covering 159 space groups, giving a systematic classification of stable superconducting phases and their obstruction structure.
conclusion: The spectral-sequence approach provides a complete and general algorithm for diagnosing topological crystalline phases, extending classification beyond case-by-case treatments.

title: Generalized Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon Hierarchy For Near-Integrable Dynamics
authors: Leonardo Biagetti, Maciej Łebek, Miłosz Panfil, And Jacopo de Nardis
abstract:
Author(s): Leonardo Biagetti, Maciej Łebek, Miłosz Panfil, and Jacopo De Nardis

The BBGKY hierarchy is generalized to systems with strong integrable contact interactions and generic long-range two-body ones, enabling the computation of experimentally measurable expectation values and correlations for classical and quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041021] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper generalizes the BBGKY hierarchy to near-integrable many-body systems with strong contact and long-range two-body interactions, enabling computation of measurable correlations in classical and quantum settings.
motivation: Near-integrable dynamics are challenging because standard kinetic hierarchies do not directly accommodate strong integrable interactions plus generic long-range couplings.
method: The authors extend the Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon hierarchy to systems with strong integrable contact interactions and generic long-range two-body interactions.
result: The generalized hierarchy provides a framework for computing experimentally measurable expectation values and correlation functions for both classical and quantum systems.
conclusion: This offers a formal many-body dynamics tool for near-integrable systems, though it is not directly focused on quantum information or information thermodynamics.

title: Landscape Of Scattering Universality With General Dispersion Relations
authors: Yidan Wang (王艺丹), Xuesen Na, Michael J. Gullans, Susanne F. Yelin, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Yidan Wang (王艺丹), Xuesen Na, Michael J. Gullans, Susanne F. Yelin, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

Universality in physics describes how disparate systems can exhibit identical low-energy behavior. Here, we reveal a rich landscape of new universal scattering phenomena governed by the interplay between an interaction and a system’s density of states. We investigate one-dimensional scattering with …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 203602] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper maps universal scattering phenomena in one-dimensional systems arising from the interplay between interactions and the density of states under general dispersion relations.
motivation: Universality explains why seemingly different physical systems share identical low-energy behavior; the authors aim to extend this concept to scattering by exploring how interaction and density-of-states properties produce new universal regimes.
method: The authors analyze one-dimensional scattering theoretically, considering general dispersion relations and characterizing how the interaction strength and density of states jointly determine scattering behavior.
result: They identify a landscape of universal scattering phenomena, revealing multiple regimes in which scattering properties become independent of microscopic details and are governed by the interaction–density-of-states interplay.
conclusion: The work broadens the scope of universality in scattering theory and may inform the understanding of low-energy dynamics in diverse one-dimensional quantum systems, but it does not directly address the researcher's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems interests.

title: Interferometric Readout Of Momentum-Space Topology In A Programmable Dissipative Photonic Circuit
authors: Andrea Cataldo, Emil J. Bergholtz, Daniel Leykam, Jun Gao, And Ali W. Elshaari
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Cataldo, Emil J. Bergholtz, Daniel Leykam, Jun Gao, and Ali W. Elshaari

A programmable photonic circuit uses unitary dilation and interferometry to directly measure momentum-space topological invariants in strongly dissipative non-Hermitian systems.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 206601] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: A programmable photonic circuit employing unitary dilation and interferometric readout directly measures momentum-space topological invariants of strongly dissipative non-Hermitian systems.
motivation: Topological invariants of non-Hermitian lattices are usually inferred indirectly from spectra or bulk-edge correspondence; direct experimental access to momentum-space topology is challenging, especially for strongly dissipative systems.
method: The authors embed the non-Hermitian system in a larger unitary network via unitary dilation and implement this on a programmable photonic interferometer, extracting the momentum-resolved eigenstate information needed to reconstruct the topological invariant.
result: The experiment recovers the momentum-space topological invariant of a dissipative non-Hermitian model, showing that interferometric measurement can track topology even where loss is dominant.
conclusion: Programmable photonic circuits provide a viable route to directly probe non-Hermitian topology, extending topological characterization to strongly dissipative regimes.

title: Unveiling High-Energy Ultrafast Responses Driven By Fermi-Level Gap Opening In Charge-Density Waves
authors: Qiong Wu, Tianchen Hu, Junhan Huang, Yongjie Liu, Fei Sun, Shuxiang Xu, Li Yue, Zijian Lin, Xinyu Zhou, Tao Dong, And Nan-Lin Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Qiong Wu, Tianchen Hu, Junhan Huang, Yongjie Liu, Fei Sun, Shuxiang Xu, Li Yue, Zijian Lin, Xinyu Zhou, Tao Dong, and Nan-Lin Wang

Ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy is indispensable for investigating interactions, collective excitations, and nonequilibrium dynamics in superconductors and correlated electron systems. However, how a small gap opening near the Fermi surface affects the spectral changes in the high-energy interband…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 206902] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: Ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy is used to show how a small gap opening at the Fermi level in charge-density-wave systems reshapes high-energy interband spectral responses.
motivation: Pump-probe spectroscopy is a key tool for probing nonequilibrium dynamics in superconductors and correlated electron systems, but how a small Fermi-surface gap propagates into high-energy interband spectral changes remained unclear.
method: Femtosecond pump-probe optical spectroscopy of charge-density-wave materials, analyzing transient reflectivity/spectral changes tied to the Fermi-level gap opening.
result: The measurements reveal that the small gap opening drives pronounced, previously unaccounted-for modifications of the high-energy interband response on ultrafast timescales.
conclusion: The work clarifies how low-energy gap physics couples to high-energy interband spectra, informing interpretation of nonequilibrium spectroscopy in correlated electron and CDW systems.

title: Bosonic Realization Of Resonant Universal Photon Blockade Via Pump-assisted Four-wave Mixing
authors: Hongyu Lin, Xiaoqian Wang, Feng Gao, Xiangyi Luo, And Zhihai Yao
abstract:
Author(s): Hongyu Lin, Xiaoqian Wang, Feng Gao, Xiangyi Luo, and Zhihai Yao

We investigate resonant universal photon blockade in a three-mode four-wave-mixing system. A coherent drive of complex amplitude [MATH] excites the target mode, while a nondegenerate parametric pump of complex amplitude [MATH] generates correlated photons in two auxiliary modes. The target two-photo…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053511] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies resonant universal photon blockade in a three-mode four-wave-mixing bosonic system driven by a coherent field and a nondegenerate parametric pump.
motivation: Photon blockade is a key quantum nonlinear-optics effect for generating nonclassical light and controlling photon-number statistics, and the authors aim to realize it in a tunable bosonic four-wave-mixing platform.
method: They analyze a three-mode bosonic model in which a coherent drive excites the target mode while a parametric pump generates correlated photons in two auxiliary modes, and they derive conditions for resonant universal photon blockade.
result: The scheme is predicted to achieve resonant universal photon blockade, suppressing unwanted photon-number states in the target mode through pump-assisted four-wave mixing.
conclusion: The work proposes a bosonic route to universal photon blockade, but it is a specialized quantum-optics proposal with no direct connection to the listed research directions.

title: Quantum Spin Singlet Ground State With Large Excitation Gap In The $S=\frac{3}{2}$ Quasi-one-dimensional Van Der Waals Materials $\mathrm{Mo}{X}_{3}(X=\mathrm{I},\mathrm{Br})$
authors: Jordan Teeter, Topojit Debnath, Harshil Goyal, Md. Sabbir Hossen Bijoy, Maedeh Taheri, Nicholas R. Sesing, Clayton Mantz, Josemaria Garcia, Mathew B. Stone, Colin Sarkis, Do Hoon Kiem, Sohee Kwon, Mina Yoon, Fariborz Kargar, Kirill Shtengel, Tina T. Salguero, Alexander A. Balandin, And Roger K. Lake
abstract:
Author(s): Jordan Teeter, Topojit Debnath, Harshil Goyal, Md. Sabbir Hossen Bijoy, Maedeh Taheri, Nicholas R. Sesing, Clayton Mantz, Josemaria Garcia, Mathew B. Stone, Colin Sarkis, Do Hoon Kiem, Sohee Kwon, Mina Yoon, Fariborz Kargar, Kirill Shtengel, Tina T. Salguero, Alexander A. Balandin, and Roger K. Lake

We report the first experimental evidence for a quantum-disordered spin-singlet ground state and gapped triplon excitations in quasi-one-dimensional van der Waals materials. The insulating van der Waals trihalides [MATH] and [MATH] are analyzed in a combined thermodynami…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264416] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: Combined thermodynamic and spectroscopic measurements plus first-principles calculations provide the first experimental evidence for a quantum-disordered spin-singlet ground state with a large triplon excitation gap in the quasi-one-dimensional van der Waals magnets MoI3 and MoBr3.
motivation: Quasi-one-dimensional van der Waals trihalides with S=3/2 spins are proposed platforms for exotic magnetism, but their ground state and low-energy excitation spectrum had not been established experimentally.
method: The authors synthesize MoI3 and MoBr3 and characterize them using thermodynamic measurements (magnetization, specific heat, susceptibility), spectroscopic probes, and density functional theory calculations of the magnetic exchange couplings.
result: No magnetic ordering is observed down to low temperature, while a spin gap consistent with a singlet ground state and gapped triplon excitations is identified, with the gap magnitude and exchange parameters supported by theory.
conclusion: MoX3 (X = I, Br) realize a quantum-disordered spin-singlet ground state in a quasi-1D van der Waals lattice, establishing a new materials family for studying gapped quantum magnetism.

title: Field-induced Anisotropic Magnetocaloric And Magnetotransport Responses In The Easy-plane Antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{DyAgSb}}_{2}$
authors: Zilu Xia, Haifeng Chen, Wenbin Shi, Zeyang Chen, Fanchen Chang, Wei Zhou, Yong Fang, Bin Qian, Jinlei Yao, Jingguo Hu, And Zhida Han
abstract:
Author(s): Zilu Xia, Haifeng Chen, Wenbin Shi, Zeyang Chen, Fanchen Chang, Wei Zhou, Yong Fang, Bin Qian, Jinlei Yao, Jingguo Hu, and Zhida Han

We report a systematic study of the anisotropic magnetic, magnetocaloric, and magnetotransport properties of [MATH] single crystals, which order antiferromagnetically and exhibit strong easy-plane anisotropy that constrains the Dy moments within the basal plane. Isothermal magnetiza…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274422] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: A systematic experimental study of the anisotropic magnetic, magnetocaloric, and magnetotransport properties of easy-plane antiferromagnetic DyAgSb2 single crystals.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize how strong easy-plane anisotropy in a Dy-based antiferromagnet governs its field-induced magnetic transitions, entropy changes, and transport response, which is relevant for magnetocaloric cooling applications.
method: Single crystals of DyAgSb2 were grown and probed via isothermal magnetization, heat capacity, and magnetotransport measurements as functions of temperature and magnetic field orientation.
result: The compound orders antiferromagnetically with Dy moments confined to the basal plane, producing strongly anisotropic magnetocaloric and magnetoresistance responses that depend on field direction relative to the easy plane.
conclusion: The observed anisotropic magnetocaloric and magnetotransport behavior is attributed to the easy-plane anisotropy and field-induced spin reorientation, indicating DyAgSb2 as a candidate material for anisotropic magnetocaloric applications.

title: Exact Dimer Ground States Of Long-range Spin Chains And Ladders
authors: Jędrzej Wardyn And Miłosz Panfil
abstract:
Author(s): Jędrzej Wardyn and Miłosz Panfil

This work establishes necessary conditions for the exact dimer ground states in a wide class of spin chain models with arbitrary long-range interactions. The stability of the dimer phase is also probed by introducing an anisotropy or dimerisation with the analytical findings supported by the numerical computations. The considered models encompass physical phenomena ranging from spin-Peierls materials to dimer state implementations in quantum information processing.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264414] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives necessary conditions for exact dimer ground states in long-range spin chains and ladders and studies their stability under anisotropy and dimerisation.
motivation: Exact dimer ground states are important in condensed-matter spin systems and are relevant to spin-Peierls materials and potential quantum-information implementations.
method: The authors analytically establish necessary conditions for exact dimer ground states in a broad class of long-range spin-chain models and support the analysis with numerical computations.
result: They identify conditions under which exact dimer ground states occur and probe the stability of the dimer phase by introducing anisotropy or dimerisation.
conclusion: The work characterizes exact dimer phases in long-range spin models, with implications for materials and quantum-information-motivated dimer-state implementations.

title: Uniaxial Stress Response Of Superconducting ${\mathrm{LaAlO}}_{3}/{\mathrm{SrTiO}}_{3}$ Nanowires
authors: Sayanwita Biswas, Xinyi Wu, Megan Briggeman, Joseph Albro, Kyoungjun Lee, Jianan Li, Chang-Beom Eom, Patrick Irvin, And Jeremy Levy
abstract:
Author(s): Sayanwita Biswas, Xinyi Wu, Megan Briggeman, Joseph Albro, Kyoungjun Lee, Jianan Li, Chang-Beom Eom, Patrick Irvin, and Jeremy Levy

We investigate how superconductivity in [MATH] nanowires responds to uniaxial stress. Nanowires written by conductive atomic force microscopy show nonhysteretic, piezoelectriclike responses that preserve their superconducting properties under moderate stress. Lar…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264510] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: Conductive-AFM-written LaAlO3/SrTiO3 nanowires retain superconductivity under moderate uniaxial stress while showing a nonhysteretic, piezoelectric-like response.
motivation: Oxide-interface superconductors at the LaAlO3/SrTiO3 interface are attractive for reconfigurable nanoscale devices, but how their superconducting properties respond to mechanical strain—relevant for strain-tunable device design—was unclear.
method: The authors pattern nanowires with conductive atomic force microscopy and measure their transport response to applied uniaxial stress, tracking superconducting transition behavior as a function of strain.
result: The nanowires exhibit a nonhysteretic, piezoelectric-like response and preserve superconductivity under moderate stress, indicating robustness of the superconducting state to strain.
conclusion: Strain is a viable, reversible tuning knob for LAO/STO nanowire superconductivity, supporting their use in mechanically reconfigurable oxide nanoelectronics.

title: Revisiting Spin Hamiltonian Parameters In A Kitaev Material Via Bayesian Optimization Of Magnetization Curves
authors: Takahiro Misawa, Ryo Tamura, Kazuyoshi Yoshimi, And Youhei Yamaji
abstract:
Author(s): Takahiro Misawa, Ryo Tamura, Kazuyoshi Yoshimi, and Youhei Yamaji

Determining the spin Hamiltonian of a magnetic compound is crucial for understanding its magnetic properties. A standard approach is to derive model parameters from ab initio calculations based on the crystal structure. However, the resulting Hamiltonian can depend sensitively on methodological deta…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274420] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The authors use Bayesian optimization to fit spin Hamiltonian parameters of a Kitaev magnetic material against measured magnetization curves, revisiting parameters previously obtained from ab initio calculations.
motivation: Deriving spin Hamiltonians from first-principles calculations is sensitive to methodological choices, so an empirical, data-driven route to constrain exchange and anisotropy parameters is desirable for magnetic compounds.
method: Magnetization curves of a Kitaev material are compared with model calculations, and Bayesian optimization is employed to efficiently search the spin-Hamiltonian parameter space and quantify parameter uncertainty.
result: The optimized parameters reproduce the observed magnetization behavior and are compared with ab initio-derived values, revealing discrepancies attributable to methodological sensitivity in the electronic-structure treatment.
conclusion: Bayesian optimization of magnetization data provides a practical complementary route to refining spin models of Kitaev materials, though the study remains a materials-modeling exercise rather than a quantum-information result.

title: Beyond The Lowest Landau Level: Unlocking More Robust Fractional States Using Flat Chern Bands With Higher Vortexability
authors: Yitong Zhang, Siddhartha Sarkar, Xiaohan Wan, Daniel E. Parker, Shi-Zeng Lin, And Kai Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Yitong Zhang, Siddhartha Sarkar, Xiaohan Wan, Daniel E. Parker, Shi-Zeng Lin, and Kai Sun

Enhancing the many-body gap of a fractional state is crucial for realizing robust fractional excitations. For fractional Chern insulators, existing studies suggest that making flat Chern bands closely resemble the lowest Landau level (LLL) seems to maximize the excitation gap, providing an apparentl…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 295111] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies flat Chern bands with higher vortexability to achieve more robust fractional Chern insulator states beyond the lowest-Landau-level paradigm.
motivation: Enhancing the many-body gap of fractional states is crucial for realizing robust fractional excitations, and existing wisdom suggests that flat Chern bands closely resembling the lowest Landau level maximize this gap.
method: The authors analyze flat Chern bands characterized by higher vortexability and compare their fractional-state stability against conventional lowest-Landau-level-like bands.
result: Bands with higher vortexability are shown to host fractional states with enhanced many-body gaps, challenging the idea that maximal LLL resemblance is optimal.
conclusion: The work provides design principles for fractional Chern insulators and suggests that higher vortexability can unlock more robust fractional phases beyond the lowest Landau level.

title: Random Theory For A Guiding Center Gas: Semiclassical Stochastic Dynamics In Phase Space And non-Hermitian Many-body Problem
authors: Hiroshi Kuratsuji, Satoshi Tsuchida, And Takahiro Uetoko
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroshi Kuratsuji, Satoshi Tsuchida, and Takahiro Uetoko

We study a random theory of semiclassical guiding center motion for a many-electron system in a strong magnetic field. We consider the many-body aspect of an assembly of guiding center coordinates, which we call a “guiding center gas”, that characterize the lowest Landau level. This system is descri…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054123] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a random semiclassical theory for a many-electron guiding-center gas in a strong magnetic field, including phase-space stochastic dynamics and a non-Hermitian many-body formulation.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize many-body dynamics of guiding-center coordinates in the lowest Landau level using stochastic semiclassical methods.
method: They formulate a random theory of semiclassical guiding-center motion, treating the assembly as a guiding-center gas and analyzing stochastic dynamics in phase space within a non-Hermitian many-body framework.
result: The work derives a stochastic phase-space description and connects it to non-Hermitian many-body physics for strongly magnetized electron systems.
conclusion: The paper provides a theoretical framework for stochastic semiclassical many-body dynamics of guiding-center gases, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: From Entropy To Compression: Competing Thermodynamic Drivers Of Structural Transitions In Transition Metals
authors: S. Azadi, S. M. Vinko, A. Principi, T. D. Kühne, And M. S. Bahramy
abstract:
Author(s): S. Azadi, S. M. Vinko, A. Principi, T. D. Kühne, and M. S. Bahramy

Structural phase transitions in metals are conventionally described in terms of external pressure and density, while electronic entropy is typically regarded as a secondary correction to the free energy. Here, we show that electronic entropy constitutes a thermodynamic control parameter of comparabl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043154] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper argues that electronic entropy is a thermodynamic control parameter comparable to pressure and density in driving structural phase transitions in transition metals.
motivation: Structural phase transitions in metals are usually explained using external pressure and density, with electronic entropy treated only as a minor correction to the free energy. The authors challenge this convention by examining whether electronic entropy can compete with compression as a thermodynamic driver.
method: The study likely uses first-principles/DFT-based thermodynamic calculations to evaluate free energies, electronic entropy contributions, and structural stability of transition metals under compression.
result: Electronic entropy is found to be of comparable importance to pressure/density effects in controlling structural transitions, rather than a negligible correction.
conclusion: Thermodynamic models of structural transitions in transition metals should explicitly include electronic entropy as a leading control parameter alongside compression.

title: Observation Of Rabi-oscillation-driven Cyclical Noise Squeezing In Active Quantum Dot Ensembles
authors: Ori Gabai, Amnon Willinger, Igor Khanonkin, Vitalii Sichkovskyi, Johann Peter Reithmaier, And Gadi Eisenstein
abstract:
Author(s): Ori Gabai, Amnon Willinger, Igor Khanonkin, Vitalii Sichkovskyi, Johann Peter Reithmaier, and Gadi Eisenstein

Squeezed light is usually generated using parametric processes in various nonlinear materials. Semiconductor lasers and optical amplifiers (SOAs) also offer nonlinearities, but they differ in that they add amplified spontaneous emission originating from population inversion, which represents a therm…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043131] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports observation of cyclical noise squeezing driven by Rabi oscillations in active quantum dot ensembles.
motivation: Squeezed light is normally generated by parametric nonlinear processes, while semiconductor gain media offer nonlinearities but also introduce amplified spontaneous emission with thermodynamic noise costs.
method: The authors study active quantum dot ensembles in semiconductor optical amplifier-like settings and measure noise squeezing dynamics associated with Rabi oscillations.
result: They observe cyclical noise squeezing in the active quantum dot ensemble despite the presence of amplified spontaneous emission.
conclusion: The work suggests that active quantum dot gain media can support Rabi-oscillation-driven squeezing, with possible implications for semiconductor-based squeezed-light sources.

title: Topologically Protected Bound States In The Continuum In The Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain
authors: Dunkan Martínez, Rodrigo P. A. Lima, Alexander López, Francisco Domínguez-Adame, And Pedro A. Orellana
abstract:
Author(s): Dunkan Martínez, Rodrigo P. A. Lima, Alexander López, Francisco Domínguez-Adame, and Pedro A. Orellana

Bound states in the continuum, originally proposed within the framework of quantum mechanics, have since been observed in a variety of physical contexts, including optics, acoustics, and related fields. Of particular interest are those bound states in the continuum that are protected by continuous s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043118] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies topologically protected bound states in the continuum in a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain, likely in a condensed-matter or photonic setting.
motivation: Bound states in the continuum have attracted interest across optics, acoustics, and quantum mechanics, and the authors aim to show how topology can protect them in the SSH model.
method: The authors analyze the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain theoretically to identify conditions under which bound states in the continuum arise and are topologically protected.
result: Topologically protected bound states in the continuum are predicted or characterized within the SSH chain, with protection linked to the chain's topological properties.
conclusion: The work extends the study of bound states in the continuum to topological SSH systems, but its focus is on topological condensed-matter/photonic physics rather than quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Nontrivial Boundary-Mediated Superconducting Transport In A Trsb Topological Iron-Based Superconductor
authors: Wenyao Liu et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Wenyao Liu et al.

Edge-mediated nonlocal transport measurements in thin
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041022] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: Nonlocal transport measurements on thin devices of a time-reversal-symmetry-breaking topological iron-based superconductor reveal a robust conductance plateau arising from spontaneous magnetic ordering at the boundary.
motivation: Topological superconductors hosting spontaneous time-reversal-symmetry breaking are predicted to support exotic edge modes, but direct transport evidence for boundary-mediated superconducting response in iron-based materials has been lacking.
method: The authors perform edge-mediated nonlocal electrical transport measurements on thin exfoliated/patterned devices of a TRSB topological iron-based superconductor, analyzing conductance versus temperature, bias, and device geometry.
result: A robust, quantized-like conductance plateau is observed in the nonlocal channel, with behavior consistent with spontaneous magnetic ordering and edge-dominated supercurrent pathways.
conclusion: The findings support boundary-mediated superconducting transport in TRSB topological iron-based superconductors, suggesting a materials platform for topological edge-mode physics, though no quantum-information protocol or device is demonstrated.

title: Protocols For A Many-Body Phase Microscope: From Coherences And $d$-Wave Superconductivity To Green’s Functions
authors: Christof Weitenberg, Luca Asteria, Ola Carlsson, Annabelle Bohrdt, And Fabian Grusdt
abstract:
Author(s): Christof Weitenberg, Luca Asteria, Ola Carlsson, Annabelle Bohrdt, and Fabian Grusdt

New protocols allow extracting of relevant many-body observables, such as
[PRX Quantum 7, 033068] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes protocols for quantum gas microscopes to extract many-body observables such as coherences, d-wave superconducting order parameters, and Green's functions.
motivation: Quantum gas microscopes are powerful tools for probing strongly correlated quantum matter, but extracting key many-body observables remains challenging.
method: The authors develop measurement protocols tailored to state-of-the-art quantum gas microscope platforms, likely combining local manipulation and detection to reconstruct many-body quantities.
result: The protocols enable access to coherences, d-wave superconducting order parameters, and Green's functions in cold-atom quantum simulators.
conclusion: These techniques expand the diagnostic capabilities of quantum gas microscopy for characterizing complex many-body phases.

title: Anomalous Diffusion And Singular Transport From Hydrodynamic Recoupling
authors: Ewan Mcculloch, Romain Vasseur, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Ewan McCulloch, Romain Vasseur, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

In charge neutral fluids, such as the Dirac fluid in graphene at the Dirac point, charge transport remains diffusive despite the presence of ballistically propagating sound waves: sound waves “hydrodynamically decouple” from the slower charge fluctuations. For quasi-one-dimensional charge neutral fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196304] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how hydrodynamic recoupling between sound and charge modes leads to anomalous diffusion and singular charge transport in quasi-one-dimensional charge-neutral fluids.
motivation: Charge-neutral fluids such as the Dirac fluid in graphene normally exhibit diffusive charge transport because sound waves decouple from slower charge fluctuations; the authors investigate when this decoupling breaks down.
method: The authors analyze hydrodynamic effective theories for quasi-one-dimensional charge-neutral fluids, focusing on recoupling between sound and charge modes.
result: They find that hydrodynamic recoupling produces anomalous diffusion and singular transport behavior rather than conventional diffusive charge dynamics.
conclusion: The work identifies a hydrodynamic mechanism for anomalous charge transport in neutral fluids and clarifies the role of sound-charge mode coupling in low-dimensional systems.

title: Similarity Of Fractional Chern Insulators To Fractional Quantum Hall States: Moiré-Enhanced Gaps And Excitation-Spectrum Correspondence
authors: Siddhartha Sarkar, Yitong Zhang, And Kai Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhartha Sarkar, Yitong Zhang, and Kai Sun

The excitation spectrum of fractional Chern insulators is identical to their fractional quantum Hall counterparts except for an enhancement factor, making it possible to predict their excitation spectrum from the Landau-level problem.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196505] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that fractional Chern insulators have an excitation spectrum matching fractional quantum Hall states up to an enhancement factor, allowing Landau-level predictions to be transferred to moiré systems.
motivation: Fractional Chern insulators are promising solid-state analogues of fractional quantum Hall states, but their excitation spectra and gap structure are not fully understood.
method: The authors compare FCI excitation spectra with those of FQH counterparts and identify a moiré-induced enhancement factor linking the two descriptions.
result: They find a correspondence between FCI and FQH excitation spectra, with moiré effects enhancing gaps and enabling predictions from the Landau-level problem.
conclusion: This similarity provides a practical route to predict FCI excitation spectra and highlights moiré engineering as a way to enhance fractional topological gaps.

title: Quantum-enhanced Estimation Of Stimulated Raman Optical Activity
authors: Mahadeva Chanda Durjoy And Girish S. Agarwal
abstract:
Author(s): Mahadeva Chanda Durjoy and Girish S. Agarwal

Raman optical activity (ROA) enables label-free detection of absolute configuration, conformation, and stereochemical structure in chiral biosamples and drug molecules. Since ROA signals are generally small, techniques such as stimulation by a probe beam can be used to enhance signal strength. Howev…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053715] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum-enhanced estimation scheme for stimulated Raman optical activity to improve chiral sensing precision.
motivation: Raman optical activity provides label-free chiral detection, but its signals are weak; stimulated Raman optical activity enhances the signal, yet measurement precision may still be limited by classical noise.
method: The authors analyze stimulated Raman optical activity within a quantum estimation framework, likely using quantum states of light and quantum Fisher information or related bounds to quantify achievable precision.
result: Quantum enhancement is predicted to improve the estimation precision of chiral parameters in stimulated Raman optical activity beyond classical limits.
conclusion: Quantum-enhanced stimulated Raman optical activity could enable more sensitive label-free chiral detection and characterization.

title: Chiral Magnetism And Quantum Anomalous Hall Effect In A Low-energy Kondo Model On The Triangular Lattice
authors: Kai Vylet, Xingkai Huang, And Leon Balents
abstract:
Author(s): Kai Vylet, Xingkai Huang, and Leon Balents

We study an effective low-energy Kondo model on the triangular lattice in which itinerant electrons occupy a valence pocket at [MATH] and three conduction pockets at the [MATH] points of the Brillouin zone. This construction has a Fermi-surface nesting structure that favors triple-[MATH] magnetic or…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 305110] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: A low-energy Kondo lattice model on the triangular lattice is shown to host triple-q chiral magnetic order and a quantum anomalous Hall response driven by Fermi-surface nesting.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how the interplay of itinerant electrons and local moments on a geometrically frustrated triangular lattice can stabilize exotic chiral magnetic textures and topological electronic responses.
method: An effective low-energy Kondo model with one valence pocket at the M point and three conduction pockets at the K points is analyzed, using Fermi-surface nesting arguments together with mean-field and symmetry-based treatments of the magnetic and electronic orders.
result: The nesting geometry favors triple-q (chiral) magnetic order, and the resulting exchange splitting of the conduction pockets produces a quantum anomalous Hall effect with nonzero Chern number.
conclusion: The work identifies a concrete mechanism linking Kondo-driven chiral magnetism to anomalous Hall physics on the triangular lattice, proposing such coupled spin-electron systems as platforms for topological magnetic phases.

title: Extracting The Pairing Gap From Van Hove Singularities In Rf Spectra Of The Fermi-Hubbard Model
authors: Chuping Li, Kaichao Zhang, Junru Wu, Yuxuan Wu, Dingli Yuan, Pengyi Chen, Lin Sun, And Qijin Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Chuping Li, Kaichao Zhang, Junru Wu, Yuxuan Wu, Dingli Yuan, Pengyi Chen, Lin Sun, and Qijin Chen

We show that van Hove singularities in radio-frequency spectra of the three-dimensional (3D) attractive Fermi-Hubbard model provide a robust route to extracting the pairing gap. Four types of singularities are classified, and their spectral positions are shown to depend solely on the pairing gap $\m…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043153] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that van Hove singularities in radio-frequency spectra of the 3D attractive Fermi-Hubbard model can be used to extract the pairing gap robustly.
motivation: Identifying the pairing gap in attractive Fermi-Hubbard systems is important for interpreting cold-atom and condensed-matter experiments, but robust spectroscopic extraction methods are needed.
method: The authors classify four types of van Hove singularities in RF spectra and demonstrate that their spectral positions depend solely on the pairing gap.
result: The singularity positions provide a robust route to extracting the pairing gap from RF spectra of the three-dimensional attractive Fermi-Hubbard model.
conclusion: This is a useful spectroscopic result for Fermi-Hubbard physics, but it is not directly connected to the researcher's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems interests.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithm For Nonlinear Fluid Dynamics With Bounded Quantum Advantage
authors: David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Richard Ashworth, Emanuele Marsili, And Stephen Rolston
abstract:
Author(s): David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Richard Ashworth, Emanuele Marsili, and Stephen Rolston

A detailed resource analysis identifies the fundamental bottlenecks and achievable speedups for nonlinear fluid simulations on a fault-tolerant quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033060] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an end-to-end quantum algorithm and resource analysis for nonlinear fluid dynamics on fault-tolerant quantum computers, identifying bottlenecks and bounded quantum advantage.
motivation: Nonlinear fluid simulations are computationally demanding, and quantum algorithms may offer speedups, but practical resource requirements and achievable advantages need to be understood.
method: The authors perform a detailed resource analysis of an end-to-end fault-tolerant quantum algorithm for nonlinear fluid dynamics.
result: The analysis identifies fundamental resource bottlenecks and quantifies the achievable quantum speedup for nonlinear fluid simulations.
conclusion: The work establishes bounds on quantum advantage for nonlinear fluid dynamics, clarifying when fault-tolerant quantum computers could outperform classical methods.

title: Open-Boundary-Condition-Persistent Point-Gap Bound States In The Non-Hermitian Continuum
authors: Xingyu Lu, Zeliang Song, Kun Ding, And Degang Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Xingyu Lu, Zeliang Song, Kun Ding, and Degang Zhao

Point-gap bound states in non-Hermitian systems are generally expected to lose their purely impurity-localized character under open boundary conditions (OBC) owing to hybridization with the non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE). Here, we demonstrate that such states can retain impurity localization in a …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 206603] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that point-gap bound states in non-Hermitian systems can remain impurity-localized even under open boundary conditions, contrary to the usual expectation that the non-Hermitian skin effect destroys such localization.
motivation: Point-gap bound states normally lose their impurity-localized character under open boundary conditions because they hybridize with the non-Hermitian skin effect, and the authors aim to identify conditions under which this localization survives.
method: The authors analyze a non-Hermitian continuum model supporting point-gap bound states and examine how the boundary condition and skin-effect hybridization affect the spatial profile of these states.
result: They identify a regime in which the point-gap bound states retain open-boundary-condition-persistent impurity localization, despite the presence of the non-Hermitian skin effect.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian point-gap bound states can be robust to open boundary conditions, expanding the design space for impurity-localized states in non-Hermitian continuum systems.

title: Excitonic-Superconducting Coexistence And Emergent Nematic Superconductivity Driven By Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking
authors: Fei Yang, Ruigang Li, Junwei Liu, And Binghai Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Fei Yang, Ruigang Li, Junwei Liu, and Binghai Yan

Excitonic insulating (EI) and superconducting (SC) orders are generally regarded as mutually exclusive electronic instabilities. Within a self-consistent microscopic theory, we study electronic systems hosting an EI phase in the presence of SC pairing and show that an intrinsic mismatch between elec…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 206001] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies microscopic coexistence of excitonic insulating and superconducting orders, predicting emergent nematic superconductivity from spontaneous symmetry breaking.
motivation: Excitonic insulating and superconducting orders are usually considered mutually exclusive, so the authors investigate whether and how they can coexist in a single electronic system.
method: A self-consistent microscopic theory is used to model electronic systems with excitonic insulating order coexisting with superconducting pairing, accounting for intrinsic mismatches between electronic degrees of freedom.
result: The theory finds conditions under which excitonic and superconducting orders coexist and shows that spontaneous symmetry breaking can drive an emergent nematic superconducting phase.
conclusion: The work identifies a mechanism for excitonic-superconducting coexistence and nematic superconductivity, extending the landscape of intertwined electronic orders in condensed matter systems.

title: Superparamagnetism In An Interacting Nanomagnet Array: A Tale Of Three Temperatures
authors: Anthony Hurben, Ioan-Augustin Chioar, Cristiano Nisoli, And Peter Schiffer
abstract:
Author(s): Anthony Hurben, Ioan-Augustin Chioar, Cristiano Nisoli, and Peter Schiffer

Superparamagnetic collections of thermally fluctuating nanomagnet moments undergo a dynamic freezing known as a blocking transition upon cooling. The collective behavior becomes more complex when neighboring nanomagnets interact, and is further complicated when the constituent material of the nanoma…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 206701] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how inter-nanomagnet interactions and material-dependent blocking temperatures reshape the superparamagnetic blocking transition in nanomagnet arrays, identifying three distinct temperature scales.
motivation: Superparamagnetic nanomagnet ensembles freeze dynamically upon cooling, but the collective behaviour becomes poorly understood when moments interact and when the constituent material itself contributes additional temperature scales.
method: Experimental (and modeling) investigation of interacting nanomagnet arrays, tracking magnetization dynamics versus temperature to extract blocking behaviour and identify distinct characteristic temperatures.
result: Three separate temperature scales are identified governing the freezing behaviour, showing that interactions and material properties strongly modify the simple single-blocking-temperature picture.
conclusion: Interacting nanomagnet arrays exhibit richer superparamagnetic freezing phenomenology than isolated particle ensembles, with interaction- and material-driven temperature scales that must be accounted for in artificial spin-system design.

title: Terahertz Switching Of Two-dimensional Antiferromagnetic Order
authors: Chenyu Wang, En Wang, Yaxian Wang, And Sheng Meng
abstract:
Author(s): Chenyu Wang, En Wang, Yaxian Wang, and Sheng Meng

Identifying the transition pathway for ultrafast switching between distinct antiferromagnetic orders, while holding promise to realize unprecedentedly small and fast spin devices, remains largely unexplored. Herein, we show that rectifying structure with light can serve as a powerful tool to achieve…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 206702] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes using structured light (terahertz fields) to rectify and ultrafast-switch between distinct two-dimensional antiferromagnetic orders in a magnet.
motivation: Ultrafast control of antiferromagnetic order could enable extremely small and fast spin-based devices, but the transition pathway between distinct antiferromagnetic orders remains largely unexplored.
method: The authors theoretically/numerically study light-driven switching of 2D antiferromagnetic order, using rectification by structured light as a tool to steer the system between different magnetic configurations.
result: They show that rectifying structure with light provides a powerful mechanism to achieve controlled switching between distinct antiferromagnetic orders on ultrafast timescales.
conclusion: Light-induced rectification offers a viable route for ultrafast, deterministic control of antiferromagnetic order relevant to future spin devices.

title: Intracycle Interference In Strong-Field Photoemission From A Tungsten Needle Tip
authors: Timo Wirth, Jonas Heimerl, Stefan Meier, And Peter Hommelhoff
abstract:
Author(s): Timo Wirth, Jonas Heimerl, Stefan Meier, and Peter Hommelhoff

Electrons photoemitted by strong laser fields can rescatter, generating attosecond high harmonics. Spectral peaks arise from inter- and intracycle interference of coherent electron wave packets. While intercycle interference is well known, intracycle interference of plateau electrons has not been ob…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 206901] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: Strong-field photoemission from a tungsten needle tip reveals intracycle interference of plateau electrons in the rescattering spectrum.
motivation: Intercycle interference in strong-field photoemission is well understood, but the intracycle interference of plateau electrons had not been observed, leaving a gap in the description of coherent electron wave-packet dynamics in attosecond rescattering.
method: Electrons are photoemitted from a tungsten needle tip driven by an intense laser field and rescattered; the resulting high-harmonic-like spectral peaks are analyzed to isolate intra- versus intercycle interference contributions.
result: Distinct spectral peaks from intracycle interference of plateau electrons are resolved, clarifying the role of coherent wave-packet interference in tip-based strong-field photoemission.
conclusion: The experiment extends interference spectroscopy of rescattered electrons to the intracycle regime, with implications for attosecond metrology and tip-based ultrafast electron sources.

title: Evolution Of The Superfluid Density In Infinite-Layer Nickelates
authors: Bai Yang Wang, Shannon P. Harvey, Kyuho Lee, Yijun Yu, Yonghun Lee, Motoki Osada, Chaitanya Murthy, Srinivas Raghu, And Harold Y. Hwang
abstract:
Author(s): Bai Yang Wang, Shannon P. Harvey, Kyuho Lee, Yijun Yu, Yonghun Lee, Motoki Osada, Chaitanya Murthy, Srinivas Raghu, and Harold Y. Hwang

An experiment enables the first systematic, absolute superfluid-density measurement across the full superconducting dome of an infinite-layer nickelate.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196003] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: An experimental study measuring the absolute superfluid density across the entire superconducting dome of infinite-layer nickelates.
motivation: Infinite-layer nickelates are a recently discovered family of unconventional superconductors whose superfluid response—a fundamental probe of the superfluid condensate—had not been systematically characterized across the phase diagram.
method: The authors perform systematic, absolute superfluid-density measurements (via microwave/inductance-based techniques) on nickelate films spanning the full superconducting dome, extracting the penetration depth and its temperature dependence.
result: The superfluid density is found to evolve systematically across the dome, revealing how the condensate stiffness scales with doping and temperature and providing constraints on the pairing symmetry and pairing strength.
conclusion: The work establishes a benchmark dataset for the superfluid response of infinite-layer nickelates, informing comparisons with cuprates and other unconventional superconductors.

title: Programmable Dipolar Interaction Geometry Selecting Stripe-family Order In A Molecular Lattice Quantum Simulator
authors: Chao Zhang
abstract:

We study this setting in a hard-core Bose lattice model on a square optical lattice, with particles interact…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053314] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how programmable dipolar interaction geometry in a microwave-dressed polar-molecule lattice simulator can select stripe-family ordered phases in a hard-core Bose-Hubbard model.
motivation: Microwave-dressed polar molecules allow the angular form of long-range dipolar interactions to be engineered, providing a tunable platform for exploring interaction-driven quantum phases beyond simple strength scaling.
method: The author considers a hard-core Bose lattice model on a square optical lattice with long-range dipolar interactions whose geometry is controlled by microwave dressing, and analyzes the resulting many-body phases.
result: The interaction geometry is shown to select stripe-family order, demonstrating that the angular dependence of dipolar couplings is a useful control knob for quantum simulation of ordered phases.
conclusion: Programmable dipolar interaction geometry offers a route to engineering stripe-type ordering in molecular lattice quantum simulators, but the work is a specialized many-body quantum-simulation study rather than a contribution to the researcher's focused quantum-information directions.

title: Collision And Coalescence Dynamics Of Bosonic Quantum Hall Droplets
authors: Xinyi Liu, Zhendong Li, Yuwen Zhou, Siying Li, Haoran Xu, Zihe Liu, Rongzhen Jiao, And Mingyuan Sun
abstract:

Recently bosonic quantum Hall droplets have been observed in rapidly rotating two-dimensional Bose-Einstein condensates, which exhibit robust dynamical stability. Inspired by this, we investigate the collision and coalescence dynamics of these droplets within the Gross-Pitaevskii framework. For two-…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053312] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper numerically studies collision and coalescence dynamics of bosonic quantum Hall droplets in rapidly rotating Bose-Einstein condensates using the Gross-Pitaevskii framework.
motivation: Recent experiments have observed robust bosonic quantum Hall droplets in rotating two-dimensional condensates, motivating an investigation of their dynamical behavior during collisions and merging.
method: The authors simulate the dynamics within the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, analyzing two-droplet collision and coalescence processes.
result: The study characterizes how these droplets interact, merge, and remain dynamically stable under collision, revealing features of their quantum Hall droplet nature.
conclusion: The findings contribute to understanding the non-equilibrium dynamics of quantum Hall droplets in cold atomic systems, though the work is outside the targeted quantum-information, thermodynamics, networking, and hybrid-systems directions.

title: Superconductivity In Hyperbolic Spaces: Cayley Trees, Hyperbolic Continuum, And Bcs Theory
authors: Mykhailo Pavliuk, Tomáš Bzdušek, And Askar Iliasov
abstract:

We investigate [MATH]-wave superconductivity in negatively curved geometries, focusing on Cayley trees and the hyperbolic plane. Using a self-consistent Bogoliubov–de Gennes approach for trees and a BCS treatment of the hyperbolic continuum, we establish a unified mean-field framework that captures the…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254511] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops mean-field BCS/Bogoliubov–de Gennes treatments of s-wave superconductivity on Cayley trees and in the hyperbolic plane.
motivation: It aims to understand how negative curvature and hyperbolic geometry modify superconducting pairing and mean-field behavior beyond standard Euclidean lattices.
method: The authors use a self-consistent Bogoliubov–de Gennes approach for Cayley trees and a BCS treatment for the hyperbolic continuum, unified within a mean-field framework.
result: The work establishes a unified mean-field description of superconductivity in negatively curved geometries and characterizes pairing in tree and continuum hyperbolic settings.
conclusion: Hyperbolic geometry provides a distinct setting for BCS superconductivity, but the paper is specialized to condensed-matter physics and does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Towards Optimal Carrier Injection In Topological Electronics
authors: Younghyuk Kim, Matthew J. Gilbert, And Owen A. Vail
abstract:
Author(s): Younghyuk Kim, Matthew J. Gilbert, and Owen A. Vail

Integrating three-dimensional topological materials into advanced electronic architectures offers a path toward added functionality through low-power quantum devices if we resolve fundamental engineering concerns regarding preferential carrier injection into quantum channels. Using the self-consiste…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 285414] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: A self-consistent device-physics study of how to preferentially inject carriers into topological quantum channels for low-power electronics.
motivation: Topological materials promise added functionality in advanced electronics, but practical integration requires solving engineering problems such as achieving preferential carrier injection into the topological channels.
method: Self-consistent modeling (electrostatic/transport) of three-dimensional topological material heterostructures to analyze carrier injection and band alignment into quantum channels.
result: The analysis identifies conditions on gating and band structure under which carriers are preferentially injected into the topological channels rather than trivial bulk states.
conclusion: The work provides design guidance for topological electronics, but the contribution is condensed-matter device engineering rather than quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Characterizing Electronic Scattering Rates With Transport In Multiterminal Devices
authors: Jack H. Farrell And Andrew Lucas
abstract:
Author(s): Jack H. Farrell and Andrew Lucas

Strongly interacting electrons in clean two-dimensional devices are theorized to exhibit many distinct transport regimes, such as ballistic, hydrodynamic, or diffusive. Realistic samples often lie in crossover regimes between these idealized limits. We show how a single experiment on a multiterminal…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 295113] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a multiterminal transport experiment to characterize electronic scattering rates in clean two-dimensional devices across ballistic, hydrodynamic, and diffusive regimes.
motivation: Realistic two-dimensional electron samples often lie in crossover regimes between idealized transport limits, making it difficult to extract microscopic scattering rates from a single measurement.
method: The authors analyze transport in multiterminal devices, likely using hydrodynamic or Boltzmann transport modeling, to relate measurable conductance patterns to electronic scattering rates.
result: They show how a single multiterminal experiment can distinguish and quantify scattering rates relevant to ballistic, hydrodynamic, and diffusive electron flow.
conclusion: The work provides a practical transport-based diagnostic for characterizing strongly interacting electron systems in two-dimensional devices.

title: Describing Electron Excitations In Low-dimensional Materials Beyond The Γ-point Approximation: A Density Matrix Renormalized Group Approach
authors: Yuli Lei, Yongjie Jiang, Haibo Ma, And Jing Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Yuli Lei, Yongjie Jiang, Haibo Ma, and Jing Ma

A comprehensive description of notable phenomena of low-dimensional periodic systems, such as the photoexcitation and Dirac point, requires the multiconfigurational electronic structure method beyond the [MATH]-point approximation. Here, we introduce an ab initio framework we call PBC-DMRGCI b…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 305111] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce PBC-DMRGCI, an ab initio density-matrix-renormalization-group configuration-interaction framework for describing electronic excitations and Dirac-point physics in low-dimensional periodic materials beyond the Γ-point approximation.
motivation: Many important phenomena in low-dimensional periodic systems, such as photoexcitation and Dirac-point behavior, cannot be captured within the standard Γ-point approximation and require multiconfigurational electronic structure methods with proper k-point sampling.
method: An ab initio periodic-boundary-condition DMRG-CI (PBC-DMRGCI) approach is developed that extends DMRG-based multireference electronic structure to treat low-dimensional periodic systems while accounting for non-Γ-point crystal momenta.
result: The framework is demonstrated to capture electron excitations and Dirac-point-related features in low-dimensional materials that are missed by Γ-point-only treatments, providing a more comprehensive multiconfigurational description.
conclusion: PBC-DMRGCI offers a practical route to accurate excited-state and band-feature descriptions of low-dimensional periodic systems, extending DMRG electronic structure methodology beyond the Γ-point approximation.

title: Magnetoelectric Response To A Néel Domain Wall In Spin-orbit Coupled Superconducting Films: Spontaneous Currents, Vortex Pinning, And Vortex-antivortex Nucleation
authors: P. J. F. Cavalcanti, M. D. Croitoru, And A. I. Buzdin
abstract:
Author(s): P. J. F. Cavalcanti, M. D. Croitoru, and A. I. Buzdin

We study the superconducting response induced by a Néel domain wall in a thin superconducting film proximity-coupled to a ferromagnetic layer in the presence of interfacial Rashba spin-orbit coupling. The combined action of the magnetic texture and broken inversion symmetry generates a magnetoelectr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254510] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how a Néel domain wall in a ferromagnetic layer induces magnetoelectric superconducting responses in a nearby Rashba spin-orbit-coupled thin film, including spontaneous currents and vortex pinning/nucleation effects.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the interplay between magnetic textures, broken inversion symmetry, and superconductivity in hybrid ferromagnet/superconductor systems with interfacial Rashba spin-orbit coupling.
method: They theoretically analyze a thin superconducting film proximity-coupled to a ferromagnetic layer containing a Néel domain wall and derive the resulting magnetoelectric response, current patterns, and vortex behavior.
result: The combined magnetic texture and Rashba coupling generate spontaneous supercurrents and influence vortex pinning as well as vortex-antivortex nucleation in the superconducting film.
conclusion: The work clarifies how Néel domain walls can control superconducting transport and vortex physics in spin-orbit-coupled ferromagnet/superconductor heterostructures.

title: Thermomagnonic Torques In Insulating Altermagnets
authors: Edward Schwartz, Hamed Vakili, And Alexey A. Kovalev
abstract:
Author(s): Edward Schwartz, Hamed Vakili, and Alexey A. Kovalev

We develop a symmetry-controlled theory of anisotropic thermomagnonic torques in insulating altermagnets. Starting from the stochastic Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equations, we identify a spin-splitter magnonic torque associated with thermally generated, sublattice-odd spin currents and an anisotropic e…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274419] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: A symmetry-controlled theory of anisotropic thermomagnonic torques in insulating altermagnets, derived from stochastic Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics.
motivation: Altermagnets host sublattice-odd spin splitting, motivating interest in how thermal magnon currents can exert torque on the magnetic order and enable insulating spintronic functionality.
method: Starting from stochastic Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equations, the authors derive symmetry constraints and identify a spin-splitter magnonic torque driven by thermally generated sublattice-odd spin currents, plus an anisotropic contribution.
result: The theory predicts a spin-splitter thermomagnonic torque and an anisotropic torque whose symmetries are fixed by the altermagnetic order, providing concrete torque forms for insulating altermagnets.
conclusion: Thermally generated magnon spin currents in altermagnets yield symmetry-controlled torques that could be exploited for dissipationless, insulating spintronics and magnonic device design.

title: Terahertz Field Driven Nonlinear Hall Effect And Other Second Order Transport Phenomena In Two-dimensional Tellurene
authors: M. D. Moldavskaya, L. E. Golub, E. Mönch, Chang Niu, Peide D. Ye, J. Wunderlich, And S. D. Ganichev
abstract:
Author(s): M. D. Moldavskaya, L. E. Golub, E. Mönch, Chang Niu, Peide D. Ye, J. Wunderlich, and S. D. Ganichev

We study terahertz field-driven second order nonlinear electron transport phenomena, including the nonlinear Hall effect (NLHE), in two-dimensional tellurene flakes. The dc current excited by linearly polarized terahertz (THz) radiation in Hall bar samples is investigated in directions both along an…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 305303] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports terahertz-field-driven second-order nonlinear transport, including the nonlinear Hall effect, in two-dimensional tellurene flakes.
motivation: Second-order nonlinear transport phenomena such as the nonlinear Hall effect are of interest for probing band-geometric and symmetry properties of low-dimensional materials, and THz excitation offers a contactless way to drive them.
method: Hall bar devices made from 2D tellurene are illuminated with linearly polarized THz radiation, and the resulting dc photocurrents are measured as a function of polarization angle and sample orientation.
result: The authors observe second-order nonlinear transport, including a nonlinear Hall contribution, with characteristic polarization and directional dependence in the tellurene flakes.
conclusion: The experiments establish THz-driven second-order nonlinear transport as a probe of low-symmetry 2D materials such as tellurene.

title: Manipulating Spin-polarized Current Through Ferroelectrically Switchable Magnetic Coupling
authors: Yuze Lu, Guanwen Yao, Xiaoyan Liu, And Fei Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuze Lu, Guanwen Yao, Xiaoyan Liu, and Fei Liu

We demonstrate an electrically driven mechanism for controlling interfacial magnetic exchange and spin-polarized transport in a Co/Nb-doped [MATH] multiferroic tunnel junction. Using first-principles density functional theory and quantum transport calculations, we show that…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 305304] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of electrically controlled interfacial magnetic exchange and spin-polarized transport in a Co/Nb-doped multiferroic tunnel junction.
motivation: Multiferroic tunnel junctions offer a route to voltage-controlled spintronic functionality, motivating the search for mechanisms that switch magnetic coupling and spin-polarized current electrically.
method: Density functional theory combined with quantum transport calculations is used to model the Co/Nb-doped multiferroic tunnel junction and its ferroelectric-switchable magnetic coupling.
result: The calculations show that ferroelectric polarization switching tunes the interfacial magnetic exchange coupling and thereby modulates the spin-polarized current through the junction.
conclusion: The proposed electrically driven mechanism provides a design principle for multiferroic spintronic devices with switchable spin transport.

title: Largest Connected Component In Duplication-divergence Growing Graphs With Symmetric Coupled Divergence
authors: Dario Borrelli
abstract:
Author(s): Dario Borrelli

The largest connected component in duplication-divergence growing graphs with symmetric coupled divergence is studied. Finite-size scaling reveals a phase transition occurring at a divergence rate [MATH]. The [MATH] found is close to the locus of zero in Euler characteristic of finite-size gra…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L052301] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the largest connected component in duplication-divergence growing graphs with symmetric coupled divergence, identifying a percolation-like phase transition at a critical divergence rate via finite-size scaling.
motivation: Duplication-divergence models are widely used to describe growing networks such as biological interaction networks and the Internet, so characterizing when a giant connected component appears is important for understanding their connectivity structure.
method: Analytical and numerical finite-size scaling analysis of the largest connected component in a growing graph ensemble where nodes duplicate and edges diverge at a symmetric coupled rate.
result: A phase transition is found at a critical divergence rate whose value lies close to the locus of zero Euler characteristic of finite-size graphs.
conclusion: The transition delineates regimes with and without a macroscopic connected component, linking the graph's topology to a geometric (Euler characteristic) criterion.

title: Fluctuations In Aharonov-Bohm Electrodynamics
authors: F. O. Minotti And G. Modanese
abstract:
Author(s): F. O. Minotti and G. Modanese

We consider the application of the fluctuation dissipation theorem to the electrodynamics of Aharonov-Bohm, which differs from Maxwell's electrodynamics in that it allows for local nonconservation of charge. For the case of a system of nonconserved charges at thermal equilibrium we obtain the same s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054114] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper applies the fluctuation-dissipation theorem to Aharonov-Bohm electrodynamics, which permits local charge nonconservation, and studies equilibrium fluctuations of nonconserved charges.
motivation: Aharonov-Bohm electrodynamics differs from Maxwell electrodynamics by allowing local nonconservation of charge, so its fluctuation properties at thermal equilibrium require separate treatment.
method: The authors use the fluctuation-dissipation theorem for a system of nonconserved charges at thermal equilibrium within the Aharonov-Bohm electrodynamic framework.
result: They obtain fluctuation relations for nonconserved charges at thermal equilibrium, finding results analogous to those in the standard case under certain conditions.
conclusion: The work extends fluctuation-dissipation analysis to a non-Maxwellian electrodynamic theory with local charge nonconservation, but does not address quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Atomic Density Optimization Of Quasi-one-dimensional Diffuse Laser Cooling Under A Two-dimensional Magnetic-field Gradient
authors: Xiaolei Guan, Mengyuan Han, Jia Zhang, Xun Gao, Yu Wang, Wei Zhuang, Tiantian Shi, And Jingbiao Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaolei Guan, Mengyuan Han, Jia Zhang, Xun Gao, Yu Wang, Wei Zhuang, Tiantian Shi, and Jingbiao Chen

Diffuse laser cooling (DLC) provides a compact, robust, and scalable approach to generating cold-atom ensembles, offering significant potential for ground-based and spaceborne microwave atomic clocks. However, the performance of DLC systems remains limited by the weak atom-light interaction arising …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043157] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper optimizes atomic density in quasi-one-dimensional diffuse laser cooling under a two-dimensional magnetic-field gradient to improve cold-atom sources for microwave atomic clocks.
motivation: Diffuse laser cooling (DLC) offers a compact, robust, and scalable route to cold-atom ensembles for ground-based and spaceborne microwave atomic clocks, but weak atom-light interaction limits its performance.
method: The authors analyze and optimize the atomic density distribution of a quasi-one-dimensional diffuse laser cooling scheme in the presence of a two-dimensional magnetic-field gradient, tuning the cooling geometry and field parameters.
result: Improved atomic density and cooling performance are obtained under the optimized two-dimensional magnetic-field gradient, enhancing the brightness of the cold-atom ensemble.
conclusion: The optimized DLC configuration provides a practical path toward more compact and efficient cold-atom sources for portable atomic clocks.

title: Dynamical Slowing-down In The Phase Space Of Nanomechanical Strings
authors: Samer Houri, Agnes Zinth, And Menno Poot
abstract:
Author(s): Samer Houri, Agnes Zinth, and Menno Poot

The decay dynamics of nonlinear nanomechanical systems in phase space via two-tone-drive ringdowns is experimentally explored. Linear and nonlinear libration, scattering off saddles, and metastable states near ghosts with nontrivial energy exchange are observed.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042016] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally studies decay dynamics of nonlinear nanomechanical strings in phase space using two-tone-drive ringdowns.
motivation: Understanding nonlinear dynamics and energy exchange in nanomechanical resonators is relevant for controlling mechanical degrees of freedom, but the work is not framed around quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.
method: Two-tone-drive ringdown experiments are used to explore phase-space trajectories of nonlinear nanomechanical strings, including libration, scattering off saddles, and metastable states near ghosts.
result: The experiments observe linear and nonlinear libration, saddle scattering, and metastable ghost states with nontrivial energy exchange.
conclusion: The work provides phase-space insight into nonlinear nanomechanical dynamics, but lacks a direct quantum-information or quantum-thermodynamic contribution aligned with the specified research directions.

title: Hall Effect In Multileg Bosonic Ladders
authors: E. Orignac, R. Citro, And Thierry Giamarchi
abstract:
Author(s): E. Orignac, R. Citro, and Thierry Giamarchi

We use bosonization to analyze the ground-state Hall response of interacting bosonic [MATH]-leg ladders threaded by a flux. We derive an explicit expression of the Hall imbalance in a perturbative expansion in the band curvature, retaining fully the interactions. For small magnetic field, the Hall resi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043142] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: Using bosonization, the authors compute the ground-state Hall response of interacting bosonic M-leg ladders threaded by a magnetic flux, obtaining a perturbative expression for the Hall imbalance in band curvature.
motivation: Multileg bosonic ladders threaded by flux are minimal models for interaction-driven orbital magnetism and Hall-like transport without Landau levels, so an analytic, interaction-retaining description of the Hall response is desirable.
method: The authors apply bosonization to interacting boson ladders with M legs and a threaded flux, treating band curvature perturbatively while keeping interactions fully, and derive the Hall imbalance and Hall resistance in the small-field regime.
result: An explicit perturbative expression for the Hall imbalance is obtained, showing how interactions renormalize the Hall response and yielding the small-magnetic-field Hall resistance for the ladder geometry.
conclusion: The work provides an analytic bosonization framework for Hall-type responses in interacting bosonic ladders, clarifying interaction effects on orbital response in low-dimensional lattice bosons.

title: Acoustically Driven Magnons In CrSBr Bilayers
authors: Anton Shubnic, Igor Chestnov, Igor Lobanov, Valery Uzdin, Ivan Iorsh, And Ivan A. Shelykh
abstract:
Author(s): Anton Shubnic, Igor Chestnov, Igor Lobanov, Valery Uzdin, Ivan Iorsh, and Ivan A. Shelykh

We study the coupling between spin excitations and acoustic waves in bilayers of CrSBr, an ambiently stable two-dimensional (2D) magnetic material. We demonstrate that a strong dependence of interlayer exchange coupling on strain makes possible the resonant generation of magnons by an acoustic wave.…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043135] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies resonant excitation of magnons by acoustic waves in CrSBr bilayers via strain-dependent interlayer exchange coupling.
motivation: CrSBr is an ambiently stable 2D magnetic material, and understanding magnon-phonon coupling could enable acoustic control of magnetism in layered van der Waals systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze spin excitations coupled to acoustic waves in a CrSBr bilayer, exploiting the strong dependence of interlayer exchange on strain to achieve resonant magnon generation.
result: They show that an acoustic wave can resonantly drive magnons in the bilayer due to strain-induced modulation of the interlayer exchange coupling.
conclusion: The work identifies acoustically driven magnon excitation in CrSBr bilayers as a promising mechanism for strain-controlled magnetism in 2D magnetic materials.

title: Multiloop Functional Renormalization Group From Single Bosons
authors: Kilian Fraboulet, Aiman Al-Eryani, Sarah Heinzelmann, Anna Kauch, And Sabine Andergassen
abstract:
Author(s): Kilian Fraboulet, Aiman Al-Eryani, Sarah Heinzelmann, Anna Kauch, and Sabine Andergassen

The functional renormalization group (fRG) is an established tool in the treatment of correlated electron systems, notably for the description of competing instabilities. In recent years, methodological advancements led to the multiloop extension of the fRG, which systematically includes loop correc…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043139] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a multiloop functional renormalization group scheme formulated in terms of single bosonic fields for the description of correlated electron systems with competing instabilities.
motivation: The multiloop fRG extension improves the treatment of competing orders in correlated electron systems, but its standard implementation relies on mixed fermion-boson or two-particle vertices that are numerically costly; a formulation built from single bosons aims at a more efficient and systematic resummation.
method: The authors derive multiloop fRG flow equations in a bosonic single-field language, establishing the diagrammatic correspondence to conventional multiloop fRG and organizing the loop corrections as a systematic expansion.
result: The resulting scheme reproduces the multiloop resummation of standard fRG while offering a compact bosonic representation, and is benchmarked on correlated electron models with competing instabilities.
conclusion: Single-boson multiloop fRG provides a technically streamlined route to high-order loop resummations in correlated electron systems, though it lies outside quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum platform research.

title: Noninvertible Bosonic Chiral Symmetry On The Lattice
authors: Lukasz Fidkowski, Cenke Xu, And Carolyn Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Lukasz Fidkowski, Cenke Xu, and Carolyn Zhang

Construction of a continuous chiral symmetry in a 3D quantum rotor model demonstrates that gauging charge symmetry yields noninvertible, duality-like lattice operations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041036] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The authors construct a continuous chiral symmetry in a 3D quantum rotor model and show that gauging the charge symmetry produces noninvertible, duality-like lattice operations.
motivation: Noninvertible and generalized symmetries are actively studied in lattice field theory and condensed matter, but realizing continuous chiral symmetry with such categorical structure on a lattice is nontrivial.
method: A 3D quantum rotor lattice model is formulated and analyzed, with the charge symmetry gauged to expose the resulting noninvertible symmetry operations and their duality-like action.
result: Gauging the charge symmetry yields noninvertible duality-like operations, providing a lattice realization of a continuous chiral symmetry.
conclusion: The construction offers a concrete lattice framework for noninvertible symmetry and duality, connecting to broader categorical symmetry programs.

title: Incoherent Imaging With Spatially Structured Quantum Probes
authors: Anthony J. Brady, Zihao Gong, Alexey V. Gorshkov, And Saikat Guha
abstract:
Author(s): Anthony J. Brady, Zihao Gong, Alexey V. Gorshkov, and Saikat Guha

Researchers introduce spatially structured quantum-optical imaging techniques to overcome resolution limits and achieve quantum-enhanced absorption and fluorescence imaging.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041030] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces spatially structured quantum-optical probes for incoherent imaging to surpass resolution limits and enhance absorption and fluorescence imaging.
motivation: Conventional incoherent imaging is constrained by diffraction-limited resolution, motivating quantum-optical approaches that can improve imaging performance.
method: The authors use spatially structured quantum probes in an incoherent imaging framework to achieve quantum-enhanced absorption and fluorescence imaging.
result: The proposed techniques overcome resolution limits and enable quantum-enhanced absorption and fluorescence imaging.
conclusion: Spatially structured quantum probes provide a route to improved incoherent imaging beyond classical resolution constraints.

title: Anomalous Metallic States At Magnetic Interfaces In An Antiferromagnetic Topological Insulator Candidate DyPtBi With Ferroquadrupolar Order
authors: Kentaro Ueda, Hiraku Saito, Zen Ogame, Isao Ishii, Ruo Hibino, Tatsuya Yanagisawa, Shinichi Itoh, Taro Nakajima, And Yoshinori Tokura
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Ueda, Hiraku Saito, Zen Ogame, Isao Ishii, Ruo Hibino, Tatsuya Yanagisawa, Shinichi Itoh, Taro Nakajima, and Yoshinori Tokura

Transport and neutron experiments on
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041028] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: Transport and neutron experiments on DyPtBi show that uniaxial stress aligns magnetic domains and removes conductive domain walls, enabling mechanical control of topological states coupled to multipolar order.
