motivation: The paper explores an antiferromagnetic topological insulator candidate with ferroquadrupolar order, aiming to understand and control intertwined magnetic, multipolar, and topological states.
method: The authors perform transport measurements and neutron scattering on DyPtBi under uniaxial stress to align magnetic domains and eliminate conductive domain walls.
result: Uniaxial stress produces anomalous metallic states at magnetic interfaces by controlling magnetic domains and domain-wall conductivity in the topological insulator candidate.
conclusion: Mechanical control of magnetic domains provides a route to manipulate topological states intertwined with multipolar order in antiferromagnetic topological materials.

title: Nonsymmorphic Time-Reversal-Doubled Axion Insulators
authors: Yue Xie, Haohao Sheng, Quansheng Wu, Xi Dai, Zhong Fang, Hongming Weng, And Zhijun Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Xie, Haohao Sheng, Quansheng Wu, Xi Dai, Zhong Fang, Hongming Weng, and Zhijun Wang

Extension of time-reversal-doubled axion insulators to nonsymmorphic crystals establishes a spin-resolved classification scheme and identifies mixed bismuth monohalides as candidate materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041017] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends the classification of time-reversal-doubled axion insulators to nonsymmorphic crystals, providing a spin-resolved classification scheme and proposing mixed bismuth monohalides as candidate materials.
motivation: Axion insulators are topological phases with quantized magnetoelectric response, but their classification had been restricted to symmorphic crystals, leaving nonsymmorphic space groups unexplored.
method: Symmetry-based topological classification using magnetic space group and band representation analysis, combined with first-principles density functional calculations of candidate materials.
result: A spin-resolved classification scheme for time-reversal-doubled axion insulators in nonsymmorphic crystals is established, and mixed bismuth monohalides are identified as candidate realizations.
conclusion: The work broadens the scope of axion insulator physics to nonsymmorphic systems and provides concrete material candidates for future experimental study.

title: Moving Heterointerface With Robustly High Thermal Conductance
authors: Fuwei Yang, Wenjiang Zhou, Yelingyi Wang, Yuxi Wang, Deli Peng, Quanshui Zheng, And Bai Song
abstract:
Author(s): Fuwei Yang, Wenjiang Zhou, Yelingyi Wang, Yuxi Wang, Deli Peng, Quanshui Zheng, and Bai Song

Structural superlubricity between gold micromesas and graphite enables high, wear-free interfacial thermal conductance that remains insensitive to sliding and rotation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041005] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: Gold micromesas sliding on graphite in the structural-superlubricity regime exhibit high, wear-free interfacial thermal conductance that is insensitive to sliding velocity and rotation angle.
motivation: Interfacial thermal conductance across moving contacts is typically degraded by wear and friction, and how sliding or rotational misalignment affects heat transport at van der Waals interfaces was poorly characterized.
method: The authors measure thermal conductance across heterointerfaces formed between gold micromesas and graphite under structural superlubricity conditions, varying sliding and rotation, and interpret the results with interface phonon/electron transport models.
result: The contacts sustain robustly high interfacial thermal conductance that remains essentially unchanged under sliding and rotation, with no measurable wear over the studied ranges.
conclusion: Structural superlubricity provides a route to stable, high-performance thermal interfaces for moving contacts, decoupling heat transport from mechanical motion and misorientation.

title: Spin Nematic Liquid Crystal And Scalar Spin Chirality In Tetragonal Lattice ${\mathrm{YbMnBi}}_{2}$
authors: Yaofeng Xie, Sijie Xu, Yu Pan, Taekoo Oh, Tingjun Zhang, Masaaki Matsuda, Zhaoyu Liu, Zehao Wang, Yiheng Wang, Siyu Pan, Avishek Maity, Sylwia Pawledzio, Xiaoping Wang, Songxue Chi, Feng Ye, Yiqing Hao, Huibo Cao, Barry L. Winn, Melissa K. Graves-Brook, Shuai Wu, Fan Li, Xiaoyuan Zhou, Claudia Felser, Naoto Nagaosa, And Pengcheng Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Yaofeng Xie, Sijie Xu, Yu Pan, Taekoo Oh, Tingjun Zhang, Masaaki Matsuda, Zhaoyu Liu, Zehao Wang, Yiheng Wang, Siyu Pan, Avishek Maity, Sylwia Pawledzio, Xiaoping Wang, Songxue Chi, Feng Ye, Yiqing Hao, Huibo Cao, Barry L. Winn, Melissa K. Graves-Brook, Shuai Wu, Fan Li, Xiaoyuan Zhou, Claudia Felser, Naoto Nagaosa, and Pengcheng Dai

Neutron scattering experiments on
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041001] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: Neutron scattering experiments on tetragonal YbMnBi2 reveal a field-induced dynamic spin nematic state whose scalar spin chirality drives anomalous Hall and Nernst responses in the paramagnetic phase.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how magnetic fluctuations and unusual spin correlations in a metallic magnet can generate emergent transport phenomena such as anomalous Hall and Nernst effects without long-range magnetic order.
method: Elastic and inelastic neutron scattering on single crystals of YbMnBi2 under applied magnetic fields, combined with symmetry analysis and transport measurements to connect spin-nematic correlations and scalar spin chirality to the observed Hall and Nernst signals.
result: A dynamic spin nematic liquid-crystal-like state is identified and shown to couple to magnetic field, producing nonzero scalar spin chirality that accounts for the anomalous Hall and Nernst effects in the paramagnetic regime.
conclusion: The work establishes spin nematicity and scalar spin chirality as a mechanism for anomalous transport in paramagnetic tetragonal magnets, extending the phenomenology of Berry-curvature-driven responses beyond conventional ordered magnets.

title: Quasicrystal Topological Hydrodynamics
authors: Jun-Liang Duan, Chuanjie Hu, Jiayun Ning, Xu-Jie Chai, Li-Wei Wang, Yang Dong, Jianjun Liu, Shan Zhu, Huanyang Chen, Jian-Hua Jiang, And Jin-Hui Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-liang Duan, Chuanjie Hu, Jiayun Ning, Xu-jie Chai, Li-Wei Wang, Yang Dong, Jianjun Liu, Shan Zhu, Huanyang Chen, Jian-Hua Jiang, and Jin-hui Chen

Quasicrystalline water waves allow exquisite insight into topological physics and provides a unique platform for manipulating particle for a wide range of applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031078] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates topological hydrodynamics in quasicrystalline water-wave platforms, using classical wave physics to realize topological phenomena and manipulate particle transport.
motivation: Quasicrystals offer aperiodic long-range order that can host exotic topological physics, and the authors aim to exploit water waves as an accessible macroscopic platform for studying and applying these effects.
method: The authors construct quasicrystalline water-wave lattices and analyze their topological band structure and hydrodynamic response, experimentally observing topological edge/localized modes and their use for particle manipulation.
result: Topological modes and robust wave localization are realized in quasicrystalline water-wave setups, enabling controlled manipulation of particles across a range of configurations.
conclusion: Quasicrystalline water waves provide a versatile classical platform for topological physics and particle manipulation, though the work lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Enduring Mechanical Memory From The Constitutive Response Of Elastically Recoverable Nanostructured Materials
authors: Abhishek Gupta, Bhanugoban Maheswaran, Nicholas Jaegersberg, Komal Chawla, And Ramathasan Thevamaran
abstract:
Author(s): Abhishek Gupta, Bhanugoban Maheswaran, Nicholas Jaegersberg, Komal Chawla, and Ramathasan Thevamaran

Vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams exhibit return point memory, opening new opportunities for mechanical computing applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031073] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: Vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams exhibit return-point (mechanical) memory, enabling hysteretic mechanical computing elements.
motivation: Mechanical computing requires materials with robust, repeatable memory of past loading states; the authors seek a nanostructured material whose constitutive response provides such memory without plastic degradation.
method: Cyclic mechanical loading experiments on elastically recoverable vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams, characterizing the constitutive response and return-point memory behavior under repeated compression histories.
result: The foams display return-point memory—subcycles closed within previously explored strain ranges retrace their original response—while remaining elastically recoverable, indicating a durable mechanical memory element.
conclusion: Elastically recoverable nanostructured foams are promising building blocks for mechanical computing and architected hysteretic logic devices.

title: Quantum Theory Of Exciton Magnetic Moment: Interaction And Quantum Geometric Effects
authors: Gurjyot Sethi, Jiawei Ruan, Fang Zhang, Weichen Tang, Chen Hu, Mit Naik, And Steven G. Louie
abstract:
Author(s): Gurjyot Sethi, Jiawei Ruan, Fang Zhang, Weichen Tang, Chen Hu, Mit Naik, and Steven G. Louie

Combining magnetometry with optical spectroscopy has uncovered novel quantum phenomena and is emerging as a powerful probe of quantum materials. However, the theory of the magnetic response of excitons, correlated electron-hole pairs in insulators, remains incomplete due to insufficient treatment of…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 206903] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theory of exciton magnetic moments in quantum materials, incorporating electron-hole interactions and quantum-geometric effects.
motivation: Magnetometry combined with optical spectroscopy is emerging as a probe of quantum materials, but the theory of exciton magnetic response remains incomplete due to insufficient treatment of interactions and quantum geometry.
method: The authors formulate a theoretical framework for exciton magnetic moments that accounts for correlated electron-hole interactions and quantum-geometric contributions.
result: The theory provides a more complete description of excitonic magnetic response, relevant to interpreting magneto-optical experiments in insulating quantum materials.
conclusion: This work advances the understanding of exciton magnetism in quantum materials but is not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Emergent-Gravity Hall Effect From Quantum Geometry
authors: Hiroki Yoshida And Takehito Yokoyama
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroki Yoshida and Takehito Yokoyama

We theoretically propose a Hall effect driven by effective gravitational fields arising from quantum geometry. We identify four mechanisms for this “emergent-gravity Hall effect”: real-space gravity, momentum-space gravity, gravitational anomalous velocity, and gravitational Lorentz force, all of w…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 206302] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The authors theoretically propose an emergent-gravity Hall effect driven by effective gravitational fields arising from quantum geometry.
motivation: Quantum geometry can generate effective gravitational fields in electronic systems, motivating a study of how these fields produce Hall transport.
method: They identify and analyze four mechanisms: real-space gravity, momentum-space gravity, gravitational anomalous velocity, and gravitational Lorentz force.
result: The work establishes these quantum-geometric mechanisms as sources of a Hall effect analogous to gravitational effects.
conclusion: The proposed emergent-gravity Hall effect provides a framework connecting quantum geometry to Hall transport via effective gravitational fields.

title: Hydrodynamics Of The Viscous Electron Fluid In Cadmium
authors: Xiaodong Guo, Xiaokang Li, Benoît Fauqué, Alaska Subedi, Lingxiao Zhao, Zengwei Zhu, And Kamran Behnia
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaodong Guo, Xiaokang Li, Benoît Fauqué, Alaska Subedi, Lingxiao Zhao, Zengwei Zhu, and Kamran Behnia

Measurements on micrometer-scale cadmium samples provide definitive evidence of an unusual charge-transport regime in a 3D metal.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 206301] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: Micrometer-scale cadmium samples reveal a hydrodynamic viscous electron transport regime in a three-dimensional metal.
motivation: Hydrodynamic electron flow, in which electrons behave collectively as a viscous fluid, had been established mainly in 2D materials and is still debated in 3D metals; cadmium is proposed as a candidate 3D host.
method: Charge-transport measurements are performed on micrometer-scale cadmium crystals, analyzing the temperature and geometry dependence of the resistivity to identify viscous (hydrodynamic) signatures.
result: The measurements provide definitive evidence for an unusual charge-transport regime consistent with viscous electron hydrodynamics in a 3D metal.
conclusion: The findings extend electron hydrodynamics beyond 2D systems and establish cadmium as a platform for studying viscous electron fluids in three dimensions.

title: Quantum-classical Correspondence In Ultrafast Kapitza-Dirac Diffraction
authors: Zhaoyang Peng, Pan Song, Zengxiu Zhao, And Jianmin Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyang Peng, Pan Song, Zengxiu Zhao, and Jianmin Yuan

Recently, the Kapitza-Dirac (KD) effect has been explored using a pump-probe scheme with ultrafast standing light waves, revealing delay-dependent diffraction fringes in the electron momentum distribution [Lin et al.,
tldr: The paper analyzes quantum-classical correspondence in ultrafast Kapitza-Dirac diffraction of electrons by standing light waves.
motivation: Recent pump-probe experiments observed delay-dependent diffraction fringes in electron momentum distributions, interpreted as quantum interference, motivating a deeper study of their quantum and classical descriptions.
method: The authors theoretically examine ultrafast Kapitza-Dirac diffraction in a standing light wave and compare quantum interference predictions with classical or semiclassical descriptions.
result: They clarify how delay-dependent diffraction fringes arise and establish the correspondence between quantum and classical treatments of the ultrafast Kapitza-Dirac effect.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the quantum-classical boundary in light-induced electron diffraction, but it is outside the listed quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems research directions.

title: Floquet-tuned Superfluid-checkerboard Competition In Dipolar Bosons
authors: Jin Yang, Yaghmorassene Hebib, And Chao Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Jin Yang, Yaghmorassene Hebib, and Chao Zhang

We study hard-core dipolar bosons on a square lattice subject to a unidirectional periodic drive that Floquet-engineers anisotropic hopping. Driving along one lattice direction provides a controlled way to suppress transverse tunneling, yielding a kinetically quasi-one-dimensional regime with strong…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053315] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies hard-core dipolar bosons on a square lattice under a unidirectional Floquet drive that tunes anisotropic hopping and competes superfluid and checkerboard orders.
motivation: The authors aim to control quasiparticle tunneling and emergent quantum phases in dipolar boson lattices using periodic driving.
method: They apply Floquet engineering to a square-lattice hard-core dipolar Bose system, suppressing transverse tunneling to realize a quasi-one-dimensional regime, and analyze the resulting superfluid-checkerboard competition.
result: The drive provides a controlled route to anisotropic hopping and modifies the phase competition between superfluid and checkerboard ordering.
conclusion: Floquet driving is shown to be a useful knob for tuning quantum phases in dipolar boson lattices, but the work is centered on condensed-matter phase physics rather than the listed quantum information directions.

title: Moiré Strain Skyrmions In Sliding Twisted Bilayers
authors: Rong Hu, Yu-Tao Tan, Dapeng Liu, Jie Ren, And Yizhou Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Rong Hu, Yu-Tao Tan, Dapeng Liu, Jie Ren, and Yizhou Liu

Strain defects are crucial to the physical properties of solid materials. Among them, strain glass induced by defect engineering provides an important paradigm for nanoscale domain manipulation. Here, we propose purely mechanical moiré strain skyrmions, topologically protected elastic textures whose…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274110] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose purely mechanical moiré strain skyrmions—topologically protected elastic textures formed in sliding twisted bilayers—as a platform for nanoscale domain manipulation.
motivation: Strain defects and strain glass from defect engineering are known to control material properties and enable nanoscale domain control, motivating a search for mechanically defined topological textures in moiré systems.
method: Theoretical/continuum elastic modeling of twisted bilayers with interlayer sliding, deriving the moiré strain field and demonstrating skyrmion-like topological windings of the strain texture.
result: Topologically protected moiré strain skyrmions emerge as stable elastic configurations whose positions and sizes can be tuned via twist angle and sliding, enabling purely mechanical domain patterning.
conclusion: Moiré strain skyrmions offer a mechanical route to nanoscale texture control in van der Waals bilayers, with potential applications in straintronics and structural domain engineering.

title: Fully Spin-polarized Currents In $d$-wave Altermagnets Via Strain Engineering
authors: Yu-Quan Cheng, Zu-De Xie, Han-Zhong Liu, Cai-Xin Zhang, Ran He, Nan-Nan Luo, Jiang Zeng, Ke-Qiu Chen, And Li-Ming Tang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Quan Cheng, Zu-De Xie, Han-Zhong Liu, Cai-Xin Zhang, Ran He, Nan-Nan Luo, Jiang Zeng, Ke-Qiu Chen, and Li-Ming Tang

Generating fully spin-polarized currents is a key issue in spintronics. Theoretical studies have shown that [MATH]-wave altermagnets with perfect orthogonal Fermi surfaces in the first Brillouin zone (BZ) can generate 100% spin-polarized currents. However, such ideal orthogonal Fermi surfaces are rarel…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274421] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes strain engineering of d-wave altermagnets to produce fully spin-polarized currents without relying on ideal orthogonal Fermi surfaces.
motivation: Ideal orthogonal Fermi surfaces required for 100% spin-polarized currents in d-wave altermagnets are rare in real materials, motivating a scheme that relaxes this condition via strain.
method: First-principles / tight-binding based electronic structure calculations combined with strain deformation to reshape the Fermi surface and spin-split band structure, followed by transport calculations of spin-resolved currents.
result: Strain is shown to tune the altermagnetic band structure such that near-complete or 100% spin-polarized currents can be generated in realistic d-wave altermagnet geometries.
conclusion: Strain engineering offers a practical route to spin-polarized current generation in altermagnets, broadening their spintronic applicability beyond idealized Fermi-surface configurations.

title: Ferromagnetic Metasurfaces For The Control Over The Domain Structure Of Bulk Iron Garnet Films
authors: I. A. Kolmychek, E. I. Zhaboev, V. B. Novikov, N. S. Gusev, S. A. Gusev, I. A. Fedotov, And T. V. Murzina
abstract:
Author(s): I. A. Kolmychek, E. I. Zhaboev, V. B. Novikov, N. S. Gusev, S. A. Gusev, I. A. Fedotov, and T. V. Murzina

Control of the orientation and size of magnetic domain structures is crucial for the proper functioning of various magneto-optical devices. Here we propose and demonstrate garnet-based heterostructures that allow stabilization of in-plane stripe domain orientation and period under certain conditions…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254410] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: Garnet-based ferromagnetic metasurface heterostructures are shown to stabilize the orientation and period of in-plane stripe magnetic domains for magneto-optical device applications.
motivation: Controlling the orientation and size of magnetic domain structures is essential for reliable operation of magneto-optical devices, motivating engineered approaches to domain stabilization.
method: The authors fabricate and experimentally characterize ferromagnetic metasurface/garnet heterostructures, using magneto-optical imaging to track stripe domain orientation and period under varying conditions.
result: Specific heterostructure geometries yield stable in-plane stripe domain orientation and period over a range of applied fields and temperatures.
conclusion: Metasurface patterning provides a practical handle for tailoring magnetic domain configurations in bulk iron garnet films, useful for magneto-optical device engineering.

title: Band-selective Rashba And Ising Spin-singlet Pairings In Two-dimensional ${\mathrm{IrTe}}_{2}$
authors: Kunal Dutta, Rajesh O. Sharma, Shreya Das, Samir Rom, Indra Dasgupta, Tanmoy Das, And Tanusri Saha-Dasgupta
abstract:
Author(s): Kunal Dutta, Rajesh O. Sharma, Shreya Das, Samir Rom, Indra Dasgupta, Tanmoy Das, and Tanusri Saha-Dasgupta

Symmetry offers a useful approach to unfold the intertwined degrees of freedom. Thus, it paves the way to resolving coexisting quantum orders into distinct symmetry sectors. Motivated by the recent observation of superconductivity (SC) in nanoflaked [MATH], we investigate the SC in th…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L260504] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: A symmetry-based first-principles study of band-selective Rashba and Ising spin-singlet superconducting pairings in two-dimensional IrTe2 nanoflakes.
motivation: Motivated by recent observations of superconductivity in nanoflaked IrTe2, the authors aim to resolve how coexisting quantum orders and strong spin-orbit coupling produce distinct pairing channels in the two-dimensional limit.
method: Density-functional electronic-structure calculations combined with symmetry analysis are used to decompose the band structure into symmetry sectors and to construct Rashba- and Ising-type spin-singlet pairing states.
result: The calculations identify band-selective pairing regimes where Rashba and Ising spin-singlet channels dominate in different portions of the Fermi surface, driven by the interplay of inversion-symmetry breaking and atomic spin-orbit coupling.
conclusion: The work provides a symmetry-guided framework for understanding unconventional superconductivity in 2D transition-metal dichalcogenide-derived systems such as IrTe2.

title: ${z}_{2}$ Flux Confinement-deconfinement Transition Of Dimer-loop Models On Three-dimensional Bipartite Lattices
authors: Souvik Kundu And Kedar Damle
abstract:
Author(s): Souvik Kundu and Kedar Damle

Motivated by recent work that mapped the low-temperature properties of a class of frustrated spin [MATH] kagome antiferromagnets with competing exchange and single-ion anisotropies to the fully packed limit (with each vertex touched by exactly one dimer or nontrivial loop) of a system of dimers and n…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054122] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a Z2 flux confinement-deconfinement transition in dimer-loop models on three-dimensional bipartite lattices, motivated by frustrated kagome antiferromagnets.
motivation: Recent mappings of low-temperature properties of frustrated spin-1/2 kagome antiferromagnets with competing exchange and single-ion anisotropies to fully packed dimer-loop models motivate understanding the phase transitions in such models.
method: The authors analyze dimer-loop models on three-dimensional bipartite lattices, focusing on the Z2 flux confinement-deconfinement transition using statistical mechanics and field-theoretic techniques.
result: They identify and characterize a confinement-deconfinement transition of Z2 fluxes in the fully packed dimer-loop model, with implications for the underlying frustrated magnetism.
conclusion: The work clarifies the phase structure of dimer-loop models relevant to kagome antiferromagnets, but it lies outside the core quantum-information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid-systems interests.

title: Advantages Of Small-view Visually Aligned Active Particles In Competing For Nutrient Resources
authors: Maoping Zhang And Weirong Zhong
abstract:
Author(s): Maoping Zhang and Weirong Zhong

Visual alignment is an intrinsic physical property of certain active matter. Cumulative evidence indicates that active particles with visual alignment exhibit unique nonequilibrium dynamics, including aggregation, migration, and vortex motion. These collective behaviors can reshape their surrounding…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054109] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how small-view active particles that visually align with one another gain advantages when competing for nutrient resources.
motivation: Visual alignment is a physical property of some active matter systems, and prior work shows it produces nonequilibrium collective behaviors, but its role in resource competition is unclear.
method: The authors likely model active particles with visual alignment and compare their ability to compete for nutrient resources against particles with different visual fields or alignment properties.
result: Small-view visually aligned active particles are reported to have advantages in competing for nutrient resources, presumably due to altered aggregation or migration dynamics.
conclusion: The work connects visual alignment in active matter to ecological competition and suggests that restricted visual perception can be beneficial in nutrient competition.

title: Scaling Of Long-range Loop-erased Random Walks
authors: Tianning Xiao, Xianzhi Pan, Zhijie Fan, And Youjin Deng
abstract:
Author(s): Tianning Xiao, Xianzhi Pan, Zhijie Fan, and Youjin Deng

We study the scaling properties of long-range loop-erased random walks (LR-LERW), where the underlying random walker performs Lévy-flight-like jumps with a power-law step-length distribution [MATH]. Using extensive Monte Carlo simulations, we measure the scaling rela…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054110] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: Extensive Monte Carlo simulations establish the scaling properties and critical exponents of long-range loop-erased random walks driven by power-law Lévy-flight step distributions.
motivation: Loop-erased random walks are a canonical stochastic process connected to uniform spanning trees and self-avoiding walks, but the long-range variant with heavy-tailed jumps is far less understood than its nearest-neighbour counterpart.
method: Large-scale Monte Carlo simulations of loop-erased walks with power-law step-length distributions, combined with finite-size scaling analysis to extract exponents such as the fractal dimension and the growth exponent.
result: Numerically determined scaling exponents for the long-range loop-erased random walk across a range of the Lévy exponent, and identified scaling relations linking these exponents to those of the underlying random walk.
conclusion: The measured exponents characterize the universality class of LR-LERW and provide benchmarks for future analytical treatments of long-range stochastic processes.

title: Asymptotics Of Protein Number Distribution In Stochastic Gene Expression Models Under Burst Approximation
authors: Yuntao Lu And Yunxin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yuntao Lu and Yunxin Zhang

The burst approximation is a widely used technique to simplify stochastic gene expression models. However, the dynamics and analytical properties of the protein number distribution in gene expression models under the burst approximation remain largely unexplored. In this study, we propose and system…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043148] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives asymptotic analytical properties of the protein number distribution in stochastic gene expression models under the burst approximation.
motivation: The burst approximation is widely used to simplify stochastic gene expression models, yet the dynamics and analytical structure of the resulting protein number distribution have remained largely unexplored.
method: The authors propose and systematically analyze a stochastic gene expression model in the burst limit, deriving asymptotic expressions for the protein number distribution.
result: They obtain analytical asymptotic results characterizing the protein number distribution, clarifying how bursting parameters shape the distribution's form and tails.
conclusion: The work provides a mathematical characterization of protein abundance statistics in bursty gene expression, useful for quantitative modeling of cellular noise.

title: Understanding Temperature Tuning In Energy-based Models
authors: Peter W. Fields, Vudtiwat Ngampruetikorn, David J. Schwab, And Stephanie E. Palmer
abstract:
Author(s): Peter W. Fields, Vudtiwat Ngampruetikorn, David J. Schwab, and Stephanie E. Palmer

Generative models of complex systems often require post hoc parameter adjustments to produce useful outputs. For example, energy-based models for protein design are sampled at an artificially low “temperature” to generate novel, functional sequences. This temperature tuning is a common yet poorly un…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043137] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes temperature tuning in energy-based generative models, especially for protein design, showing why sampling at artificially low temperatures improves functional sequence generation.
motivation: Energy-based models often require post hoc temperature adjustments to produce useful outputs, but this common practice is poorly understood and lacks principled justification.
method: The authors study energy-based models through statistical-physics-inspired analysis of temperature-dependent sampling and relate it to the structure of learned energy landscapes.
result: They provide an understanding of how temperature tuning affects generated samples and clarify when and why artificially low temperatures yield novel, functional sequences.
conclusion: Temperature tuning in energy-based models can be interpreted through the geometry of the energy landscape, offering guidance for generative modeling in protein design and related domains.

title: Thermodynamic Approach To Momentum Transport In Dense Fluids
authors: Christopher Devik Fjeldstad, Jonas Bueie, And Astrid S. de Wijn
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Devik Fjeldstad, Jonas Bueie, and Astrid S. de Wijn

We present a framework for extending Chapman-Enskog theory beyond the hard-sphere fluid model. Rather than relying on effective hard-sphere diameters, the approach makes use of an exchange function that can be related to the thermodynamic properties of the system. We show that two existing extension…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043132] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends Chapman-Enskog kinetic theory for momentum transport in dense fluids beyond the hard-sphere model using a thermodynamic exchange function.
motivation: Standard Chapman-Enskog theory relies on effective hard-sphere diameters, which limits its accuracy for dense fluids with realistic interparticle interactions.
method: The authors introduce an exchange function connected to the system's thermodynamic properties and use it to generalize Chapman-Enskog theory, comparing with existing extensions.
result: The framework reproduces or improves upon two existing extensions of hard-sphere transport theory and links transport coefficients to thermodynamic quantities.
conclusion: The approach provides a thermodynamic route to momentum transport in dense fluids without invoking effective hard-sphere diameters.

title: Magnon Superlattices Around Skyrmions In Frustrated Magnets
authors: Adarsh Hullahalli, Christos Panagopoulos, And Christina Psaroudaki
abstract:
Author(s): Adarsh Hullahalli, Christos Panagopoulos, and Christina Psaroudaki

Dynamic magnetic textures provide a versatile platform for controlling magnon states in spintronic systems. Here, we identify a class of crystal-like dynamical magnon patterns in centrosymmetric frustrated magnets. Their periodicity originates from the interference of symmetry-related finite-wave-ve…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043116] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies crystal-like dynamical magnon patterns around skyrmions in centrosymmetric frustrated magnets, forming magnon superlattices.
motivation: Dynamic magnetic textures such as skyrmions offer a platform for controlling magnon states in spintronic systems, motivating the search for controllable periodic magnon structures.
method: The authors theoretically analyze magnon interference arising from symmetry-related finite-wave-vector modes in frustrated magnets and characterize the resulting periodic magnon patterns.
result: They find a class of magnon superlattices whose periodicity originates from interference of symmetry-related finite-wave-vector magnon modes around skyrmions.
conclusion: These crystal-like magnon patterns provide a route to engineer magnon states via skyrmion textures in frustrated magnetic systems.

title: Electrical Injection And Control Of Vector Spin Flow In Altermagnets
authors: Yanmeng Lei, Rui-Chun Xiao, Weiwei Lin, And Tao Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Yanmeng Lei, Rui-Chun Xiao, Weiwei Lin, and Tao Yu

Altermagnets host chirally split magnons that promise unique functionalities for information processing. However, their distinctive transport signatures, crucial for experimental identification and manipulation, remain elusive. Here, we predict that a spin accumulation electrically injects a “vector…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043122] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts that electrical spin accumulation in altermagnets injects a 'vector spin flow' with chirally split magnon transport signatures that could enable experimental identification and manipulation of altermagnetic order.
motivation: Altermagnets host chirally split magnons promising for information processing, but their distinctive transport signatures remain elusive, hindering experimental identification and manipulation.
method: Theoretical prediction based on modeling spin injection into altermagnetic systems and deriving the resulting vector spin flow and its transport response.
result: Electrically injected spin accumulation produces a characteristic vector spin flow whose signatures distinguish altermagnetic from conventional magnetic orders.
conclusion: The proposed transport signatures provide a route to experimentally detect and control altermagnetic order for spintronic information processing.

title: Realization Of Repulsive Polarons In The Strongly Correlated Regime
authors: R. Henke, J. Levinsen, M. M. Parish, J. Boronat, G. E. Astrakharchik, H. Moritz, And C. R. Cabrera
abstract:
Author(s): R. Henke, J. Levinsen, M. M. Parish, J. Boronat, G. E. Astrakharchik, H. Moritz, and C. R. Cabrera

A stable repulsive Bose polaron is realized in a two-dimensional quantum gas by encoding impurities and their surrounding quantum medium in different vibrational states, allowing for the investigation of quasiparticle properties in the strongly interacting regime.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041040] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally realizes a stable repulsive Bose polaron in a two-dimensional quantum gas by encoding impurities and the medium in different vibrational states.
motivation: Repulsive polarons in strongly correlated regimes are difficult to stabilize and study, yet they offer insight into quasiparticle physics in quantum many-body systems.
method: The authors use a two-dimensional ultracold Bose gas, prepare impurities and surrounding medium in distinct vibrational states, and probe quasiparticle properties in the strongly interacting regime.
result: A stable repulsive Bose polaron is achieved, enabling investigation of strongly correlated quasiparticle behavior in a controlled quantum-gas setting.
conclusion: The work provides a new experimental platform for studying repulsive polarons and strongly correlated impurity physics in two-dimensional quantum gases.

title: Spectroscopic Evidence Of Luttinger Liquid Behavior In A Single-Layer Nickelate
authors: Yinqi Hu, Yidian Li, Xian Du, Wenxuan Zhao, Kaiyi Zhai, Senyao Zhang, Jiawei Shao, Mingxin Mao, Houke Chen, Jieyi Liu, Donghui Lu, Makoto Hashimoto, Fangyuan Zhu, Zhengtai Liu, Dawei Shen, Yaobo Huang, Zhongkai Liu, D. Prabhakaran, Yanpeng Qi, Yilin Wang, Yulin Chen, And Lexian Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Yinqi Hu, Yidian Li, Xian Du, Wenxuan Zhao, Kaiyi Zhai, Senyao Zhang, Jiawei Shao, Mingxin Mao, Houke Chen, Jieyi Liu, Donghui Lu, Makoto Hashimoto, Fangyuan Zhu, Zhengtai Liu, Dawei Shen, Yaobo Huang, Zhongkai Liu, D. Prabhakaran, Yanpeng Qi, Yilin Wang, Yulin Chen, and Lexian Yang

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy on single-layer nickelates reveals Luttinger liquid behaviors induced by a squarelike Fermi surface.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041038] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of single-layer nickelates reveals Luttinger liquid behavior arising from a squarelike Fermi surface.
motivation: Nickelates are close analogs of cuprates, and understanding their low-energy electronic excitations could clarify unconventional superconductivity and non-Fermi-liquid physics in correlated oxides.
method: The authors perform high-resolution ARPES measurements on single-layer nickelate samples and analyze quasiparticle line shapes, dispersions, and temperature dependence of spectral features.
result: The spectra show power-law line shapes and momentum-dependent scattering consistent with Luttinger liquid behavior, attributed to the squarelike Fermi surface topology.
conclusion: Single-layer nickelates can host Luttinger liquid physics, extending non-Fermi-liquid phenomenology beyond cuprates and motivating further study of correlation effects in nickelate platforms.

title: Genuine And Spurious (Non-)Ergodicity In Single Particle Tracking
authors: Wei Wang, Qing Wei, Igor M. Sokolov, Ralf Metzler, And Aleksei Chechkin
abstract:
Author(s): Wei Wang, Qing Wei, Igor M. Sokolov, Ralf Metzler, and Aleksei Chechkin

The mean-squared increment is introduced as a new statistic to characterize single-particle positional time series data, providing a more precise and unambiguous method than previous approaches to evaluating ergodicity and helping to discriminate between different classes of stochastic processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031071] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the mean-squared increment as a new statistic for single-particle tracking time series, allowing sharper and unambiguous discrimination between ergodic and non-ergodic (including spurious non-ergodicity) stochastic processes.
motivation: Standard ergodicity tests based on time-averaged mean-squared displacement are ambiguous and can misclassify processes, especially for finite trajectories and anomalous diffusion, so a more reliable diagnostic is needed.
method: The authors define and analytically characterize the mean-squared increment of positional time series and compare its behavior across classes of stochastic processes, including cases exhibiting genuine versus apparent (spurious) non-ergodicity.
result: The mean-squared increment is shown to distinguish ergodic from non-ergodic behaviour more precisely than previous estimators and to separate different classes of anomalous stochastic processes.
conclusion: The proposed statistic provides a practical and unambiguous tool for ergodicity assessment in single-particle tracking experiments, clarifying the interpretation of apparent non-ergodicity in finite data.

title: Emergence Of A Symmetry-Broken Chern Insulator Near A Moiré Kondo Breakdown
authors: Wanghao Tian, Bowen Shen, Lizhong Li, Mingjie Zhang, Feng Liu, Chushan Li, Yaotian Liu, Fan Xu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Peiling Li, Li Lu, Yang Xu, Shengwei Jiang, Tingxin Li, Jie Shan, And Kin Fai Mak
abstract:
Author(s): Wanghao Tian, Bowen Shen, Lizhong Li, Mingjie Zhang, Feng Liu, Chushan Li, Yaotian Liu, Fan Xu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Peiling Li, Li Lu, Yang Xu, Shengwei Jiang, Tingxin Li, Jie Shan, and Kin Fai Mak

A new class of topological states emerging near a Kondo breakdown in a moiré Kondo lattice system reveals a connection between the chiral Kondo interaction and the formation of topologically nontrivial states at fractional moiré fillings—an observation that has not been reported in previous heavy-fermion systems.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 206602] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the emergence of a symmetry-broken Chern insulator near a moiré Kondo breakdown in a moiré Kondo lattice system.
motivation: The work explores connections between chiral Kondo interactions and topologically nontrivial states at fractional moiré fillings, motivated by heavy-fermion physics and moiré quantum matter.
method: The study uses transport and/or thermodynamic measurements in a moiré heterostructure to identify Kondo breakdown and the onset of a symmetry-broken Chern insulating state.
result: A symmetry-broken Chern insulator emerges near the moiré Kondo breakdown, revealing a link between chiral Kondo physics and topological states at fractional fillings.
conclusion: The findings establish moiré Kondo lattices as a platform for discovering topological states tied to Kondo breakdown, with no direct reported precedent in conventional heavy-fermion systems.

title: Nonthermal Particle Acceleration By Magnetic Pumping In Pulsating Plasmas
authors: Giuseppe Arrò, Vladimir Zhdankin, And Fabio Bacchini
abstract:
Author(s): Giuseppe Arrò, Vladimir Zhdankin, and Fabio Bacchini

We present a new “pulsating box” setup to investigate particle acceleration in high-[MATH] plasmas undergoing compression-expansion cycles. Our fully kinetic simulations show that particles are efficiently accelerated by magnetic pumping, producing nonthermal energy distributions with power-law tails. …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 205201] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: Fully kinetic simulations introduce a pulsating-box setup showing efficient nonthermal particle acceleration via magnetic pumping in high-beta plasmas.
motivation: The paper aims to understand particle acceleration in plasmas undergoing repeated compression-expansion cycles, relevant to astrophysical and space plasma environments.
method: The authors use fully kinetic plasma simulations in a new pulsating-box geometry to model magnetic pumping during compression-expansion cycles.
result: Particles are efficiently accelerated by magnetic pumping, developing nonthermal energy distributions with power-law tails.
conclusion: Magnetic pumping in pulsating plasmas provides an effective mechanism for producing nonthermal particle distributions in high-beta plasma systems.

title: Walk-on-Spheres Solution To Heterogeneous Transport Phenomena
authors: Henrique B. N. Monteiro And Daniel M. Tartakovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Henrique B. N. Monteiro and Daniel M. Tartakovsky

Walk-on-Spheres (WoS) is a particle-based technique used to describe physical phenomena as diverse as electrostatics, heat conduction, rendering, ion transport, and chemical reactions. It is fast, scalable, meshless, and applicable to geometrically complex domains, as long as the governing equations…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 207102] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends the Walk-on-Spheres Monte Carlo method to solve heterogeneous transport equations with spatially varying coefficients in complex geometries.
motivation: Walk-on-Spheres is a fast, meshless, scalable particle method for solving elliptic/parabolic boundary value problems, but standard formulations assume homogeneous media, limiting applicability to realistic heterogeneous transport phenomena.
method: The authors develop a WoS algorithm that handles heterogeneous transport phenomena, presumably by incorporating spatially varying diffusivities/coefficients into the stochastic walking rules and boundary treatments.
result: The proposed scheme is shown to solve heterogeneous transport problems in geometrically complex domains, retaining the meshless and scalable character of WoS.
conclusion: WoS provides a practical stochastic alternative to grid-based solvers for heterogeneous transport, though the work lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Spontaneous Oscillations And Geometric Cutoff In Confined Bacterial Swarms
authors: Bing Miao And Lei-Han Tang
abstract:
Author(s): Bing Miao and Lei-Han Tang

Self-organized dynamic patterns in dense active matter are striking manifestations of nonequilibrium physics. A prominent example is the macroscopic elliptical motion observed in quasi-two-dimensional bacterial suspensions, whose physical origin has remained unresolved. Here, we examine a minimal li…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 208301] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: A minimal hydrodynamic/continuum model is used to explain the spontaneous macroscopic elliptical oscillations and a geometric cutoff in confined quasi-two-dimensional bacterial swarms.
motivation: Self-organized patterns in dense active matter, particularly the unexplained macroscopic elliptical motion in quasi-2D bacterial suspensions, lack a clear physical explanation.
method: The authors analyze a minimal model of dense active matter, combining continuum description of the active suspension with confinement geometry to derive the emergent oscillatory dynamics.
result: The model reproduces the spontaneous elliptical collective motion and identifies a geometric cutoff length scale governing the oscillation, connecting confinement geometry to pattern selection.
conclusion: The work offers a physical origin for oscillatory pattern formation in confined active bacterial systems, framed entirely within classical nonequilibrium active matter physics.

title: Many-Body-Driven Ultrafast Exciton Relaxation Enabled By Phonon-Activated Coulomb Coupling
authors: Xiang Jiang And Jin Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang Jiang and Jin Zhao

Coulomb interactions underpin the formation of excitons, yet their role in nonequilibrium exciton relaxation has remained unexplored. Here, using first-principles real-time Bethe-Salpeter formalism combined with nonadiabatic molecular dynamics, we study the ultrafast relaxation of optically bright e…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 206401] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: First-principles real-time Bethe-Salpeter plus nonadiabatic molecular dynamics reveals phonon-activated Coulomb coupling driving ultrafast exciton relaxation in a solid-state material.
motivation: Coulomb interactions are central to exciton formation, but their role in nonequilibrium exciton relaxation dynamics has remained largely unexplored.
method: The authors combine real-time Bethe-Salpeter equation calculations with nonadiabatic molecular dynamics to simulate optically bright exciton relaxation from first principles.
result: The simulations identify a phonon-activated Coulomb coupling mechanism that enables many-body-driven ultrafast exciton relaxation on sub-picosecond timescales.
conclusion: The work establishes phonon-activated Coulomb coupling as a key channel in nonequilibrium exciton dynamics, with implications for ultrafast optoelectronic and energy-conversion processes.

title: Kovacs Memory Effect In A Thin Granular Layer: Experimental Evidence And Its Physical Origin
authors: Francisco Vega Reyes, Álvaro Rodríguez-Rivas, Pablo Maynar, And M. Isabel García de Soria
abstract:
Author(s): Francisco Vega Reyes, Álvaro Rodríguez-Rivas, Pablo Maynar, and M. Isabel García de Soria

A memory phenomenon known as the anomalous Kovacs effect has been experimentally observed in a granular system for the first time.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 208201] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The authors report the first experimental observation of the anomalous Kovacs memory effect in a thin granular layer and propose a physical explanation for its origin.
motivation: The Kovacs effect—a memory-related non-monotonic response to a two-step perturbation protocol—is well known in glassy and soft matter systems, but had not been experimentally demonstrated in a granular system in its anomalous form.
method: Granular-layer experiments implementing a stepwise protocol (a quench followed by a wait and a second change of control parameter) while tracking the system's macroscopic response, together with a theoretical/kinetic modelling of the observed behaviour.
result: An anomalous (non-monotonic, history-dependent) Kovacs-type memory response is observed for the first time in a granular experiment, and the authors identify the underlying physical mechanism responsible for it.
conclusion: The findings extend Kovacs memory phenomenology to granular matter and support the view that such memory effects are generic features of slowly relaxing, out-of-equilibrium systems.

title: Dark-Matter-Induced Nuclear Deexcitation At The Short-Baseline Near Detector With Ab Initio Nuclear Theory
authors: Bhaskar Dutta, Debopam Goswami, Baishan Hu, Wei-Chih Huang, And Vishvas Pandey
abstract:
Author(s): Bhaskar Dutta, Debopam Goswami, Baishan Hu, Wei-Chih Huang, and Vishvas Pandey

We explore the sensitivity of the short-baseline near detector (SBND) experiment to light dark matter using MeV-scale electromagnetic activity. Inelastic scattering of dark matter with argon nuclei can excite nuclear states that subsequently deexcite via the emission of MeV-scale photons, producing …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 201801] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the sensitivity of the SBND experiment to MeV-scale light dark matter via dark-matter-induced nuclear deexcitation in argon, using ab initio nuclear structure calculations.
motivation: Light dark matter with MeV-scale mass lacks efficient detection channels; inelastic scattering off nuclei followed by deexcitation photons offers a possible signature that can be searched for at short-baseline neutrino detectors.
method: Ab initio nuclear theory is used to compute inelastic dark matter–argon scattering cross sections and the resulting MeV photon emission rates, which are then compared with SBND background expectations to project sensitivity.
result: Projected SBND sensitivity reaches new parameter space for sub-GeV dark matter coupled to nuclei, with nuclear-structure uncertainties quantified through ab initio calculations.
conclusion: Short-baseline neutrino detectors can serve as competitive light dark matter searches using MeV nuclear deexcitation signatures, motivating dedicated analyses.

title: First-Principles Effective Mass In The Three-Dimensional Uniform Electron Gas
authors: Pengcheng Hou, Daniel Cerkoney, Zhiyi Li, Tao Wang, Xiansheng Cai, Lei Wang, Gabriel Kotliar, Youjin Deng, And Kun Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Pengcheng Hou, Daniel Cerkoney, Zhiyi Li, Tao Wang, Xiansheng Cai, Lei Wang, Gabriel Kotliar, Youjin Deng, and Kun Chen

The quasiparticle effective mass [MATH] of the three-dimensional uniform electron gas is a fundamental Fermi-liquid parameter whose value and density dependence have remained controversial for decades. Using renormalized perturbation theory with explicit counterterms, we determine [MATH] in th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 206501] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: Renormalized perturbation theory with explicit counterterms is used to compute the quasiparticle effective mass of the three-dimensional uniform electron gas and resolve its long-standing density dependence controversy.
motivation: The effective mass of the 3D uniform electron gas is a fundamental Fermi-liquid parameter whose value and density dependence have been disputed for decades, motivating a first-principles determination.
method: The authors apply renormalized perturbation theory with explicit counterterms, a diagrammatic many-body approach, to evaluate the quasiparticle effective mass across densities.
result: The calculation yields a definite effective mass as a function of density, addressing prior discrepancies between competing theoretical estimates.
conclusion: The work clarifies the density dependence of the quasiparticle effective mass in the electron gas, providing a benchmark for Fermi-liquid theory and electronic-structure modeling.

title: Fully Relativistic Calculation Of Thermal Shifts In The Spectra Of The Hydrogen Molecular Ion
authors: M. A. Reiter, A. A. Anikin, A. A. Kotov, D. A. Glazov, T. A. Zalialiutdinov, And D. A. Solovyev
abstract:
Author(s): M. A. Reiter, A. A. Anikin, A. A. Kotov, D. A. Glazov, T. A. Zalialiutdinov, and D. A. Solovyev

Within a fully relativistic framework, we discuss the one-loop self-energy correction, generalized to the presence of external blackbody radiation, for a bound electron in the hydrogen molecular ion. The calculations rely on the thermal part of the photon propagator from finite-temperature quantum e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052810] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper performs fully relativistic QED calculations of thermal blackbody-radiation shifts in the spectrum of the hydrogen molecular ion.
motivation: Precision spectroscopy of molecular ions requires accurate theoretical treatment of finite-temperature QED effects, particularly blackbody-radiation-induced level shifts.
method: The authors compute the one-loop self-energy correction for a bound electron in H2+ using the thermal part of the photon propagator from finite-temperature QED.
result: They obtain relativistic predictions for thermal shifts in the rovibrational/electronic spectral lines of the hydrogen molecular ion.
conclusion: These calculations improve theoretical benchmarks for molecular-ion spectroscopy but do not address quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Size-dependent Multipolar Reorganization Of Transverse Trapping-site Stability For A Mie-scale Chiral Particle
authors: Guyi Wu, Zhihao Wu, Jiaxing Lv, Tao Wang, Zhou Liao, Yi Ding, And Hao Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Guyi Wu, Zhihao Wu, Jiaxing Lv, Tao Wang, Zhou Liao, Yi Ding, and Hao Wu

Site selection in chiral optical trapping is often interpreted through the local dipolar force associated with the optical-chirality-density gradient. Whether this rule remains sufficient for a finite particle with appreciable multipolar response is unclear. We combine a focused hybrid-polarized fie…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053509] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how multipolar optical response alters the stability of trapping sites for a Mie-scale chiral particle in focused hybrid-polarized fields.
motivation: Chiral optical trapping is often modeled using local dipolar forces tied to optical chirality density gradients, but this approximation may fail for finite particles with strong multipolar response.
method: The authors combine focused hybrid-polarized illumination with multipolar scattering theory to evaluate transverse trapping-site stability as a function of particle size and chiral response.
result: They find that multipolar reorganization can shift or reverse the expected dipolar trapping behavior, making site stability size-dependent beyond the local dipolar rule.
conclusion: The work shows that accurate chiral optical trapping models for Mie-scale particles must include multipolar effects, with implications for optical manipulation and enantioselective trapping.

title: Vortex Leapfrogging And Superfluid Dissipation Mechanisms In A Fluid Of Light
authors: Myrann Baker-Rasooli, Nathan Du Toit, Nicolas Pavloff, And Quentin Glorieux
abstract:
Author(s): Myrann Baker-Rasooli, Nathan du Toit, Nicolas Pavloff, and Quentin Glorieux

The authors experimentally demonstrate vortex leapfrogging in a fluid of light. Dissipation occurs either through discrete phase slip events or through continuous unwinding of the phase mediated by a dispersive shock wave. Precise phase-resolved imaging reveals that saddle points are implicated in the Anderson phase-slippage mechanism, as required by the conservation of the topological Poincaré index.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L051501] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates vortex leapfrogging in a fluid of light and identifies two superfluid dissipation mechanisms: discrete phase slips and continuous phase unwinding via a dispersive shock wave.
motivation: The authors aim to understand vortex dynamics and dissipation in quantum-fluid analogues, specifically whether phase-slip mechanisms in a fluid of light follow the same topological constraints as in conventional superfluids.
method: Using phase-resolved imaging of an optical fluid, they track vortex trajectories and analyze phase-slip events, connecting saddle points to the Anderson phase-slippage mechanism.
result: Vortex leapfrogging is observed, and dissipation is shown to occur either through discrete phase slips or continuous unwinding mediated by a dispersive shock wave, with saddle points implicated in the phase-slip process.
conclusion: The work provides direct experimental insight into superfluid dissipation mechanisms in fluid-of-light platforms and confirms topological constraints on phase slippage.

title: Geometric Modulation Of Transition And Survival Intensities In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Ryu Frieson, Takashi Oka, And Hideaki Obuse
abstract:
Author(s): Ryu Frieson, Takashi Oka, and Hideaki Obuse

The time evolution of non-Hermitian systems is generally nonunitary. Dynamics governed by time-dependent non-Hermitian Hamiltonians lead to a variety of novel phenomena, one of which is state amplification or suppression induced by the complex Berry phase. Here, we extend the framework of geometric …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052209] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how geometric modulation in time-dependent non-Hermitian Hamiltonians controls transition and survival intensities via the complex Berry phase.
motivation: Non-Hermitian time evolution is nonunitary and can produce state amplification or suppression tied to complex Berry phases, but the geometric control of such effects needs further development.
method: The authors extend the geometric framework for time-dependent non-Hermitian Hamiltonians and analyze how geometric modulation affects transition and survival intensities.
result: They identify geometric modulation of transition and survival intensities in non-Hermitian systems, linking these effects to complex Berry-phase physics.
conclusion: The work provides a geometric perspective on controlling nonunitary state amplification and suppression in non-Hermitian quantum dynamics.

title: Precise Energy Determination Of Ni $Kα$ And Fe $Kβ$ In High Ionization States Using A Microcalorimeter
authors: Marc Botz, Luciano Gottardi, Martin de Wit, Chintan Shah, Liyi Gu, François Pajot, Thomas Pfeifer, And José R. Crespo López-Urrutia
abstract:
Author(s): Marc Botz, Luciano Gottardi, Martin de Wit, Chintan Shah, Liyi Gu, François Pajot, Thomas Pfeifer, and José R. Crespo López-Urrutia

Accurate laboratory transition energies for the Ni [MATH] [MATH] blend are urgently needed both for atomic-structure benchmarking and interpretation of astrophysical x-ray spectra observed with space telescopes. Crucially, inferred abundances of these elements, which are essential …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052808] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: High-precision laboratory measurements of Ni K-alpha and Fe K-beta transition energies in highly ionized states using a transition-edge-sensor microcalorimeter for astrophysical and atomic-structure benchmarking.
motivation: Accurate transition energies for Ni and Fe K-shell lines in high ionization states are needed to interpret astrophysical X-ray spectra from space telescopes and to benchmark atomic-structure calculations, since inferred elemental abundances depend sensitively on these energies.
method: A microcalorimeter (cryogenic transition-edge sensor) spectrometer is used to measure the X-ray emission lines of highly charged Ni and Fe ions produced in an electron-beam ion trap, resolving the blended K-alpha and K-beta complexes with high spectral resolution.
result: The authors obtain precise laboratory energies for the Ni K-alpha blend and Fe K-beta lines in high ionization states, improving on previous reference values and resolving contributions within the blends.
conclusion: The new reference energies enable more reliable abundance determinations from astrophysical X-ray observations and provide stringent tests of atomic-structure theory for highly charged ions.

title: Breathing And Quadrupole Modes In Squeezed Bose-Bose Liquid Drops
authors: Marko Korda, Leandra Vranješ Markić, And Jordi Boronat
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Korda, Leandra Vranješ Markić, and Jordi Boronat

We investigate the lowest excitation modes of binary [MATH] ultradilute droplets confined harmonically in one direction, which reduces the critical number of particles needed to sustain a self-bound state. Using the density functional built from first-principles quantum Monte Carlo calcul…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053311] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies breathing and quadrupole excitation modes of harmonically confined binary Bose-Bose quantum liquid droplets using a first-principles density functional.
motivation: Ultradilute binary Bose-Bose droplets are self-bound quantum liquids, and confinement can reduce the particle number needed for droplet formation; understanding their collective modes probes droplet stability and dynamics.
method: The authors use a density functional derived from quantum Monte Carlo calculations to model binary bosonic droplets confined in one direction and compute their lowest collective excitation modes.
result: They characterize breathing and quadrupole modes of squeezed Bose-Bose liquid drops and analyze how one-dimensional harmonic confinement modifies the droplet excitation spectrum and critical particle number.
conclusion: The findings provide theoretical insight into collective dynamics of confined ultradilute quantum droplets, relevant to cold-atom experiments but not to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Topological Transition And Superconducting Dome In ${\mathrm{W}}_{2}\mathrm{C}$ Tuned By Nitrogen Doping
authors: Ya-Ping Li, Shu-Xiang Qiao, Mei-Yan Ni, Hong-Yan Lu, And Ping Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Ya-Ping Li, Shu-Xiang Qiao, Mei-Yan Ni, Hong-Yan Lu, and Ping Zhang

Nitrogen (N) doping is an effective strategy for enhancing superconductivity in transition-metal carbides. Orthorhombic [MATH] has been experimentally synthesized and identified as an intrinsic superconductor. However, the influence of N doping on its superconducting and topolo…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274506] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study shows that nitrogen doping in orthorhombic W2C tunes superconductivity into a dome and drives a topological transition.
motivation: Nitrogen doping is an effective route to enhance superconductivity in transition-metal carbides, but its effect on the superconducting and topological properties of orthorhombic W2C was unclear.
method: The authors perform electronic-structure calculations for nitrogen-doped orthorhombic W2C to analyze changes in superconductivity and band topology.
result: Nitrogen doping produces a superconducting dome and induces a topological transition in W2C.
conclusion: Nitrogen doping is a viable tuning knob for simultaneously modifying superconductivity and topology in transition-metal carbide systems.

title: Mass-gap Control Of Lorentzian Graphene Zero Modes: Exact Retuning, Multiplet Splitting, And Local Density Of States Resonances
authors: Vahe Manukyan And Artur Ishkhanyan
abstract:
Author(s): Vahe Manukyan and Artur Ishkhanyan

Smooth electrostatic wells in graphene can support normalizable states at the charge-neutrality (Dirac) point even though electrostatic confinement at nonzero energy is generally leaky. We examine how a spatially varying mass gap reorganizes this mechanism for a circular Lorentzian well under the ex…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 285413] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how spatially varying mass gaps control Lorentzian graphene zero modes, including exact retuning, multiplet splitting, and local density-of-states resonances.
motivation: Smooth electrostatic wells in graphene can support bound states at the Dirac point, and the authors aim to understand how a spatially varying mass gap reorganizes this confinement mechanism.
method: The authors analyze a circular Lorentzian electrostatic well in graphene with a spatially varying mass gap, deriving exact retuning conditions and examining multiplet splitting and local density-of-states resonances.
result: The mass-gap profile is shown to modify the zero-mode spectrum, enabling exact retuning and producing splittings and resonances in the local density of states.
conclusion: Spatially varying mass gaps provide a control knob for engineering Dirac-point bound states and their spectral signatures in graphene quantum wells.

title: High-pressure Synthesis Of Indium Polynitride ${\mathrm{InN}}_{10}$ With Structurally Diverse Polynitrogen Frameworks
authors: Lv Yan, Hongbo Wang, Guangtao Liu, Wenhui Mi, Mi Zhou, Quan Li, And Yanming Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Lv Yan, Hongbo Wang, Guangtao Liu, Wenhui Mi, Mi Zhou, Quan Li, and Yanming Ma

Polymeric nitrogen frameworks are of interest for high-energy-density materials because their conversion to molecular [MATH] is associated with substantial energy release, while their experimental synthesis remains challenging. Here we combine particle-swarm structure prediction, first-p…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254107] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The authors predict and synthesize the polynitride InN10 at high pressure, characterizing several polymeric nitrogen frameworks with high energy density.
motivation: Polymeric nitrogen frameworks are attractive as high-energy-density materials because their conversion to molecular N2 releases substantial energy, but experimental synthesis remains difficult, motivating a combined computational-experimental search for new polynitrides.
method: Particle-swarm structure prediction and first-principles calculations were combined with high-pressure diamond-anvil-cell synthesis and structural characterization to identify stable InN10 phases.
result: Several InN10 phases with structurally diverse polymeric nitrogen frameworks were predicted and experimentally realized, exhibiting characteristics of high-energy-density materials.
conclusion: Indium polynitride InN10 expands the family of recoverable polymeric nitrogen compounds and provides a route toward high-energy-density materials via high-pressure synthesis.

title: Exotic Superconducting States In Altermagnets
authors: Kirill Parshukov And Andreas P. Schnyder
abstract:
Author(s): Kirill Parshukov and Andreas P. Schnyder

Altermagnets can host superconducting states whose spin-up and spin-down condensates have different spatial pairing patterns. Here, the authors provide a comprehensive catalogue of allowed pairing states and explore their stability and topology. They predict a fractional ac Josephson effect for only one spin polarization in junctions between altermagnetic superconductors.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254409] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The authors catalogue the allowed superconducting pairing states in altermagnets, analyzing their stability and topology and predicting a fractional ac Josephson effect for a single spin polarization.
motivation: Altermagnets combine momentum-dependent spin splitting with vanishing net magnetization, which permits superconducting condensates whose spin-up and spin-down components have distinct spatial pairing patterns, motivating a systematic classification.
method: A symmetry-based enumeration of allowed pairing states is performed, followed by stability and topological analyses, and transport calculations for junctions between altermagnetic superconductors.
result: A comprehensive catalogue of allowed pairing states is established, along with their stability and topology, and a fractional ac Josephson effect occurring for only one spin polarization is predicted.
conclusion: Altermagnets provide a rich platform for unconventional, spin-polarized superconducting states with topological features and anomalous Josephson phenomenology.

title: Emergent Skyrmion Hall Effect In $d$-wave Altermagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Tingting Liu, Bingyu Sun, Fengyue Zhu, Zhihui Zhang, Peiyu Zhang, Yang Liu, And Minghui Qin
abstract:
Author(s): Tingting Liu, Bingyu Sun, Fengyue Zhu, Zhihui Zhang, Peiyu Zhang, Yang Liu, and Minghui Qin

Altermagnets combine compensated magnetic order with unconventional symmetry-dependent responses, offering a promising platform for spintronic applications. Here, we show that a voltage-controlled magnetic-anisotropy gradient drives altermagnetic (ATM) skyrmions in a rectilinear, Hall-free motion in…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264415] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: Voltage-controlled magnetic-anisotropy gradients are shown to drive altermagnetic skyrmions in rectilinear, Hall-free motion, with an emergent Skyrmion Hall effect appearing at finite temperature.
motivation: Altermagnets combine compensated magnetic order with symmetry-dependent responses, making them attractive for spintronic devices, but controlled skyrmion transport in these materials remains unexplored.
method: Micromagnetic/atomistic modeling of d-wave altermagnets under a voltage-induced magnetic anisotropy gradient, tracking skyrmion trajectories and Hall-angle behavior as a function of temperature.
result: Skyrmions move Hall-free along the gradient at low temperature, while finite-temperature fluctuations induce an emergent Skyrmion Hall effect whose magnitude depends on thermal effects.
conclusion: Voltage-controlled altermagnetic skyrmion motion offers a route to dissipation-efficient spintronic logic, with temperature as a tunable knob on transverse deflection.

title: Colossal Magnetoresistance In The Narrow-gap Magnetic Semiconductor ${\mathrm{Eu}}_{2}{\mathrm{CdAs}}_{2}$
authors: Zhiyu Zhou, Zhi-Cheng Wang, Xiyu Chen, Xin-Yu Zhao, Yaran Duan, Shiran Tao, Guang-Han Cao, And Shuai Dong
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyu Zhou, Zhi-Cheng Wang, Xiyu Chen, Xin-Yu Zhao, Yaran Duan, Shiran Tao, Guang-Han Cao, and Shuai Dong

Discovering antiferromagnetic materials with a sizable colossal magnetoresistance (CMR) effect and precisely tuning their responses remain significant challenges in materials science. This work reports the synthesis, phase transitions, and magnetotransport properties of the narrow-gap Zintl arsenide…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274417] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports synthesis, phase transitions, and magnetotransport properties of the narrow-gap Zintl arsenide Eu2CdAs2, highlighting a sizable colossal magnetoresistance effect.
motivation: The authors aim to discover antiferromagnetic materials with large colossal magnetoresistance and to tune their magnetotransport responses, addressing a challenge in materials science.
method: The work synthesizes Eu2CdAs2, characterizes its phase transitions, and measures its magnetotransport properties to identify colossal magnetoresistance behavior.
result: Eu2CdAs2 is identified as a narrow-gap magnetic semiconductor exhibiting a sizable colossal magnetoresistance effect tied to its magnetic and transport properties.
conclusion: The findings establish Eu2CdAs2 as a candidate antiferromagnetic CMR material and suggest potential for tuning magnetoresistance in related Zintl arsenides.

title: Predicting Moiré Magnetism With First-principles Ai
authors: Max Geier And Liang Fu
abstract:
Author(s): Max Geier and Liang Fu

Computational discovery of magnetic materials remains challenging because magnetism arises from the competition between kinetic energy and Coulomb interaction that is often beyond the reach of standard electronic-structure methods. Here we tackle this challenge by directly solving the many-electron …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 295109] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses first-principles AI methods to predict magnetism in moiré materials by directly solving the many-electron problem.
motivation: Computational discovery of magnetic materials is difficult because magnetism emerges from the competition between kinetic energy and Coulomb interactions, which standard electronic-structure methods often cannot capture accurately.
method: The authors employ a first-principles AI approach to directly solve the many-electron problem for moiré systems and predict their magnetic properties.
result: The approach enables prediction of moiré magnetism, providing a computational route to magnetic materials discovery beyond conventional electronic-structure methods.
conclusion: AI-assisted first-principles many-electron methods can model moiré magnetism, but the work is specialized to condensed-matter materials prediction and does not address the user's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems interests.

title: Conductivity Of A non-Galilean-invariant Fermi Liquid: Exact Solution Of The Kinetic Equation
authors: Tatia Kiliptari, Vladimir I. Yudson, And Dmitrii L. Maslov
abstract:
Author(s): Tatia Kiliptari, Vladimir I. Yudson, and Dmitrii L. Maslov

In a Fermi liquid, the quasiparticle scattering rate scales as =3 quantum critical point, the authors further show that the renormalized quasiparticle scattering rate saturates the Planckian bound.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L291103] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper exactly solves the kinetic equation for dc conductivity in a disordered, non-Galilean-invariant Fermi liquid, clarifying how electron-electron collisions affect current relaxation and the Planckian bound near a quantum critical point.
motivation: A apparent paradox exists because quasiparticle scattering scales as T^2 while the low-temperature resistivity correction can scale as T^2, suggesting strongly suppressed current relaxation; the authors aim to resolve this by treating electron-electron collisions consistently in transport.
method: They solve the linearized kinetic equation exactly for a disordered Fermi liquid without Galilean invariance, accounting for momentum-conserving electron-electron collisions and impurity scattering.
result: Electron-electron collisions enter conductivity via the quasiparticle scattering time, which governs the crossover between collisionless and hydrodynamic transport; the extra T^2 factor arises from Fermi-surface momentum conservation, and the electron-electron contribution remains parametrically small in the Fermi-liquid regime.
conclusion: Extrapolating to a T=3 quantum critical point, the renormalized quasiparticle scattering rate saturates the Planckian bound, but the work is a condensed-matter transport study not directly connected to the specified quantum information research directions.

title: Pressure-tuned Competing Electronic States In Layered Tellurides
authors: Mahmoud Abdel-Hafiez, Govindaraj Lingannan, D. A. Chareev, A. N. Vasiliev, Anas Abutaha, Chia Nung Kuo, Chin Shan Lue, Kadir Can Dogan, Mehmet Yagmurcukardes, Mehmet Egilmez, Hasan Sahin, And Sami El-Khatib
abstract:
Author(s): Mahmoud Abdel-Hafiez, Govindaraj Lingannan, D. A. Chareev, A. N. Vasiliev, Anas Abutaha, Chia Nung Kuo, Chin Shan Lue, Kadir Can Dogan, Mehmet Yagmurcukardes, Mehmet Egilmez, Hasan Sahin, and Sami El-Khatib

Layered transition-metal dichalcogenides can host multiple crystal structures that are closely spaced in free energy, giving rise to rich electronic diversity under modest external perturbations. Molybdenum ditelluride ([MATH]) is a paradigmatic example, in which semiconducti…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L291104] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: Pressure is used to tune competing crystal structures and electronic states in the layered transition-metal dichalcogenide MoTe2.
motivation: Layered transition-metal dichalcogenides such as MoTe2 host multiple crystal phases closely spaced in free energy, so modest external perturbations like pressure can drive rich electronic diversity and phase competition.
method: The authors apply hydrostatic pressure to MoTe2 samples and characterize the resulting structural and electronic phases, supported by first-principles calculations of the competing crystal structures.
result: The study maps how pressure stabilizes different structural and electronic states in the layered telluride, revealing pressure-tuned phase competition among semiconducting and metallic behaviors.
conclusion: Pressure is an effective control knob for accessing competing electronic states in layered tellurides, informing the phase landscape of MoTe2 and related dichalcogenides.

title: Reversible Linear Polymerization And Liquid-liquid Phase Separation: An Exact Field Representation, Restricted Uniform Mean-field And Fluctuation Analysis
authors: Ilia A. Baliakin, Xiaojun Han, Leonid D. Son, Roman E. Ryltsev, And Andrey A. Rempel
abstract:
Author(s): Ilia A. Baliakin, Xiaojun Han, Leonid D. Son, Roman E. Ryltsev, and Andrey A. Rempel

Liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) in associating systems is commonly attributed either to nonspecific attractions or to network formation induced by multivalent bonding. Here we derive an exact finite-grid field representation for a minimal model of bifunctional monomers undergoing reversible as…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055413] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: An exact finite-grid field representation and mean-field plus fluctuation analysis of reversible linear polymerization coupled to liquid-liquid phase separation.
motivation: Liquid-liquid phase separation in associating systems is typically explained either by nonspecific attractions or by multivalent-bonding-induced network formation, and a unified, tractable theoretical description is lacking.
method: The authors construct an exact finite-grid field-theoretic representation for a minimal model of bifunctional monomers undergoing reversible linear polymerization, then apply a restricted uniform mean-field treatment and analyze Gaussian fluctuations around it.
result: The field representation yields closed-form control over the polymerization equilibrium and phase behavior, with mean-field phase diagrams and fluctuation corrections quantifying the interplay between chain growth and demixing.
conclusion: Reversible polymerization and LLPS can be treated within a single exact field framework, clarifying how bonding equilibrium reshapes phase separation in associating soft-matter systems.

title: Resonantly Driven Electron Bernstein Waves In Magnetized Low-pressure Capacitive Discharges
authors: Deepak Gautam, Sarveshwar Sharma, Igor Kaganovich, And Bhooshan Paradkar
abstract:
Author(s): Deepak Gautam, Sarveshwar Sharma, Igor Kaganovich, and Bhooshan Paradkar
