[Phys. Rev. E 114, L053202] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies resonantly driven electron Bernstein waves in mildly magnetized low-pressure capacitively coupled plasma discharges.
motivation: The authors aim to understand wave physics and discharge dynamics in magnetized capacitive plasmas, a regime relevant to plasma processing and fundamental discharge physics.
method: The work uses theoretical/analytical modeling and likely particle-in-cell or fluid simulations of capacitively coupled plasma discharges under mild magnetization.
result: The paper identifies resonantly driven electron Bernstein wave excitation and characterizes its role in the discharge dynamics.
conclusion: The findings clarify magnetized CCP physics but have no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Structure Of Higher-order Interactions Controls Oscillation Death And Multistability In Excitable Networks
authors: Shenbagavalli V, Dianavinnarasi Joseph, And Suresh Kumarasamy
abstract:
Author(s): Shenbagavalli V, Dianavinnarasi Joseph, and Suresh Kumarasamy

We study coupled FitzHugh-Nagumo oscillators on a small-world network in which the activator and the inhibitor diffuse through independent channels, with an added three-body coupling whose structure is varied among an all-to-all form, a simplicial complex built on the network triangles, and a random…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054212] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how higher-order three-body coupling structures affect oscillation death and multistability in networks of coupled FitzHugh-Nagumo oscillators.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how the structure of higher-order interactions, beyond pairwise coupling, controls collective dynamics such as oscillation suppression and multistability in excitable networks.
method: They model coupled FitzHugh-Nagumo oscillators on a small-world network with independent activator/inhibitor diffusion channels and compare all-to-all, simplicial-complex, and random three-body coupling structures.
result: The structure of the higher-order interactions is found to qualitatively control the onset of oscillation death and the emergence of multistable regimes.
conclusion: Higher-order interaction architecture is a key determinant of dynamical regimes in excitable oscillator networks, with implications for complex systems beyond pairwise coupling.

title: Mechanical Pairing And Self-assembled Chains Of Nonconvex Granular Rotors
authors: Thomas Barois, Mélanie Labiausse, Jean-François Boudet, Juho S. Lintuvuori, And Hamid Kellay
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Barois, Mélanie Labiausse, Jean-François Boudet, Juho S. Lintuvuori, and Hamid Kellay

Combining experiments and simulations, this paper explores the collective behavior of active granular rotors. It is shown that an effective attractive interaction controlled by rotational activity and particle shape leads to the particles’ self-assembly into chainlike structures.

#AdvancingField #TheoryExperiment


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055409] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: Experiments and simulations show that nonconvex active granular rotors develop an effective rotation- and shape-controlled attraction that drives them to self-assemble into chainlike structures.
motivation: Active granular matter is a rich testbed for collective behavior, but the mechanisms by which rotational activity and particle shape generate effective interactions between macroscopic driven particles remain poorly understood.
method: The authors combine tabletop experiments on shaken nonconvex granular rotors with numerical simulations of the same system to map out collective dynamics and effective interactions.
result: They find an effective attractive interaction whose strength depends on rotational activity and particle geometry, leading to spontaneous formation of chainlike assemblies and mechanical pairing.
conclusion: Shape and activity alone can engineer tunable effective interactions in classical active matter, offering a design principle for self-assembled structures at the granular scale.

title: Countoscope For Self-propelled Particles
authors: Tristan Cerdin, Talia Calazans, C. Douarche, And Sophie Marbach
abstract:
Author(s): Tristan Cerdin, Talia Calazans, C. Douarche, and Sophie Marbach

Particle number fluctuations [MATH], measured in virtual observation boxes of an image or a simulation, offer a way to quantify particle dynamics when particle tracking is impractical, such as in high-density systems. While traditionally limited to equilibrium diffusive systems, we extend this appro…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054116] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends the countoscope method, based on particle-number fluctuations in virtual observation boxes, from equilibrium diffusive systems to self-propelled particles.
motivation: Particle tracking is often impractical in high-density systems, and existing countoscope approaches were limited to equilibrium diffusive dynamics, leaving active matter systems unaddressed.
method: The authors generalize the countoscope framework to analyze particle number fluctuations of self-propelled particles in virtual boxes within images or simulations.
result: The extension enables quantification of particle dynamics for active/self-propelled systems without requiring individual particle tracking.
conclusion: The work provides a practical statistical-physics tool for characterizing dense active matter, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Mean-field Theory For The Three-state Active Lattice Gas Model
authors: Ana L. N. Dias, Ronald Dickman, And Tiago Venzel Rosembach
abstract:
Author(s): Ana L. N. Dias, Ronald Dickman, and Tiago Venzel Rosembach

We develop a mean-field description including spatial structure for a simplified version of the three-state active matter model studied by Venzel et al. [
tldr: The paper develops a spatially structured mean-field theory for a three-state active lattice gas model and numerically integrates the resulting coupled nonlinear equations on a triangular lattice.
motivation: The work aims to extend mean-field descriptions of active matter by including spatial structure for a simplified three-state model previously studied by Venzel et al.
method: The authors derive a triangular lattice of coupled nonlinear differential equations and integrate them numerically.
result: The analysis yields a mean-field characterization of the model's collective behavior, though the abstract does not specify quantitative phase boundaries or critical behavior.
conclusion: The paper contributes to classical active matter theory but has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Resetting-based Designated Information Distribution
authors: Xiaojuan Ma, Yan Wang, And Indranil Gupta
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaojuan Ma, Yan Wang, and Indranil Gupta

For a network of [MATH] nodes under random gossip dynamics, we show that by introducing the additional resetting mechanism (with rate [MATH]) to a designated subset of [MATH] nodes, the expected sum of all node values is asymptotically equal to [MATH] times the sum of the initial values of the [MATH] des…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054309] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how stochastic resetting applied to a designated subset of nodes in a random gossip network controls the asymptotic distribution of information across all nodes.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how intentionally resetting selected nodes can shape the long-time aggregate behavior of values propagated through random gossip dynamics.
method: They study a network of M nodes with random gossip interactions and introduce a resetting mechanism at rate r for K designated nodes, then derive the asymptotic expected sum of all node values.
result: They show that the expected total node value becomes asymptotically proportional to the sum of the initial values of the K designated nodes.
conclusion: Resetting a chosen subset of nodes provides a tunable mechanism for designated information distribution in gossip networks.

title: Parity-controlled Emergence Of Ordered Phases On Hierarchical Lattices
authors: Sumitra Rudra, Damien Foster, And Sanjay Kumar
abstract:
Author(s): Sumitra Rudra, Damien Foster, and Sanjay Kumar

We determine the complete phase structure of the frustrated Ising model with competing nearest-neighbor, next-nearest-neighbor, and four-spin plaquette interactions, using real-space renormalization on four members of hierarchical square lattices characterized by their coarse-graining scales. The co…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L052102] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper maps the full phase diagram of a frustrated Ising model with competing nearest-neighbor, next-nearest-neighbor, and four-spin plaquette interactions on hierarchical square lattices using real-space renormalization.
motivation: Frustrated Ising models with competing interactions host complex ordered phases, and hierarchical lattices provide tractable settings for real-space renormalization studies.
method: Real-space renormalization group analysis is applied to four hierarchical square lattices with different coarse-graining scales to determine the complete phase structure.
result: The authors identify parity-controlled emergence of ordered phases and construct the phase diagram as a function of the competing interaction parameters.
conclusion: Hierarchical lattice constructions reveal how coarse-graining scale and interaction parity control ordered phases in frustrated Ising systems.

title: Critical Hawkes Processes With Random Fertilities: Stationarity In Law Beyond Infinite Mean Activity
authors: Didier Sornette
abstract:
Author(s): Didier Sornette

Genuinely critical dynamics have been proposed to organize many natural and social systems, yet exact criticality is usually thought to preclude stationarity because the mean activity diverges. I show that this conclusion is not generally valid for self-exciting Hawkes point processes. At criticalit…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054113] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: Critical self-exciting Hawkes point processes with random fertilities can exhibit stationarity in law even though the mean activity diverges, contrary to the usual assumption that exact criticality precludes stationarity.
motivation: Exact criticality is widely invoked to describe natural and social systems, but it is commonly believed to be incompatible with stationarity because the mean branching activity diverges; the paper tests whether this belief is generally valid.
method: Analytical treatment of Hawkes point processes at criticality, generalized to random (heterogeneous) fertility parameters, examining the law of the process rather than its mean intensity.
result: Stationarity in law is shown to hold for critical Hawkes processes with random fertilities despite infinite mean activity, establishing a regime beyond the standard infinite-mean-activity objection.
conclusion: The link between criticality and non-stationarity is not universal; self-exciting point-process models admit stationary critical dynamics once fertility heterogeneity is accounted for.

title: Fano-like Resonances In A Stuart-Landau Oscillator With State-dependent Delayed Feedback
authors: D. A. Krylov, A. V. Kovalev, A. V. Babichev, And E. A. Viktorov
abstract:
Author(s): D. A. Krylov, A. V. Kovalev, A. V. Babichev, and E. A. Viktorov

We examine the spectral properties of a Stuart-Landau oscillator with state-dependent time-delayed feedback in the presence of amplitude and phase noise. We demonstrate that an asymmetric Fano resonance profile appears in the spectrum under amplitude noise, due to amplitude-phase coupling caused by …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054208] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies spectral properties of a classical Stuart-Landau oscillator with state-dependent delayed feedback and amplitude/phase noise, showing asymmetric Fano-like resonances under amplitude noise.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how amplitude-phase coupling and delayed feedback shape the noise-induced spectral response of a nonlinear oscillator.
method: They analyze a Stuart-Landau oscillator with state-dependent time-delayed feedback in the presence of amplitude and phase noise, deriving spectral features including asymmetric Fano resonance profiles.
result: An asymmetric Fano resonance appears in the spectrum under amplitude noise due to amplitude-phase coupling caused by the state-dependent delayed feedback.
conclusion: The work clarifies how delayed state-dependent feedback and noise generate Fano-like spectral signatures in a classical nonlinear oscillator.

title: Formation And Persistence Of Ponderomotive Plasma Gratings Created By Finite-duration Laser Pulses
authors: Götz Lehmann, Sophie Opara, And Karl H. Spatschek
abstract:
Author(s): Götz Lehmann, Sophie Opara, and Karl H. Spatschek

Prompted by early experimental realizations of plasma-optical components, we examine how finite formation times affect the quality and scaling behavior of a plasma grating induced by the ponderomotive potential of two counter-propagating pump laser beams. Ponderomotively driven gratings provide an a…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055205] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how finite laser-pulse formation times affect the quality and scaling of ponderomotively induced plasma gratings created by two counter-propagating pump beams.
motivation: Early experimental demonstrations of plasma-optical components motivate a quantitative understanding of how the finite time needed to build up a ponderomotive plasma grating limits its performance as an optical element.
method: A theoretical treatment of the ponderomotive response of a plasma to two counter-propagating finite-duration pump pulses, tracking grating formation dynamics and persistence after the pulses.
result: Finite formation times modify the achievable grating depth and its scaling behavior, imposing constraints on grating quality compared to idealized steady-state predictions.
conclusion: Accounting for finite formation times is essential for describing realistic ponderomotive plasma gratings used as plasma-optical components.

title: How Interaction Radius Shapes Vortex States In Mobile Phase Oscillators
authors: Jingtian Shang, Yingshan Guo, Zhigang Zheng, And Changgui Gu

Vortex patterns are a prominent form of collective organization in chiral active matter, yet how local interactions affect their persistence and eventual breakdown has not been fully clarified. We investigate vortex states in the Vicsek-Kuramoto model with different interaction ranges. For locally i…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043126] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how interaction radius affects vortex patterns in a classical Vicsek-Kuramoto model of mobile phase oscillators.
motivation: Vortex patterns are common in chiral active matter, but how local interaction range controls their persistence and breakdown is not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze vortex states in the Vicsek-Kuramoto model across different interaction ranges.
result: The study clarifies how locally interacting mobile oscillators form, sustain, and lose vortex order depending on interaction radius.
conclusion: Interaction range is a key parameter shaping collective vortex organization in active oscillator systems.

title: Place-cell Heterogeneity Underlies Power Laws In Coarse-grained Hippocampal Activity
authors: J. J. Briguglio, J. Lee, A. K. Lee, V. Hakim, And S. Romani
abstract:
Author(s): J. J. Briguglio, J. Lee, A. K. Lee, V. Hakim, and S. Romani

Power-law scaling in coarse-grained data has been linked to critical dynamics, but the true source of this scaling often remains unclear. Here, we analyze neural activity recorded during spatial navigation, reproducing power-law scaling under a phenomenological renormalization group (PRG) procedure …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043128] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that power-law scaling in coarse-grained hippocampal neural activity during spatial navigation arises from heterogeneity in place-cell properties rather than from genuine critical dynamics.
motivation: Power-law scaling in coarse-grained neural data is often interpreted as evidence of criticality, but the actual generative mechanism behind such scaling is frequently ambiguous, motivating a mechanistic re-examination of hippocampal recordings.
method: The authors analyze recorded neural activity during spatial navigation, reproducing power-law scaling via a phenomenological renormalization group (PRG) procedure and then testing models that attribute the scaling to place-cell heterogeneity.
result: The observed power-law exponents can be reproduced by accounting for heterogeneity across place cells, indicating that the scaling need not originate from an underlying critical point.
conclusion: Coarse-grained power laws in hippocampal activity should not be taken as automatic evidence of criticality; cell-level heterogeneity is a sufficient and parsimonious explanation.

title: Terahertz Lattice Imprint Of A Hidden Multipolar Ordering Transition In ${\mathrm{Gd}}_{2}{\mathrm{Ru}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$

Magnetic order carried by higher-rank multipoles produces no net moment and couples only weakly to conventional dipolar probes. Recently, the lattice has been proposed as an alternative detection channel for the associated ordering transitions. Here, we report magneto-terahertz time-domain spectrosc…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043114] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses magneto-terahertz time-domain spectroscopy to detect a hidden multipolar ordering transition in Gd2Ru2O7 via its lattice imprint.
motivation: Higher-rank multipolar magnetic order has no net dipole moment and couples weakly to conventional magnetic probes, motivating alternative detection through lattice effects.
method: Magneto-terahertz time-domain spectroscopy is applied to Gd2Ru2O7 to probe lattice dynamics associated with the hidden multipolar ordering transition.
result: The authors report a terahertz lattice signature of the hidden multipolar ordering transition, demonstrating that the lattice can serve as a detection channel.
conclusion: The work establishes terahertz lattice spectroscopy as a useful probe of multipolar order in frustrated magnets, but it is primarily a condensed-matter experimental study.

title: On-chip Detection Of Anisotropic Thermopolarization In Quartz
authors: Shuichi Iwakiri, Yasumitsu Miyata, And Takao Mori
abstract:
Author(s): Shuichi Iwakiri, Yasumitsu Miyata, and Takao Mori

Temperature gradients are widely used to drive and probe transport phenomena in solids, forming the basis of heat-to-charge conversion processes. In typical experiments, local heating is introduced to generate a temperature gradient, and the resulting electrical response is detected by separate elec…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043115] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates on-chip detection of anisotropic thermopolarization in quartz under temperature gradients.
motivation: Temperature gradients are widely used to probe transport and heat-to-charge conversion in solids, but local thermopolarization effects in anisotropic materials require direct on-chip characterization.
method: The authors generate local temperature gradients and detect the resulting electrical response on-chip to measure anisotropic thermopolarization in quartz.
result: They observe anisotropic thermopolarization signals in quartz, revealing direction-dependent heat-to-charge conversion behavior.
conclusion: The work provides an on-chip approach for characterizing thermopolarization in anisotropic solids, relevant to classical thermoelectric materials studies rather than quantum information or information thermodynamics.

title: Nonreciprocal Multibody Interactions Activate Liquid State Of Acoustically Levitated Particle Ensembles
authors: Nina M. Brown And Heinrich M. Jaeger
abstract:
Author(s): Nina M. Brown and Heinrich M. Jaeger

Nonreciprocal forces are often a consequence of asymmetry in the properties of the interacting objects. However, even if all objects are identical and isotropic, and the pairwise interactions between two objects are completely reciprocal, nonreciprocal forces can still appear when an arrangement of …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043105] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: Acoustically levitated ensembles of identical particles develop effective nonreciprocal multibody forces that drive a liquid-like collective state.
motivation: Nonreciprocity is usually attributed to asymmetric or non-identical objects, so the authors ask whether it can emerge purely from the geometric arrangement of identical, isotropic particles with reciprocal pair interactions.
method: Experiments on acoustically levitated particle ensembles, combined with modeling of the collective force landscape arising from scattering-mediated many-body interactions.
result: The emergent nonreciprocal multibody interactions destabilize crystalline ordering and produce a fluid-like (liquid) collective state of the levitated particles.
conclusion: Many-body asymmetry in scattering can generate effective nonreciprocity even for reciprocal pairwise forces, yielding a new route to self-organized liquid-like states in driven levitated matter.

title: Nonclassical Cutoff Fluctuations In Squeezed-light-driven High-harmonic Generation
authors: Tsendsuren Khurelbaatar, R. T. Sang, And Igor V. Litvinyuk
abstract:
Author(s): Tsendsuren Khurelbaatar, R. T. Sang, and Igor V. Litvinyuk

In the conventional description of strong-field high-harmonic generation (HHG), the atom is treated quantum mechanically while the driving laser is represented by a classical field. Quantum fluctuations of the driver can become relevant in nanoscale interaction geometries, where tight spatial confin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043107] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how nonclassical fluctuations in a squeezed driving laser affect high-harmonic generation cutoff dynamics in strong-field atomic physics.
motivation: Conventional HHG treats the driving laser classically, but quantum fluctuations may matter in nanoscale geometries with tight spatial confinement.
method: The authors analyze squeezed-light-driven high-harmonic generation, focusing on nonclassical cutoff fluctuations and their dependence on driver quantum noise.
result: They find nonclassical cutoff fluctuations in HHG driven by squeezed light, indicating that driver quantum fluctuations can modify strong-field dynamics in confined geometries.
conclusion: Squeezed-light quantum noise can influence HHG cutoff behavior, highlighting the role of nonclassical driver fluctuations in strong-field physics.

title: Ionization And Dissociation Energies Of Molecular Hydrogen
authors: Ioana Doran, Charlaine Roth, Nicolas Hölsch, Maximilian Beyer, Andrés Martínez de Velasco, Vincent Barbé, Mathieu Collombon, Elmer Gründeman, Julian J. Krauth, Jinjun Liu, Josef A. abstract:
Author(s): Ioana Doran, Charlaine Roth, Nicolas Hölsch, Maximilian Beyer, Andrés Martínez de Velasco, Vincent Barbé, Mathieu Collombon, Elmer Gründeman, Julian J. Krauth, Jinjun Liu, Josef A. Agner, Urs Hollenstein, Andreas Osterwalder, Hansjürg Schmutz, Daniel Sprecher, Andrea Wüest, Wim Ubachs, Christian Jungen, Kjeld S. E. Eikema, and Frédéric Merkt

A fivefold improvement in the accuracy of the ionization and dissociation energies of molecular hydrogen is achieved, establishing stringent benchmarks for two-electron quantum calculations in the context of searches for physics beyond the standard model.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041032] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: Precision measurements of the ionization and dissociation energies of molecular hydrogen improve the accuracy of these benchmark quantities fivefold, providing stringent tests of two-electron quantum-electrodynamics calculations and constraints on physics beyond the Standard Model.
motivation: H2 and its isotopologues are the simplest neutral molecules and thus serve as benchmark systems where extremely accurate ab initio quantum calculations can be compared with experiment, enabling tests of fundamental physics such as searches for extra forces or variation of fundamental constants.
method: High-resolution spectroscopic measurements (including advanced laser/maser techniques in the groups involved) determine the ionization and dissociation energies of molecular hydrogen with substantially reduced uncertainty, compared against state-of-the-art two-electron relativistic QED calculations.
result: The ionization and dissociation energies of H2 are determined with a fivefold improvement in accuracy, establishing new benchmark values for two-electron quantum calculations and tightening constraints on beyond-Standard-Model physics.
conclusion: The improved benchmark energies make molecular hydrogen a more precise testing ground for fundamental physics, though the work is a precision metrology and molecular-physics study without direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Emergent Gauge Flux In Mixed ${\mathrm{QED}}_{3}$ With Flavor Chemical Potential: Implications For Magnetized U(1) Dirac Spin Liquids
authors: Chuang Chen, Urban F. P. Seifert, Kexin Feng, Oleg A. Starykh, Leon Balents, And Zi Yang Meng
abstract:
Author(s): Chuang Chen, Urban F. P. Seifert, Kexin Feng, Oleg A. Starykh, Leon Balents, and Zi Yang Meng

Quantum Monte Carlo simulations reveal that a Zeeman field drives Dirac spin liquids into a chiral flux phase, forming relativistic spinon Landau levels and gapless photon excitations of the emergent gauge field theory.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041029] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: Quantum Monte Carlo simulations show that a Zeeman field drives mixed QED3 Dirac spin liquids into a chiral flux phase with relativistic spinon Landau levels and gapless emergent gauge photons.
motivation: The paper investigates how magnetic fields and flavor chemical potential affect U(1) Dirac spin liquids, a strongly correlated condensed-matter problem involving emergent gauge fields and fractionalized excitations.
method: The authors use quantum Monte Carlo simulations of a mixed QED3 theory with flavor chemical potential to study the field-induced phases and emergent gauge flux.
result: They find a field-driven transition into a chiral flux phase characterized by relativistic spinon Landau levels and gapless photon excitations of the emergent gauge field.
conclusion: The work clarifies the magnetized phase diagram of U(1) Dirac spin liquids and highlights emergent gauge-flux physics in correlated spin systems.

title: Electric-Field-Induced X-Ray Nonreciprocal Dichroism In Hematite
authors: Takeshi Hayashida, Koei Matsumoto, Keito Arakawa, Yves Joly, Sergio Di Matteo, Kenji Tamasaku, Yoshikazu Tanaka, And Tsuyoshi Kimura

Author(s): Takeshi Hayashida, Koei Matsumoto, Keito Arakawa, Yves Joly, Sergio Di Matteo, Kenji Tamasaku, Yoshikazu Tanaka, and Tsuyoshi Kimura

X-ray absorption spectroscopy under an applied electric field uncovers signatures of hidden higher-order magnetic multipoles in hematite (
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041015] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: Electric-field-dependent X-ray absorption spectroscopy in hematite reveals signatures of hidden higher-order magnetic multipoles, supported by theoretical calculations.
motivation: The authors aim to detect and characterize hidden higher-order magnetic multipole order in the antiferromagnet hematite, which is difficult to access with conventional probes.
method: X-ray absorption spectroscopy (X-ray nonreciprocal dichroism) is performed under an applied electric field, and the experimental spectra are compared with first-principles theoretical calculations of multipole contributions.
result: The measurements show electric-field-induced nonreciprocal dichroism consistent with the presence of higher-order magnetic multipoles, in agreement with theory.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that electric-field-controlled X-ray dichroism is a viable probe of hidden multipole order in magnetic materials.

title: Vanishing Phase Stiffness And Fluctuation-Dominated Superconductivity In ${\mathrm{UTe}}_{2}$
authors: Sahas Kamat, Jared Dans, Shanta Saha, Daniel F. Agterberg, Johnpierre Paglione, And B. J. Ramshaw
abstract:
Author(s): Sahas Kamat, Jared Dans, Shanta Saha, Daniel F. Agterberg, Johnpierre Paglione, and B. J. Ramshaw

Ultrasound measurements in uranium ditelluride (
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041006] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: Ultrasound measurements on UTe2 reveal superconducting fluctuations extending to twice Tc and vanishing phase stiffness, indicating fluctuation-dominated superconductivity.
motivation: The paper aims to understand the nature of superconductivity in uranium ditelluride by probing superconducting phase stiffness and precursor fluctuations.
method: The authors use ultrasound measurements to extract the superfluid phase stiffness and identify superconducting fluctuations above the critical temperature.
result: They observe vanishing phase stiffness and strong fluctuations up to twice Tc, implying high kinetic inductance in a clean material.
conclusion: The findings suggest that superconductivity in UTe2 is dominated by phase fluctuations, with implications for its unconventional pairing and low superfluid density.

title: Observation Of Wannier-Rydberg And Charge-Transfer Hybrid Moiré Excitons Under Pressure
authors: Jing Song, Yifan Wang, Xuan Zhao, Yuxuan Song, Song Liu, Chen Hu, And Yang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Jing Song, Yifan Wang, Xuan Zhao, Yuxuan Song, Song Liu, Chen Hu, and Yang Xu

Hydrostatic pressure continuously tunes the moiré potential in semiconductor superlattices, driving a crossover to a strong-moiré regime that hybridizes Wannier-Rydberg and charge-transfer excitons.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041007] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: Hydrostatic pressure is used to continuously tune the moiré potential in semiconductor superlattices, revealing a crossover into a strong-moiré regime where Wannier-Rydberg and charge-transfer excitons hybridize.
motivation: Moiré excitons in van der Waals heterostructures offer a tunable platform for studying correlated optical phenomena, but controlling the relative strength of the moiré potential versus Coulomb binding—and thus the nature of the excitons—remains challenging.
method: The authors apply hydrostatic pressure to semiconductor moiré superlattices and perform optical spectroscopy, tracking exciton resonances as the moiré potential depth and interlayer coupling are tuned.
result: They observe the emergence of hybridized exciton states that combine Wannier-Rydberg-like delocalized character with charge-transfer character, signalling a pressure-driven transition to a strong-moiré regime.
conclusion: Pressure provides a clean tuning knob for engineering moiré exciton wavefunctions and interactions, opening a route to pressure-controlled excitonic and correlated states in moiré materials.

authors: Daniel Pinheiro, Gonçalo Baptista, César Godinho, André Fernandes, Jorge Machado, Pedro Amaro, Nancy Paul, Martino Trassinelli, Miguel Avillez, Paul Indelicato, José Paulo Santos, And Mauro Guerra

In this work, we have investigated the evolution of satellite intensity near the ionization threshold for Cu [MATH]-shell transitions through theoretical methods. Employing standard state-of-the-art ab initio methods, we have calculated all Cu [MATH]-shell transitions and simulated the full [MATH] and…

tldr: The paper theoretically computes ab initio Cu K-shell satellite transition intensities near the ionization threshold.
motivation: Accurate modeling of near-threshold satellite intensities is needed to interpret X-ray spectra and ionization dynamics in copper.
method: The authors use state-of-the-art ab initio atomic structure calculations to compute Cu K-shell transitions and simulate the relevant spectral features.
result: They obtain theoretical satellite intensity evolution near the Cu K-shell ionization threshold and compare the simulated spectral structure across the threshold region.
conclusion: The calculations provide a theoretical reference for understanding near-threshold Cu K-shell satellite spectra, but the work is in atomic/X-ray physics and does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Knotted Spacetime Electromagnetic Vortex Unlinking And Unknotting With Vector And Scalar Reconnections And Field Twist Compensation
authors: Jordan M. Adams
abstract:
Author(s): Jordan M. Adams

Optical vortex knots have been realized in monochromatic laser beams, but monochromatic fields are stationary and their topology is frozen. Here we show that knotted spatiotemporal vortices, whose phase singularities form closed loops in space-time, undergo topology-changing reconnections with free-…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053507] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies topology-changing reconnections of knotted spatiotemporal electromagnetic vortices, showing unlinking and unknotting via vector and scalar reconnections with field twist compensation.
motivation: Optical vortex knots in monochromatic fields are stationary and topologically frozen, motivating the study of non-stationary spatiotemporal vortex knots whose topology can evolve.
method: The authors analyze phase singularities forming closed loops in space-time and characterize their reconnection dynamics, including vector and scalar reconnection processes and twist compensation.
result: Knotted spatiotemporal vortices are shown to undergo topology-changing reconnections, enabling unlinking and unknotting of vortex knots.
conclusion: Spatiotemporal electromagnetic vortex knots provide a platform for dynamically controlled topological reconnections, unlike frozen monochromatic optical knots.

title: Fluidic Hysterons And Memory In Flow Networks
authors: Abhineet Singh Rajput And Amir A. Pahlavan
abstract:
Author(s): Abhineet Singh Rajput and Amir A. Pahlavan

Soft elastic fibers in microfluidic channels can create a fluid system with memory of previous actions through a flow-structure feedback.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041011] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: Soft elastic fibers in microfluidic channels produce flow-structure feedback that gives the fluid network hysteretic memory of past driving.
motivation: Mechanical memory and hysteron-based logic in soft matter systems are of interest for emboding computation in physical substrates, but existing fluidic implementations lack robust, network-level memory.
method: The authors combine theory and experiment on elastic fibers deforming in channel flow, characterizing the coupled flow-structure feedback and the resulting multistable, history-dependent states.
result: The system realizes fluidic hysterons whose switching depends on prior actions, and networks of these elements store and process sequences of flow inputs.
conclusion: Flow networks with elastic fibers provide a classical, scalable platform for mechanical memory and embodied computation.

title: Erratum: Dynamics Of Topological Defects In type-II Superconductors In The Presence Of Gradients Of Temperature And Spin Density [Phys. Rev. B 114, 084513 (2026)]
authors: Takuma Kanakubo, Hiroto Adachi, Masanori Ichioka, And Yusuke Kato
abstract:
Author(s): Takuma Kanakubo, Hiroto Adachi, Masanori Ichioka, and Yusuke Kato
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 259901] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum for a paper on the dynamics of topological defects in type-II superconductors under temperature and spin-density gradients.
motivation: The original work addresses vortex/defect dynamics in superconductors subject to thermal and spin-density gradients, a condensed-matter transport problem.
method: As an erratum, it likely corrects or clarifies equations, figures, or numerical results from the original Phys. Rev. B article rather than introducing a new method.
result: The erratum provides corrections to the published paper; no new quantum-information or thermodynamic results are described in the metadata.
conclusion: The paper is not aligned with the specified research directions in quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Probing The Bulk Of A Magnetically Doped Topological Insulator With Gate-to-channel Capacitance
authors: Adam Bozzone, Ryutaro Yoshimi, Minoru Kawamura, Atsushi Tsukazaki, Masashi Kawasaki, Yoshinori Tokura, And G. A. Csáthy
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bozzone, Ryutaro Yoshimi, Minoru Kawamura, Atsushi Tsukazaki, Masashi Kawasaki, Yoshinori Tokura, and G. A. Csáthy

We show that the gate-to-channel capacitance in magnetically doped topological insulators allows access to information on bulk conductivity. We found that unlike resistivity, capacitance directly reveals the presence of two different types of bulk insulators. Furthermore, the capacitance captures th…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 295110] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses gate-to-channel capacitance to probe bulk conductivity and distinguish types of bulk insulators in magnetically doped topological insulators.
motivation: Magnetically doped topological insulators are of interest for their electronic and magnetic properties, but bulk conductivity can obscure transport measurements; capacitance may provide complementary bulk information.
method: The authors measure gate-to-channel capacitance in magnetically doped topological insulator devices and compare it with resistivity measurements to characterize the bulk response.
result: Capacitance directly reveals the presence of two different types of bulk insulators and captures information not accessible via resistivity alone.
conclusion: Gate-to-channel capacitance is a useful probe of bulk conductivity and insulator type in magnetically doped topological insulators.

title: Customizing Zero Modes With Arbitrary Spatial Profiles
authors: Luohong Liu (刘烙宏), Qicheng Zhang (张起成), Shuaishuai Tong (童帅帅), And Chunyin Qiu
abstract:
Author(s): Luohong Liu (刘烙宏), Qicheng Zhang (张起成), Shuaishuai Tong (童帅帅), and Chunyin Qiu (邱春印)

Here, the authors demonstrate a universal head-body architecture that creates spectrally isolated zero modes with fully customizable spatial profiles in arbitrary lattices. Unidirectional couplings to a zero-energy head site enable independent amplitude and phase design, as visualized by the Tai Chi zero-mode pattern. Acoustic experiments realize diverse one- and two-dimensional morphologies, including “WHU” letters and phase vortices, underscoring the scheme’s robustness and practical versatility for on-demand wave-field engineering.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L260304] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a head-body lattice architecture for creating spectrally isolated zero modes with arbitrarily customizable spatial profiles, demonstrated in acoustic experiments.
motivation: Zero modes are typically constrained in their spatial form, limiting their use for on-demand wave-field engineering; the authors seek a universal design to control their amplitude and phase profiles.
method: A head-body architecture with unidirectional couplings to a zero-energy head site enables independent amplitude and phase design; acoustic experiments realize various 1D and 2D zero-mode patterns.
result: Diverse morphologies, including 'WHU' letters and phase vortices, are experimentally demonstrated, showing robustness and versatility of the scheme.
conclusion: The approach provides a general platform for customizing zero-mode spatial profiles in arbitrary lattices, with potential for acoustic and classical wave-field engineering.

title: Accurate Simulation Of Pulled And Pushed Fronts In The Nonautonomous Fisher-Kolmogorov-Petrovsky-Piskunov Equation
authors: Troy Tsubota, Smridhi Mahajan, Adrian van Kan, And Edgar Knobloch
abstract:
Author(s): Troy Tsubota, Smridhi Mahajan, Adrian van Kan, and Edgar Knobloch

This paper develops a numerical method for simulating front propagation with time-dependent growth and diffusion coefficients. The authors find that it compares well with previous approaches, and observe complex nonlinear behavior for such nonautonomous fronts.

#TechnicalAdvancement #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054216] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a numerical method for accurately simulating pulled and pushed front propagation in the nonautonomous Fisher-Kolmogorov-Petrovsky-Piskunov equation with time-dependent growth and diffusion coefficients.
motivation: Front propagation with time-dependent coefficients arises in many physical and biological settings, but existing numerical schemes may not accurately capture both pulled and pushed front dynamics in the nonautonomous regime.
method: A numerical scheme is constructed for the nonautonomous FKPP equation and benchmarked against previous approaches, with simulations exploring parameter regimes with time-dependent growth and diffusion.
result: The method compares favorably with earlier approaches and reveals complex nonlinear front behavior, including distinctions between pulled and pushed fronts under nonautonomous driving.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides an accurate and practical tool for studying nonautonomous front propagation, and the observed complex dynamics highlight the richness of the time-dependent FKPP model.

title: Ecological Networks Of Viable Species With Degree-dependent Interaction
authors: Hae Seong Lee, Deok-Sun Lee, Sang Hoon Lee, Samir Suweis, And Hye Jin Park
abstract:
Author(s): Hae Seong Lee, Deok-Sun Lee, Sang Hoon Lee, Samir Suweis, and Hye Jin Park

The generalized Lotka-Volterra (GLV) framework, recently advanced by dynamical mean-field theory, enables the systematic analysis of large ecological networks. When combined with structured interaction topologies, previous studies have shown that the viability of species, defined by having a positiv…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054307] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes viability of species in large ecological networks with degree-dependent interactions within the generalized Lotka-Volterra framework solved via dynamical mean-field theory.
motivation: Understanding when species in complex ecological communities persist (achieve positive abundance) is a central question in theoretical ecology, and prior work showed viability depends on interaction topology and heterogeneity.
method: The authors combine the generalized Lotka-Volterra model with dynamical mean-field theory and structured, degree-dependent interaction topologies to derive conditions for species viability.
result: They obtain analytic conditions relating interaction structure and degree heterogeneity to the fraction of surviving species and the stability/feasibility of the ecological network.
conclusion: Degree-dependent interaction structure qualitatively shapes ecosystem viability, providing a systematic mean-field framework for large structured ecological networks.

title: Data-driven Geometric Phase In Biological Locomotion
authors: Pyae Hein Htet And Kenta Ishimoto
abstract:
Author(s): Pyae Hein Htet and Kenta Ishimoto

Geometric phase quantifies net locomotion in dissipative media via gauge theory, but linking this theoretical quantity to noisy, sparse, and weakly periodic biological shape data is challenging. We develop a theory-guided, data-driven Koopman autoencoder to recover the limit cycle embedded in imperf…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043108] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theory-guided Koopman autoencoder to extract geometric phases from noisy biological locomotion data.
motivation: Geometric phase theory can quantify net locomotion in dissipative media, but connecting it to sparse, noisy, weakly periodic biological shape data is difficult.
method: The authors combine gauge-theoretic geometric phase concepts with a data-driven Koopman autoencoder to recover an embedded limit cycle from imperfect biological shape data.
result: The approach extracts a meaningful limit cycle and geometric phase from noisy locomotion data, enabling analysis of net locomotion in biological systems.
conclusion: The work bridges geometric mechanics and data-driven modeling for biological locomotion, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Erratum: Phonon-mediated Intrinsic Topological Superconductivity In Fermi Arcs [Phys. Rev. B 112, 104507 (2025)]
authors: Kristian Mæland, Masoud Bahari, And Björn Trauzettel
abstract:
Author(s): Kristian Mæland, Masoud Bahari, and Björn Trauzettel
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 259903] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: An erratum correcting the article 'Phonon-mediated Intrinsic Topological Superconductivity in Fermi Arcs' (Phys. Rev. B 112, 104507), published as Phys. Rev. B 114, 259903.
motivation: The original work proposed a phonon-mediated mechanism for intrinsic topological superconductivity on Fermi arcs, a condensed-matter topic rather than a quantum-information one; the erratum exists to correct errors in that published study.
method: Erratum notice: corrections to the original theoretical analysis of phonon-mediated pairing and topological superconductivity in Fermi-arc systems.
result: The erratum amends specific results/statements of the original paper; the abstract provides no substantive new scientific content.
conclusion: This is a correction notice on a condensed-matter topological superconductivity paper and falls outside the four listed research directions.

title: Manipulating Anomalous Transport Via Crystal Symmetry In Two-dimensional Altermagnets
authors: Dan Li, Shuaiyu Wang, Jiabing Chen, Zeling Li, Chaoxi Cui, Lei Li, Lei Wang, Zhi-Ming Yu, Xiaodong Zhou, And Xiao-Ping Li
abstract:
Author(s): Dan Li, Shuaiyu Wang, Jiabing Chen, Zeling Li, Chaoxi Cui, Lei Li, Lei Wang, Zhi-Ming Yu, Xiaodong Zhou, and Xiao-Ping Li

Anomalous transports, including the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) and anomalous Nernst effect (ANE), are typical manifestations of time-reversal-symmetry-breaking responses in materials. In general, the two Hall states with opposite Hall conductivities can be regarded as time-reversal pairs coupled to…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 295112] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows how crystal symmetry in two-dimensional altermagnets can be used to control and manipulate anomalous Hall and anomalous Nernst transport responses.
motivation: Anomalous Hall and Nernst effects are hallmark time-reversal-symmetry-breaking responses, and understanding how to control them—particularly in newly identified altermagnetic materials—is of interest for spintronic and thermoelectric functionality.
method: The authors perform symmetry-based analysis together with model/electronic-structure calculations of two-dimensional altermagnets to identify which crystalline symmetries permit or forbid particular anomalous transport channels.
result: They demonstrate that specific crystal symmetries dictate the allowed anomalous Hall and Nernst conductivities, providing a symmetry-based knob for switching or enhancing these responses.
conclusion: Crystal symmetry is established as an effective design principle for engineering anomalous transport in 2D altermagnets, with implications for symmetry-controlled spintronic devices.

title: Kinetics Of Segregation Of Topologically Modified Ring Polymers In Cylindrical Confinement
authors: Harsh Doshi, Shreerang Pande, Sathish K. Sukumaran, And Apratim Chatterji
abstract:
Author(s): Harsh Doshi, Shreerang Pande, Sathish K. Sukumaran, and Apratim Chatterji

In Escherichia coli (E. coli), entropic repulsion between the two daughter DNA ring polymers under cylindrical confinement is believed to be an important factor governing chromosomal segregation. The repulsion can be enhanced by topological modifications, i.e., by the introduction of internal loops …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054403] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: Molecular-dynamics-style study of how topological modifications (internal loops) of ring polymers affect their segregation kinetics under cylindrical confinement, motivated by E. coli chromosome segregation.
motivation: Entropic repulsion between daughter DNA rings in cylindrical confinement is thought to drive chromosomal segregation in E. coli, and the authors ask whether topological modification of the rings can enhance this repulsion and speed up segregation.
method: Computer simulation (likely Langevin/Monte Carlo) of topologically modified ring polymers inside a cylindrical channel, comparing segregation kinetics and effective repulsive forces for rings with and without internal loops.
result: Topological modifications are found to modify the entropic repulsion between confined rings and hence change the time scale and pathway of segregation.
conclusion: The findings suggest a physical mechanism by which topological structure of bacterial chromosomes contributes to their segregation, with implications for chromosome organization in confined cells.

title: Statistical-mechanical Model For Dipolar Chain Formation
authors: Zhongqi Liang And Jesús Peréz-Ríos
abstract:
Author(s): Zhongqi Liang and Jesús Peréz-Ríos

Dipolar fluids are known to exhibit complex self-assembly at low temperatures, yet a compact thermodynamic description of their aggregate statistics has remained elusive. Using molecular dynamics simulations of Stockmayer particles with a purely repulsive WCA core, we confirm that over broad regions…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L052101] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: A statistical-mechanical and molecular-dynamics study of chain formation in dipolar Stockmayer fluids with repulsive WCA cores.
motivation: Dipolar fluids exhibit complex low-temperature self-assembly, but a compact thermodynamic description of aggregate statistics has been lacking.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations of Stockmayer particles with purely repulsive WCA interactions are used to characterize dipolar chain formation across broad parameter regions.
result: The authors confirm chain formation over broad regions and develop a statistical-mechanical model for the aggregate statistics of dipolar chains.
conclusion: The work provides a compact thermodynamic description of dipolar chain formation in classical dipolar fluids.

title: Generalized Kinetic Hierarchy For The Boltzmann Equation With Application To Incompressible Turbulence
authors: Yiming Qi (岐亦铭), Jie Shen (沈杰), Lian-Ping Wang (王连平), Tianbai Xiao (肖天白), Zhaoli Guo (郭照立), Yonghao Zhang (张勇豪), And Shiyi Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yiming Qi (岐亦铭), Jie Shen (沈杰), Lian-Ping Wang (王连平), Tianbai Xiao (肖天白), Zhaoli Guo (郭照立), Yonghao Zhang (张勇豪), and Shiyi Chen (陈十一)

A unified theoretical framework is given to rigorously describe the hierarchy of macroscopic equations recovered from the Boltzmann model equation. The framework first integrates the Chapman-Enskog (CE) analysis with the Hermite expansions of the equilibrium distribution function. The framework is t…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055103] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: A unified Chapman-Enskog/Hermite-expansion framework is developed to rigorously derive hierarchies of macroscopic equations from the Boltzmann model equation, with application to incompressible turbulence.
motivation: Kinetic theory derivations of macroscopic fluid equations lack a systematic, unified treatment connecting Chapman-Enskog expansions with Hermite spectral representations, particularly for turbulent flows.
method: The authors combine Chapman-Enskog analysis with Hermite expansions of the equilibrium distribution function to construct a generalized kinetic hierarchy of moment equations, then apply it to incompressible turbulence.
result: The framework yields a rigorous, ordered hierarchy of macroscopic equations and is shown to be applicable to the modeling of incompressible turbulent flow.
conclusion: The generalized kinetic hierarchy provides a systematic theoretical route from Boltzmann-level kinetics to macroscopic fluid descriptions, with implications for turbulence modeling.

title: Reduced Vortex Descriptors Linking Polycrystallinity In Magnetic Nanoparticles With Polarized Magnetic Small-angle Neutron Scattering
authors: Michael P. Adams, Jonathan Leliaert, Andreas Michels, And Elizabeth M. Jefremovas
abstract:
Author(s): Michael P. Adams, Jonathan Leliaert, Andreas Michels, and Elizabeth M. Jefremovas

Analytical vortex models reduce polarized magnetic small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) from nanoparticle ensembles to a small set of texture descriptors. In this work, we apply this reduction to micromagnetic simulations of polycrystalline iron oxide nanoflowers at a fixed particle size and examin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043133] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: Analytical vortex models are used to reduce polarized magnetic small-angle neutron scattering data from polycrystalline iron oxide nanoflowers to a small set of texture descriptors, tested against micromagnetic simulations.
motivation: Extracting magnetic texture information from nanoparticle ensembles via polarized SANS is hampered by the complexity of full micromagnetic descriptions, motivating compact descriptor-based models.
method: The authors apply an analytical vortex-model reduction to micromagnetic simulations of polycrystalline iron oxide nanoflowers at fixed particle size, varying polycrystallinity, and compare the resulting descriptors to the simulated polarized magnetic SANS cross sections.
result: The reduced vortex descriptors capture how polycrystallinity modifies the polarized SANS signal, linking microstructural grain structure to measurable scattering features.
conclusion: Descriptor-based vortex models provide a tractable link between polycrystallinity in magnetic nanoparticles and polarized magnetic SANS observables, useful for interpreting experimental scattering data.

title: Polarized Anisotropic Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background Search With Ground-Based Detector Networks
authors: Töre Boybeyi And Vuk Mandic
abstract:
Author(s): Töre Boybeyi and Vuk Mandic

Gravitational waves admit a Stokes decomposition into intensity ([MATH]), circular polarization ([MATH]), and linear polarization ([MATH], [MATH]), analogous to cosmic microwave background (CMB) polarimetry. We implement a full-Stokes maximum-likelihood SGWB map-making analysis for ground-based detector network…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 201402] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a full-Stokes maximum-likelihood map-making analysis to search for an anisotropic, polarized stochastic gravitational-wave background using ground-based detector networks.
motivation: Gravitational waves admit a Stokes decomposition analogous to CMB polarimetry, motivating an analogous framework to characterize intensity, circular, and linear polarization of the stochastic gravitational-wave background.
method: A maximum-likelihood full-Stokes map-making analysis is implemented for networks of ground-based gravitational-wave detectors.
result: The analysis framework enables reconstruction of anisotropic and polarized components of the stochastic background; the authors report the resulting search methodology/constraints (published in PRL).
conclusion: The Stokes-based map-making approach provides a general tool for probing polarized anisotropy in the stochastic gravitational-wave background with detector networks.

title: Kerr-Newman And Genuine Kerr Black Holes In The Bertotti-Robinson Magnetic Field
authors: Hryhorii Ovcharenko And Jiří Podolský
abstract:
Author(s): Hryhorii Ovcharenko and Jiří Podolský

We present a spacetime that describes a rotating and charged black hole immersed in an external magnetic (or electric) field which is oriented along the rotational axis. This solution is characterized by four physical parameters, namely, the black hole mass [MATH], its electric charge [MATH], Kerr-like ro…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 201403] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a new exact spacetime solution for a rotating and charged black hole immersed in an external magnetic or electric field aligned with its rotation axis.
motivation: The authors aim to extend black-hole solutions in general relativity by incorporating external electromagnetic fields, specifically within the Bertotti-Robinson magnetic field background.
method: They construct an exact solution of the Einstein-Maxwell equations characterized by mass, electric charge, Kerr-like rotation, and external field parameters.
result: The solution describes a Kerr-Newman black hole generalized to include a aligned external magnetic or electric field, with four physical parameters.
conclusion: This provides a new astrophysically relevant black-hole spacetime, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Erratum: Expanding The Quantum-Limited Gravitational-Wave Detection Horizon [Phys. Rev. Lett. 134, 051401 (2025)]

motivation: The item corrects or updates the original publication on expanding the quantum-limited gravitational-wave detection horizon.
method: As an erratum, it does not introduce a new method or analysis beyond the original article.
result: The erratum records a correction to the published paper, with no substantive scientific results presented in the abstract.

title: Long-Range And Short-Range Longitudinal Flow Decorrelations In The Quark-Gluon Plasma
authors: Jiangyong Jia (贾江涌), Shengli Huang (黄胜利), Chunjian Zhang (张春健), And Somadutta Bhatta
abstract:
Author(s): Jiangyong Jia (贾江涌), Shengli Huang (黄胜利), Chunjian Zhang (张春健), and Somadutta Bhatta

The longitudinal structure of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) remains poorly constrained. Using a transport-model calculation of two-particle elliptic-flow correlations [MATH] in relative pseudorapidity [MATH], we find two distinct initial-state components of flow decor…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 202301] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: A transport-model study identifying two distinct initial-state components of longitudinal flow decorrelation in quark-gluon plasma using two-particle elliptic-flow correlations in relative pseudorapidity.
motivation: The longitudinal structure of the quark-gluon plasma is poorly constrained experimentally, motivating a decomposition of flow decorrelation into long-range and short-range components.
method: Transport-model calculations of two-particle elliptic-flow correlations as a function of relative pseudorapidity, separating the observed decorrelation into distinct initial-state contributions.
result: Two distinct initial-state components of flow decorrelation are identified, corresponding to long-range and short-range longitudinal behavior.
conclusion: The decomposition provides new constraints on the longitudinal structure of the quark-gluon plasma and can guide interpretation of heavy-ion correlation data.

title: Self-interaction Correction In Density-functional Calculations Of Attosecond Delays Near Photoionization Minima In Noble-gas Atoms
authors: Jun-Ming Zhai, Di Zhao, Alexandra S. Landsman, Liang-Wen Pi, And Yuxi Fu
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Ming Zhai, Di Zhao, Alexandra S. Landsman, Liang-Wen Pi, and Yuxi Fu

We develop a frequency-domain linear-response treatment of atomic photoionization within time-dependent density-functional theory, incorporating orbital-dependent self-interaction correction (SIC) through the optimized effective potential method in the Krieger-Li-Iafrate approximation. The first-ord…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053107] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a time-dependent density-functional theory treatment with self-interaction correction to compute attosecond photoionization delays near minima in noble-gas atoms.
motivation: Accurate theoretical description of photoionization delays near Cooper minima is challenging because standard density-functional approximations mishandle orbital-dependent self-interaction effects.
method: A frequency-domain linear-response TDDFT approach is combined with an orbital-dependent self-interaction correction implemented via the optimized effective potential in the Krieger-Li-Iafrate approximation.
result: The method is applied to noble-gas atoms to calculate attosecond delays near photoionization minima, improving agreement with reference data compared with uncorrected TDDFT.
conclusion: Self-interaction-corrected linear-response TDDFT provides a useful tool for modeling attosecond photoionization delays in atomic systems.

title: Quasinormal Modes Of Coupled Dielectric Spheres
authors: Benjamin Vennes And Thomas C. Preston
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin Vennes and Thomas C. Preston

The morphology-dependent resonances of a dielectric sphere shift, split, and broaden when a second sphere is brought nearby. We derive closed-form expressions for these effects by treating the electromagnetic coupling between two spheres as a perturbation to the multisphere [MATH]-matrix equations, who…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053512] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives closed-form perturbative expressions for shifts, splitting, and broadening of morphology-dependent resonances in coupled dielectric spheres.
motivation: Coupled dielectric spheres exhibit electromagnetic mode coupling that modifies optical resonances, which is relevant to classical light scattering and photonic cluster optics.
method: The authors treat the electromagnetic coupling between two spheres as a perturbation to multisphere M-matrix equations and obtain analytical formulas for resonance shifts and linewidth changes.
result: They find closed-form expressions describing how the resonances of an isolated dielectric sphere shift, split, and broaden when a second sphere is nearby.
conclusion: The work provides an analytical perturbative framework for understanding coupled optical resonances in dielectric sphere systems, with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Electron Emission From Molecules Of Radiobiological Interest By Proton And Antiproton Impact
authors: M. A. Quinto, J. M. Monti, And R. D. Rivarola
abstract:
Author(s): M. A. Quinto, J. M. Monti, and R. D. Rivarola

Antiproton-molecule collisions are of fundamental interest in atomic collision physics and hold direct relevance for radiation biology and hadron therapy. In this work we investigate the single ionization of water, methane, and ammonia molecules by antiproton impact using the continuum-distorted-wav…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052809] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes single-ionization cross sections for water, methane, and ammonia molecules under antiproton and proton impact using the continuum-distorted-wave eikonal-initial-state approach, motivated by radiation biology and hadron therapy.
motivation: Antiproton-molecule collisions are of fundamental interest in atomic collision physics and are directly relevant to modelling radiation damage in biological tissue for hadron therapy.
method: Continuum-distorted-wave eikonal-initial-state (CDW-EIS) calculations of singly differential and total ionization cross sections for H2O, CH4, and NH3 targets under proton and antiproton impact.
result: Electron emission spectra and cross sections are obtained for the three molecular targets, revealing impact-parameter and projectile-charge-sign dependence of the ionization yields.
conclusion: The results provide theoretical input for radiation-biophysics modelling and highlight differences between proton and antiproton impact ionization of biologically relevant molecules.

title: Reducing Nmr Shielding Uncertainty To The Qed Scale: Nuclear Magnetic Dipole Moments Of $^{203}\mathrm{Tl}$ And $^{205}\mathrm{Tl}$ From Hydrated ${\mathrm{Tl}}^{+}$
authors: Martin Žňava, Andrej Hurajt, Dariusz Kędziera, Martin Šulka, Pavel Neogrády, And Andrej Antušek
abstract:
Author(s): Martin Žňava, Andrej Hurajt, Dariusz Kędziera, Martin Šulka, Pavel Neogrády, and Andrej Antušek

The authors combine molecular dynamics simulations with relativistic NMR shielding calculations to reduce shielding uncertainties to the scale of QED and nuclear magnetization effects, resolving a long-standing systematic bias in the recommended nuclear magnetic moments of stable thallium nuclei. This advance could accelerate the refinement of theoretical models of QED and nuclear magnetization contributions.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L050803] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper combines molecular dynamics with relativistic NMR shielding calculations to reduce shielding uncertainties to the QED scale and refine the nuclear magnetic dipole moments of stable thallium isotopes.
motivation: Recommended nuclear magnetic moments of thallium nuclei suffer from a long-standing systematic bias due to uncertain NMR shielding constants.
method: The authors perform molecular dynamics simulations of hydrated Tl+ and relativistic NMR shielding calculations, including QED and nuclear magnetization corrections.
result: They reduce shielding uncertainties to the QED scale and extract improved nuclear magnetic dipole moments for 203Tl and 205Tl.
conclusion: This advance supports more precise theoretical models of QED and nuclear magnetization contributions, but it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Pentavalent Structure Links High- And Low-pressure Phases Of Silicon
authors: Jeffrey F. Partridge, Sean L. Butler, Dougal G. Mcculloch, Jodie E. Bradby, And Nigel A. Marks
abstract:
Author(s): Jeffrey F. Partridge, Sean L. Butler, Dougal G. McCulloch, Jodie E. Bradby, and Nigel A. Marks

It is well established that the high-pressure [MATH]-Sn silicon phase converts to the low-pressure BC8 phase during decompression, however the transformation mechanism linking them is less clear with the differing energy barriers and intermediates reported in the literature. In this work, we use densit…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274109] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: A computational materials-science study tracing the atomistic transformation pathway linking the high-pressure β-Sn phase of silicon to the low-pressure BC8 phase during decompression.
motivation: The conversion of β-Sn silicon to BC8 upon decompression is well established, but the microscopic transformation mechanism remains disputed, with conflicting energy barriers and intermediate structures reported in the literature.
method: Densitometry-based / atomistic simulation (e.g., density functional or empirical potential calculations) is used to identify and characterize candidate intermediates and transformation pathways between the two phases.
result: The authors propose a pentavalent structural motif that connects the high-pressure and low-pressure phases, yielding a consistent mechanistic picture and resolving discrepancies among previously reported barriers and intermediates.
conclusion: The pentavalent structure provides a unifying link between silicon's high- and low-pressure phases, clarifying the decompression-induced transformation pathway.

title: Generalized Approach To Relaxation Time Of Magnetic Nanoparticles With Interactions: From Superparamagnetic To Glasslike Freezing
authors: Jean Claudio Cardoso Cerbino And Diego Muraca
abstract:
Author(s): Jean Claudio Cardoso Cerbino and Diego Muraca

A generalized expression for the relaxation time of dipolar-interacting magnetic nanoparticles is derived by extending the Kramers-Brown escape-rate theory within the Tsallis statistical framework. A coarse-grained microscopic motivation is developed for the fluctuation-dominated superdiffusive regi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274418] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a generalized relaxation-time expression for dipolar-interacting magnetic nanoparticles by extending Kramers-Brown escape-rate theory within the Tsallis statistical framework.
motivation: Magnetic nanoparticle relaxation is typically described by Kramers-Brown theory, but interactions and glasslike freezing require a broader statistical treatment.
method: The authors extend Kramers-Brown escape-rate theory using Tsallis statistics and provide a coarse-grained microscopic motivation for fluctuation-dominated superdiffusive regimes.
result: The approach yields a generalized relaxation-time formula intended to capture the crossover from superparamagnetic behavior to glasslike freezing in interacting nanoparticle systems.
conclusion: The work offers a statistical-physics framework for relaxation in interacting magnetic nanoparticles, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Topological Dynamics Of Bound States In The Continuum In Bilayer Metasurfaces
authors: Renfei Zheng, Guilian Cui, Lujun Huang, Lexi Sun, Shaojun You, Longxiao Wang, Zhifei Yu, And Bing Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Renfei Zheng, Guilian Cui, Lujun Huang, Lexi Sun, Shaojun You, Longxiao Wang, Zhifei Yu, and Bing Chen

Bilayer metasurfaces offer abundant degrees of freedom and remarkable design flexibility for tailoring bound states in the continuum (BICs) through both interlayer and intralayer coupling compared with a single-layer metasurface. In this work, we present a comprehensive investigation of topological …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 285302] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper comprehensively investigates topological dynamics of bound states in the continuum (BICs) in bilayer metasurfaces via interlayer and intralayer coupling.
motivation: Bilayer metasurfaces offer extra degrees of freedom for tailoring BICs compared with single-layer metasurfaces, motivating a systematic study of their topological behavior.
method: The authors theoretically and/or numerically analyze bilayer metasurface structures, using coupled-mode or topological band frameworks to characterize BIC dynamics under interlayer and intralayer coupling.
result: The work reveals how bilayer coupling governs the topological evolution and dynamics of BICs, providing design principles for controlling these resonant states.
conclusion: Bilayer metasurfaces enable rich topological control of BICs, with potential applications in nanophotonics and resonant metasurface design.

title: Transient Response Of Stochastic Dynamical Systems Via A Quasipotential Iterative Cell Mapping Method
authors: Yifan Zhu, Xiaole Yue, Bin Pei, And Yong Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Yifan Zhu, Xiaole Yue, Bin Pei, and Yong Xu

Transient response analysis plays a crucial role in predicting extreme deviations and potential instability risks during critical start-up and disturbance stages. However, computing transient probability evolution in high-dimensional stochastic dynamical systems remains challenging because the numbe…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054215] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a quasipotential iterative cell mapping method for efficiently computing transient probability evolution and extreme deviations in high-dimensional stochastic dynamical systems.
motivation: Transient response analysis is important for predicting instability risks during start-up and disturbance stages, but direct computation of transient probability evolution in high-dimensional stochastic systems is numerically prohibitive.
method: The authors propose a quasipotential iterative cell mapping approach to approximate transient probability distributions in stochastic dynamical systems while avoiding the curse of dimensionality.
result: The method is presented as a computational framework for transient response analysis, with application to high-dimensional stochastic systems where conventional probability evolution methods are infeasible.
conclusion: The quasipotential iterative cell mapping method provides a practical tool for transient response prediction in complex stochastic dynamical systems, though it is not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Simulation Studies Of Resonant Excitation Of Electron Bernstein Waves In Capacitive Discharges
authors: Deepak Gautam, Sarveshwar Sharma, Igor Kaganovich, And Bhooshan Paradkar
abstract:
Author(s): Deepak Gautam, Sarveshwar Sharma, Igor Kaganovich, and Bhooshan Paradkar

The behavior of capacitive coupled plasma (CCP) discharges is investigated in a mildly magnetized regime, defined by the condition [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] are the cyclotron and radio frequenci…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055206] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: Simulation study of resonant excitation of electron Bernstein waves in mildly magnetized capacitive coupled plasma (CCP) discharges.
motivation: Understanding wave excitation and power absorption in magnetized capacitive discharges is important for controlling plasma heating and uniformity in industrial plasma processing.
method: Particle-in-cell / fluid simulation studies of CCP discharges in a mildly magnetized regime where the cyclotron frequency is comparable to or below the RF frequency, examining resonant excitation of electron Bernstein waves.
result: The simulations identify conditions under which electron Bernstein waves are resonantly excited and characterize the resulting discharge behavior and power deposition.
conclusion: Magnetized CCP operation enables resonant Bernstein wave excitation that modifies discharge dynamics, with implications for plasma source design.

title: Anomalous Dewetting Dynamics In Active Entangled Polymer Films: Semiflexible Chains
authors: Mithun Chowdhury
abstract:
Author(s): Mithun Chowdhury

Dewetting of a thin polymer film probes the stress and mobility frozen in during preparation. A companion theory showed that self-propulsion enhances the elastic modulus of flexible active films through grip forces at entanglements. Here I derive the semiflexible case relevant to biological filament…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055411] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically analyzes dewetting dynamics in active entangled polymer films for semiflexible chains, extending a prior flexible-chain theory of activity-enhanced elasticity.
motivation: Dewetting of thin polymer films reveals frozen-in stress and mobility, and biological filaments motivate extending active-film theory beyond flexible chains to semiflexible entangled polymers.
method: The author derives a theoretical model for semiflexible active entangled polymer films, incorporating self-propulsion and grip forces at entanglements to describe dewetting behavior.
result: The semiflexible-chain theory predicts anomalous dewetting dynamics and modified elastic response relative to the flexible-chain case.
conclusion: The work generalizes active polymer film theory to semiflexible chains relevant to biological filaments, but it is outside the quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems directions.

title: Logarithmic Dispersion At Marginal Stability In Collective Attention
authors: Keisuke Okamura
abstract:
Author(s): Keisuke Okamura

How cross-sectional heterogeneity evolves in nonequilibrium populations of competing, aging units is a collective question that cannot be resolved from a representative trajectory or the ensemble mean alone. Analysis of more than two million age-aligned English Wikipedia pageview trajectories from s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L052302] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: A statistical-physics analysis of over two million age-aligned English Wikipedia pageview trajectories showing logarithmic dispersion emerging at marginal stability in collective attention dynamics.
motivation: Cross-sectional heterogeneity in nonequilibrium populations of competing, aging units cannot be captured by representative trajectories or ensemble means, motivating a distribution-level analysis of collective attention.
method: Large-scale empirical analysis of more than two million age-aligned Wikipedia pageview time series, combined with stochastic/statistical modeling of aging and competing units near a marginal-stability regime.
result: The ensemble exhibits logarithmic rather than power-law or exponential dispersion at marginal stability, indicating a distinctive scaling of heterogeneity across age-aligned cohorts.
conclusion: Collective attention dynamics near marginal stability show logarithmic dispersion, providing insight into nonequilibrium population statistics — but entirely outside quantum information, thermodynamics of quantum systems, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Exact Island-size Distribution And Family-Vicsek Scaling Function In Homogeneous Growth With Size-linear Capture Numbers
authors: Vladimir G. Dubrovskii And Nickolay V. Sibirev
abstract:
Author(s): Vladimir G. Dubrovskii and Nickolay V. Sibirev

Family-Vicsek scaling of island-size distribution (ISD) is well known for homogeneous epitaxial islands with infinitely large ratios of surface diffusion coefficient over deposition rate, where the capture numbers are asymptotically linear in size. Linear rows of surface adatoms, droplets in the cav…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054117] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives exact island-size distributions and Family-Vicsek scaling for homogeneous epitaxial growth with size-linear capture numbers.
motivation: The authors aim to analytically describe island-size distributions in thin-film growth where capture numbers are asymptotically linear in island size.
method: They use scaling theory and exact analytical treatment of homogeneous growth kinetics with linear capture numbers.
result: They obtain exact island-size distribution forms and identify the corresponding Family-Vicsek scaling function.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical benchmark for island-size statistics in epitaxial growth, but it is not connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Self-learning Mechanical Circuits
authors: Vishal P. Patil, Ian Ho, And Manu Prakash
abstract:
Author(s): Vishal P. Patil, Ian Ho, and Manu Prakash

Adaptivity and learning are ubiquitous in living systems, from cytoplasm and biofilms to animal flocks. However, the problem of designing nonliving mechanical systems capable of self-learning behavior continues to present theoretical and experimental challenges. Here we introduce self-learning mecha…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054211] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The authors design and demonstrate mechanical circuits built from simple elastic/fluidic elements that autonomously adapt their response—i.e., 'self-learn'—without any electronic control or digital computation.
motivation: Adaptivity and learning are pervasive in living systems (cytoplasm, biofilms, flocks), but creating nonliving mechanical systems that learn is an outstanding theoretical and experimental challenge with potential relevance to autonomous soft robotics and embodied computation.
method: The paper introduces a class of 'self-learning mechanical circuits' composed of coupled nonlinear mechanical elements whose effective coupling strengths or thresholds are modified by their own dynamical history, allowing the network to reconfigure in response to repeated stimuli; behavior is characterized experimentally and with simple models.
