result: The circuits exhibit history-dependent adaptation, converging toward improved performance on simple tasks without external computation or global control, demonstrating learning-like behavior in purely mechanical media.
conclusion: Mechanical networks can perform elementary forms of learning and adaptation, opening a route toward nonliving, embodied adaptive matter; the work is classical and fully macroscopic, with no quantum information or thermodynamic-information content.

title: Promotion Of Cooperation In Deme-structured Populations With Growth-merging Dynamics
authors: Damien Ribière, Alia Abbara, And Anne-Florence Bitbol
abstract:
Author(s): Damien Ribière, Alia Abbara, and Anne-Florence Bitbol

The spatial structure of populations may promote the emergence and maintenance of cooperation. Cooperation in the prisoner's dilemma is favored under specific update rules in evolutionary graph theory models with one individual per node of a graph, but this effect vanishes in models with well-mixed …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054404] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how growth-merging dynamics in deme-structured (subdivided) populations can promote the evolution of cooperation in prisoner's dilemma games.
motivation: Spatial structure is known to favor cooperation in evolutionary graph models with one individual per node, but this effect disappears in well-mixed or deme-structured populations, motivating a search for mechanisms that restore cooperation in such settings.
method: The authors analyze evolutionary game dynamics in deme-structured populations where demes grow and merge, using analytical modeling and possibly simulations of prisoner's dilemma update rules.
result: Growth-merging dynamics are shown to favor cooperation under certain conditions, in contrast to standard well-mixed deme models where cooperation typically vanishes.
conclusion: Population-level growth and merging provide a structural mechanism promoting cooperation, extending spatial reciprocity ideas beyond single-individual-per-node graph models.

title: Product Expansion Of Reservoir States For Robust Chaotic Time Series Prediction
authors: Kaiwen Jiang, Michael Small, And Yong Zou
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiwen Jiang, Michael Small, and Yong Zou

Reservoir computing (RC) excels at chaotic time series prediction but suffers from high sensitivity to hyperparameters (spectral radius, sparsity) and requires large reservoirs, limiting its utility. To overcome these limitations, we propose an enhanced RC framework that introduces time-shift transf…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054209] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an enhanced reservoir computing framework using time-shift transformations and product expansions of reservoir states to make chaotic time series prediction more robust to hyperparameter choices.
motivation: Reservoir computing predicts chaotic time series well but is highly sensitive to hyperparameters such as spectral radius and sparsity and demands large reservoirs, which limits practical use.
method: The authors introduce time-shift transformations and a product expansion of reservoir states within a modified reservoir computing architecture, then benchmark it on chaotic time series prediction tasks.
result: The proposed framework reportedly reduces sensitivity to hyperparameters and improves prediction performance while requiring smaller reservoirs.
conclusion: Product-expanded reservoir states offer a more robust and efficient route to chaotic time series forecasting, though the work remains within classical machine learning and nonlinear dynamics.

title: Exact Amplitude Relations For Diffusion-limited Aggregation
authors: Thomas C. Halsey
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas C. Halsey

It has been known for several decades that the third moment of the multifractal spectrum of the harmonic measure for diffusion-limited aggregates is linked to the underlying fractal dimension of the cluster. We demonstrate, using an argument based on the Hastings-Levitov formulation of diffusion-lim…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054111] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives exact amplitude relations for diffusion-limited aggregation using the Hastings-Levitov formulation, linking multifractal spectrum moments to fractal dimension.
motivation: For decades, the third moment of the multifractal spectrum of harmonic measure in diffusion-limited aggregates has been known to relate to the cluster's fractal dimension. This work aims to clarify and extend such relations.
method: The author uses an argument based on the Hastings-Levitov formulation of diffusion-limited aggregation to derive exact amplitude relations.
result: Exact amplitude relations are obtained, providing a more precise connection between multifractal spectrum moments and the underlying fractal dimension of the cluster.
conclusion: The findings refine the theoretical understanding of diffusion-limited aggregation and its multifractal properties, with implications for fractal growth models.

title: Mapping The Limits Of Equilibrium In Sheared Granular Liquid Crystals
authors: Jacopo Bilotto, Martin Trulsson, And Jean-François Molinari
abstract:
Author(s): Jacopo Bilotto, Martin Trulsson, and Jean-François Molinari

While elongated particles in viscous fluids follow Jeffery orbits, their dynamics in dense granular flows remain unresolved. We demonstrate that sheared, low-friction granular rods do not follow these orbits, but instead reach a quasiequilibrium state quantitatively described by classical liquid cry…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043151] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: Sheared dense granular flows of elongated, low-friction rods are shown to abandon Jeffery orbits and instead settle into a quasiequilibrium state captured quantitatively by classical liquid-crystal theory.
motivation: Elongated particles in viscous fluids follow Jeffery orbits, but the orientational dynamics of rods in dense granular flows is unresolved, and it is unclear whether equilibrium-like descriptions apply.
method: Numerical simulations (discrete-element-type modelling) of sheared granular rods with low interparticle friction, combined with comparisons to classical liquid-crystal equilibrium theory.
result: The rods do not follow Jeffery orbits; instead their steady-state orientational statistics match predictions of classical liquid-crystal theory, defining the limits of an equilibrium-like description.
conclusion: Dense granular rod flows admit a quasiequilibrium mapping to liquid crystals, offering a predictive framework while delimiting where such equilibrium analogies break down.

title: Geometric Brownian Motion With Intermittent Entries And Exits
authors: Suvam Pal, Viktor Stojkoski, Arnab Pal, And Trifce Sandev
abstract:
Author(s): Suvam Pal, Viktor Stojkoski, Arnab Pal, and Trifce Sandev

We study a generalized geometric Brownian motion framework that incorporates both entries of new units and exit mechanisms for the current population, extending earlier stochastic resetting models where these rates are treated as identical. The model captures realistic features observed in many econ…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043145] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a generalized geometric Brownian motion model with intermittent entry and exit mechanisms for populations or units, extending stochastic resetting frameworks.
motivation: The authors aim to capture realistic economic and population dynamics where new units enter and existing units exit at different rates, going beyond models that treat entry and exit as identical.
method: They formulate and analyze a stochastic process combining geometric Brownian motion with state-dependent or rate-based entry and exit mechanisms, likely using analytical and numerical methods for stochastic differential equations.
result: The model characterizes how differing entry and exit rates modify the distribution and long-time behavior of the process compared with standard stochastic resetting or geometric Brownian motion.
conclusion: The work provides a more realistic stochastic framework for systems with intermittent population changes, but it does not address quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Geometric Origin Of Oxygen Ordering And The Solubility Limit In Niobium
authors: Dingxin Fan, Guangming Cheng, Kyle Zhao, And Nan Yao
abstract:
Author(s): Dingxin Fan, Guangming Cheng, Kyle Zhao, and Nan Yao

We investigate early-stage Nb oxidation by combining first-principles calculations with high-resolution transmission electron microscopy. An ordered ε phase is identified, in which O atoms occupy octahedral interstitial sites in an alternating layered configuration. Oxygen incorporation proceeds thr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043125] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: Combined DFT and HRTEM study reveals an ordered epsilon phase of oxygen interstitials in niobium and explains the solubility limit of oxygen in Nb.
motivation: Niobium oxidation and oxygen solubility strongly affect the performance of Nb-based superconducting devices, so understanding early-stage O incorporation and its structural ordering is technologically important.
method: First-principles density functional calculations are combined with high-resolution transmission electron microscopy to identify O interstitial site occupancy and the resulting ordered structures.
result: An ordered epsilon phase is found in which O atoms occupy octahedral interstitial sites in an alternating layered configuration, and the geometric origin of the oxygen solubility limit is identified.
conclusion: Oxygen ordering in Nb is governed by geometric/structural factors, which sets the solubility limit and clarifies early-stage oxidation behavior relevant to Nb-based device fabrication.

title: Four-body Postcollision Interaction And Two-photon Pathways In Neon Double-core-hole States
authors: Abhishek Verma et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Abhishek Verma et al.

Double-core-hole (DCH) states offer a unique window into electron correlation and multielectron dynamics. Using intense x-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) pulses and high photon-energy resolution, we generate DCH states in neon via sequential absorption of two x-ray photons within the [MATH] core-hole l…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043127] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: An experimental XFEL study of neon double-core-hole states revealing four-body postcollision interaction effects and two-photon absorption pathways.
motivation: Double-core-hole states provide a sensitive probe of electron correlation and multielectron dynamics in atomic systems, motivating high-resolution spectroscopic investigation with intense x-ray pulses.
method: Intense x-ray free-electron laser pulses with high photon-energy resolution are used to create DCH states in neon via sequential two-photon absorption within the core-hole lifetime, with electron/ion spectroscopy resolving the decay channels.
result: The measurements reveal signatures of four-body postcollision interaction and identify competing two-photon pathways populating the double-core-hole states.
conclusion: The findings refine the understanding of correlated multielectron dynamics and postcollision interaction in x-ray-driven atomic photoionization.

title: AI-Newton: A Concept-driven Physical Law Discovery System Without Prior Physical Knowledge
authors: You-Le Fang, Dong-Shan Jian, Xiang Li, And Yan-Qing Ma
abstract:
Author(s): You-Le Fang, Dong-Shan Jian, Xiang Li, and Yan-Qing Ma

While current artificial intelligence (AI)-driven methods excel at deriving empirical models from individual experiments, a significant challenge remains in uncovering the common fundamental physics that underlie these models—a task at which human physicists are adept. To bridge this gap, we introdu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043129] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce AI-Newton, a concept-driven system that rediscovers fundamental physical laws from experimental data without being given prior physical knowledge.
motivation: Existing AI methods produce empirical fits to individual experiments but fail to uncover the shared underlying physics that human physicists identify across datasets.
method: A concept-driven symbolic/AI framework that abstracts reusable physical concepts from multiple experimental datasets and composes them into candidate law structures, which are then validated against data.
result: The system recovers known physical laws (e.g., classical mechanics relations) from synthetic and real data, demonstrating that shared concepts can be induced without hard-coded physics priors.
conclusion: Concept formation is a viable route toward automated discovery of unifying physical theory, offering a step beyond per-experiment empirical modeling.

title: Beyond Constant Error: Heteroscedastic Bayesian Model Combination For Modeling Unmeasured Nuclei
authors: B. Knight, S. Lalit, P. Giuliani, K. Godbey, W. Nazarewicz, A. Ravlić, And P.-G. Reinhard
abstract:
Author(s): B. Knight, S. Lalit, P. Giuliani, K. Godbey, W. Nazarewicz, A. Ravlić, and P.-G. Reinhard

Experimentally inaccessible regions of the nuclear chart remain a challenge for global models of atomic nuclei to predict. This includes exotic nuclei near particle drip lines, superheavy elements at the extremes of mass and charge, and the neutron-rich pathways of astrophysical processes in explosi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043130] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a heteroscedastic Bayesian model-combination framework for extrapolating nuclear mass and structure models into experimentally inaccessible regions of the nuclear chart.
motivation: Global nuclear models must predict properties of exotic nuclei near drip lines, superheavy elements, and r-process pathways where no data exist, and standard constant-error assumptions misrepresent extrapolation uncertainty.
method: The authors extend Bayesian model averaging/combination by allowing model-error variances to vary (heteroscedasticity) across the nuclear chart, using available experimental data to constrain the local error behavior of several nuclear models.
result: The heteroscedastic approach yields more realistic, position-dependent uncertainty quantification for predicted nuclear observables than constant-error Bayesian combination, particularly in regions far from measured nuclei.
conclusion: Accounting for non-constant model error improves the reliability of extrapolations and uncertainty estimates for unmeasured nuclei, informing both nuclear structure theory and astrophysical r-process modeling.

title: Data-driven Progressive Discovery Of Physical Laws
authors: Mingkun Xia And Weiwei Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingkun Xia and Weiwei Zhang

Symbolic regression is a powerful tool for knowledge discovery, enabling the extraction of interpretable mathematical expressions directly from data. However, conventional symbolic discovery typically follows an end-to-end, “one-step” process, which often generates lengthy and physically meaningless…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043120] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a data-driven progressive symbolic regression approach for discovering interpretable physical laws from data.
motivation: Conventional symbolic regression often uses an end-to-end one-step search, which can produce lengthy and physically meaningless expressions.
method: It introduces a progressive discovery framework that builds interpretable mathematical expressions in stages rather than performing a single end-to-end symbolic search.
result: The approach is presented as improving the extraction of interpretable and physically meaningful laws from data compared with conventional symbolic discovery.
conclusion: The work is relevant to symbolic regression and automated scientific discovery but has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Cosmological And High-Energy Physics Implications From Gravitational-Wave Background Searches In LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA’s O1–O4a Runs
authors: A. G. Abac et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): A. G. Abac et al. (LIGO Scientific Collaboration, Virgo Collaboration, and KAGRA Collaboration)

Numerous well-motivated particle-physics-based models are constrained using the most recent LIGO-Virgo gravitational-wave data.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041023] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA stochastic gravitational-wave background searches from O1–O4a are used to constrain cosmological and high-energy particle-physics models.
motivation: Numerous well-motivated particle-physics and cosmological scenarios predict stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds, and the latest observing runs provide an opportunity to test them.
method: Cross-correlation searches for an isotropic stochastic gravitational-wave background in LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA data from the O1 through O4a runs are interpreted in terms of predicted spectra from various cosmological and particle-physics models.
result: The non-detection (or measured spectrum) places new upper bounds on model parameters, ruling out or constraining regions of parameter space for the considered scenarios.
conclusion: Gravitational-wave background searches provide competitive, complementary constraints on high-energy physics and cosmology, with prospects improving as detector sensitivity grows.

title: Erratum: Faster Quantum Chemistry Simulations On A Quantum Computer With Improved Tensor Factorization And Active Volume Compilation [prx Quantum 6, 030337 (2025)]
authors: Athena Caesura, Cristian L. Cortes, William Pol, Sukin Sim, Mark Steudtner, Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, Michael Streif, And Christofer S. Tautermann
abstract:
Author(s): Athena Caesura, Cristian L. Cortes, William Pol, Sukin Sim, Mark Steudtner, Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, Michael Streif, and Christofer S. Tautermann
[PRX Quantum 7, 049901] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting the authors' prior PRX Quantum paper on faster quantum chemistry simulations using improved tensor factorization and active volume compilation.
motivation: The original work aimed to reduce quantum resource requirements for chemistry simulations by improving tensor factorization and compilation techniques; the erratum serves to correct errors in that published work.
method: As an erratum, it reports corrections to the original manuscript rather than introducing new methodology, presumably amending equations, data, or resource estimates from the tensor-factorization and active-volume-compilation approach.
result: The corrections revise specific details of the original publication (e.g., figures, tables, or resource counts) without altering the overall scope of the quantum chemistry simulation results.
conclusion: The erratum contains no new research contribution of relevance to quantum information theory, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Theory For The Power Threshold Of The $L\text{−}H$ Transition In Tokamaks
authors: B. de Lucca, P. Ricci, B. Labit, D. Mancini, L. N. Stenger, And Z. Tecchiolli
abstract:
Author(s): B. De Lucca, P. Ricci, B. Labit, D. Mancini, L. N. Stenger, and Z. Tecchiolli

Flux-driven two-fluid simulations in a diverted tokamak exhibit a confinement transition when a critical heating threshold is exceeded, as in experimental observations of the L-H transition. The simulations show that electromagnetic drift-wave turbulence spontaneously generates a sheared $\mathbit{E…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 205101] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: Flux-driven two-fluid simulations of a diverted tokamak reproduce the L-H confinement transition and predict the power threshold from spontaneous sheared E×B flow generation by electromagnetic drift-wave turbulence.
motivation: The physics behind the heating-power threshold of the L-H transition in tokamaks is not fully understood; a first-principles theory would help predict and control confinement regimes in fusion devices.
method: Global flux-driven two-fluid (drift-wave) simulations including electromagnetic effects in a diverted tokamak geometry, analyzing turbulence-driven flow generation as heating is increased.
result: A confinement transition occurs above a critical heating power, associated with spontaneous sheared E×B flow generated by turbulence, yielding a threshold that can be compared with experimental scaling.
conclusion: The simulations offer a theory for the L-H power threshold rooted in turbulence self-organization, supporting predictive modelling of tokamak edge transport.

title: Image Quality Gain And Efficiency Limits In In-line Imaging
authors: Timur E. Gureyev, David M. Paganin, And Harry M. Quiney
abstract:
Author(s): Timur E. Gureyev, David M. Paganin, and Harry M. Quiney

In-line phase-contrast imaging, also known as propagation-based imaging or Gabor holography, is capable of delivering significant gains in image quality, compared to attenuation-based imaging at the same radiation dose. Image quality metrics, including signal-to-noise ratio and spatial resolution, a…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053508] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes image quality gains and efficiency limits of in-line (propagation-based) phase-contrast imaging relative to attenuation-based imaging at fixed radiation dose.
motivation: In-line phase-contrast imaging can substantially improve image quality over conventional attenuation contrast, but a quantitative framework relating dose, signal-to-noise ratio, and spatial resolution is needed to establish fundamental efficiency limits.
method: The authors develop an analytical/theoretical treatment of image quality metrics — SNR and spatial resolution — for in-line phase-contrast imaging, comparing performance against attenuation-based imaging under equal dose constraints, presumably using wave-optics propagation and contrast-transfer analysis.
result: The paper derives conditions and scaling laws quantifying when and how much image quality gain in-line phase contrast can deliver, and identifies the limits on imaging efficiency imposed by dose and resolution trade-offs.
conclusion: In-line phase-contrast imaging offers quantifiable image quality advantages but is bounded by fundamental efficiency limits, providing guidance for optimal design of propagation-based imaging setups.

title: From Compressed- To Stretched-exponential Dynamics In Metallic Glasses
authors: Birte Riechers, Achraf Atila, Reza Rashidi, Fabian Westermeier, Michael Sprung, And Robert Maaß
abstract:
Author(s): Birte Riechers, Achraf Atila, Reza Rashidi, Fabian Westermeier, Michael Sprung, and Robert Maaß

The microscopic dynamics of metallic glasses are fundamentally governed by their out-of-equilibrium state. In this study, we combine synchrotron x-ray photon correlation spectroscopy with atomistic simulations to track the evolution of structural dynamics from the out-of-equilibrium glassy solid int…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274202] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: Combining synchrotron x-ray photon correlation spectroscopy with atomistic simulations, the authors track how structural relaxation dynamics in metallic glasses evolve from compressed-exponential to stretched-exponential behaviour as the out-of-equilibrium glass ages toward equilibrium.
motivation: The microscopic relaxation dynamics of metallic glasses are controlled by their non-equilibrium state, but a clear picture of how those dynamics cross over between different functional forms during aging is lacking.
method: The study uses synchrotron-based x-ray photon correlation spectroscopy (XPCS) to measure the intermediate scattering function, complemented by atomistic molecular-dynamics simulations of the glass-forming system.
result: The measured correlation functions show a systematic transition from compressed-exponential to stretched-exponential decay as the glass relaxes from its initial out-of-equilibrium state toward a more stable configuration.
conclusion: The observed crossover links macroscopic relaxation signatures to microscopic structural heterogeneity in glasses, offering a quantitative window on aging and equilibration in disordered materials.

title: Normal-field Evolution And The Breakdown Of Classical Tearing In Current Sheets
authors: Grzegorz Kowal And Diego A. Falceta-Gonçalves
abstract:
Author(s): Grzegorz Kowal and Diego A. Falceta-Gonçalves

Classical resistive tearing theory assumes a prescribed current-sheet equilibrium, but a finite normal magnetic field can evolve the background on the tearing timescale. For a transversely pressure-balanced Harris profile of initial half-thickness [MATH] and asymptotic reconnecting-field magnitude ${B}…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055204] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: A plasma-physics study of how a finite normal magnetic field modifies the Harris current-sheet equilibrium and destroys classical resistive tearing on the tearing timescale.
motivation: Classical resistive tearing theory presumes a fixed equilibrium current sheet, an assumption that fails when a normal magnetic field evolves the background as fast as the tearing mode grows.
method: Analytical treatment of a transversely pressure-balanced Harris profile with initial half-thickness and asymptotic reconnecting field, examining the coupled evolution of the background equilibrium and the tearing instability.
result: The normal field drives background evolution on the tearing timescale, so the standard prescribed-equilibrium tearing picture breaks down and modified growth behaviour results.
conclusion: Tearing in current sheets with a finite normal field requires a time-dependent equilibrium treatment rather than the classical static Harris-sheet analysis.

title: Automated Physics-informed Neural-network-based Calibration Of Highly Segmented Silicon Telescopes
authors: M. Rejmund, A. Lemasson, P. Morfouace, D. Ramos, J. Taieb, And J. D. Frankland
abstract:
Author(s): M. Rejmund, A. Lemasson, P. Morfouace, D. Ramos, J. Taieb, and J. D. Frankland

Transfer and multinucleon transfer reactions are essential tools for probing nuclear structure and reaction dynamics, requiring precise determination of the particle identification, energy, and emission angles of reaction products. The increasing granularity of modern silicon telescope arrays signif…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043143] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an automated physics-informed neural-network method to calibrate highly segmented silicon telescope arrays used in nuclear reaction experiments.
motivation: Transfer and multinucleon transfer reaction studies require precise particle identification, energy, and emission-angle determination, which becomes challenging as silicon telescope arrays grow more highly segmented.
method: The authors use physics-informed neural networks to automate the calibration of segmented silicon telescopes, likely leveraging detector physics constraints and experimental data to infer calibration parameters.
result: The approach is presented as an automated calibration procedure for highly segmented silicon telescope arrays, aimed at improving the determination of reaction-product properties.
conclusion: The work is relevant to nuclear detector instrumentation and data analysis rather than quantum information science, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Order By Inertia In Spinning Active Matter: Holey Fluids And Spin-Textured Crystals
authors: Camille Jorge And Denis Bartolo
abstract:
Author(s): Camille Jorge and Denis Bartolo

Experiments with macroscopic spinning particles that stir the surrounding fluid at high Reynolds numbers reveal that inertia plays an organizing role in active systems, promoting the emergence of collective structured phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041034] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that inertia organizes macroscopic spinning active particles into structured collective phases, including holey fluids and spin-textured crystals.
motivation: Active matter experiments often focus on overdamped or low-Reynolds-number regimes; this work explores how inertia affects collective organization in spinning particle systems.
method: Experiments use macroscopic spinning particles that stir surrounding fluid at high Reynolds numbers, and the resulting collective phases are characterized experimentally.
result: Inertia promotes the emergence of collective structured phases, specifically holey fluids and spin-textured crystals.
conclusion: Inertia can play an organizing role in active systems, generating ordered collective structures beyond those found in overdamped active matter.

title: Atomistic Simulation Of Subcritical Crack Growth In Glass In Vacuum
authors: Swati Gupta, Mark A. Wilson, Scott J. Grutzik, And Derek H. Warner
abstract:
Author(s): Swati Gupta, Mark A. Wilson, Scott J. Grutzik, and Derek H. Warner

We report atomistic simulations of subcritical crack growth rates in silica glass that quantitatively align with experimental data. This result was achieved by a careful selection of simulation cell geometry and boundary conditions, a novel crack tip tracking algorithm, a robust interatomic potentia…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 206101] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: Atomistic simulations reproduce experimentally measured subcritical crack growth rates in silica glass in vacuum using tailored cell geometry, a crack-tip tracking algorithm, and a robust interatomic potential.
motivation: Subcritical crack growth governs the slow, stress-driven failure of brittle glasses, but quantitative agreement between atomistic simulation and experiment has been elusive, limiting predictive modeling of fracture.
method: Molecular dynamics/atomistic simulations of silica glass with carefully chosen simulation cell geometry and boundary conditions, a novel crack tip tracking algorithm, and a validated interatomic potential.
result: The simulated subcritical crack growth rates quantitatively match experimental data for glass in vacuum.
conclusion: Careful simulation design enables quantitative, experimentally consistent atomistic modeling of crack kinetics in amorphous silica, offering a predictive route for studying fracture in brittle materials.

title: Surface-induced Contraction Mechanism Of Basal Plane Dislocations In 4H-SiC: Dislocation Dynamics Analysis
authors: Atsuo Hirano, Noboru Takahashi, And Akiyuki Takahashi
abstract:
Author(s): Atsuo Hirano, Noboru Takahashi, and Akiyuki Takahashi

Basal plane dislocations (BPDs) in the epitaxial layer in 4H-SiC is one of the remarkable manufacturing issues because they degrade device performance. Although most BPDs are converted to threading edge dislocations (TEDs), some remain. Therefore, elucidating the mechanism of BPD-TED conversion is c…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264106] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: Dislocation dynamics simulations explain how basal plane dislocations in 4H-SiC epitaxial layers are converted into threading edge dislocations near the surface.
motivation: Basal plane dislocations degrade 4H-SiC device performance; most convert to benign threading edge dislocations but some persist, so the conversion mechanism must be understood.
method: Dislocation dynamics (DD) analysis is used to model the stress and force conditions that drive BPD-TED conversion at the surface.
result: A surface-induced contraction mechanism is identified, showing how image forces and strain fields near the surface drive basal plane dislocations to contract and convert.
conclusion: The proposed mechanism clarifies BPD-TED conversion and could guide epitaxial growth strategies to eliminate residual BPDs in SiC devices.

title: Erratum: Thermoelectric Semiconductor Database: DFT-based Discovery And Experimental Validation [Phys. Rev. B 113, 205203 (2026)]
authors: Yujie Xia, Mingran Kong, Pu Miao, Xiangjun Tan, Shaoqiu Lyu, Muzhi Wang, Tiejun Zhu, Chenguang Fu, And Tiantian Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Xia, Mingran Kong, Pu Miao, Xiangjun Tan, Shaoqiu Lyu, Muzhi Wang, Tiejun Zhu, Chenguang Fu, and Tiantian Zhang
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 289901] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: An erratum correcting a DFT-based thermoelectric semiconductor database paper with experimental validation.
motivation: The original work aimed to provide a first-principles database of thermoelectric semiconductors to accelerate materials discovery for thermoelectric energy conversion.
method: High-throughput density functional theory calculations of electronic and thermal transport properties, combined with experimental synthesis and characterization of selected candidates; the erratum corrects errors in the published record.
result: Corrections to the previously published database entries and associated experimental data are reported.
conclusion: The erratum ensures the accuracy of the thermoelectric materials database, but contains no quantum information, thermodynamics-of-information, or quantum-device content.

title: Diffusive-scaling Lax-Wendroff Lattice Boltzmann Method On Nonuniform Grids: Theory, Stability, And Validation
authors: Irwan Ary Dharmawan
abstract:
Author(s): Irwan Ary Dharmawan

We analyze the diffusive-scaling asymptotics of the two-dimensional D2Q9 lattice Boltzmann scheme with a Bhatnagar–Gross–Krook (BGK) collision step and a Lax–Wendroff transport step on separable nonuniform grids, obtained from a uniform computational grid by two independent one-dimensional diffeomor…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055302] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops and analyzes a diffusive-scaling Lax-Wendroff lattice Boltzmann (D2Q9-BGK) scheme on separable nonuniform grids, providing stability theory and numerical validation.
motivation: Nonuniform grids are needed to efficiently resolve multiscale features in lattice Boltzmann simulations, but a rigorous asymptotic and stability theory for Lax-Wendroff transport steps on such grids was lacking.
method: The authors derive diffusive-scaling asymptotics for the D2Q9 BGK scheme with a Lax-Wendroff transport step on grids generated by two independent one-dimensional diffeomorphisms, and perform a stability analysis supported by numerical tests.
result: The analysis yields conditions under which the scheme recovers the correct diffusion asymptotics and remains stable on nonuniform grids, confirmed by validation benchmarks.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical and practical foundation for using Lax-Wendroff lattice Boltzmann methods on nonuniform grids in classical computational fluid dynamics.

title: Dynamical Investigation Of A Multirhythmic Vibroimpact Self-sustained System With Enhanced Memory Damping Regime According To Correlated Noise Excitation
authors: R. Mbakob Yonkeu, Norbert Marwan, E. N. Francoise, R. Yamapi, And Jurgen Kurths
abstract:
Author(s): R. Mbakob Yonkeu, Norbert Marwan, E. N. Francoise, R. Yamapi, and Jurgen Kurths

Investigating the dynamics of vibroimpact self-sustaining systems is of immense scientific interest, because systems that undergo vibroimpact interactions can be found in various engineering contexts. Repercussions and associated noise are prevalent in mechanical engineering. Conversely, in a self-s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054214] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes the nonlinear dynamics of a multirhythmic vibroimpact self-sustained mechanical system driven by correlated noise under an enhanced memory damping regime.
motivation: Vibroimpact self-sustaining systems appear widely in mechanical engineering, where impacts and associated noise are pervasive; understanding their dynamics is therefore of practical engineering interest.
method: The authors study a deterministic-stochastic vibroimpact oscillator model incorporating correlated noise excitation and a memory (fractional-like) damping term, using analytical and numerical dynamical-systems techniques.
result: The study characterizes the system's multirhythmic responses, bifurcation structure, and the influence of noise correlation and memory damping on its self-sustained impact dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides insight into how correlated noise and enhanced memory damping shape the dynamical regimes of vibroimpact self-sustained systems, with implications for mechanical engineering design.

title: Surface Energy Driven Crumpling Transition In Thin Sheets
authors: Aashna Chawla And Deepak Kumar
abstract:
Author(s): Aashna Chawla and Deepak Kumar

Thin sheets have been predicted to transition from a flat to a crumpled state at a high enough temperature driven by thermal fluctuations. However, such a thermal crumpling transition has been elusive in experiments. We report the observation of a capillary crumpling transition in thin solid sheets …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055503] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: Thin solid sheets are observed to undergo a capillary-driven crumpling transition, a classical-mechanical analogue of the long-sought thermal crumpling transition predicted for fluctuating membranes.
motivation: Theory predicts that thermally fluctuating thin sheets should crumple above a critical temperature, but experimental realization of a thermal crumpling transition has remained elusive, motivating a search for alternative driving mechanisms.
method: The authors experimentally study thin solid sheets and analyze their flat-to-crumpled morphology change, attributing the transition to capillary forces rather than thermal fluctuations.
result: A capillary crumpling transition is observed in thin solid sheets, reproducing the flat-to-crumpled morphological change expected from the thermal crumpling scenario.
conclusion: Capillary effects can substitute for thermal fluctuations in driving crumpling, offering an accessible experimental route to membrane crumpling phenomenology.

title: Electrohydraulic Fields Generated By Active Transport At Tissue Interfaces
authors: Amit Singh Vishen, Ahandeep Manna, And Frank Jülicher
abstract:
Author(s): Amit Singh Vishen, Ahandeep Manna, and Frank Jülicher

Living cells and tissues can generate complex patterns of electric fields and fluid flows, which can play important role in physiology. Both fields and flows are rooted in ion transport across biological interfaces—cell membranes and epithelial cell layers. Here, we develop a unified electrohydrauli…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043150] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a unified electrohydraulic theory describing how ion transport across cell membranes and epithelial layers generates coupled electric fields and fluid flows in living tissues.
motivation: Cells and tissues produce complex patterns of electric fields and flows that matter physiologically, and both arise from ion transport across biological interfaces, yet a unified continuum description was lacking.
method: A theoretical electrohydraulic framework is constructed that couples ion transport, electric potential, and fluid flow at tissue interfaces, likely analyzed via continuum transport equations and linear stability or boundary-condition analysis.
result: The model shows how active ion transport at membranes and epithelial layers produces characteristic electrohydraulic field patterns, linking transport activity to emergent electric and flow structures.
conclusion: Electrohydraulic coupling at biological interfaces offers a general mechanism for pattern formation in physiology, with implications for tissue-scale electrical and fluid dynamics.

title: Explosive Connectivity And Mechanical Rigidity In Cubic Lattice Structures
authors: Trenton Lau And Gary P. T. Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Trenton Lau and Gary P. T. Choi

We study explosive connectivity and mechanical rigidity in three-dimensional cubic lattice structures under Achlioptas-type product-rule dynamics. Our work combines extensive numerical simulation with a theoretical framework based on rigorous finite-size scaling. Using massive-scale simulations up t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043134] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies explosive connectivity transitions and mechanical rigidity in three-dimensional cubic lattice structures under Achlioptas-type product-rule dynamics using large-scale simulations and finite-size scaling.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how nonstandard percolation-like connectivity rules affect rigidity and network formation in cubic lattices.
method: They combine massive-scale numerical simulations with a theoretical framework based on rigorous finite-size scaling analysis.
result: The work characterizes explosive connectivity behavior and its relation to mechanical rigidity in cubic lattice structures, supported by scaling analyses.
conclusion: The findings clarify the interplay between connectivity transitions and rigidity in three-dimensional lattice systems, but are outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Contraction-deformation Coupling Enables The Wave-driven Morphodynamics And Mode-locking Of Confined Active Gel Droplets
authors: Ryota Sakamoto And Arash Abedijaberi
abstract:
Author(s): Ryota Sakamoto and Arash Abedijaberi

Wavelike patterns play fundamental roles in living systems, from single cells to cell collectives, organizing essential functions from wound repair to morphogenesis. While biochemical waves are well established, it remains unclear how the force propagation of cytoskeletal contraction waves regulates…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043109] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that coupling between contraction and deformation in confined active gel droplets produces wave-driven morphodynamics and mode-locking behavior, mimicking wavelike patterning in living systems.
motivation: Biochemical waves are well understood, but how mechanical force propagation from cytoskeletal contraction waves organizes large-scale shape changes in cells and cell collectives remains unclear.
method: Confined active gel droplets are modeled/observed with a contraction-deformation coupling, analyzing the resulting wave dynamics and mode-locking of the oscillatory patterns.
result: The coupling is found to be sufficient to generate wave-driven morphodynamics and to lock the droplet's shape oscillations into discrete modes.
conclusion: Contraction-deformation coupling provides a generic mechanism for force-driven pattern formation and mode-locking in active, cytoskeletal-like materials.

title: Orientation-Dependent Structural Phase Transitions And Melting In Shock-Compressed MgO
authors: Raymond F. Smith, Saransh Singh, Zixuan Ye, Marius Millot, Melissa Sims, Anirudh Hari, Jon H. Eggert, Federica Coppari, And June K. Wicks
abstract:
Author(s): Raymond F. Smith, Saransh Singh, Zixuan Ye, Marius Millot, Melissa Sims, Anirudh Hari, Jon H. Eggert, Federica Coppari, and June K. Wicks

Shockwave observations resolve the high pressure structural transition and melting temperature of MgO, a critical planetary building block.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041019] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: Shockwave experiments resolve the high-pressure structural phase transition and melting behavior of MgO, a key planetary building block.
motivation: MgO is a major component of planetary interiors, and its high-pressure phase diagram and melting curve are important for understanding rocky planet evolution and shock-compression physics.
method: The authors use shockwave observations, likely combining dynamic compression experiments with structural characterization, to identify phase transitions and melting under high pressure.
result: The study resolves orientation-dependent structural phase transitions and determines the melting temperature of MgO under shock compression.
conclusion: These findings refine the high-pressure phase diagram of MgO and provide constraints relevant to planetary interior models and shock physics.

title: All-Order Structure Of Static Gravitational Interactions And The Seventh Post-Newtonian Potential
authors: Giacomo Brunello, Manoj K. Mandal, Pierpaolo Mastrolia, Raj Patil, Matteo Pegorin, Sid Smith, And Jan Steinhoff
abstract:
Author(s): Giacomo Brunello, Manoj K. Mandal, Pierpaolo Mastrolia, Raj Patil, Matteo Pegorin, Sid Smith, and Jan Steinhoff

The symmetry of the post-Newtonian static sector enables the construction of the post-Newtonian two-body potential at any odd order, and the construction of the static contribution at the seventh post-Newtonian order for the first time.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 201401] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper exploits the symmetry of the post-Newtonian static sector to construct the two-body gravitational potential at arbitrary odd orders and explicitly derives the static contribution at seventh post-Newtonian order for the first time.
motivation: High-order post-Newtonian potentials are needed to match precision gravitational-wave observations of inspiraling binaries, requiring systematic all-order methods rather than order-by-order computation.
method: Uses the structural symmetry of the static post-Newtonian sector, combined with modern amplitudes/effective-field-theory techniques, to build the conservative two-body potential at any odd post-Newtonian order.
result: Provides a general all-order construction for odd-order static potentials and obtains the seventh post-Newtonian static potential explicitly.
conclusion: The framework extends precision gravitational dynamics for binary systems, though it concerns classical gravitational physics with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Lower Limit On The Double-Alpha Decay Of $^{224}\mathrm{Ra}$
authors: P. Belli, R. Bernabei, F. Cappella, V. Caracciolo, R. Cerulli, F. A. Danevich, V. Yu. Denisov, A. Incicchitti, D. V. Kasperovych, V. R. Klavdiienko, A. Leoncini, And V. I. Tretyak
abstract:
Author(s): P. Belli, R. Bernabei, F. Cappella, V. Caracciolo, R. Cerulli, F. A. Danevich, V. Yu. Denisov, A. Incicchitti, D. V. Kasperovych, V. R. Klavdiienko, A. Leoncini, and V. I. Tretyak

A GAGG:Ce crystal scintillator contaminated by thorium was used to search for double-[MATH] decay of [MATH]. Considering that the daughter nucleus is [MATH] with the half-life of 0.144 s, the time-amplitude method was utilized to search for [MATH] [MATH] events, whi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 202501] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: A GAGG:Ce crystal scintillator contaminated with thorium was used to search for the double-alpha decay of 224Ra, setting a lower limit on its half-life.
motivation: Double-alpha decay is a rare nuclear decay mode that has been rarely searched for experimentally, and nuclides like 224Ra offer a possible test case given the fast decay of the daughter nucleus.
method: A thorium-contaminated GAGG:Ce scintillator was operated as a detector, and a time-amplitude analysis was applied to search for the characteristic two-alpha coincidence events, exploiting the 0.144 s half-life of the daughter 220Rn.
result: No evidence for double-alpha decay of 224Ra was observed, and a lower limit on the half-life was established.
conclusion: The result constrains the double-alpha decay probability of 224Ra, contributing to the broader experimental study of rare nuclear decay modes.

title: Grain-Scale Origin Of Stick-Slip Waves In Silo Discharge: Influence Of Cohesion
authors: David Luce, Adrien Gans, Nicolas Vandewalle, And Sébastien Kiesgen de Richter
abstract:
Author(s): David Luce, Adrien Gans, Nicolas Vandewalle, and Sébastien Kiesgen de Richter

We track individual grains during the discharge of a quasi-2D silo and measure their instantaneous acceleration. This reveals collective deceleration waves which propagate upward through the packing, even though the outlet flow rate remains steady and follows the Beverloo law. Their characteristic f…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 208202] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: Tracking individual grains in a quasi-2D silo reveals collective deceleration waves propagating upward through the packing during discharge, and the authors examine how cohesion influences these stick-slip waves.
motivation: Discharge of granular material from silos follows the empirical Beverloo law with a steady outlet flow, yet the internal grain-scale dynamics that produce collective, wave-like behavior remain poorly understood, particularly when intergranular cohesion is present.
method: Individual grains are tracked experimentally during discharge of a quasi-2D silo, with instantaneous accelerations measured to identify collective deceleration waves, and cohesion is varied to probe its influence on wave characteristics.
result: Collective deceleration waves propagate upward through the packing even though the outlet flow rate stays constant and obeys the Beverloo law, with cohesion modifying the waves' characteristic properties.
conclusion: Stick-slip wave phenomena in silo discharge have a grain-scale origin, and cohesion plays a controlling role in their dynamics, linking microscopic grain interactions to macroscopic flow behavior.

title: Compressive Splitting In Brittle Solids: The Inverse Of Wrinkling In Sheets
authors: Maryam Khodadad, Francois Barthelat, John D. Clayton, George Gazonas, And Kaushik Dayal
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Khodadad, Francois Barthelat, John D. Clayton, George Gazonas, and Kaushik Dayal

Theory and experiments suggest that the mysterious fractures that appear when a brittle material is compressed result from a hidden buildup of internal tension.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 196101] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: A mechanics study proposing that cracks appearing under compression in brittle solids originate from a hidden buildup of internal tension, framed as the inverse phenomenon of wrinkling in thin sheets.
motivation: The origin of mysterious fractures that nucleate when brittle materials are compressed has remained poorly understood, motivating a combined theoretical and experimental investigation.
method: Theory and experiments on compressed brittle solids are combined to model the internal stress state and identify the mechanism driving splitting.
result: The authors argue that compressive splitting arises from a hidden internal tension buildup, establishing an analogy (inverse relationship) with wrinkling in sheets.
conclusion: The work offers a mechanical explanation for compressive fracture in brittle media, but has no connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Direct Sound Speed Measurements Of MgO Along Planetary Adiabats Up To 400 GPa Using Shock-ramp Compression
authors: Hannah J. Bausch, Joshua P. Townsend, Jean-Paul Davis, Sakun Duwal, Christopher T. Seagle, Tirzah M. Abbott, Alisha N. Clark, And Steven D. Jacobsen
abstract:
Author(s): Hannah J. Bausch, Joshua P. Townsend, Jean-Paul Davis, Sakun Duwal, Christopher T. Seagle, Tirzah M. Abbott, Alisha N. Clark, and Steven D. Jacobsen

Accurate models of planetary formation and evolution rely on equation-of-state (EOS) models for their constituent materials across wide ranges of pressure, temperature, and density. Currently, estimates of thermoelastic properties along Earth-like pressure and temperature adiabats (the geotherm) req…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274108] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports direct sound-speed measurements of MgO along planetary adiabats up to 400 GPa using shock-ramp compression to constrain equation-of-state models of planetary interiors.
motivation: Accurate models of planetary formation and evolution require equation-of-state data for constituent materials such as MgO across wide ranges of pressure, temperature, and density, particularly along Earth-like geotherm adiabats where existing data are sparse.
method: Shock-ramp compression experiments were used to drive MgO samples to multi-hundred-gigapascal pressures along adiabatic paths, with direct sound-speed measurements used to extract thermoelastic properties.
result: The measurements provide sound velocities and derived thermoelastic parameters for MgO along planetary adiabats up to 400 GPa, tightening constraints on equation-of-state models at geophysically relevant conditions.
conclusion: These data improve models of planetary interior structure and thermal evolution, offering experimentally grounded benchmarks for MgO along adiabatic compression paths.

title: Prospective Coding And Path Integration Emerge As Equilibrium Solutions Of Self-organizing Neural Networks With Firing-rate Adaptation
authors: Facundo Emina And Emilio Kropff
abstract:
Author(s): Facundo Emina and Emilio Kropff

Continuous attractor neural networks traditionally rely on prewired recurrent connectivity to model spatial representations, path integration, and anticipatory dynamics. However, the biological mechanisms through which this structured connectivity emerges via learning remain relatively unexplored. T…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054405] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that prospective coding and path integration can emerge as equilibrium solutions in self-organizing continuous attractor neural networks whose recurrent connectivity is learned rather than prewired, with firing-rate adaptation shaping the dynamics.
motivation: Continuous attractor networks typically assume structured recurrent connectivity is given, leaving open how such connectivity could arise biologically through learning.
method: The authors study self-organizing neural network models with firing-rate adaptation and derive/analyze equilibrium solutions of the learning dynamics for spatial representation and anticipatory (prospective) coding.
result: Path integration and prospective coding emerge as equilibrium solutions of the self-organizing dynamics, without hand-wired recurrent weights.
conclusion: Learning-based self-organization with adaptation suffices to generate attractor-based spatial and anticipatory representations, offering a biologically plausible account of their emergence.

title: Rate-sensitive Attenuation Of Elasticity In Growth-conditioned Biofilms
authors: L. Dinis, M. Calero, J. Martín-Roca, V. Bianco, A. K. Monnappa, I. López-Montero, B. Orgaz, C. Valeriani, And F. Monroy
abstract:
Author(s): L. Dinis, M. Calero, J. Martín-Roca, V. Bianco, A. K. Monnappa, I. López-Montero, B. Orgaz, C. Valeriani, and F. Monroy

This work investigates the oscillatory rheology of bacterial biofilms grown under either static or shaken conditions. The authors find that mature static-grown biofilms exhibit a frequency-dependent crossover from elastic-dominated to dissipation-dominated behavior, whereas shaken biofilms remain predominantly solidlike. They model these results with a rate-sensitive two-state description.

#BiophysicsSpotlight #TheoryExperiment


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055412] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: Oscillatory rheology reveals that static-grown bacterial biofilms soften with driving frequency while shaken-grown biofilms remain predominantly elastic, explained by a rate-sensitive two-state model.
motivation: Biofilms are viscoelastic living materials whose mechanical response depends on growth conditions, yet the frequency- and rate-dependence of their solid-to-liquid crossover is poorly characterized.
method: The authors perform oscillatory shear rheology on mature bacterial biofilms grown under static versus shaken conditions, and fit the data with a rate-sensitive two-state constitutive description.
result: Static-grown biofilms show a frequency-dependent crossover from elasticity-dominated to dissipation-dominated response, whereas shaken biofilms stay solidlike across the probed range.
conclusion: Growth-induced mechanical conditioning controls the rate sensitivity of biofilm elasticity, and a simple two-state model captures the observed rheological behavior.

title: Spontaneous Bending Of Cylindrical Hydrogels
authors: Javier Rojo-González, Adrián Arenas-Gullo, And Alberto Fernandez-Nieves
abstract:
Author(s): Javier Rojo-González, Adrián Arenas-Gullo, and Alberto Fernandez-Nieves

Among thermoresponsive hydrogels, poly-N-isopropylacrylamide gels are well known for their marked deswelling behavior near [MATH]; under slow, quasistatic heating, the gel shrinks affinely. In contrast, a rapid temperature quench above [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055410] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates spontaneous bending of cylindrical poly-N-isopropylacrylamide hydrogels driven by rapid temperature quenches above the volume phase transition temperature.
motivation: Thermoresponsive hydrogels such as PNIPAM deswell markedly near their critical temperature; while slow quasistatic heating yields affine shrinkage, the response to rapid quenches and the resulting mechanical instabilities remain poorly understood.
method: Cylindrical PNIPAM gel samples are subjected to rapid temperature quenches and their shape evolution and deswelling dynamics are characterized experimentally, presumably combined with a mechanical/continuum model of the inhomogeneous swelling.
result: Rapid quenching produces non-uniform internal stresses that cause the cylindrical gels to bend spontaneously, in contrast to the affine, shape-preserving shrinkage observed under slow heating.
conclusion: The work clarifies how quench rate controls the emergence of mechanical instabilities in thermoresponsive hydrogels, linking deswelling kinetics to macroscopic shape deformation.

title: Greedy Nearest-neighbor Approach To Quantify Site Revisitation: Comparing Two Sympatric Raven Species
authors: Bar Ashkenazi, Miguel de Guinea, Michael Assaf, And Ran Nathan
abstract:
Author(s): Bar Ashkenazi, Miguel de Guinea, Michael Assaf, and Ran Nathan

A central challenge in movement ecology is to describe ecologically meaningful residence sites from raw tracking data due to heterogeneous sampling frequency and uncertain site boundaries. Here, we develop a greedy nearest-neighbor clustering approach with local reassignment and polygon-based site c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043149] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a greedy nearest-neighbor clustering method with local reassignment and polygon-based site detection to identify and quantify revisitation of residence sites in animal GPS tracking data, applied to two sympatric raven species.
motivation: Movement ecology lacks robust tools to extract ecologically meaningful residence sites from raw tracking data, which suffers from heterogeneous sampling frequency and ambiguous site boundaries.
method: A greedy nearest-neighbor clustering algorithm with local reassignment is combined with polygon-based site construction to define residence areas and count revisit events in tracking trajectories.
result: The approach yields stable site definitions and revisitation statistics that are compared across two sympatric raven species, revealing species-specific differences in site use.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a practical, sampling-robust framework for quantifying site revisitation in movement ecology, though it lies entirely outside quantum information science.

title: Erratum: Simultaneous X-ray Diffraction Measurements Of Nine Pressure Calibrants To 140 GPa [Phys. Rev. B 113, 144113 (2026)]
authors: Guoyin Shen And Jesse S. Smith
abstract:
Author(s): Guoyin Shen and Jesse S. Smith
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 259902] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting a high-pressure physics paper on simultaneous X-ray diffraction measurements of nine pressure calibrants up to 140 GPa.
motivation: The original work aimed to cross-calibrate multiple pressure standards under identical high-pressure conditions to improve consistency of pressure determination in diamond anvil cell experiments.
method: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction was used to measure nine pressure calibrants simultaneously up to 140 GPa; this erratum reports corrections to the published data/analysis.
result: The erratum provides corrected values or figures for the pressure calibration measurements reported in Phys. Rev. B 113, 144113.
conclusion: The corrected results refine the pressure calibration reference data for high-pressure experiments, with no connection to quantum information science.

title: Energy-based Model Integrated With Artificial Intelligence For Electrospinning Jet Profiles
authors: Gaoxiao Jiang, Rui Ma, And Chen-Xu Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Gaoxiao Jiang, Rui Ma, and Chen-Xu Wu

We develop an energy-based theoretical framework to predict jet morphologies in electrospinning. tldr: An energy-based theoretical model combined with artificial intelligence is developed to predict jet morphology in electrospinning.
motivation: Understanding and predicting the morphology of charged polymer jets in electrospinning is important for controlling the resulting fibers, but a unified predictive framework is lacking.
method: The charged polymer jet is modeled as a one-dimensional elastic curve in a uniform electric field, incorporating external-field energy and an effective local curvature term, and the model is integrated with AI-based methods.
result: The framework predicts jet profiles/morphologies in electrospinning, in agreement with expected behavior of the modeled energies.
conclusion: The energy-based plus AI approach offers a route to predicting electrospinning jet shapes, with relevance to polymer processing rather than quantum science.

title: Long-range Assortativity
authors: Pablo I. Fierens And Leandro Chaves Rêgo
abstract:
Author(s): Pablo I. Fierens and Leandro Chaves Rêgo

The study of homophily in networks usually involves investigating whether nodes have a tendency to make more direct connections with similar nodes than what would happen in a random network. However, the study of homophily between nodes that are not directly connected is also of interest. Remarkably…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054308] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies long-range assortativity and homophily in networks, extending assortativity analysis beyond directly connected nodes.
motivation: Homophily research often focuses on direct connections, but correlations between non-adjacent nodes can also reveal important network structure.
method: The authors develop and analyze a framework for quantifying assortativity and homophily at longer network distances, likely using random-network baselines and network-theoretic measures.
result: The paper characterizes long-range assortativity patterns and shows how indirect similarity relationships differ from standard direct-neighbor assortativity.
conclusion: Long-range assortativity provides a broader view of network mixing and homophily, with implications for understanding network organization beyond local connections.
